accomplices-in-sexual-offences-indian-la.en:
Consider this situation. A college student is raped at a party by one man. A second man keeps watch at the door. A third films it and sends the clip to a group chat. Later, a policeman who knows one of the families makes sure the evidence goes missing. Ask most people how many criminals are in that story and they will count one.

Indian law counts at least four. It has separate offences for the person who joins in, the person who records or forwards, the person who destroys evidence and, when the survivor is a child, the person who knew and said nothing. This is general information, not legal advice.

## The group: why every member is guilty of rape

Section 70 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) does not ask which member of a group committed the act. Where a woman is raped by one or more persons "constituting a group or acting in furtherance of a common intention", each of them "shall be deemed to have committed the offence of rape" [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

The sentence is at least 20 years' rigorous imprisonment and can run for the rest of natural life. If she is under 18, it is imprisonment for the rest of natural life, or death. A man acting alone faces a minimum of 10 years under Section 64 [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

So the man at the door is not a witness. If a court finds he shared the group's intention, which the prosecution must prove, he is sentenced as a rapist. Police registered 1,537 gang-rape cases in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## The camera: filming and sharing as separate crimes

Recording an assault is its own set of crimes, added to whatever else the person did.

Section 77 of the BNS treats sharing a private image of a woman without her consent as voyeurism: 1 to 3 years on a first conviction, 3 to 7 on a repeat [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Under the Information Technology Act, publishing or transmitting sexually explicit material online carries up to 5 years and a fine of up to Rs 10 lakh under Section 67A, and up to 7 years on a repeat [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. The law punishes the transmitting and does not ask about the motive. Someone who forwards the clip "so people know what happened" has transmitted it.

If the person in the video is under 18, Section 67B reaches past the one holding the phone: creating, collecting, browsing, downloading or exchanging such material carries the same penalties [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. In September 2024 the Supreme Court held that storing child sexual abuse material is itself an offence under Section 15 of POCSO when the circumstances show the intent the law specifies, even if it is never shared [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]].

Police registered 2,197 cases under Section 67A in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That counts FIRs, not clips in circulation.

## The cover-up: destroying evidence

On 10 June 2019 a court in Pathankot convicted six of the seven people tried for the rape and murder of an eight-year-old girl in Kathua. Three were sentenced to life imprisonment for murder and 25 years for gang rape. The other three were policemen. They were not convicted of the rape or the murder. They got five years each for destroying evidence [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]]. One accused was acquitted.

The law also punishes the quieter cover-up, the one done by doing nothing. Under Section 199 of the BNS, a police officer who fails to record an FIR for rape, sexual assault, acid attack or trafficking faces 6 months to 2 years' rigorous imprisonment. Under Section 200, the person in charge of a hospital that refuses a rape survivor free treatment faces up to 1 year [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## The silence: POCSO's duty to report, and abetment

When the survivor is a child, silence is a crime. Section 19 of the POCSO Act puts a duty on anyone who knows a child has been sexually abused to report it. Section 21 punishes failing to report with up to 6 months in prison or a fine; the head of a company or institution who fails to report abuse by a subordinate faces up to 1 year and a fine [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

That covers the teacher who was told, the hostel warden who saw, the relative who did not want to break the family. POCSO separately punishes abetting an offence and attempting one.

Of the 69,191 POCSO cases registered in 2024, 218 fell under Sections 17 to 22, which cover abetment, attempt, failure to report and false complaints together [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The figure needs care: NCRB counts each FIR once, under its most serious offence, so a case that charges an abuser and also the adult who hid the abuse is counted under the assault.

Even so, set it beside another figure from the same report. In the 44,126 penetrative assault cases, the offender was a stranger or unidentified in only 1,492 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Abuse by someone the household knows is rarely invisible to every other adult. The law against silence was written for those adults, and it almost never shows up in the data as the main charge.

## The bystander: what the law does and does not require

Two duties apply to everyone. If the survivor is a child and you know, you must report. And whoever the survivor is, you must not identify her. Section 72 of the BNS punishes publishing the name of a rape survivor, or any detail that could reveal who she is, with up to 2 years in prison unless she authorises it in writing [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The Supreme Court has said this covers social media and facts that identify her "even in a remote manner" [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Police registered just 11 cases under Section 72 in July-December 2024, the new code's first six months [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

None of these provisions makes a friend an offender for keeping an adult survivor's confidence. Around an adult's rape, they put duties on institutions: the police station that must record the complaint, and the hospital that must treat her free and inform the police [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

You can do more than the minimum. Anyone can report a cognizable offence at any police station, wherever it happened; that is the Zero FIR in Section 173 of the BNSS [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Since 20 February 2026, platforms must remove nude or sexual images of a person within two hours of that person's complaint [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. If a clip reaches you, do not forward it, make sure she or someone she trusts knows it exists, and report it.
accomplices-in-sexual-offences-indian-la.hg:
Ek situation sochiye. Ek college student ka ek party mein ek aadmi rape karta hai. Doosra aadmi darwaze pe pehra deta hai. Teesra video banata hai aur clip ek group chat mein bhej deta hai. Baad mein ek policeman, jo ek family ko jaanta hai, ensure karta hai ki evidence gayab ho jaaye. Zyada tar log poochhne pe kahenge ki is kahani mein ek hi criminal hai.

Indian law kam se kam chaar ginta hai. Usmein alag offences hain us insaan ke liye jo saath deta hai, jo record ya forward karta hai, jo evidence mitata hai, aur agar survivor bachcha hai, toh us insaan ke liye jo jaanta tha aur chup raha. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Group: har member rape ka doshi kyun hai

Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ka Section 70 yeh nahi poochhta ki group mein se kisne act kiya. Jab kisi woman ka rape ek ya zyada log "constituting a group or acting in furtherance of a common intention" karte hain, toh un mein se har ek "shall be deemed to have committed the offence of rape" [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Saza kam se kam 20 saal ki rigorous imprisonment hai aur poori natural life tak ja sakti hai. Agar woh 18 se kam hai, toh saza natural life tak ki imprisonment ya death hai. Akele rape karne wale aadmi ko Section 64 ke under kam se kam 10 saal milte hain [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Toh darwaze pe khada aadmi witness nahi hai. Agar court maanta hai ki uska bhi group wala intention tha, jo prosecution ko prove karna hota hai, toh use rapist ki tarah saza milti hai. Police ne 2024 mein gang rape ke 1,537 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Camera: video banana aur share karna alag crimes

Assault record karna apne aap mein crimes ka ek set hai, jo us insaan ke baaki kaam ke upar judta hai.

BNS ka Section 77 kisi woman ki private image uski consent ke bina share karne ko voyeurism maanta hai: pehli conviction pe 1 se 3 saal, dobara pe 3 se 7 saal [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Information Technology Act ke Section 67A ke under online sexually explicit material publish ya transmit karne pe 5 saal tak ki jail aur 10 lakh rupaye tak ka fine hai, aur dobara karne pe 7 saal tak [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Law transmit karne ko saza deta hai, motive nahi poochhta. Jo clip "taaki logon ko pata chale kya hua" soch kar forward karta hai, usne bhi transmit kiya hai.

Agar video mein dikh raha insaan 18 se kam hai, toh Section 67B phone pakadne wale se aage tak jaata hai: aisa material banana, collect karna, browse karna, download karna ya exchange karna, sab pe wahi saza hai [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. September 2024 mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki child sexual abuse material store karna bhi POCSO ke Section 15 ke under offence hai, jab circumstances law mein likha intent dikhate hon, chahe woh kabhi share na hua ho [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]].

Police ne 2024 mein Section 67A ke under 2,197 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh FIRs ki ginti hai, circulate ho rahe clips ki nahi.

## Cover-up: evidence mitana

10 June 2019 ko Pathankot ki ek court ne Kathua mein aath saal ki bachchi ke rape aur murder ke case mein trial pe rahe saat mein se chhe logon ko convict kiya. Teen ko murder ke liye life imprisonment aur gang rape ke liye 25 saal mile. Baaki teen policemen the. Unhe rape ya murder ke liye convict nahi kiya gaya. Unhe evidence mitane ke liye paanch-paanch saal mile [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]]. Ek accused acquit hua.

Law us chupke wale cover-up ko bhi saza deta hai, jo kuch na karke hota hai. BNS ke Section 199 ke under, jo police officer rape, sexual assault, acid attack ya trafficking ki FIR record nahi karta, use 6 mahine se 2 saal ki rigorous imprisonment ho sakti hai. Section 200 ke under, jo hospital in-charge rape survivor ko free treatment dene se mana karta hai, use 1 saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Chuppi: POCSO ki report karne ki duty, aur abetment

Jab survivor bachcha ho, toh chup rehna crime hai. POCSO Act ka Section 19 har us insaan pe duty daalta hai jo jaanta hai ki kisi bachche ka sexual abuse hua hai, ki woh report kare. Section 21 report na karne pe 6 mahine tak ki jail ya fine deta hai. Kisi company ya institution ka head jo apne subordinate ke abuse ko report nahi karta, use 1 saal tak ki jail aur fine ho sakta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Isme woh teacher aata hai jise bataya gaya tha, woh hostel warden jisne dekha tha, woh rishtedaar jo family todna nahi chahta tha. POCSO alag se offence ko abet karne aur attempt karne ko bhi saza deta hai.

2024 mein register hue 69,191 POCSO cases mein se 218 Sections 17 se 22 ke under the, jo abetment, attempt, report na karna aur jhoothi complaint, sab ek saath cover karte hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Is figure ko dhyaan se padhna zaroori hai: NCRB har FIR ko ek hi baar ginta hai, uske sabse serious offence ke under. Toh jis case mein abuser aur abuse chhupane wale adult dono pe charge laga, woh assault ke under gina jaata hai.

Phir bhi, isi report ka ek aur figure saath mein rakhiye. 44,126 penetrative assault cases mein offender sirf 1,492 mein stranger ya unidentified tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jo abuse ghar ka jaana-pehchaana insaan karta hai, woh baaki har adult se poori tarah chhupa nahi rehta. Chuppi ke khilaaf law unhi adults ke liye likha gaya tha, aur data mein woh main charge ke roop mein lagbhag kabhi nahi dikhta.

## Bystander: law kya maangta hai aur kya nahi

Do duties sab pe lagti hain. Agar survivor bachcha hai aur aap jaante hain, toh aapko report karna hai. Aur survivor koi bhi ho, aapko uski pehchaan nahi kholni. BNS ka Section 72 rape survivor ka naam, ya koi bhi detail jisse pata chal sake woh kaun hai, publish karne pe 2 saal tak ki jail deta hai, jab tak woh khud likh kar permission na de [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Supreme Court ne kaha hai ki yeh social media pe bhi lagta hai, aur un facts pe bhi jo use "even in a remote manner" identify karein [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Naye code ke pehle chhe mahino, July-December 2024, mein police ne Section 72 ke under sirf 11 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

In mein se koi bhi provision kisi dost ko sirf isliye offender nahi banata ki usne ek adult survivor ki baat raaz rakhi. Adult ke rape ke case mein yeh duties institutions pe hain: police station jise complaint record karni hai, aur hospital jise use free treat karna hai aur police ko inform karna hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Aap minimum se zyada kar sakte hain. Koi bhi insaan cognizable offence ki report kisi bhi police station pe kar sakta hai, chahe woh kahin bhi hua ho. Yahi BNSS ke Section 173 ka Zero FIR hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. 20 February 2026 se platforms ko kisi insaan ki nude ya sexual images uski complaint ke do ghante ke andar hatani hoti hain [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. Agar koi clip aap tak pahunche, toh forward mat kijiye, ensure kijiye ki use ya uske kisi bharose wale ko pata ho ki woh exist karti hai, aur report kijiye.

allahabad-attempt-to-rape-order-stayed-2.en:
In 2021, in Uttar Pradesh, two men were accused of trying to rape an 11-year-old girl. A trial court summoned them for attempt to rape under the Indian Penal Code and the POCSO Act. On 17 March 2025, deciding a revision petition filed by the accused, Justice Ram Manohar Narayan Mishra of the Allahabad High Court ruled that what they were alleged to have done was not an attempt to rape [[livelaw-allahabad-stay-2025]].

This file does not repeat the High Court's description of the acts. It does not need to. The question the case raised is about law and language: how judges draw the line between "preparation" and "attempt" in a child's case, and how they write about it.

## The line between preparation and attempt

Criminal law usually punishes three stages: planning or preparing a crime, attempting it, and committing it. Preparation is usually not a crime by itself. An attempt is. The High Court held that the prosecution had not shown the accused went beyond preparation, and directed that they be tried instead under Section 354-B of the IPC (assault with intent to disrobe a woman) read with Sections 9 and 10 of POCSO, which cover aggravated sexual assault without penetration [[livelaw-allahabad-stay-2025]] [[scobserver-allahabad-stay-2025]].

Those are lesser offences than attempt to rape. Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which replaced the IPC for crimes after 1 July 2024, assault with intent to disrobe is Section 76, with three to seven years [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The difference is not technical for the family. It changes what the accused are tried for and the sentence they could face.

Attempt is not a rare charge. Police registered 2,561 cases of attempt to rape in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Every one of them turns on the same kind of judgment about where an act stopped and why.

## Nine days to a stay

The ruling spread fast, and the way it reached the Supreme Court is itself instructive. On 24 March 2025 one bench dismissed a petition against it because the petitioner had no standing in the case. The court then took up the matter on its own, after a letter from the women's organisation We the Women of India [[scobserver-allahabad-stay-2025]].

On 26 March 2025 Justices B.R. Gavai and Augustine George Masih stayed the High Court's observations. They said the remarks were unknown to the "canons of law" and showed an "inhuman approach". They also noted that this was no slip made in a hurry: the judgment had not been "dictated at the spur of the moment", but delivered almost four months after it was reserved [[pti-allahabad-stay-2025]]. The court issued notice to the Union and Uttar Pradesh governments.

> A judgment written after four months of thought is a considered view. That is why the Supreme Court treated its language as a problem, not a typo.

## A pattern, not one judge

Three weeks later the same bench was confronted with another Allahabad High Court order, from 11 March 2025, granting bail to a man accused of rape and saying the woman had "invited trouble" for herself. Justice Gavai said bail could be granted, but "one has to be careful when saying such things especially on this side" [[scroll-invited-trouble-2025]].

Neither remark was new in kind. In 2023 the Supreme Court had already issued a Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes, telling judges to stop using phrases that blame or shame women [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

## How it ended, in 2026

The case was finally decided in a judgment dated 10 February 2026. A bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant said the efforts to sensitise judges "have not borne the fruit that was expected" [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]]. It set aside the High Court's order and restored the trial court's original summons for attempt to rape. It also directed the National Judicial Academy to set up an expert committee, chaired by its director, former Supreme Court judge Aniruddha Bose, to draft guidelines on sensitivity in sexual-offence cases [[hansindia-sc-sets-aside-allahabad-2026]]. On 14 July 2026 the court approved those guidelines and ordered them sent to every High Court and district court, and to prosecutors and the police [[theprint-sc-sensitivity-guidelines-2026]].

That is a stronger outcome than the stay. But note what it took: nationwide outrage, a letter, a Supreme Court bench willing to act on its own. Most children's cases never get that. At the end of 2024, 2,86,903 POCSO cases were waiting for trial [[ncrb-cii-2024]], and almost none of their orders will ever be read outside the courtroom.

## What this means for a family

Imagine the parents of a 12-year-old in Bareilly who reported an attack on their daughter. They hear in court that the charge is being reduced. They are not lawyers. What they can do: ask the public prosecutor to explain the change in writing, ask whether the state will challenge it, and ask a District Legal Services Authority lawyer for free help. Anyone who knows that a child has been sexually abused must report it to the police or the Special Juvenile Police Unit [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]].

The 2025 Allahabad case shows two things at once. A single judge's words can make a child's case worse, and the system can correct it when enough people pay attention. The work is making that correction routine. This is general information, not legal advice.
allahabad-attempt-to-rape-order-stayed-2.hg:
2021 mein Uttar Pradesh mein do aadmiyon par 11 saal ki ek bachchi ke rape ki koshish ka aarop laga. Trial court ne unhe Indian Penal Code aur POCSO Act ke under attempt to rape ke liye summon kiya. 17 March 2025 ko accused ki revision petition par faisla dete hue Allahabad High Court ke Justice Ram Manohar Narayan Mishra ne kaha ki unpar jo karne ka aarop hai, woh attempt to rape nahi hai [[livelaw-allahabad-stay-2025]].

Yeh file High Court ke act wale description ko nahi dohrayegi. Iski zaroorat bhi nahi hai. Is case ne jo sawaal uthaya, woh law aur bhasha ka hai: ek bachchi ke case mein judges "preparation" aur "attempt" ke beech line kaise kheenchte hain, aur us baare mein likhte kaise hain.

## Preparation aur attempt ke beech ki line

Criminal law aam taur par teen stages ko dekhta hai: crime ki planning ya taiyari, uski koshish, aur use poora karna. Sirf taiyari aam taur par khud mein crime nahi hoti. Koshish hoti hai. High Court ne kaha ki prosecution yeh nahi dikha paaya ki accused preparation se aage gaye, aur unpar IPC ki Section 354-B (aurat ke kapde utaarne ki niyat se hamla) ke saath POCSO ki Sections 9 aur 10 mein case chalane ko kaha, jo bina penetration ke aggravated sexual assault ke liye hain [[livelaw-allahabad-stay-2025]] [[scobserver-allahabad-stay-2025]].

Yeh attempt to rape se halke offences hain. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita mein, jo 1 July 2024 ke baad ke crimes par IPC ki jagah laagu hai, kapde utaarne ki niyat se hamla Section 76 hai, jisme teen se saat saal ki saza hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Parivaar ke liye yeh farq technical nahi hai. Isse badalta hai ki accused par kis cheez ka trial chalega aur unhe kitni saza ho sakti hai.

Attempt koi rare charge nahi hai. 2024 mein police ne attempt to rape ke 2,561 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Har case isi tarah ke faisle par tika hota hai ki act kahan ruka aur kyun.

## Nau din mein rok

Ruling tezi se phaili, aur Supreme Court tak pahunchne ka raasta khud kuch sikhata hai. 24 March 2025 ko ek bench ne iske khilaaf ek petition yeh keh kar khaarij kar di ki petitioner ka is case se koi lena-dena nahi (locus nahi). Phir women's organisation We the Women of India ki ek chitthi ke baad court ne yeh maamla khud uthaya [[scobserver-allahabad-stay-2025]].

26 March 2025 ko Justices B.R. Gavai aur Augustine George Masih ne High Court ke observations par rok laga di. Unhone kaha ki yeh remarks "canons of law" yaani law ke usoolon ke liye anjaan hain aur ek "inhuman approach", yaani amaanviya soch, dikhate hain. Unhone yeh bhi note kiya ki yeh jaldbaazi ki galti nahi thi: judgment "dictated at the spur of the moment" nahi tha, yaani usi pal court mein nahi bola gaya tha, balki reserve hone ke lagbhag chaar mahine baad diya gaya [[pti-allahabad-stay-2025]]. Court ne Union aur Uttar Pradesh sarkaron ko notice bheja.

> Chaar mahine soch kar likha gaya judgment ek soch-samjha hua view hota hai. Isiliye Supreme Court ne uski bhasha ko problem maana, typing ki galti nahi.

## Ek judge nahi, ek pattern

Teen hafte baad wahi bench ek aur Allahabad High Court order ke saamne thi, jo 11 March 2025 ka tha. Usme rape ke ek accused ko bail dete hue kaha gaya tha ki aurat ne khud "invited trouble", yaani museebat ko bulaya. Justice Gavai ne kaha ki bail di ja sakti hai, lekin "one has to be careful when saying such things especially on this side", yaani khaas taur par judges ki taraf se aisi baatein kehte waqt dhyaan rakhna chahiye [[scroll-invited-trouble-2025]].

Dono remarks apni tarah ke naye nahi the. 2023 mein hi Supreme Court ne Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes nikali thi, jisme judges ko aise shabd chhodne ko kaha gaya tha jo aurton ko blame ya sharminda karte hain [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

## 2026 mein kaise khatam hua

Case ka final faisla 10 February 2026 ki tareekh wale judgment mein aaya. Chief Justice Surya Kant ki bench ne kaha ki judges ko sensitise karne ki koshishon ka "have not borne the fruit that was expected", yaani ummeed ke mutabik nateeja nahi mila [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]]. Bench ne High Court ka order radd kiya aur trial court ka attempt to rape wala original summons wapas laagu kar diya. Court ne National Judicial Academy ko ek expert committee banane ko kaha, jiske chairman uske director, Supreme Court ke former judge Aniruddha Bose hain, taaki sexual offence cases mein sensitivity par guidelines ban sakein [[hansindia-sc-sets-aside-allahabad-2026]]. 14 July 2026 ko court ne in guidelines ko manzoori di aur inhe har High Court aur district court, prosecutors aur police tak bhejne ka order diya [[theprint-sc-sensitivity-guidelines-2026]].

Yeh stay se mazboot nateeja hai. Lekin dekhiye isme kya laga: desh bhar ka gussa, ek chitthi, aur ek Supreme Court bench jo khud kadam uthane ko taiyar thi. Zyadatar bachchon ke cases ko yeh nahi milta. 2024 ke end mein 2,86,903 POCSO cases trial ke intezaar mein the [[ncrb-cii-2024]], aur unke orders lagbhag kabhi courtroom ke bahar nahi padhe jaayenge.

## Ek parivaar ke liye iska matlab

Sochiye, Bareilly mein ek 12 saal ki bachchi ke maa-baap ne uspar hue hamle ki report ki. Court mein unhe pata chalta hai ki charge ghataya ja raha hai. Woh lawyer nahi hain. Woh kya kar sakte hain: public prosecutor se is badlaav ki wajah likh kar maangein, poochein ki kya state ise challenge karega, aur District Legal Services Authority ke lawyer se free madad maangein. Jise bhi pata ho ki kisi bachche ke saath sexual abuse hua hai, use police ya Special Juvenile Police Unit ko report karna hota hai [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]].

2025 ka Allahabad case ek saath do baatein dikhata hai. Ek judge ke shabd ek bachchi ke case ko aur bigaad sakte hain, aur jab kaafi log dhyaan dein toh system use sudhaar sakta hai. Asli kaam is sudhaar ko routine banana hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

aparajita-bill-returned-centre-objection.en:
In September 2024, a month after the rape and murder of a doctor at RG Kar Medical College and Hospital in Kolkata, West Bengal's Assembly voted unanimously for the Aparajita Woman and Child Bill. It made death mandatory where a rape victim dies or is left in a vegetative state [[barandbench-aparajita-bill-2024]], and made life imprisonment the minimum, and death the maximum, for every rape under Section 64 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita [[livelaw-aparajita-explainer-2024]]. Because criminal law is shared between the Centre and the states, the bill needed the President's assent, and on 6 September 2024 the Governor reserved it for her consideration [[livelaw-aparajita-explainer-2024]].

In July 2025 it came back. The Governor sent the bill to the state government to consider objections raised by the Union Home Ministry [[theprint-aparajita-bill-returned-2025]] [[scroll-aparajita-bill-returned-2025]]. This is general information, not legal advice; here is what the objections were and why they matter.

## Objection 1: a minimum of life for every rape

Under the BNS today, rape carries at least 10 years' rigorous imprisonment and up to life; aggravated forms, such as rape by police, relatives, guardians or teachers, carry 10 years up to imprisonment for the rest of natural life [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The bill would have made life the floor for every rape. The Home Ministry called that "excessively harsh and disproportionate" [[theprint-aparajita-bill-returned-2025]].

Proportionality sounds like a lawyer's word, but it decides real cases. When every rape carries the same minimum as murder, a judge who has doubts about a case has only two choices: a life sentence or an acquittal. The risk is that the second becomes more tempting.

## Objection 2: erasing the protection for young girls

The bill would have deleted Section 65 of the BNS [[theprint-aparajita-bill-returned-2025]]. That section exists to treat crimes against children more seriously: raping a girl under 16 carries at least 20 years, and raping a girl under 12 carries at least 20 years or death [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The ministry said removing the age-based classification "undermines the principle of proportionality in sentencing" [[theprint-aparajita-bill-returned-2025]]. In other words, a law sold as protecting children would have removed the one section that singles out crimes against them.

## Objection 3: taking the decision away from judges

The bill made death mandatory where the victim dies or is left in a persistent vegetative state. Under the BNS, such a case already carries at least 20 years, up to the rest of natural life, or death [[indiacode-bns-2023]], with the judge deciding which. The ministry objected that removing judicial discretion "violates established legal norms and Supreme Court rulings" [[theprint-aparajita-bill-returned-2025]].

The RG Kar case shows how that discretion works. In January 2025 a Sealdah court convicted the accused and, after weighing the case, decided it was not "rarest of the rare", sentencing him to imprisonment for the rest of his natural life [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. Under the Aparajita Bill, that weighing would not have been allowed.

## What tougher sentences cannot fix

Back in 2013, the Justice Verma Committee, set up after the 2012 Delhi gang rape, advised against the death penalty for rape, noting it "may not have a deterrent effect" [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. The data since then explain why. In 96.8% of rape cases registered in India in 2024, the offender was known to the victim; family members were accused in 2,134 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. When the accused is an uncle, a neighbour or a boyfriend, a mandatory life or death sentence can make a family less likely to go to the police, not more.

And in West Bengal itself, the problem was never too-light sentences. In 2024 the state had the lowest conviction rate for crimes against women of any state, 1.6%, with 3,84,388 such cases pending trial at year's end [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A harsher maximum does nothing for a case that never reaches a verdict.

## Where it stands

The bill is not law. Accounts differ on whether it went back via the President or directly from the Governor, but either way it was returned for the state to reconsider [[theprint-aparajita-bill-returned-2025]]. The state could revise it or pass it again; we could not confirm that it has done either. The bill also proposed faster investigations, 21 days instead of two months [[livelaw-aparajita-explainer-2024]]. That part was not among the objections reported. If West Bengal wants to protect women, faster investigations, working forensic labs and trials that end are where the proof will be.
aparajita-bill-returned-centre-objection.hg:
September 2024 mein, Kolkata ke RG Kar Medical College and Hospital mein ek doctor ke rape aur murder ke ek mahine baad, West Bengal Assembly ne sarvsammati se Aparajita Woman and Child Bill paas kiya. Isne us case mein maut ki saza mandatory kar di jahan rape victim ki maut ho jaaye ya woh vegetative state mein chali jaaye [[barandbench-aparajita-bill-2024]], aur Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ke Section 64 ke under har rape ke liye umrqaid ko minimum aur maut ko maximum saza bana diya [[livelaw-aparajita-explainer-2024]]. Kyunki criminal law Centre aur states ke beech saajha hai, bill ko President ki manzoori chahiye thi, aur 6 September 2024 ko Governor ne ise unke vichaar ke liye reserve kar diya [[livelaw-aparajita-explainer-2024]].

July 2025 mein yeh wapas aa gaya. Governor ne bill ko state government ke paas bhej diya taaki woh Union Home Ministry ke objections par vichaar kare [[theprint-aparajita-bill-returned-2025]] [[scroll-aparajita-bill-returned-2025]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi; neeche hai ki objections kya the aur kyun maayne rakhte hain.

## Objection 1: har rape ke liye umrqaid ki minimum saza

Aaj BNS ke under rape ki saza kam se kam 10 saal ki rigorous imprisonment aur umrqaid tak hai; aggravated forms, jaise police, rishtedaar, guardian ya teacher dwara rape, mein 10 saal se lekar baaki ki poori natural life tak ki qaid hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Bill har rape ke liye umrqaid ko neeche ki seema bana deta. Home Ministry ne ise "excessively harsh and disproportionate" kaha [[theprint-aparajita-bill-returned-2025]].

Proportionality vakeelon ka shabd lagta hai, lekin yeh asli cases ka faisla karta hai. Jab har rape ki minimum saza murder jitni ho, toh jis judge ko case par shak ho uske paas sirf do raaste bachte hain: umrqaid ya bari karna. Khatra yeh hai ki doosra raasta zyada lubhaane lagta hai.

## Objection 2: chhoti ladkiyon ki protection mita dena

Bill BNS ka Section 65 hata deta [[theprint-aparajita-bill-returned-2025]]. Yeh section bachchon ke khilaf crimes ko zyada gambhirta se lene ke liye hai: 16 se kam umar ki ladki ke rape par kam se kam 20 saal, aur 12 se kam umar ki ladki ke rape par kam se kam 20 saal ya maut [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Ministry ne kaha ki umar ke hisaab se yeh classification hatana "undermines the principle of proportionality in sentencing" [[theprint-aparajita-bill-returned-2025]]. Yaani bachchon ko bachane ke naam par becha gaya law wahi ek section hata deta jo unke khilaf crimes ko alag se pehchaanta hai.

## Objection 3: judges se faisla chheen lena

Bill ne un cases mein maut mandatory kar di jahan victim ki maut ho jaaye ya woh persistent vegetative state mein chali jaaye. BNS ke under aisa case pehle se kam se kam 20 saal, baaki natural life tak, ya maut ki saza rakhta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]], aur judge tay karta hai kaunsi. Ministry ne objection kiya ki judicial discretion hatana "violates established legal norms and Supreme Court rulings" [[theprint-aparajita-bill-returned-2025]].

RG Kar case dikhata hai ki yeh discretion kaise kaam karta hai. January 2025 mein Sealdah court ne accused ko convict kiya aur case ko tolne ke baad tay kiya ki yeh "rarest of the rare" nahi hai, aur use baaki natural life ki qaid di [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. Aparajita Bill ke under yeh tolna allowed nahi hota.

## Sakht sazayein kya theek nahi kar sakti

2013 mein, 2012 ke Delhi gang rape ke baad bani Justice Verma Committee ne rape ke liye death penalty ke khilaf salah di thi, yeh kehte hue ki iska "may not have a deterrent effect" [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Tab se ka data batata hai kyun. 2024 mein India mein register hue 96.8% rape cases mein offender victim ka jaan-pehchaan wala tha; 2,134 cases mein accused parivaar ke log the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jab accused chacha, padosi ya boyfriend ho, toh mandatory umrqaid ya maut ki saza parivaar ko police tak jaane se aur rok sakti hai, badha nahi sakti.

Aur khud West Bengal mein problem kabhi halki sazayein nahi thi. 2024 mein women ke khilaf crimes mein state ka conviction rate kisi bhi state se kam, 1.6%, tha, aur saal ke aakhir mein aise 3,84,388 cases trial ke intezaar mein the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jo case kabhi verdict tak pahunchta hi nahi, uske liye sakht maximum saza kuch nahi karti.

## Ab kya sthiti hai

Bill law nahi hai. Is par alag alag accounts hain ki yeh President ke zariye wapas gaya ya seedha Governor se, lekin dono tarah yeh state ko dobara vichaar ke liye lautaya gaya [[theprint-aparajita-bill-returned-2025]]. State ise badal sakta hai ya phir se paas kar sakta hai; hum confirm nahi kar paaye ki usne inme se kuch kiya. Bill ne tez investigation ka bhi proposal diya tha, do mahine ki jagah 21 din [[livelaw-aparajita-explainer-2024]]. Woh hissa report hue objections mein shaamil nahi tha. Agar West Bengal women ko bachana chahta hai, toh tez investigations, kaam karti forensic labs aur khatam hone wale trials hi asli saboot honge.

attempt-to-rape-cases-two-states.en:
Police in India registered 2,561 cases of attempt to rape in 2024. West Bengal accounted for 809 of them and Rajasthan for 778: together, 62% of the national total. The next two states were far behind, Assam with 155 and Odisha with 118 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A map this lopsided may say as much about how police in each state decide what to call an attack as about where attacks happen.

## Two states, 62% of the cases

Put the attempt figures next to each state's other sexual-offence numbers and the pattern sharpens. West Bengal registered 1,118 rape cases and 809 attempts, so attempts come close to its rape count. Rajasthan registered 4,871 rapes, the most in India, and 778 attempts, a far smaller share [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Odisha shows the other end. It recorded only 118 attempts, but 7,299 cases of assault to outrage a woman's modesty and the highest rate of that offence in the country, 31.5 per lakh women. Rajasthan led the count for that offence too, with 8,276 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

None of this proves that a given state undercharges or overcharges. NCRB itself warns that states should not be compared on crime figures alone. But when neighbouring states register the same kind of incident in such different columns, the column is telling you about the police station as much as the crime.

## Attempt, assault or rape: where the legal lines fall

Consider one incident. A man forces his way into a room where a woman is alone and is stopped only because someone else walks in. At the station, the officer writing the FIR has several options, and each carries a different punishment.

Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), rape carries at least 10 years and up to life [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Assault to outrage a woman's modesty (Section 74) carries 1 to 5 years, sexual harassment (Section 75) up to 3 years, and assault to disrobe (Section 76) 3 to 7 years [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Attempt to rape is a separate head in NCRB's tables, apart from rape and from these lesser offences. Whether an incident is an attempt turns on how far the man got and what he meant to do, and police make the first call on both.

The counting rule then hides part of the picture. NCRB records each FIR once, under its most serious offence [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. An FIR that lists both attempt to rape and assault to outrage modesty shows up under only one of those heads. One that lists only Section 74 never appears as an attempt at all, whatever the woman said happened.

The law's own lines leave people out too. The BNS defines rape as an act by a man against a woman, so an attack of this kind on an adult man cannot be recorded as attempted rape at all [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## A falling national count: 3,288 in 2022, 2,561 in 2024

Nationally, attempt-to-rape cases fell from 3,288 in 2022 to 2,796 in 2023 and 2,561 in 2024, a drop of more than a fifth in two years [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Over the same period, the five lesser sexual offences that NCRB used to group together, from outrage of modesty to stalking, barely moved: 83,344 in 2022, 83,891 in 2023 and 83,908 in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

That does not prove relabelling. It does mean a falling attempt count cannot be read as fewer attacks on its own. In 2024, police also registered 8,409 cases of assault with intent to disrobe, an offence the BNS punishes with 3 to 7 years [[ncrb-cii-2024]] [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Where a case lands between these heads is a decision, and nobody publishes how it is made.

> The section in an FIR is the first judgment anyone passes on a sexual assault. It is made by a police officer, often within hours.

## When a court cuts the charge: the 2026 Supreme Court case

Courts can move the line as well. A High Court reduced the charges in a child sexual assault case from attempt to rape under Section 376 IPC and Section 18 of the POCSO Act to Section 354B IPC, the disrobing offence created in 2013, and to lesser POCSO sections [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]] [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].

The Supreme Court took up the order on its own. On 10 February 2026 a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and N.V. Anjaria said efforts to sensitise judges "have not borne the fruit that was expected". It asked an expert committee of the National Judicial Academy, headed by former judge Aniruddha Bose, to draft guidelines on sensitivity in sexual-offence cases [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]].

That case reached the country's top court. Most charging decisions, made at a police station or in a trial court, are never examined at that level.

## If your case was charged too low

This is general information, not legal advice. Start with the FIR. Under Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), the victim gets a free copy, and a report can be made at any police station [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Check the sections against what you told the police. If a station will not record the complaint properly, the law lets you write to the Superintendent of Police and then approach a magistrate.

In rape and sexual harassment cases, a magistrate, as far as practicable a woman, must record the survivor's statement [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Say everything in your own words. You are also entitled to an update on the investigation within 90 days [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

The label matters, but only if the trial ends. In West Bengal, courts convicted in just 1.6% of crimes-against-women trials in 2024, and 3,84,388 cases were pending at the end of the year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Getting the right section on the FIR is the first fight. A free lawyer from the District Legal Services Authority can help with the ones that follow.
attempt-to-rape-cases-two-states.hg:
2024 mein India ki police ne attempt to rape ke 2,561 cases register kiye. Inmein se 809 West Bengal mein the aur 778 Rajasthan mein: dono milkar national total ka 62%. Agle do states kaafi peeche the, Assam 155 ke saath aur Odisha 118 ke saath [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Itna ek-tarfa map shayad utna hi yeh batata hai ki har state ki police kisi attack ko kya naam deti hai, jitna yeh ki attacks kahan hote hain.

## Do states, 62% cases

Attempt ke figures ko har state ke baaki sexual-offence numbers ke saath rakhiye, toh pattern aur saaf ho jaata hai. West Bengal ne rape ke 1,118 cases aur 809 attempts register kiye, yaani attempts uske rape count ke kaafi kareeb hain. Rajasthan ne 4,871 rapes register kiye, jo India mein sabse zyada hain, aur 778 attempts, jo uske rape count ka bahut chhota hissa hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Odisha doosra chhor dikhata hai. Wahan sirf 118 attempts record hue, lekin assault to outrage a woman's modesty ke 7,299 cases, aur is offence ka desh mein sabse zyada rate, 31.5 per lakh women. Is offence ke count mein bhi Rajasthan sabse aage tha, 8,276 ke saath [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Isse yeh saabit nahi hota ki koi state kam ya zyada charge karta hai. NCRB khud warn karta hai ki states ko sirf crime figures ke base par compare nahi karna chahiye. Lekin jab padosi states ek jaisi ghatna ko itne alag columns mein register karte hain, toh column jitna crime ke baare mein batata hai, utna hi police station ke baare mein bhi.

## Attempt, assault ya rape: kanooni lines kahan khinchti hain

Ek ghatna socho. Ek aadmi zabardasti ek kamre mein ghusta hai jahan ek woman akeli hai, aur ruk sirf isliye jaata hai kyunki koi aur andar aa jaata hai. Station par FIR likhne wale officer ke paas kai options hain, aur har ek ki saza alag hai.

Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) mein rape ki saza kam se kam 10 years aur life tak hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Assault to outrage a woman's modesty (Section 74) mein 1 se 5 years, sexual harassment (Section 75) mein 3 years tak, aur assault to disrobe (Section 76) mein 3 se 7 years [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. NCRB ki tables mein attempt to rape ek alag head hai, rape aur in chhote offences dono se alag. Koi ghatna attempt hai ya nahi, yeh is par tikta hai ki aadmi kahan tak pahuncha aur uska iraada kya tha, aur dono par pehla faisla police karti hai.

Phir counting ka rule tasveer ka ek hissa chhupa deta hai. NCRB har FIR ko ek hi baar, uske sabse gambhir offence ke under record karta hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jis FIR mein attempt to rape aur assault to outrage modesty dono likhe hon, woh in dono mein se sirf ek head ke under dikhti hai. Jis FIR mein sirf Section 74 likha ho, woh kabhi attempt ki tarah dikhti hi nahi, chahe woman ne kuch bhi bataya ho.

Law ki apni lines bhi logon ko bahar chhod deti hain. BNS rape ko ek aadmi ka ek woman ke khilaaf kiya gaya act maanta hai, isliye kisi adult aadmi par aisa attack attempted rape ki tarah record ho hi nahi sakta [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Girta hua national count: 2022 mein 3,288, 2024 mein 2,561

Poore desh mein attempt-to-rape cases 2022 ke 3,288 se ghatkar 2023 mein 2,796 aur 2024 mein 2,561 ho gaye, do saal mein ek-paanchve se zyada ki giraavat [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Isi dauraan woh paanch chhote sexual offences jinhe NCRB pehle ek saath group karta tha, outrage of modesty se lekar stalking tak, lagbhag wahin ke wahin rahe: 2022 mein 83,344, 2023 mein 83,891 aur 2024 mein 83,908 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Isse relabelling saabit nahi hoti. Lekin iska matlab yeh zaroor hai ki sirf girte attempt count ko kam attacks ki tarah nahi padha ja sakta. 2024 mein police ne assault with intent to disrobe ke 8,409 cases bhi register kiye, ek aisa offence jiski saza BNS mein 3 se 7 years hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]] [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Koi case in heads mein se kahan girta hai, yeh ek faisla hai, aur yeh faisla kaise hota hai, yeh koi publish nahi karta.

> FIR mein likha section kisi sexual assault par pehla judgment hota hai. Yeh ek police officer deta hai, aksar kuch hi ghanton mein.

## Jab court charge kam kar de: 2026 ka Supreme Court case

Courts bhi line khiska sakte hain. Ek High Court ne ek child sexual assault case mein charges ko Section 376 IPC aur POCSO Act ke Section 18 ke under attempt to rape se ghata kar Section 354B IPC, yaani 2013 mein bana disrobing offence, aur POCSO ke chhote sections mein badal diya [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]] [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].

Supreme Court ne yeh order khud uthaya. 10 February 2026 ko Chief Justice Surya Kant aur Justices Joymalya Bagchi aur N.V. Anjaria ki bench ne kaha ki judges ko sensitise karne ki koshishon ne "have not borne the fruit that was expected", yaani woh nateeja nahi diya jiski ummeed thi. Court ne National Judicial Academy ki ek expert committee ko, jiske head former judge Aniruddha Bose hain, sexual-offence cases mein sensitivity par guidelines draft karne ko kaha [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]].

Yeh case desh ki sabse oonchi court tak pahuncha. Zyada tar charging faisle, chahe police station mein hon ya trial court mein, kabhi us level par jaanche nahi jaate.

## Agar aapka case kam charge hua hai

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi. Shuruaat FIR se kijiye. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ke Section 173 ke under victim ko FIR ki free copy milti hai, aur report kisi bhi police station mein ki ja sakti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Sections ko us baat se milaaiye jo aapne police ko batayi thi. Agar koi station complaint theek se record nahi karta, toh law aapko Superintendent of Police ko likhne aur phir magistrate ke paas jaane ka raasta deta hai.

Rape aur sexual harassment cases mein ek magistrate, jahan tak mumkin ho ek woman, survivor ka statement record karta hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Sab kuch apne shabdon mein boliye. Aapko 90 days ke andar investigation ka update paane ka bhi haq hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Label maayne rakhta hai, lekin tabhi jab trial khatam ho. West Bengal mein 2024 mein crimes-against-women trials mein se sirf 1.6% mein conviction hua, aur saal ke aakhir mein 3,84,388 cases pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. FIR par sahi section likhwana pehli ladaai hai. District Legal Services Authority ka free lawyer aage ki ladaaiyon mein madad kar sakta hai.

bail-in-sexual-offence-cases-answered.en:
After the FIR, the question that keeps many survivors awake is not about the trial. It is whether he will be back in the lane by the weekend. The answer depends on the offence, the court and what the court is told.

It matters because the wait is long: at the end of 2024, 1,85,785 rape cases were pending trial in India, 89.8% of those before the courts that year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Where the accused spends that time is decided at the bail stage. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Can he get bail before he is even arrested?

Sometimes. Anticipatory bail is an order, sought before any arrest, that a person be released on bail if he is arrested.

For two offences the law shuts that door. Section 482(4) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) bars anticipatory bail for anyone accused of raping a girl under 16 or of the gang rape of a girl under 18 [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), the first carries at least 20 years and the second imprisonment for the rest of natural life, or death [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The bar for girls under 16 dates from 2018 [[indiacode-cla-2018]].

Outside those two offences and the Atrocities Act (below), a man accused of raping an adult woman can apply, and a court decides. And the bar does not keep anyone in jail for good: once arrested, he can still seek regular bail.

## He has been arrested. What will the judge weigh?

In a rape case, bail is for the judge to decide; it is neither automatic nor ruled out. The prosecution can point to how serious the charge is (rape carries at least 10 years [[indiacode-bns-2023]]), to any risk that he will run, and to any sign that he could threaten the survivor or witnesses or tamper with evidence.

That last point is where your information counts. The public prosecutor can tell the judge only what he or she knows. Before the hearing, give the investigating officer and the prosecutor a written, dated note of every threat, visit or call from the accused's side.

**What must a judge not weigh?** Your clothes or your character. The Supreme Court's 2023 handbook on gender stereotypes rejects the idea that a woman's clothing invites sexual contact, and quotes a 2022 Kerala sessions court bail order that described the complainant as "exposing to dresses which are having some sexual provocative one" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. An order that reasons like that can be challenged in a higher court.

**Will I be told what is happening?** Police must update you on the investigation within 90 days [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## If he gets bail, can he come near me?

Not with the court's blessing. On 18 March 2021, in Aparna Bhat v. State of Madhya Pradesh, the Supreme Court struck down a High Court order granting bail on condition that the accused ask the complainant to tie a rakhi on him. It ruled that bail conditions "should not mandate, require or permit contact between the accused and the victim", and that courts must not suggest compromise or marriage [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]].

**Which conditions can I ask for?** Through the prosecutor or your own lawyer, ask the court to write them in specific words: no contact in person, by phone, online or through relatives; staying away from your home, workplace and college; no approach to witnesses. A vague order is hard to enforce. Keep a copy of the bail order.

## I am a Dalit or Adivasi survivor. Will I be told about bail hearings?

Yes, if the case is registered under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. Two things change.

First, the Act bars anticipatory bail for its offences. After a 2018 Supreme Court ruling required senior police approval before arrests and allowed a preliminary enquiry before an FIR, Parliament amended the Act in August 2018: no enquiry or approval is needed, and the bar on anticipatory bail applies despite any court judgment [[prs-sc-st-poa-amendment-bill-2018]].

Second, Section 15A, added in 2015, gives you the right to timely notice of court proceedings, including bail hearings, and makes it the state's duty to protect you, your dependants and your witnesses from intimidation, coercion, inducement or violence [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

All of this depends on the FIR naming the Act, so ask for it in your complaint. A public servant who is not from a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe and wilfully neglects the duty to register the FIR under the right sections faces six months to one year in prison [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

Outside this Act, do not assume the court will hear from you automatically. Give the prosecutor your objections in writing, and ask the District Legal Services Authority for a free lawyer [[nalsa]].

## What if he breaks a bail condition?

Bail is not final: the prosecution can ask the court to cancel it.

1. **Save the proof:** screenshots, call logs, the date and time, who came and what was said. Do not negotiate.
2. **Report it in writing** to the investigating officer and the public prosecutor, and ask them to move the court to cancel bail.
3. **Treat a threat as a new offence** and report it to the police. In danger, call 112.

**He has been convicted. Can he still get out?** An appeal court can suspend a sentence while it hears the appeal, and that order can be challenged too. In December 2019 a Delhi court sentenced a former MLA, Kuldeep Singh Sengar, to imprisonment for the remainder of his life for the 2017 rape of a minor girl in Unnao [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]]. In December 2025 the Delhi High Court suspended the sentence pending his appeal; the Supreme Court stayed that order on 29 December 2025 [[scobserver-unnao-stay-2025]] and set it aside on 15 May 2026, sending the question back to the High Court, where the appeal is pending [[livelaw-unnao-sc-2026]].

One gap to know: Section 482(4) names only offences against girls, while the right to updates belongs to any victim, including boys, men and transgender survivors. Bail decides where the accused waits. It does not decide the case.
bail-in-sexual-offence-cases-answered.hg:
FIR ke baad jo sawaal kai survivors ko raat bhar jagaye rakhta hai, woh trial ke baare mein nahi hota. Woh ye hota hai ki kya weekend tak woh wapas gali mein ghoom raha hoga. Jawab offence, court aur court ko kya bataya gaya, in teeno par depend karta hai.

Ye isliye maayne rakhta hai kyunki intezaar lamba hai: 2024 ke end mein India mein 1,85,785 rape cases trial ke liye pending the, us saal court ke saamne aaye cases ka 89.8% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Accused ye waqt kahan bitayega, ye bail stage par tay hota hai. Ye general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Kya use arrest se pehle hi bail mil sakti hai?

Kabhi-kabhi. Anticipatory bail ek order hai, jo arrest se pehle maanga jaata hai, ki agar person arrest ho to use bail par chhod diya jaaye.

Do offences ke liye law ye darwaaza band karta hai. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ka Section 482(4) us insaan ko anticipatory bail se rokta hai jis par 16 se kam umar ki ladki ke rape ya 18 se kam umar ki ladki ke gang rape ka aarop hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke under pehle offence mein kam se kam 20 years ki saza hai, aur doosre mein baaki natural life ki imprisonment, ya death [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. 16 se kam umar ki ladkiyon wala bar 2018 se hai [[indiacode-cla-2018]].

In do offences aur Atrocities Act (neeche dekho) ke bahar, kisi adult aurat ke rape ka accused apply kar sakta hai, aur court decide karti hai. Aur ye bar kisi ko hamesha ke liye jail mein nahi rakhta: arrest ke baad woh regular bail maang hi sakta hai.

## Woh arrest ho gaya hai. Judge kya dekhega?

Rape case mein bail ka faisla judge karta hai; na woh automatic hai, na naamumkin. Prosecution bata sakta hai ki charge kitna serious hai (rape mein kam se kam 10 years ki saza hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]), kya uske bhaagne ka khatra hai, aur kya woh survivor ya witnesses ko dhamka sakta hai ya evidence se chhed-chhaad kar sakta hai.

Aakhri point par tumhari information kaam aati hai. Public prosecutor judge ko sirf wahi bata sakta hai jo use pata ho. Hearing se pehle investigating officer aur prosecutor ko accused ki taraf se aaye har threat, visit ya call ka likhit, dated note do.

**Judge ko kya nahi dekhna chahiye?** Tumhare kapde ya tumhara character. Supreme Court ki 2023 ki gender stereotypes handbook is soch ko reject karti hai ki aurat ke kapde sexual contact ko invite karte hain, aur 2022 ke ek Kerala sessions court bail order ko quote karti hai jisne complainant ke baare mein likha tha "exposing to dresses which are having some sexual provocative one" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Aisi reasoning wale order ko higher court mein challenge kiya ja sakta hai.

**Kya mujhe bataya jaayega ki kya ho raha hai?** Police ko 90 din ke andar tumhe investigation ka update dena hota hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Bail mil gayi, to kya woh mere paas aa sakta hai?

Court ki marzi se to nahi. 18 March 2021 ko Aparna Bhat v. State of Madhya Pradesh mein Supreme Court ne ek High Court order ko khaarij kiya jisne is shart par bail di thi ki accused complainant se rakhi bandhwaane ki request kare. Court ne kaha ki bail conditions "should not mandate, require or permit contact between the accused and the victim", aur courts compromise ya shaadi ka sujhaav nahi de sakti [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]].

**Main kaunsi conditions maang sakti hoon?** Prosecutor ya apne lawyer ke through court se kaho ki conditions specific shabdon mein likhe: koi contact nahi, na milkar, na phone par, na online, na relatives ke through; tumhare ghar, workplace aur college se door rehna; witnesses se door rehna. Gol-mol order ko lagu karwana mushkil hota hai. Bail order ki copy apne paas rakho.

## Main Dalit ya Adivasi survivor hoon. Kya mujhe bail hearings ki khabar di jaayegi?

Haan, agar case SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act ke under register hai. Do cheezein badal jaati hain.

Pehli, ye Act apne offences ke liye anticipatory bail par rok lagata hai. 2018 mein Supreme Court ke ek ruling ne arrest se pehle senior police ki approval zaroori kar di thi aur FIR se pehle preliminary enquiry allow ki thi. Uske baad August 2018 mein Parliament ne Act amend kiya: koi enquiry ya approval zaroori nahi, aur anticipatory bail par rok kisi bhi court judgment ke bawajood lagu hogi [[prs-sc-st-poa-amendment-bill-2018]].

Doosri, 2015 mein joda gaya Section 15A tumhe court proceedings, bail hearings samet, ka time par notice paane ka right deta hai, aur state ki duty banata hai ki woh tumhe, tumhare dependants aur tumhare witnesses ko intimidation, coercion, inducement ya violence se bachaye [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

Ye sab is par tika hai ki FIR mein Act ka naam ho, isliye complaint mein hi ise maango. Jo public servant Scheduled Caste ya Scheduled Tribe se nahi hai aur sahi sections mein FIR register karne ki duty jaan-boojh kar neglect karta hai, use six months se one year tak jail ho sakti hai [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

Is Act ke bahar ye maan kar mat chalo ki court apne aap tumhari baat sunegi. Prosecutor ko apne objections likhit mein do, aur District Legal Services Authority se free lawyer maango [[nalsa]].

## Agar woh bail condition tod de to?

Bail final nahi hoti: prosecution court se use cancel karne ko keh sakta hai.

1. **Proof sambhaalo:** screenshots, call logs, date aur time, kaun aaya aur kya bola. Koi negotiation mat karo.
2. **Likhit mein report karo** investigating officer aur public prosecutor ko, aur unse kaho ki court mein bail cancel karne ki application dein.
3. **Threat ko naya offence maano** aur police mein report karo. Khatre mein ho to 112 call karo.

**Use conviction mil gayi. Kya woh phir bhi bahar aa sakta hai?** Appeal court appeal sunte waqt sentence suspend kar sakti hai, aur us order ko bhi challenge kiya ja sakta hai. December 2019 mein Delhi court ne former MLA Kuldeep Singh Sengar ko Unnao mein 2017 mein ek minor ladki ke rape ke liye remainder of his life ki imprisonment ki saza di [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]]. December 2025 mein Delhi High Court ne appeal pending rehne tak sentence suspend kar diya; Supreme Court ne 29 December 2025 ko us order par stay lagaya [[scobserver-unnao-stay-2025]] aur 15 May 2026 ko use set aside karke sawaal wapas High Court bhej diya, jahan appeal pending hai [[livelaw-unnao-sc-2026]].

Ek gap jaan lo: Section 482(4) sirf ladkiyon ke khilaaf offences ka naam leta hai, jabki updates paane ka right har victim ka hai, ladkon, mardon aur transgender survivors samet. Bail ye tay karti hai ki accused intezaar kahan karega. Case ka faisla bail se nahi hota.

bns-first-years-sexual-offences-timeline.en:
On 1 July 2024 India replaced its criminal laws in a single day. For sexual-violence cases, the record of the 28 months since is mixed. Most of the old law was renumbered. One offence was added and one was deleted. The backlog in the fast-track courts grew.

This timeline runs from the warning Parliament received before it passed the new codes to the Cabinet decision of November 2026. It is general information, not legal advice.

## November 2023: the warning Parliament received

Since the Supreme Court's Navtej Singh Johar ruling of 6 September 2018, Section 377 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) had applied only to non-consensual acts and bestiality [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]]. It was the section that covered forced sex against an adult man or a transgender person. The draft Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) left it out.

On 10 November 2023, Parliament's Standing Committee on Home Affairs warned that omitting Section 377 would leave non-consensual sexual offences against men, transgender persons and animals unpunished, and recommended keeping it. The government did not accept the recommendation [[prs-standing-committee-bns-2023]]. That year, police had registered 888 cases under the section [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## 1 July 2024: the switch

The BNS, the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) and the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam came into force on 1 July 2024 [[air-new-criminal-laws-2024]]. Offences committed before that date are still prosecuted under the IPC, so the two codes will sit side by side in courts for years.

For sexual offences, the new code did three things [[indiacode-bns-2023]]:

- **Carried over.** Rape is still an act by "a man" against "a woman" (Section 63), punishable with at least 10 years (Section 64). The exception for a husband whose wife is 18 or older stayed.
- **Added.** Section 69 made it an offence to obtain sex by "deceitful means" or by a promise of marriage made with no intention of keeping it, punishable with up to 10 years.
- **Deleted.** Section 377 has no counterpart.

The procedure code wrote the Zero FIR and the e-FIR into the statute and gave victims a right to an update on the investigation within 90 days. It allows two months for a rape investigation and two months from the chargesheet for the trial, with no consequence for missing either [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Late 2024: the first cases, and a court that would not fill a gap

**9 August 2024.** A doctor was raped and murdered at RG Kar Medical College and Hospital in Kolkata [[livelaw-rg-kar-task-force-2024]]. The crime fell in the new code's second month, so the trial ran entirely under the BNS. On 20 January 2025 a Sealdah court sentenced the convicted man to imprisonment for the rest of his natural life under Sections 64, 66 and 103(1) [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]].

**28 August 2024.** Hearing a petition on the missing offence, the Delhi High Court asked the Centre to decide within six months, remarking that "there can't be a vacuum to an offence" [[barandbench-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]].

**14 October 2024.** A Supreme Court bench led by Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud refused to entertain a similar plea. The court said it could not direct that a particular act is an offence: "we cannot compel the parliament to introduce the provision" [[livelaw-sc-bns-sexual-offences-men-pil-2024]].

**July to December 2024.** Police registered 1,325 cases under Section 69 in its first six months, and 11 under Section 72 for disclosing a victim's identity [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The public did not see these numbers until May 2026.

## 2026: the High Court, the first data, the fast-track extension

**March 2026.** After about a year and a half without a government decision, the Delhi High Court revived the petition, said "the decision is nowhere in sight" and ordered the Centre to file an affidavit within four weeks [[theprint-pti-delhi-hc-restores-pil-2026]]. By August the court was reported as saying it could not itself create a Section 377-like offence, and that this was a question of legislative policy for Parliament. We could not confirm whether the petition was formally closed.

**6 May 2026.** The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) released Crime in India 2024 [[theprint-ncrb-juveniles-2026]], the first edition to carry both codes. Of the 29,536 rape cases registered in 2024, 19,683 were filed under the IPC and 9,853 under the BNS. The row for "unnatural offences" is gone, marked as a section "deleted in BNS" [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

**23 July 2026.** The Law Ministry told the Rajya Sabha that rape and POCSO cases pending before Fast Track Special Courts rose from 2,04,122 at the end of 2024 to 2,45,579 at the end of 2025. New cases jumped to 1,43,936 in 2025, while disposals fell to 66,500 [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]].

**4 November 2026.** The Union Cabinet extended the fast-track courts scheme for five years, to 31 March 2031, with an outlay of Rs 3,788.04 crore and provision for up to 850 courts, against 779 functioning now [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]].

## What the first 28 months tell us

**The new offence was used at once. The missing one is still missing.** Section 69 produced 1,325 cases in six months. The gap flagged in November 2023 has been to two courts, and both pointed back to Parliament. Until Parliament acts, an adult man or a transgender person who is sexually assaulted cannot file a rape case. Sexual abuse of a transgender person carries only six months to two years under the Transgender Persons Act [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. Anyone under 18 is covered by POCSO, whatever their gender [[pocso-act-2012]].

**Deadlines did not shorten the queue.** The code allows two months for a rape trial. The Fast Track Special Courts set up for rape and POCSO cases ended 2025 with 2,45,579 cases waiting.

> A deadline with no consequence is a wish, not a rule.

**The numbers need care.** The 2024 figures are split by the date of the offence, not the date of the report, so the two columns are not two half-years. And a new row, such as Section 69, is a new category, not a new crime wave.

For a survivor, the practical points are short. The date of the offence decides the code. You can report at any police station, or electronically. And you are owed an update on the investigation within 90 days: ask for it in writing.
bns-first-years-sexual-offences-timeline.hg:
1 July 2024 ko India ne ek hi din mein apne criminal laws badal diye. Sexual violence ke cases ke liye uske baad ke 28 mahinon ka record mila-jula hai. Purane law ke zyadatar hisse ko bas naye numbers mile. Ek offence joda gaya aur ek hata diya gaya. Fast-track courts ka backlog aur badh gaya.

Yeh timeline us warning se shuru hoti hai jo naye codes pass karne se pehle Parliament ko mili thi, aur November 2026 ke Cabinet decision tak jaati hai. Yeh general jaankari hai, legal advice nahin.

## November 2023: woh warning jo Parliament ko mili thi

Supreme Court ke 6 September 2018 ke Navtej Singh Johar faisle ke baad se Indian Penal Code (IPC) ka Section 377 sirf non-consensual acts aur bestiality par lagta tha [[scobserver-navtej-johar-2018]]. Yahi woh section tha jo kisi adult man ya transgender person ke saath zabardasti kiye gaye sex ko cover karta tha. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke draft mein ise chhod diya gaya.

10 November 2023 ko Parliament ki Standing Committee on Home Affairs ne warn kiya ki Section 377 hatane se men, transgender persons aur animals ke khilaaf non-consensual sexual offences bina saza ke reh jaayenge, aur ise rakhne ki recommendation di. Government ne yeh recommendation nahin maani [[prs-standing-committee-bns-2023]]. Us saal police ne is section ke under 888 cases darj kiye the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## 1 July 2024: badlaav ka din

BNS, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) aur Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 1 July 2024 ko laagu hue [[air-new-criminal-laws-2024]]. Us date se pehle hue offences par ab bhi IPC ke under hi case chalta hai, isliye courts mein dono codes barson tak saath-saath chalenge.

Sexual offences ke liye naye code ne teen kaam kiye [[indiacode-bns-2023]]:

- **Jaisa tha waisa raha.** Rape ab bhi "a man" ka "a woman" ke khilaaf kiya gaya act hai (Section 63), aur saza kam se kam 10 saal hai (Section 64). Jis husband ki wife 18 ya usse zyada ki hai, uske liye exception bhi bana raha.
- **Joda gaya.** Section 69 ne "deceitful means" se, ya shaadi ke aise vaade se jise nibhane ka iraada hi nahin tha, sex haasil karne ko offence banaya. Saza 10 saal tak hai.
- **Hataya gaya.** Section 377 ka koi counterpart nahin hai.

Procedure code ne Zero FIR aur e-FIR ko statute mein likh diya aur victims ko 90 din ke andar investigation ka update paane ka right diya. Yeh rape ki investigation ke liye do mahine aur chargesheet ke baad trial ke liye do mahine deta hai, par dono mein se koi bhi deadline tootne par kuch nahin hota [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## 2024 ka aakhri hissa: pehle cases, aur ek court jisne gap bharne se mana kiya

**9 August 2024.** Kolkata ke RG Kar Medical College and Hospital mein ek doctor ka rape aur murder hua [[livelaw-rg-kar-task-force-2024]]. Crime naye code ke doosre mahine mein hua, isliye poora trial BNS ke under chala. 20 January 2025 ko Sealdah court ne convict hue aadmi ko Sections 64, 66 aur 103(1) ke under uski baaki natural life tak ki jail ki saza sunayi [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]].

**28 August 2024.** Gayab offence par ek petition sunte hue Delhi High Court ne Centre se chhe mahine ke andar faisla karne ko kaha, aur remark kiya ki "there can't be a vacuum to an offence", yaani kisi offence ki jagah khaali nahin chhodi ja sakti [[barandbench-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]].

**14 October 2024.** Chief Justice D.Y. Chandrachud ki Supreme Court bench ne aisi hi ek plea sunne se mana kar diya. Court ne kaha ki woh yeh direct nahin kar sakti ki koi khaas act offence hai: "we cannot compel the parliament to introduce the provision" [[livelaw-sc-bns-sexual-offences-men-pil-2024]].

**July se December 2024.** Police ne Section 69 ke under uske pehle chhe mahinon mein 1,325 cases darj kiye, aur victim ki identity disclose karne ke liye Section 72 ke under 11 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Public ko yeh numbers May 2026 se pehle dekhne ko nahin mile.

## 2026: High Court, pehla data, fast-track courts ka extension

**March 2026.** Lagbhag dedh saal tak government ka koi decision na aane par Delhi High Court ne petition ko dobara zinda kiya, kaha ki "the decision is nowhere in sight", aur Centre ko chaar hafte ke andar affidavit file karne ka order diya [[theprint-pti-delhi-hc-restores-pil-2026]]. August tak ki reports ke mutabik court keh rahi thi ki woh khud Section 377 jaisa offence nahin bana sakti, aur yeh Parliament ki legislative policy ka sawaal hai. Petition formally band hui ya nahin, yeh hum confirm nahin kar paaye.

**6 May 2026.** National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) ne Crime in India 2024 release ki [[theprint-ncrb-juveniles-2026]], pehla edition jismein dono codes hain. 2024 mein darj 29,536 rape cases mein se 19,683 IPC ke under file hue aur 9,853 BNS ke under. "Unnatural offences" wali row gayab hai, aur us par likha hai ki section "deleted in BNS" hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

**23 July 2026.** Law Ministry ne Rajya Sabha ko bataya ki Fast Track Special Courts mein pending rape aur POCSO cases 2024 ke end ke 2,04,122 se badh kar 2025 ke end mein 2,45,579 ho gaye. 2025 mein naye cases uchhal kar 1,43,936 ho gaye, jabki disposals gir kar 66,500 reh gaye [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]].

**4 November 2026.** Union Cabinet ne fast-track courts ki scheme paanch saal ke liye, 31 March 2031 tak, badha di. Outlay Rs 3,788.04 crore ka hai aur 850 courts tak ka provision hai, jabki abhi 779 chal rahi hain [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]].

## Pehle 28 mahine hamein kya batate hain

**Naya offence turant use hua. Jo gayab tha, woh ab bhi gayab hai.** Section 69 se chhe mahinon mein 1,325 cases bane. November 2023 mein jis gap ki taraf ishaara kiya gaya tha, woh do courts tak pahunch chuka hai, aur dono ne wapas Parliament ki taraf ishaara kiya. Jab tak Parliament kuch nahin karti, jis adult man ya transgender person ke saath sexual assault hota hai, woh rape ka case file nahin kar sakta. Transgender person ke sexual abuse par Transgender Persons Act ke under sirf chhe mahine se do saal ki saza hai [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. 18 se kam umar ka har insaan POCSO ke under cover hai, gender koi bhi ho [[pocso-act-2012]].

**Deadlines se line chhoti nahin hui.** Code rape ke trial ke liye do mahine deta hai. Rape aur POCSO cases ke liye bani Fast Track Special Courts ke paas 2025 ke end mein 2,45,579 cases wait kar rahe the.

> Jis deadline ke tootne par kuch na ho, woh rule nahin, bas ek khwahish hai.

**Numbers ko dhyan se padhna hoga.** 2024 ke figures offence ki date se bante hain, report ki date se nahin, isliye do columns ka matlab saal ke do barabar hisse nahin hai. Aur Section 69 jaisi nayi row ek nayi category hai, nayi crime wave nahin.

Survivor ke liye kaam ki baatein chhoti hain. Kaun sa code lagega, yeh offence ki date tay karti hai. Report kisi bhi police station mein, ya electronically, ki ja sakti hai. Aur 90 din ke andar investigation ka update tumhara haq hai: use likh kar maango.

child-rape-two-laws-bns-and-pocso.en:
Imagine two cousins in one house in Nagpur, a girl and a boy, both 13, both sexually assaulted by the same adult relative. The FIR for the girl can carry two laws: Section 65 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act. The FIR for the boy can carry only one. Nothing about the harm explains the difference. It comes from one word in the penal code. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Two statutes, one act

Section 63 of the BNS defines rape as an act by a man against a woman, and counts sex with a girl under 18 as rape "with or without her consent" [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. POCSO, in force since 14 November 2012, calls the same act penetrative sexual assault and defines the victim as a child: any person below 18 [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

So the two laws overlap for girls, and only for girls. They were never designed as a pair. One is a general penal code that writes rape as a crime against women. The other is a special law for children, whose offences are committed against "a child" of any gender [[pocso-act-2012]].

## Girls: Section 65 of the BNS and POCSO side by side

For a girl, both laws stack the sentence by her age.

| | BNS (girls only) | POCSO (any child) |
|---|---|---|
| Base sentence | At least 10 years (Section 64) | At least 10 years (Section 4) |
| Child under 16 | At least 20 years (Section 65) | At least 20 years (Section 4) |
| Heaviest sentence | Natural life or death, if she is under 12 | Natural life or death, for aggravated assault (Section 6) |

The columns match because Parliament made them match [[indiacode-bns-2023]] [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. The order in which it did so is worth knowing. The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018, in force from 21 April 2018, brought in death as a possible sentence for the rape of a girl under 12 [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]]. PRS Legislative Research noted that the punishment for the rape of boys was left unchanged [[prs-cla-bill-2018]]. The POCSO amendment that gave every child the same ceiling came into force on 16 August 2019 [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. For more than a year, the law's heaviest sentence depended on whether the child was a girl.

The BNS still adds two things for her. Any fine under Section 65 must be paid to the victim, and gang rape of a girl under 18 carries imprisonment for the rest of natural life, or death [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Boys: why POCSO is the only door

For the boy, the BNS is silent. Rape can be committed only against a woman, and the new code has no counterpart to Section 377 of the old Indian Penal Code, which it dropped without a replacement [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. POCSO is his whole protection. It is a strong one: the same offences, the same minimum sentences, the same Special Court.

It is also the door fewest people knock on. Police recorded 892 boys among the 44,567 child victims of penetrative sexual assault in 2024, about 2 in every 100 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That share reflects who gets reported, not who gets abused. And on the day he turns 18, this door closes with nothing behind it.

## 784 against 43,313: why almost every case goes through POCSO

If both laws apply to a girl, which one do police use? In 2024, NCRB recorded 784 cases with girl victims under the rape head. Under POCSO Sections 4 and 6, penetrative and aggravated penetrative sexual assault, it recorded 43,313 cases with girl victims [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Part of this is a counting rule. NCRB counts each FIR once, under its most serious offence, and its POCSO head includes FIRs where POCSO is read with the rape sections of the BNS or IPC [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. So the 43,313 are not cases where the penal code was ignored. They are cases where POCSO led. Practice varies too: Himachal Pradesh, Goa and Chandigarh record many child cases under the rape head [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

POCSO leads because it was written around a child. Police must record the statement at the child's home or a place the child chooses, as far as practicable through a woman officer, and out of uniform. The child must never come into contact with the accused and cannot be kept in a police station at night. Anyone who knows of the abuse must report it [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

## Special courts and sentences: what the choice changes

On the main sentence, nothing. Since 2019, a person who commits this offence against a 13-year-old boy faces the same 20-year minimum as one who commits it against a 13-year-old girl. Police get the same two months to finish the investigation under either law [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

The differences sit at the edges, and they fall one way. The bar on anticipatory bail covers anyone accused of raping a girl under 16 or of gang rape of a girl under 18. It is written by reference to BNS sections that protect only girls [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. The rule that sends the fine to the victim is in the BNS as well.

What both children share is the POCSO trial. A Special Court in each district hears the case. Lawyers put their questions through the judge, the child must not be exposed to the accused while testifying, and the court presumes the accused committed the offence unless the contrary is proved [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. The child's evidence is to be recorded within 30 days and the trial finished, as far as possible, within a year [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Neither door is quick or sure. For POCSO Sections 4 and 6, the conviction rate in 2024 was 30.2%, with 1,70,455 cases pending trial at the end of the year. For girls whose cases were tried under the rape head, it was 31.4% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Two laws, and about three convictions in ten under each.

For a family, the statute book reduces to one fact: a child of any gender is protected, and POCSO is the law to ask for by name.
child-rape-two-laws-bns-and-pocso.hg:
Sochiye, Nagpur ke ek hi ghar mein do cousins hain, ek ladki aur ek ladka, dono 13 saal ke, aur dono par ek hi adult rishtedaar ne sexual assault kiya hai. Ladki ki FIR mein do kanoon lag sakte hain: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ka Section 65 aur Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act. Ladke ki FIR mein sirf ek lag sakta hai. Nuksaan mein aisa kuch nahi hai jo is farq ko samjhaaye. Yeh farq penal code ke ek shabd se aata hai. Yeh general jaankari hai, legal advice nahi.

## Do kanoon, ek hi act

BNS ka Section 63 rape ko aise define karta hai: ek aadmi ka aurat ke khilaaf kiya gaya act. Aur 18 se kam umar ki ladki ke saath sex ko woh rape ginta hai, "with or without her consent" [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. POCSO, jo 14 November 2012 se laagu hai, usi act ko penetrative sexual assault kehta hai aur victim ko child ke roop mein define karta hai: 18 se kam umar ka koi bhi insaan [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Isliye yeh dono kanoon ladkiyon ke liye overlap karte hain, aur sirf ladkiyon ke liye. Inhe kabhi ek jodi ki tarah design nahi kiya gaya. Ek general penal code hai, jo rape ko auraton ke khilaaf crime ke roop mein likhta hai. Doosra bachchon ke liye bana special kanoon hai, jiske offences kisi bhi gender ke "a child" ke khilaaf hote hain [[pocso-act-2012]].

## Ladkiyan: BNS ka Section 65 aur POCSO, saath-saath

Ladki ke liye dono kanoon saza ko uski umar ke hisaab se badhate hain.

| | BNS (sirf ladkiyan) | POCSO (koi bhi bachcha) |
|---|---|---|
| Basic saza | Kam se kam 10 saal (Section 64) | Kam se kam 10 saal (Section 4) |
