| Bachcha 16 se kam ka | Kam se kam 20 saal (Section 65) | Kam se kam 20 saal (Section 4) |
| Sabse bhaari saza | Natural life ya death, agar woh 12 se kam ki ho | Natural life ya death, aggravated assault ke liye (Section 6) |

Dono columns isliye milte hain kyunki Parliament ne inhe milaya [[indiacode-bns-2023]] [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Usne yeh kis order mein kiya, yeh jaanna zaroori hai. Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018, jo 21 April 2018 se laagu hua, 12 se kam umar ki ladki ke rape ke liye death ko ek possible saza ke roop mein laaya [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]]. PRS Legislative Research ne note kiya tha ki ladkon ke rape ki saza jaisi thi waisi hi chhod di gayi [[prs-cla-bill-2018]]. Jis POCSO amendment ne har bachche ko wahi upari seema di, woh 16 August 2019 ko laagu hua [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Ek saal se zyada tak kanoon ki sabse bhaari saza is baat pe tiki rahi ki bachcha ladki hai ya nahi.

BNS ladki ke liye ab bhi do cheezein alag se jodta hai. Section 65 ke tehat jo bhi fine lage woh victim ko dena hota hai, aur 18 se kam umar ki ladki ke gang rape pe baaki poori natural life ki qaid, ya death, hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Ladke: POCSO hi akela darwaza kyun hai

Ladke ke liye BNS chup hai. Rape sirf aurat ke khilaaf ho sakta hai, aur naye code mein puraane Indian Penal Code ke Section 377 ka koi counterpart nahi hai; use bina kisi replacement ke hata diya gaya [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. POCSO hi uski poori suraksha hai. Aur yeh suraksha kamzor nahi hai: wahi offences, wahi minimum sazayein, wahi Special Court.

Yahi woh darwaza bhi hai jise sabse kam log khatkhatate hain. 2024 mein police ne penetrative sexual assault ke 44,567 child victims mein 892 ladke record kiye, yaani har 100 mein lagbhag 2 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh hissa batata hai ki report kiski hoti hai, yeh nahi ki abuse kiska hota hai. Aur jis din woh 18 ka hota hai, yeh darwaza band ho jaata hai, aur uske peeche kuch nahi hai.

## 784 ke saamne 43,313: lagbhag har case POCSO se hi kyun guzarta hai

Agar ladki pe dono kanoon lagte hain, to police kaun sa use karti hai? 2024 mein NCRB ne rape head ke tehat girl victims wale 784 cases record kiye. POCSO ke Section 4 aur 6, yaani penetrative aur aggravated penetrative sexual assault, ke tehat usne girl victims wale 43,313 cases record kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Iska ek hissa ginne ka rule hai. NCRB har FIR ko ek hi baar ginta hai, uske sabse serious offence ke tehat, aur uske POCSO head mein woh FIRs bhi shaamil hain jinmein POCSO ko BNS ya IPC ke rape sections ke saath padha gaya [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yaani yeh 43,313 aise cases nahi hain jinmein penal code ko ignore kiya gaya. Yeh woh cases hain jinmein POCSO aage raha. Practice bhi har jagah ek jaisi nahi hai: Himachal Pradesh, Goa aur Chandigarh kai child cases rape head ke tehat record karte hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

POCSO isliye aage rehta hai kyunki use bachche ko dhyaan mein rakh kar likha gaya hai. Police ko statement bachche ke ghar pe ya uski pasand ki jagah pe lena hota hai, jahan tak ho sake ek woman officer ke zariye, aur bina uniform ke. Bachche ka accused se kabhi saamna nahi hona chahiye, aur use raat mein police station mein nahi rakha ja sakta. Jo bhi abuse ke baare mein jaanta hai, use report karna hi hota hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

## Special courts aur sazayein: is choice se kya badalta hai

Main saza pe, kuch nahi. 2019 se, jo insaan 13 saal ke ladke ke khilaaf yeh offence karta hai, use wahi 20 saal ki minimum saza milti hai jo 13 saal ki ladki ke khilaaf karne wale ko. Police ko dono kanoonon mein investigation poori karne ke liye wahi do mahine milte hain [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Farq kinaaron pe hain, aur sab ek hi taraf jhukte hain. Anticipatory bail pe rok us insaan pe lagti hai jis par 16 se kam umar ki ladki ke rape ka ya 18 se kam umar ki ladki ke gang rape ka ilzaam ho. Yeh rok BNS ke un sections ke hawaale se likhi gayi hai jo sirf ladkiyon ko protect karte hain [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Fine victim ko dene wala rule bhi BNS mein hi hai.

Dono bachchon ko jo ek jaisa milta hai, woh hai POCSO ka trial. Har district mein ek Special Court case sunta hai. Lawyers apne sawaal judge ke zariye poochhte hain, gawahi dete waqt bachche ka accused se saamna nahi hona chahiye, aur court maan kar chalta hai ki offence accused ne hi kiya hai, jab tak ulta saabit na ho [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Bachche ka evidence 30 din ke andar record hona chahiye aur trial, jahan tak ho sake, ek saal ke andar poora [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Koi bhi darwaza na tez hai, na pakka. POCSO ke Section 4 aur 6 mein 2024 ka conviction rate 30.2% tha, aur saal ke end mein 1,70,455 cases trial ka intezaar kar rahe the. Jin ladkiyon ke cases rape head ke tehat chale, unmein yeh rate 31.4% tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Do kanoon, aur dono mein das mein se lagbhag teen convictions.

Ek family ke liye poori kanoon ki kitaab ek baat mein simat jaati hai: kisi bhi gender ka bachcha protected hai, aur POCSO woh kanoon hai jise naam lekar maangna hai.

city-police-chargesheet-rates-crimes-aga.en:
Broadly, a police investigation into a crime against a woman ends in one of two ways. Police file a charge-sheet, which tells a court there is a case to try, or they file a final report, which closes it. In 2024, police in India's 19 largest cities chose the charge-sheet in 76.8% of the crimes-against-women cases they disposed of [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Nearly one case in four was never sent for trial.

Which side of that line a complaint falls on depends heavily on the city it is filed in.

## Nineteen cities, and the two ends of the table

NCRB's Crime in India 2024 prints a charge-sheeting rate for each of the 19 cities with more than 20 lakh people. Together they registered 50,584 crimes against women that year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The ends of the table are far apart:

| Police force | Charge-sheeting rate, crimes against women, 2024 |
|---|---|
| Kolkata (highest of 19 cities) | 98.5% |
| India, all police | 77.2% |
| 19 cities together | 76.8% |
| Ghaziabad | 65.8% |
| Jaipur (lowest of 19 cities) | 55.7% |

In Kolkata almost every case police finished was sent for trial. In Jaipur more than four in ten were not [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Now read a second column beside it. Jaipur had the highest rate of registered crime against women of the 19 cities: 199.0 per lakh women, on 2,894 cases. Kolkata had nearly the lowest: 28.8, on 1,958 cases [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The city that records the most complaints per head sends the smallest share to court. The city that records almost the fewest sends nearly all of them. (City rates use 2011 Census populations, so treat them as rough [[ncrb-cii-2024]].)

## What a charge-sheet is, and what the rate measures

A charge-sheet is the report police file when they believe the evidence supports a trial. The alternative is a final report: police tell the court the case was false, a mistake of fact or a civil dispute, or true but without enough evidence or with the accused untraced [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The charge-sheeting rate is charge-sheeted cases as a share of all cases police disposed of in the year. Three things are outside it.

**Speed.** Cases still under investigation are not in the fraction at all.

**The complaint that never became an FIR.** A force that registers every complaint carries its hardest cases into the count. A force that turns complaints away at the desk can charge-sheet nearly everything it accepts. The table cannot tell these two apart, in any city.

**Quality.** The rate does not say whether the charge-sheet will stand up in court.

NCRB only compiles what state police send it, and says it is not responsible for the authenticity of the information [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. It also warns that more crime registered in a city "is not an indicator of its being comparatively unsafe" [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]].

## The states: Rajasthan 54.1%, Mizoram 95.9%

The spread among states is just as wide. Rajasthan had the lowest charge-sheeting rate in the country at 54.1%. Mizoram had the highest of any state at 95.9%, and among large states Andhra Pradesh led at 94.4% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Rajasthan's number has a visible source. Its police closed 12,217 crimes-against-women cases in 2024 with a "final report false", a third of the 36,895 such closures in all of India [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That label is a police classification after investigation, not a court finding, and NCRB does not publish the reasons behind it. It could mean FIRs that are written readily and then dropped, investigations that give up early, complaints police chose not to believe, or a mix. The table cannot say. Jaipur's 55.7% sits inside that pattern.

For a woman in Jaipur, the FIR is only the first hurdle. The closure report is the larger risk.

## Charge-sheeted is not convicted: the West Bengal paradox

Kolkata's 98.5% looks like a model. Then follow the cases into court. West Bengal, the state Kolkata is the capital of, had the lowest conviction rate for crimes against women of any state in 2024: 1.6%, with 203 convictions against 12,301 acquittals. It also had the largest backlog in India, 3,84,388 cases pending at the end of the year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The state figures cover all of West Bengal, not Kolkata alone.

Andhra Pradesh shows the same split inside one state: 94.4% charge-sheeted, 5.4% convicted. For India the two numbers are 77.2% and 25.7% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

A force can post a near-perfect rate by sending everything forward, including cases too thinly investigated to survive a trial. A high rate beside a conviction rate near zero means cases reach court and fail there, whether the cause is the investigation, the prosecution or years of delay.

> A low charge-sheeting rate means cases end in the police station. A high one with almost no convictions means they end in court. Either way, the complainant is the one left waiting.

## Your rights while police investigate

Imagine a 24-year-old in Ghaziabad who files a complaint of sexual harassment against her landlord. The law gives her these. This is general information, not legal advice.

- **A free copy of the FIR**, given at once [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **A progress update within 90 days**, by any means, including electronic communication [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **A deadline in the gravest cases.** Rape and POCSO investigations must finish within two months of the information being recorded, though the law sets no penalty for missing it [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **The papers.** If she has a lawyer, free copies of the police report, FIR and statements within 14 days of the accused first appearing in court [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **A hearing** before any prosecution is withdrawn [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

If police close her case with a final report, that is their classification, not a verdict. She can ask for a copy and have a lawyer read it before she decides what to do next.

A city's charge-sheeting rate is an average. These rights are how one complainant pushes her own case to the right side of it.
city-police-chargesheet-rates-crimes-aga.hg:
Mote taur par, aurat ke khilaaf kisi crime ki police investigation do mein se ek tareeke se khatam hoti hai. Ya toh police charge-sheet file karti hai, jo court ko batati hai ki trial ke layak case hai, ya phir final report, jo case ko band kar deti hai. 2024 mein India ke 19 sabse bade shehron ki police ne jitne crimes-against-women cases nipataaye, unme se 76.8% mein charge-sheet ka raasta chuna [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Lagbhag har chaar mein se ek case trial ke liye bheja hi nahi gaya.

Koi complaint is line ke kis taraf giregi, yeh kaafi had tak is par depend karta hai ki woh kis shehar mein file hui.

## Unnees shehar, aur table ke do chhor

NCRB ki Crime in India 2024 un 19 shehron mein se har ek ka charge-sheeting rate chhaapti hai jinki population 20 lakh se zyada hai. Us saal in sabne milkar 50,584 crimes against women register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Table ke dono chhor ek doosre se bahut door hain:

| Police force | Charge-sheeting rate, crimes against women, 2024 |
|---|---|
| Kolkata (19 shehron mein sabse zyada) | 98.5% |
| India, poori police | 77.2% |
| 19 shehar milaakar | 76.8% |
| Ghaziabad | 65.8% |
| Jaipur (19 shehron mein sabse kam) | 55.7% |

Kolkata mein police ne jo cases nipataaye, unme se lagbhag har case trial ke liye bheja gaya. Jaipur mein das mein se chaar se zyada nahi bheje gaye [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Ab iske saath ek doosra column padhiye. 19 shehron mein register hue crime against women ka sabse zyada rate Jaipur ka tha: 199.0 per lakh women, 2,894 cases par. Kolkata ka rate lagbhag sabse kam tha: 28.8, 1,958 cases par [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jo shehar population ke hisaab se sabse zyada complaints record karta hai, wahi sabse chhota hissa court bhejta hai. Jo shehar lagbhag sabse kam record karta hai, woh lagbhag sab bhej deta hai. (City rates 2011 Census ki population par nikaale jaate hain, isliye inhe mota andaaza hi maaniye [[ncrb-cii-2024]].)

## Charge-sheet kya hai, aur yeh rate kya naapta hai

Charge-sheet woh report hai jo police tab file karti hai jab use lagta hai ki evidence trial ke layak hai. Doosra raasta final report hai: police court ko batati hai ki case false tha, mistake of fact ya civil dispute tha, ya sach tha lekin evidence kaafi nahi mila ya accused ka pata nahi chala [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Charge-sheeting rate ka matlab hai: saal mein police ne jitne cases nipataaye, unme charge-sheet wale cases ka hissa. Teen cheezein iske bahar reh jaati hain.

**Speed.** Jo cases abhi investigation mein hain, woh is fraction mein hain hi nahi.

**Woh complaint jo kabhi FIR nahi bani.** Jo police har complaint register karti hai, uski ginti mein sabse mushkil cases bhi aa jaate hain. Jo police desk par hi complaints lauta deti hai, woh jitne cases leti hai un sab mein lagbhag charge-sheet file kar sakti hai. Table in dono mein fark nahi bata sakti, kisi bhi shehar ke liye.

**Quality.** Rate yeh nahi batata ki charge-sheet court mein tik paayegi ya nahi.

NCRB sirf wahi data compile karta hai jo state police use bhejti hai, aur kehta hai ki information ki authenticity ki zimmedaari uski nahi hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Woh yeh chetaavni bhi deta hai ki kisi shehar mein zyada crime register hona "is not an indicator of its being comparatively unsafe" [[ncrb-cii-2024-word-of-caution]].

## States: Rajasthan 54.1%, Mizoram 95.9%

States ke beech bhi fark utna hi bada hai. Desh mein sabse kam charge-sheeting rate Rajasthan ka tha, 54.1%. Kisi bhi state mein sabse zyada Mizoram ka tha, 95.9%, aur bade states mein Andhra Pradesh 94.4% ke saath sabse aage tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Rajasthan ke number ki wajah data mein dikhti hai. Uski police ne 2024 mein 12,217 crimes-against-women cases "final report false" ke saath band kiye, jo poore India ke aise 36,895 closures ka ek-tihaai hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh label investigation ke baad ki police classification hai, court ka faisla nahi, aur NCRB iske peeche ki wajahein publish nahi karta. Iska matlab yeh ho sakta hai ki FIRs aasaani se likhi jaati hain aur phir chhod di jaati hain, ya investigations jaldi haar maan leti hain, ya police ne complaints par yakeen na karna chuna, ya in sabka mel. Table yeh nahi bata sakti. Jaipur ka 55.7% isi pattern ke andar aata hai.

Jaipur ki kisi aurat ke liye FIR sirf pehli rukaavat hai. Bada khatra closure report hai.

## Charge-sheet ka matlab conviction nahi: West Bengal ka paradox

Kolkata ka 98.5% ek model jaisa dikhta hai. Ab in cases ke peeche-peeche court tak chaliye. West Bengal, jiski capital Kolkata hai, ka 2024 mein crimes against women ka conviction rate kisi bhi state mein sabse kam tha: 1.6%, yaani 203 convictions ke saamne 12,301 acquittals. India ka sabse bada backlog bhi wahin tha: saal ke end mein 3,84,388 cases pending [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. State ke yeh figures poore West Bengal ke hain, sirf Kolkata ke nahi.

Andhra Pradesh ek hi state ke andar yahi fark dikhata hai: 94.4% mein charge-sheet, 5.4% mein conviction. India ke liye yeh do numbers 77.2% aur 25.7% hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Koi police sab kuch aage bhej kar lagbhag perfect rate dikha sakti hai, un cases ko bhi jinki investigation itni kamzor hai ki woh trial mein tik nahi paayenge. Jab charge-sheeting rate ooncha ho aur conviction rate zero ke kareeb, toh matlab yeh hai ki cases court tak pahunch rahe hain aur wahin fail ho rahe hain, chahe wajah investigation ho, prosecution ho ya saalon ki deri.

> Kam charge-sheeting rate ka matlab hai ki cases police station mein khatam ho jaate hain. Ooncha rate aur lagbhag zero convictions ka matlab hai ki woh court mein khatam ho jaate hain. Dono haalat mein intezaar complainant ko hi karna padta hai.

## Jab police investigate kar rahi ho, tab aapke haq

Sochiye Ghaziabad ki ek 24 saal ki ladki ke baare mein, jo apne landlord ke khilaaf sexual harassment ki complaint file karti hai. Law use yeh cheezein deta hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

- **FIR ki free copy**, turant [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **90 din ke andar progress update**, kisi bhi tareeke se, electronic communication se bhi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Sabse gambhir cases mein deadline.** Rape aur POCSO ki investigation information record hone ke do mahine ke andar poori honi chahiye, halaanki deadline miss hone par law mein koi saza nahi hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Kaagzaat.** Agar uske paas lawyer hai, toh accused ke court mein pehli baar pesh hone ke 14 din ke andar police report, FIR aur statements ki free copies [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Sunwaai**, kisi bhi prosecution ko wapas lene se pehle [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Agar police uska case final report ke saath band kar deti hai, toh yeh police ki classification hai, koi faisla nahi. Woh uski copy maang sakti hai aur aage kya karna hai yeh tay karne se pehle kisi lawyer ko padhwa sakti hai.

Kisi shehar ka charge-sheeting rate ek average hai. Yeh haq woh tareeka hain jisse ek akeli complainant apne case ko us average ke sahi taraf dhakel sakti hai.

cognizable-bailable-compoundable-sexual-.en:
Imagine a 19-year-old in Kanpur who reports that a neighbour assaulted her on the stairs of their building. The officer writes the FIR. A few days later the man is home on bail, and an uncle is asking her family to "settle it". She assumes someone was paid. Perhaps nobody was. Three legal labels attached to the offence shape every step of that week.

Every offence in Indian law is tagged three ways: cognizable or non-cognizable, bailable or non-bailable, compoundable or not. The tags decide whether police must act on their own, whether the accused can claim bail as a right, and whether a compromise can legally end the case. This explainer decodes them for sexual and gender offences. It is general information, not legal advice.

## Cognizable: when police must act on their own

A cognizable offence is one in which police can register a case and start investigating without waiting for a magistrate's order. For a non-cognizable offence, the complainant generally has to go through a magistrate first. The label is fixed by law for each offence, but an FIR does not print it.

For sexual offences, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) answers the question itself. Section 199 calls rape and its aggravated forms, assault to outrage a woman's modesty (Section 74), assault to disrobe (Section 76), voyeurism (Section 77) and words or gestures insulting a woman's modesty (Section 79) cognizable offences, and says an officer who fails to record an FIR for any of them faces six months to two years of rigorous imprisonment [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

The label carries a duty. In Lalita Kumari v. Government of Uttar Pradesh (2013), a five-judge Supreme Court bench held that registering an FIR is mandatory when information discloses a cognizable offence, and that action must be taken against officers who refuse [[sc-lalita-kumari-2013]]. Section 173 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) adds that the report can be made at any police station, wherever the offence took place, and that the victim gets a free copy [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

There is one limit. For offences punishable with three to under seven years, police may, with a Deputy Superintendent's permission, hold a preliminary enquiry of up to 14 days before registering. Rape, with its 10-year minimum, falls outside that window [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Bailable or not: what the label means for the accused

If an offence is bailable, bail is the accused's right: once he offers it, he must be released. If it is non-bailable, bail is not banned. It becomes a judge's decision.

So the man in Kanpur being home on bail does not mean money changed hands, and it does not mean he has been cleared. Either the law gave him bail as a right, or a court weighed the case and granted it. The case goes on.

Some laws on gender offences fix the labels themselves. Offences under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 are cognizable and non-bailable [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. Every offence under the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 is non-bailable and non-compoundable [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]]. For the gravest cases the BNSS also shuts off anticipatory bail, the order that protects a person from arrest in advance: it is barred for anyone accused of raping a girl under 16 or of gang rape of a girl under 18 [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

When a court does grant bail, there are rules about how. In 2021 the Supreme Court struck down a High Court order that made a man accused of sexual assault ask the complainant to tie a rakhi on him, and ruled that bail conditions must not require or permit contact with the victim [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]].

## Compoundable: why a 'samjhauta' is not a verdict

Compounding means the person wronged agrees to end the case, and the accused is treated as acquitted. Only offences the law lists as compoundable can be ended this way. For everything else, a private agreement does not close the case.

Some laws say this outright. The Dowry Prohibition Act and the PC-PNDT Act declare every offence under them non-compoundable [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]] [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]]. In sexual-offence cases, the Supreme Court has told judges not to suggest or entertain any compromise, including marriage [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. A panchayat "samjhauta", a payment or a marriage offer is exactly the kind of settlement that ruling tells courts to turn away.

> The labels describe what the law allows. The court registers describe what happens.

In 2024, 16,396 cases of cruelty by a husband or his relatives ended in compromise or compounding, more than the 10,689 that ended in conviction [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB does not say how those compromises were reached. They can reflect reconciliation, mediation or pressure on the woman, and the data cannot tell these apart.

One law does allow a settlement, on the complainant's terms. Under the POSH Act, a workplace complaint can go to conciliation only if the woman asks for it, and money cannot be the basis of the settlement [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

## Complaint-only offences: the PC-PNDT exception

Sex selection shows that the three labels are not the whole story. Every offence under the PC-PNDT Act is cognizable, non-bailable and non-compoundable. Yet a court can take up a case only on a complaint by the Appropriate Authority, an officer it authorises, or a person or organisation that has first given the authority at least 15 days' notice [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]].

So the strongest labels in the book sit behind a gate held by a district health official. In 2024 police registered only 31 cases under the Act in all of India [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That count misses complaints that authorities file directly in court, but it shows how little of this law runs through a police station.

## Reading the labels on your own FIR

An FIR lists sections, not labels. Take your free copy, note each section, and ask a legal-aid lawyer how each one is classified. The table covers the labels set out in the text of the laws discussed here.

| Offence | What the law says |
|---|---|
| Rape, assault to outrage modesty, assault to disrobe, voyeurism, insult to modesty (BNS Sections 64-68, 70-71, 74, 76, 77, 79) | Cognizable; an officer who will not record the FIR can be jailed |
| Rape of a girl under 16, gang rape of a girl under 18 | No anticipatory bail |
| Child marriage (PCMA 2006) | Cognizable, non-bailable |
| Dowry (Dowry Prohibition Act 1961) | Non-bailable, non-compoundable |
| Sex selection (PC-PNDT Act) | Cognizable, non-bailable, non-compoundable; a court acts only on a formal complaint |

Then ask three questions. Did police register the case, or send you to a magistrate? Is the accused out because the offence is bailable, or because a judge decided? Is anyone asking you to "settle" something a court has been told not to entertain?

One more protection applies if the pressure comes from the state's side. A prosecutor cannot quietly withdraw a case: the court must give the victim a hearing before it allows any withdrawal [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
cognizable-bailable-compoundable-sexual-.hg:
Socho Kanpur ki ek 19-year-old ladki report karti hai ki ek padosi ne building ki seedhiyon par uske saath assault kiya. Officer FIR likh leta hai. Kuch din baad woh aadmi bail par ghar wapas aa jaata hai, aur ek chacha uski family se keh rahe hain ki "baat yahin khatam karo". Ladki ko lagta hai ki kisi ne paise khilaaye honge. Ho sakta hai kisi ne nahi khilaaye. Us hafte ka har kadam offence par lage teen legal labels se tay hota hai.

Indian law mein har offence par teen tarah ka tag lagta hai: cognizable ya non-cognizable, bailable ya non-bailable, compoundable ya nahi. Yeh tags tay karte hain ki police khud se action legi ya nahi, accused bail ko apna haq bata sakta hai ya nahi, aur compromise se case kanooni taur par khatam ho sakta hai ya nahi. Yeh explainer sexual aur gender offences ke liye in labels ko decode karta hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Cognizable: jab police ko khud action lena hota hai

Cognizable offence woh hai jismein police magistrate ke order ka intezaar kiye bina case register karke investigation shuru kar sakti hai. Non-cognizable offence mein complainant ko aam taur par pehle magistrate ke paas jaana padta hai. Har offence ka label law mein tay hota hai, lekin FIR par yeh print nahi hota.

Sexual offences ke liye Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) khud jawab deti hai. Section 199 rape aur uske aggravated forms, assault to outrage a woman's modesty (Section 74), assault to disrobe (Section 76), voyeurism (Section 77) aur woman ki modesty ka insult karne wale words ya gestures (Section 79) ko cognizable offences kehta hai, aur kehta hai ki jo officer inmein se kisi ki bhi FIR record nahi karta, use six months se two years tak ki rigorous imprisonment ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Is label ke saath ek duty bhi aati hai. Lalita Kumari v. Government of Uttar Pradesh (2013) mein Supreme Court ki five-judge bench ne kaha ki jab information se cognizable offence saamne aaye, toh FIR register karna mandatory hai, aur mana karne wale officers par action hona chahiye [[sc-lalita-kumari-2013]]. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ka Section 173 yeh bhi kehta hai ki report kisi bhi police station mein ki ja sakti hai, offence chahe kahin bhi hua ho, aur victim ko FIR ki free copy milti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Ek limit hai. Jin offences mein three se seven saal se kam ki saza hai, unmein police Deputy Superintendent ki permission se FIR se pehle 14 din tak preliminary enquiry kar sakti hai. Rape mein minimum 10-year ki saza hai, isliye woh is window ke bahar hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Bailable ya nahi: accused ke liye is label ka matlab

Agar offence bailable hai, toh bail accused ka haq hai: jaise hi woh bail deta hai, use chhodna padega. Agar offence non-bailable hai, toh bail par ban nahi lagta. Bas faisla judge ke haath mein chala jaata hai.

Isliye Kanpur wale aadmi ka bail par ghar hona na yeh saabit karta hai ki paise chale, na yeh ki woh bari ho gaya. Ya toh law ne use haq ke taur par bail di, ya court ne case dekh kar bail di. Case chalta rehta hai.

Gender offences ke kuch laws apne labels khud tay karte hain. Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 ke offences cognizable aur non-bailable hain [[indiacode-pcma-2006]]. Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 ka har offence non-bailable aur non-compoundable hai [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]]. Sabse gambhir cases mein BNSS anticipatory bail bhi band kar deta hai, yaani woh order jo kisi ko pehle se arrest se bachata hai: 16 saal se kam umar ki ladki ke rape ya 18 saal se kam umar ki ladki ke gang rape ke accused ko yeh nahi mil sakti [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Jab court bail deta bhi hai, toh uske bhi rules hain. 2021 mein Supreme Court ne High Court ka woh order radd kiya jismein sexual assault ke ek accused ko complainant se rakhi bandhwane ko kaha gaya tha, aur kaha ki bail conditions mein victim se contact na zaroori ho, na allowed ho [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]].

## Compoundable: 'samjhauta' verdict kyun nahi hai

Compounding ka matlab hai ki jiske saath galat hua woh case khatam karne par raazi ho jaaye, aur accused ko acquit hua maana jaaye. Sirf woh offences is tarah khatam ho sakte hain jinhe law compoundable list karta hai. Baaki sab mein private samjhauta case band nahi karta.

Kuch laws yeh seedhe likhte hain. Dowry Prohibition Act aur PC-PNDT Act apne har offence ko non-compoundable kehte hain [[indiacode-dowry-prohibition-1961]] [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]]. Sexual-offence cases mein Supreme Court ne judges ko kaha hai ki koi bhi compromise, shaadi samet, na sujhaayein aur na entertain karein [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. Panchayat ka "samjhauta", paisa ya shaadi ka offer theek usi tarah ka settlement hai jise yeh ruling courts ko thukrane ko kehti hai.

> Labels batate hain ki law kya allow karta hai. Court ke registers batate hain ki asal mein kya hota hai.

2024 mein husband ya uske rishtedaaron ki cruelty ke 16,396 cases compromise ya compounding par khatam hue, jo conviction wale 10,689 cases se zyada hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB nahi batata ki yeh compromise kaise hue. Yeh reconciliation, mediation ya woman par dabaav, kuch bhi ho sakta hai, aur data inmein farak nahi kar sakta.

Ek law settlement allow karta hai, lekin complainant ki sharton par. POSH Act mein workplace complaint conciliation mein tabhi ja sakti hai jab woman khud maange, aur settlement ka base paisa nahi ho sakta [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

## Complaint-only offences: PC-PNDT ka exception

Sex selection dikhata hai ki teen labels poori kahani nahi hain. PC-PNDT Act ka har offence cognizable, non-bailable aur non-compoundable hai. Phir bhi court case tabhi utha sakta hai jab complaint Appropriate Authority kare, ya uska authorise kiya officer, ya koi person ya organisation jisne pehle authority ko kam se kam 15 days ka notice diya ho [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]].

Yaani kitaab ke sabse strong labels ek district health official ke haath mein rakhe gate ke peeche hain. 2024 mein poore India mein police ne is Act ke under sirf 31 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Is count mein woh complaints nahi hain jo authorities seedhe court mein file karti hain, lekin isse dikhta hai ki yeh law police station se kitna kam guzarta hai.

## Apni FIR par labels kaise padhein

FIR mein sections likhe hote hain, labels nahi. Apni free copy lijiye, har section note kijiye, aur legal-aid lawyer se poochiye ki har section kis category mein aata hai. Neeche ki table mein woh labels hain jo yahan discuss kiye gaye laws ke text mein likhe hain.

| Offence | Law kya kehta hai |
|---|---|
| Rape, assault to outrage modesty, assault to disrobe, voyeurism, modesty ka insult (BNS Sections 64-68, 70-71, 74, 76, 77, 79) | Cognizable; FIR record na karne wale officer ko jail ho sakti hai |
| 16 saal se kam umar ki ladki ka rape, 18 saal se kam umar ki ladki ka gang rape | Anticipatory bail nahi |
| Child marriage (PCMA 2006) | Cognizable, non-bailable |
| Dowry (Dowry Prohibition Act 1961) | Non-bailable, non-compoundable |
| Sex selection (PC-PNDT Act) | Cognizable, non-bailable, non-compoundable; court sirf formal complaint par action leta hai |

Phir teen sawaal poochiye. Kya police ne case register kiya, ya aapko magistrate ke paas bhej diya? Kya accused isliye bahar hai kyunki offence bailable hai, ya isliye kyunki judge ne faisla kiya? Kya koi aapse aisi cheez "settle" karne ko keh raha hai jise entertain na karne ko court ko kaha gaya hai?

Agar dabaav state ki taraf se aaye, toh ek aur protection hai. Prosecutor chupchaap case withdraw nahi kar sakta: koi bhi withdrawal allow karne se pehle court ko victim ki baat sunni padti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

court-orders-on-sexual-violence-ignored.en:
A Supreme Court direction is supposed to end an argument. For people facing sexual harassment, sexual violence or violence over whom they choose to love, it has often begun a second wait: for governments to do what the court said. This timeline follows four such directions, from 1997 to 2025, through the dates the gaps went on record.

| Direction | Given | The record later |
|---|---|---|
| Complaints committees for sexual harassment at work | 13 August 1997 | 2012: several states had not complied |
| Special cells and fast-track courts for honour crimes | 27 March 2018 | December 2025: no fast-track courts in Delhi |
| A One Stop Centre in every district | 11 December 2018, within a year | July 2026: 985 of 1,033 approved centres operational |
| District Officers and Local Committees under the POSH Act | 3 December 2024, by 31 January 2025 | May 2025: unclear in four states and union territories |

## 1997 and 2012: Vishaka's committees, and the rebuke

**13 August 1997.** In Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan, a three-judge bench led by Chief Justice J.S. Verma laid down guidelines against sexual harassment of working women and declared them binding until Parliament passed a law. Every employer was to have a complaints committee headed by a woman, with at least half its members women and a third party, such as an NGO, to guard against pressure from senior staff [[sc-vishaka-1997]].

**19 October 2012.** Fifteen years later, in Medha Kotwal Lele v. Union of India, the court found that several state governments had not complied. It ordered committees at taluka, district and state level, gave states with a single state-wide committee two months to form more, and warned that "laws with sloppy enforcement are not enough" [[sci-posh-enforcement-judgment-2023]].

**2013 and 2023.** Parliament's law, the POSH Act, came into force on 9 December 2013, more than 15 years after Vishaka. On 12 May 2023 the Supreme Court found "serious lapses in the enforcement" of that Act, and called it "a sorry state of affairs" [[sci-posh-enforcement-judgment-2023]].

## 2018: Shakti Vahini and the honour-crime courts still missing in 2025

**27 March 2018.** In Shakti Vahini v. Union of India, the Supreme Court held that the right to choose a life partner is a facet of individual liberty, and ordered preventive, remedial and punitive measures against honour crimes [[barandbench-shakti-vahini-madras-pil-2021]]. They included special cells, fast-track and special courts and district-level monitoring committees [[barandbench-honour-killing-fast-track-2025]].

**December 2025.** More than seven years later, the Delhi High Court was told that no fast-track courts for honour-killing cases had been set up in Delhi. The court closed the petition, asking the petitioners to approach its administrative side and the Delhi government [[barandbench-honour-killing-fast-track-2025]].

For a couple threatened over an inter-caste or inter-faith relationship, the 2018 judgment promised protection and a quick trial of their attackers. In the national capital, part of that system had still not been built.

## 2018: a One Stop Centre in every district

**11 December 2018.** In Nipun Saxena v. Union of India, the court wrote: "All the States/Union Territories are requested to set up at least one 'one stop centre' in every district within one year from today" [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. The verb was "requested". The year ran out in December 2019.

**March 2025.** By then 802 centres were functional [[pib-nirbhaya-fund-2025]].

**July 2026.** 985 of 1,033 approved centres were operational [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]]. Nearly a fifth of them had become operational only after March 2025, more than five years past the deadline, and 48 approved centres were still not running.

## 2024-2025: POSH deadlines and the missing Local Committees

**3 December 2024.** Following up its 2023 judgment, the Supreme Court set dates. Every state was to notify a District Officer for each district by 31 December 2024. Local Committees and government Internal Committees were to be constituted by 31 January 2025, and public and private organisations in every district surveyed for Internal Committees [[sc-posh-order-2025-05-21]].

The Local Committee is the forum the Act gives a woman whose workplace has fewer than ten workers or whose complaint is against the employer himself, and it takes complaints from domestic workers [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

**21 May 2025.** Affidavits showed that every state had appointed District Officers. On Local Committees, compliance was unclear in Delhi, Haryana, Jharkhand and Kerala; Haryana, for one, gave no details for Jind, Karnal and Nuh. Several states gave no information on the survey [[sc-posh-order-2025-05-21]].

**12 August 2025.** The court was told that only the Andaman and Nicobar Islands had completed the survey, and gave states and union territories six more weeks [[livelaw-posh-district-survey-2025]].

Imagine a 22-year-old in a six-person garment shop in Karnal, harassed by the owner. The law never required her shop to have an Internal Committee. Her forum is the district's Local Committee, and in May 2025 the Supreme Court's own record could not say whether it existed.

## Using the record: compliance affidavits, contempt and RTI

An order creates a duty; the duty gets done when someone keeps checking. On POSH, where the Supreme Court has kept the case open since 2023, states had to answer on affidavit within months of the December 2024 deadlines. Citizens can check too. What follows is general information, not legal advice.

**Read the orders.** Where the court is monitoring, states must file compliance affidavits. The order of 21 May 2025 annexes a status report on them [[sc-posh-order-2025-05-21]].

**Use the Right to Information Act.** Ask the district administration who the District Officer is, when the Local Committee was constituted and where the One Stop Centre is. RTI has opened harder doors: the Hema Committee report on women in Malayalam cinema, given to the Kerala government in December 2019, became public on 19 August 2024 only after the State Information Commission ordered its release and the Kerala High Court rejected a challenge [[nie-hema-report-release-2024]].

**Know what contempt means.** A court can treat wilful disobedience of its directions as contempt, and courts do use the threat. In an order reported on 15 October 2026, in a case on menstrual hygiene, the Supreme Court gave states "one last opportunity" to report compliance and warned of contempt notices to their Chief Secretaries [[livelaw-sc-menstrual-contempt-oct-2026]]. A lawyer can advise whether a contempt petition is worth filing; a District Legal Services Authority can provide one free [[nalsa]].

Behind every gap in this timeline is someone looking for a door a court had already promised.
court-orders-on-sexual-violence-ignored.hg:
Supreme Court ka direction ek behas ko khatam karne ke liye hota hai. Lekin jo log sexual harassment, sexual violence ya apni pasand se pyaar karne par violence jhelte hain, unke liye aksar yahin se ek doosra intezaar shuru hua hai: is baat ka ki sarkarein woh karein jo court ne kaha. Yeh timeline 1997 se 2025 tak ke aise chaar directions ko un tareekhon ke zariye follow karti hai jab yeh kami record par aayi.

| Direction | Kab diya gaya | Baad ka record |
|---|---|---|
| Kaam ki jagah sexual harassment ke liye complaints committees | 13 August 1997 | 2012: kai states ne compliance nahi kiya tha |
| Honour crimes ke liye special cells aur fast-track courts | 27 March 2018 | December 2025: Delhi mein koi fast-track court nahi |
| Har district mein One Stop Centre | 11 December 2018, ek saal ke andar | July 2026: 1,033 approved centres mein se 985 chalu |
| POSH Act ke tahat District Officers aur Local Committees | 3 December 2024, 31 January 2025 tak | May 2025: chaar states aur union territories mein tasveer saaf nahi |

## 1997 aur 2012: Vishaka ki committees, aur court ki phatkaar

**13 August 1997.** Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan mein Chief Justice J.S. Verma ki aguwai wali teen judges ki bench ne working women ke sexual harassment ke khilaaf guidelines banayi, aur kaha ki jab tak Parliament law nahi banati, yeh binding rahengi. Har employer ke yahan ek complaints committee honi thi, jiski head ek mahila ho, jisme kam se kam aadhe members mahilayein hon, aur senior staff ke dabaav se bachne ke liye ek third party, jaise koi NGO, bhi shaamil ho [[sc-vishaka-1997]].

**19 October 2012.** Pandrah saal baad, Medha Kotwal Lele v. Union of India mein, court ne paaya ki kai state governments ne compliance kiya hi nahi tha. Usne taluka, district aur state level par committees ka order diya, aur jin states mein poore state ke liye sirf ek committee thi, unhe aur committees banane ke liye do mahine diye. Saath hi chetavni di ki "laws with sloppy enforcement are not enough", yaani dheele enforcement wale laws kaafi nahi hain [[sci-posh-enforcement-judgment-2023]].

**2013 aur 2023.** Parliament ka law, POSH Act, 9 December 2013 ko laagu hua, Vishaka ke 15 saal se bhi zyada baad. 12 May 2023 ko Supreme Court ne is Act mein bhi "serious lapses in the enforcement" paaye, yaani enforcement mein gambhir kamiyan, aur ise "a sorry state of affairs" kaha, yaani afsosnaak haalat [[sci-posh-enforcement-judgment-2023]].

## 2018: Shakti Vahini, aur honour-crime courts jo 2025 mein bhi nahi the

**27 March 2018.** Shakti Vahini v. Union of India mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki apna life partner chunne ka haq individual liberty ka hissa hai, aur honour crimes ke khilaaf preventive, remedial aur punitive measures ka order diya [[barandbench-shakti-vahini-madras-pil-2021]]. Inme special cells, fast-track aur special courts, aur district-level monitoring committees shaamil the [[barandbench-honour-killing-fast-track-2025]].

**December 2025.** Saat saal se bhi zyada baad, Delhi High Court ko bataya gaya ki Delhi mein honour-killing cases ke liye koi fast-track court bani hi nahi hai. Court ne petition band kar di, aur petitioners se kaha ki woh High Court ki administrative side aur Delhi government ke paas jayein [[barandbench-honour-killing-fast-track-2025]].

Inter-caste ya inter-faith relationship ki wajah se dhamkiyan jhel rahe couple se 2018 ke judgment ne protection ka, aur unke hamlavaron ke jaldi trial ka, vaada kiya tha. Desh ki rajdhani mein us system ka ek hissa tab tak bana hi nahi tha.

## 2018: har district mein One Stop Centre

**11 December 2018.** Nipun Saxena v. Union of India mein court ne likha: "All the States/Union Territories are requested to set up at least one 'one stop centre' in every district within one year from today", yaani sabhi states aur union territories se request hai ki aaj se ek saal ke andar har district mein kam se kam ek One Stop Centre banayein [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Shabd tha "requested". Woh ek saal December 2019 mein khatam ho gaya.

**March 2025.** Tab tak 802 centres chal rahe the [[pib-nirbhaya-fund-2025]].

**July 2026.** 1,033 approved centres mein se 985 chal rahe the [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]]. Inme se kareeb paanchva hissa March 2025 ke baad hi chalu hua tha, yaani deadline ke paanch saal se bhi zyada baad, aur 48 approved centres tab bhi shuru nahi hue the.

## 2024-2025: POSH ki deadlines aur gayab Local Committees

**3 December 2024.** Apne 2023 ke judgment ke follow-up mein Supreme Court ne tareekhein tay kar di. Har state ko 31 December 2024 tak har district ke liye ek District Officer notify karna tha. Local Committees aur sarkari Internal Committees 31 January 2025 tak banni thi, aur har district mein public aur private organisations ka survey hona tha ki unme Internal Committee hai ya nahi [[sc-posh-order-2025-05-21]].

Local Committee woh forum hai jo Act us aurat ko deta hai jiske workplace mein das se kam workers hain ya jiski complaint khud employer ke khilaaf hai. Domestic workers ki complaints bhi yahin aati hain [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

**21 May 2025.** Affidavits se pata chala ki har state ne District Officers appoint kar diye the. Local Committees par Delhi, Haryana, Jharkhand aur Kerala ka compliance saaf nahi tha; Haryana ne, misaal ke taur par, Jind, Karnal aur Nuh ki koi details nahi di. Kai states ne survey par koi information hi nahi di [[sc-posh-order-2025-05-21]].

**12 August 2025.** Court ko bataya gaya ki survey sirf Andaman and Nicobar Islands ne poora kiya hai, aur usne states aur union territories ko chhe hafte aur diye [[livelaw-posh-district-survey-2025]].

Maan lijiye Karnal ki ek garment shop mein chhe log kaam karte hain, aur wahan ki 22 saal ki ek worker ko maalik harass karta hai. Law ne uski dukaan ke liye Internal Committee kabhi zaroori ki hi nahi. Uska forum district ki Local Committee hai, aur May 2025 mein Supreme Court ka apna record yeh nahi bata sakta tha ki woh Committee bani bhi hai ya nahi.

## Record ka istemaal: compliance affidavits, contempt aur RTI

Order se zimmedari banti hai; zimmedari tab poori hoti hai jab koi lagataar check karta rahe. POSH par Supreme Court ne 2023 se case khula rakha hai, isliye December 2024 ki deadlines ke kuch hi mahinon ke andar states ko affidavit par jawab dena pada. Citizens bhi check kar sakte hain. Aage jo likha hai woh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

**Orders padhiye.** Jis case ki nigrani court kar rahi ho, usme states ko compliance affidavits file karne padte hain. 21 May 2025 ke order ke saath in par ek status report lagi hai [[sc-posh-order-2025-05-21]].

**Right to Information Act ka istemaal kijiye.** District administration se poochiye ki District Officer kaun hai, Local Committee kab bani aur One Stop Centre kahan hai. RTI ne isse mushkil darwaze bhi khole hain: Malayalam cinema mein mahilaon par Hema Committee ki report December 2019 mein Kerala government ko di gayi thi, aur 19 August 2024 ko tabhi public hui jab State Information Commission ne use release karne ka order diya aur Kerala High Court ne uske khilaaf challenge khaarij kar diya [[nie-hema-report-release-2024]].

**Contempt ka matlab samajhiye.** Court apne direction ko jaan-boojh kar na maanne ko contempt maan sakti hai, aur courts is dhamki ka istemaal karti bhi hain. 15 October 2026 ko report hue ek order mein, menstrual hygiene ke ek case mein, Supreme Court ne states ko compliance report karne ka "one last opportunity", yaani ek aakhri mauka, diya aur unke Chief Secretaries ko contempt notice bhejne ki chetavni di [[livelaw-sc-menstrual-contempt-oct-2026]]. Contempt petition file karna theek rahega ya nahi, yeh lawyer bata sakta hai; District Legal Services Authority free lawyer de sakti hai [[nalsa]].

Is timeline ke har gap ke peeche koi insaan hai, jo us darwaze ko dhoondh raha hai jiska vaada court pehle hi kar chuki thi.

death-penalty-for-rape-india-timeline.en:
Weeks after the 2012 Delhi gang rape, a three-member committee led by Justice J.S. Verma advised the government against the death penalty for rape, warning that it "may not have a deterrent effect" [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Parliament went the other way. Between 2013 and 2023 it added death to India's rape laws four times. Courts, which have to weigh each crime and each convict separately, have been far more cautious with it. This timeline sets each change in the law beside what happened in court. It is general information, not legal advice.

## 2013: death enters the rape law

- **23 January 2013:** the three-member Justice J.S. Verma Committee submits its report. It advises against death for rape and recommends removing the exception that lets a husband rape his wife [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Parliament follows neither recommendation.
- **Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013:** a new Section 376A of the IPC makes rape that causes a woman's death or leaves her in a persistent vegetative state punishable with at least 20 years, imprisonment for the rest of natural life, or death. Gang rape gets a minimum of 20 years, extendable to natural life, but not death [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].
- The same law adds Section 376E, which lets a court sentence a man convicted of rape a second time to death [[livelaw-shakti-mills-death-sentence-2014]].

The committee was set up in December 2012, after the Delhi gang rape, to advise on how the law should respond. On two of its clearest recommendations, against death for rape and against the marital rape exception, Parliament went the other way.

## 2014 and 2021: Shakti Mills, sentenced and commuted

- **4 April 2014:** a Mumbai sessions court sentences three repeat offenders in the 2013 Shakti Mills gang rape cases to death under Section 376E. It is the first time any court uses the repeat-offender provision [[livelaw-shakti-mills-death-sentence-2014]].
- **25 November 2021:** the Bombay High Court (Justices S.S. Jadhav and P.K. Chavan) commutes all three death sentences to life imprisonment, holding that a constitutional court cannot award punishment based on public opinion [[barandbench-shakti-mills-hc-2021]].

More than seven years passed between the death sentences and the commutation. For the survivors, that was seven more years of a case without an ending.

> A new punishment in the statute book is a promise. Whether it is kept is decided years later, by a judge reading one file.

## 2018 and 2019: girls under 12, and POCSO

- **21 April 2018:** an ordinance, later the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018, makes the rape of a girl under 12 punishable with at least 20 years, natural life or death (Section 376AB), and the gang rape of a girl under 12 punishable with natural life or death (Section 376DB). Parliament's Act gets assent on 11 August 2018 [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]].
- **2019:** an amendment to the POCSO Act raises the minimum for aggravated penetrative sexual assault on a child from 10 to 20 years and adds death as the maximum [[prs-pocso-amendment-bill-2019]].

Consider what this means in a real home. Imagine a 9-year-old in Jaipur abused by an uncle. Whether the case is ever reported depends on the adults around her, many of whom may also be his family. A harsher sentence does nothing for her unless someone first goes to the police. The 2018 and 2019 laws raised the ceiling; they did not change who a child can tell.

## 2020: four hangings at Tihar

- **5 May 2017:** the Supreme Court (Justices Dipak Misra, R. Banumathi and Ashok Bhushan) dismisses the appeals of the four adult convicts in the 2012 Delhi gang rape and murder and confirms their death sentences, holding that the aggravating circumstances outweighed the mitigating ones [[sc-mukesh-nct-delhi-2017]].
- **20 March 2020:** the four are hanged together at Tihar Jail at 5:30 am. Of the other two accused, one was found dead in jail in March 2013 and the juvenile was released in 2015 after three years in a correctional home [[tribune-nirbhaya-execution-2020]].

Seven years and three months separated the crime from the executions, in one of the most closely followed rape cases in India's history.

## 2023 to 2025: the BNS, and RG Kar's "not rarest of the rare"

- **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (in force 1 July 2024):** death stays for the rape of a girl under 12 (Section 65), for rape that causes death or a persistent vegetative state (Section 66) and for a second rape conviction (Section 71). Section 70 widens it to the gang rape of any girl under 18 [[indiacode-bns-2023]].
- **3 September 2024:** after the RG Kar Medical College case, the West Bengal Assembly unanimously passes the Aparajita Bill, making death mandatory where a rape victim dies or is left in a vegetative state [[barandbench-aparajita-bill-2024]]. On 6 September the Governor reserves it for the President, since a state cannot change central criminal law without presidential assent [[livelaw-aparajita-explainer-2024]].
- **20 January 2025:** a Sealdah court in Kolkata sentences the RG Kar convict to life imprisonment for the rest of his natural life under Sections 64, 66 and 103(1) of the BNS, refuses the CBI's plea for death and orders the state to pay Rs 17 lakh to the family. The judge says the crime "does not fall under the rarest of the rare category" and that courts must resist "the temptation to bow to public pressure or emotional appeals" [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]].
- **7 February 2025:** the Calcutta High Court dismisses the West Bengal government's appeal for death, leaving the CBI to pursue its own [[barandbench-rg-kar-hc-2025]].

Read together, the record shows two institutions pulling in different directions. Legislatures answer public anger by adding death to more sections. Judges, bound by the "rarest of the rare" test, keep asking whether a single case justifies it, and two courts, in 2021 and in 2025, have said in plain words that public opinion cannot decide a sentence. For a survivor, the harder question comes before any sentence: whether her case reaches a verdict at all.
death-penalty-for-rape-india-timeline.hg:
2012 ke Delhi gang rape ke kuch hi hafton baad, Justice J.S. Verma ki aguaai wali teen members ki committee ne sarkaar ko salaah di ki rape ke liye maut ki sazaa na laayi jaaye, kyunki woh "may not have a deterrent effect", yaani shaayad logon ko crime se rok na paaye [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Parliament ulti disha mein gaya. 2013 aur 2023 ke beech usne India ke rape laws mein chaar baar maut ki sazaa jodi. Courts, jinhe har crime aur har convict ko alag se tolna hota hai, is sazaa ko lekar kahin zyada saavdhaan rahe hain. Yeh timeline kaanoon ke har badlaav ke saath rakhti hai ki court mein kya hua. Yeh general jaankari hai, legal advice nahi.

## 2013: rape law mein maut ki sazaa aati hai

- **23 January 2013:** teen members wali Justice J.S. Verma Committee apni report deti hai. Woh rape ke liye maut ki sazaa ke khilaaf salaah deti hai, aur kehti hai ki woh exception hataaya jaaye jo pati ko apni patni ka rape karne ki chhoot deta hai [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Parliament dono mein se koi salaah nahi maanta.
- **Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013:** IPC ka naya Section 376A kehta hai ki agar rape se aurat ki maut ho jaaye ya woh persistent vegetative state mein chali jaaye, toh sazaa kam se kam 20 saal, baaki natural life tak qaid, ya maut hai. Gang rape ke liye minimum 20 saal, jo natural life tak badh sakti hai, par maut nahi [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].
- Isi kaanoon ne Section 376E joda, jisse court doosri baar rape ke liye convict hue aadmi ko maut ki sazaa de sakti hai [[livelaw-shakti-mills-death-sentence-2014]].

Yeh committee December 2012 mein, Delhi gang rape ke baad, yeh salaah dene ke liye bani thi ki kaanoon ko kaise jawaab dena chahiye. Uski do sabse saaf salaahon par, rape ke liye maut ki sazaa ke khilaaf aur marital rape exception ke khilaaf, Parliament ulti disha mein gaya.

## 2014 aur 2021: Shakti Mills, sazaa aur commutation

- **4 April 2014:** Mumbai ki ek sessions court 2013 ke Shakti Mills gang rape cases ke teen repeat offenders ko Section 376E ke tahat maut ki sazaa deti hai. Pehli baar kisi court ne repeat-offender wala provision use kiya [[livelaw-shakti-mills-death-sentence-2014]].
- **25 November 2021:** Bombay High Court (Justices S.S. Jadhav aur P.K. Chavan) teeno death sentences ko life imprisonment mein badal deti hai, aur kehti hai ki constitutional court public opinion ke basis par sazaa nahi de sakti [[barandbench-shakti-mills-hc-2021]].

Death sentences aur commutation ke beech saat saal se zyada guzar gaye. Survivors ke liye yeh saat aur saal the ek aise case ke, jiska ant nahi aa raha tha.

> Kaanoon ki kitaab mein nayi sazaa ek vaada hai. Woh nibhaaya jaayega ya nahi, yeh saalon baad ek judge ek file padhkar tay karta hai.

## 2018 aur 2019: 12 saal se chhoti ladkiyan, aur POCSO

- **21 April 2018:** ek ordinance, jo baad mein Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018 bana, 12 saal se kam umar ki ladki ke rape ke liye kam se kam 20 saal, natural life ya maut ki sazaa rakhta hai (Section 376AB), aur 12 saal se kam umar ki ladki ke gang rape ke liye natural life ya maut (Section 376DB). Parliament ke Act ko 11 August 2018 ko manzoori milti hai [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]].
- **2019:** POCSO Act mein amendment bachche par aggravated penetrative sexual assault ki minimum sazaa 10 se 20 saal karta hai, aur maximum sazaa maut [[prs-pocso-amendment-bill-2019]].

Sochiye ek asli ghar mein iska kya matlab hai. Imagine kijiye Jaipur ki ek 9 saal ki bachchi, jiska abuse ek chacha karta hai. Case kabhi report hoga ya nahi, yeh uske aas-paas ke badon par nirbhar hai, jinmein se kai shaayad uske bhi parivaar wale hain. Jab tak koi police ke paas nahi jaata, kadi sazaa us bachchi ke kisi kaam ki nahi. 2018 aur 2019 ke kaanoonon ne sazaa ki upari seema badhaayi; unhone yeh nahi badla ki bachcha kisse baat kar sakta hai.

## 2020: Tihar mein chaar phaansiyan

- **5 May 2017:** Supreme Court (Justices Dipak Misra, R. Banumathi aur Ashok Bhushan) 2012 ke Delhi gang rape aur murder ke chaar adult convicts ki appeals khaarij karti hai aur unki death sentences ko sahi thehraati hai, yeh kehte hue ki aggravating circumstances mitigating circumstances se bhaari the [[sc-mukesh-nct-delhi-2017]].
- **20 March 2020:** chaaron ko Tihar Jail mein subah 5:30 baje ek saath phaansi di jaati hai. Baaki do accused mein se ek March 2013 mein jail mein mara paaya gaya tha, aur juvenile ko correctional home mein teen saal ke baad 2015 mein chhod diya gaya tha [[tribune-nirbhaya-execution-2020]].

India ke sabse zyada dhyaan se follow kiye gaye rape cases mein se ek mein bhi, crime aur phaansi ke beech saat saal aur teen mahine ka fasla tha.

## 2023 se 2025: BNS, aur RG Kar ka "not rarest of the rare"

- **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (1 July 2024 se laagu):** maut ki sazaa 12 saal se kam umar ki ladki ke rape (Section 65), rape jisse maut ya persistent vegetative state ho (Section 66), aur doosre rape conviction (Section 71) ke liye bani rehti hai. Section 70 ise 18 saal se kam umar ki kisi bhi ladki ke gang rape tak badha deta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].
- **3 September 2024:** RG Kar Medical College case ke baad West Bengal Assembly sarvsammati se Aparajita Bill paas karti hai, jo rape victim ki maut ya vegetative state mein jaane par maut ki sazaa ko mandatory banata hai [[barandbench-aparajita-bill-2024]]. 6 September ko Governor ise President ke liye reserve kar dete hain, kyunki koi state presidential manzoori ke bina central criminal law nahi badal sakta [[livelaw-aparajita-explainer-2024]].
- **20 January 2025:** Kolkata ki Sealdah court RG Kar convict ko BNS Sections 64, 66 aur 103(1) ke tahat baaki natural life ke liye life imprisonment deti hai, CBI ki maut ki maang thukraati hai, aur state ko parivaar ko Rs 17 lakh dene ka order deti hai. Judge kehte hain ki crime "does not fall under the rarest of the rare category", aur courts ko "the temptation to bow to public pressure or emotional appeals" se bachna chahiye [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]].
- **7 February 2025:** Calcutta High Court West Bengal government ki maut ki sazaa wali appeal khaarij karti hai, aur CBI apni alag appeal aage le jaati hai [[barandbench-rg-kar-hc-2025]].

Saath padhein toh record do institutions ko alag-alag disha mein kheenchte dikhata hai. Legislatures public gusse ka jawaab zyada sections mein maut ki sazaa jodkar dete hain. Judges, "rarest of the rare" test se bandhe, har baar poochhte hain ki kya ek case use justify karta hai, aur do courts ne, 2021 aur 2025 mein, saaf shabdon mein kaha hai ki public opinion sazaa tay nahi kar sakti. Survivor ke liye mushkil sawaal kisi bhi sazaa se pehle aata hai: kya uska case faisle tak pahunchega bhi.

dignity-privacy-rights-rape-survivors-co.en:
Most people think survivors' rights come from the sections of a criminal code. Many of the most practical ones did not. The rule that a doctor may not perform a "finger test", that a newspaper may not hint at who a survivor is, that a workplace must have a complaints committee, that sex with a 16-year-old wife is rape: each began as a judge reading a fundamental right, such as privacy, dignity or equality, and turning it into an instruction someone could be held to. This explainer follows that thread through a handful of rulings and shows how to use them. It is general information, not legal advice.

## Rights that judges can enforce

A right in the Constitution becomes useful when a court says what it requires in a particular room. The tool for this is Article 141: what the Supreme Court declares is law for every court in India. In 1997 the Court went further and said its own guidelines would be "treated as the law declared by this Court under Article 141" until Parliament acted [[sc-vishaka-rajasthan-1997]].

The same method runs through later cases. In its 2022 abortion judgment, the Court relied on the nine-judge 2017 privacy ruling in K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India, which linked a woman's legal right to an abortion to her constitutional right to make reproductive choices under Article 21 [[sc-x-principal-secretary-2022]]. Once privacy and bodily choice are rights, a hospital, a police station or a court that ignores them is not being rude. It is breaking the law.

## Integrity and dignity: the two-finger test, 2013 and 2022

In April 2013, in Lillu v. State of Haryana, two judges held that the "two-finger test" violates a rape survivor's right to privacy, physical and mental integrity and dignity [[barandbench-lillu-2013]]. The test treated a survivor's sexual history as evidence, as if it could decide whether she was raped.

A judgment does not reach every casualty ward on its own. On 31 October 2022, deciding a rape appeal from Jharkhand, the Court said the test "has no scientific basis", ruled that anyone who conducts it in breach of its directions "shall be guilty of misconduct", and ordered governments to circulate the Health Ministry's 2014 guidelines to all government and private hospitals and to review medical curricula so that the test is no longer prescribed [[scconline-shailendra-rai-2022]]. The Court also called it patriarchal and sexist to doubt a rape complaint because the woman is sexually active. Rights language became a disciplinary rule with a named consequence.

Dignity reaches bail orders too. On 18 March 2021, in Aparna Bhat v. State of Madhya Pradesh, the Court struck down a High Court bail condition that asked a man accused of sexual assault to have the complainant tie a rakhi on him. It ruled that bail conditions must not require or permit contact with the victim, that judges must not suggest compromise or marriage, and that every judge must receive gender-sensitisation training [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]].

## Equality at work: Vishaka's guidelines as law

The 1997 Vishaka case was prompted by the gang rape of a social worker in a Rajasthan village. There was no law on sexual harassment at work. A bench headed by Chief Justice J.S. Verma wrote one: employers had to set up complaints committees headed by a woman, with at least half their members women and an outside member to guard against pressure [[sc-vishaka-rajasthan-1997]].

Parliament took more than 15 years to turn those guidelines into a statute: the workplace harassment law was enacted on 22 April 2013 and came into force on 9 December 2013 [[sci-posh-enforcement-judgment-2023]]. For all those years, a woman's right to a safe workplace rested on a judgment. Rights-based rules can arrive long before the legislature, but they work only if people know they exist.

## Privacy: anonymity even in a remote manner

Naming a rape victim has been a crime since the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1983, which also required rape trials to be held in camera [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. The gap was indirect identification: a relative's name, a school, a village. On 11 December 2018, in Nipun Saxena v. Union of India, the Court closed the gap. No one may publish a victim's name "or even in a remote manner disclose any facts which can lead to the victim being identified" [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. The bar now sits in Section 72 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

Privacy continues inside the courtroom. Rape and POCSO trials must be held in camera, as far as practicable before a woman judge, and nothing about the proceedings may be published without the court's permission [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Marriage is no shield: 2017 and the 2022 abortion ruling

The rape law contained an exception: sex by a man with his wife was not rape, and it applied even to wives as young as 15. This was Exception 2 to Section 375 of the IPC. On 11 October 2017, in Independent Thought v. Union of India, the Court read the exception down so that it protects no husband whose wife is under 18 [[sc-independent-thought-2017]].

The exception still covers wives aged 18 and above. It now sits in Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which says that sex by a man with his own wife, if she is not under 18, is not rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. But on 29 September 2022, in X v. Principal Secretary, the Court held that "rape" in the abortion rules includes rape by a husband, so a woman pregnant through marital rape can seek termination up to 24 weeks, like any other rape survivor [[sc-x-principal-secretary-2022]]. The ruling applies only to the abortion law and left the criminal exception to a separate pending case.

> Many of these protections did not come from Parliament. They were rights a judge was asked to enforce, by a petitioner who refused to accept that nothing could be done.

The practical lesson: when a doctor, editor, police officer or judge breaks one of these rules, name the judgment. A complaint that says "this violates the Supreme Court's 2022 direction" is harder to brush aside than one that says "this felt wrong".
dignity-privacy-rights-rape-survivors-co.hg:
Zyada tar log sochte hain ki survivors ke rights criminal code ke sections se aate hain. Sabse kaam ke kai rights wahan se nahi aaye. Yeh rule ki doctor "finger test" nahi kar sakta, ki koi akhbaar ishaare se bhi nahi bata sakta ki survivor kaun hai, ki har workplace mein complaints committee honi chahiye, ki 16 saal ki wife ke saath sex rape hai: inme se har ek tab shuru hua jab kisi judge ne ek fundamental right, jaise privacy, dignity ya equality, ko padha aur use aisi instruction mein badal diya jiske liye kisi ko jawabdeh banaya ja sake. Yeh explainer kuch rulings ke through is dhaage ko follow karta hai aur dikhata hai ki inhe kaise use karna hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Woh rights jo judges laagu karwa sakte hain

Constitution mein likha right tab kaam ka banta hai jab court bataata hai ki kisi khaas kamre mein uska matlab kya hai. Iska tool hai Article 141: Supreme Court jo declare karta hai, woh India ke har court ke liye law hai. 1997 mein Court ne isse bhi aage jaakar kaha ki uski apni guidelines "treated as the law declared by this Court under Article 141" maani jaayengi jab tak Parliament kuch nahi karti [[sc-vishaka-rajasthan-1997]].

Baad ke cases mein bhi yahi tareeka chalta hai. Apne 2022 ke abortion judgment mein Court ne K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India ke nau-judge wale 2017 privacy ruling pe bharosa kiya, jisne abortion ke legal right ko Article 21 ke under aurat ke reproductive choices karne ke constitutional right se joda [[sc-x-principal-secretary-2022]]. Jab privacy aur apne body ke faisle rights hain, toh jo hospital, police station ya court inhe ignore karta hai, woh sirf rude nahi ho raha. Woh law tod raha hai.

## Integrity aur dignity: two-finger test, 2013 aur 2022

April 2013 mein, Lillu v. State of Haryana mein, do judges ne kaha ki "two-finger test" rape survivor ke privacy, physical aur mental integrity aur dignity ke right ka ullanghan karta hai [[barandbench-lillu-2013]]. Yeh test survivor ki sexual history ko saboot ki tarah treat karta tha, jaise usse tay ho sakta ho ki uska rape hua ya nahi.

Ek judgment apne aap har casualty ward tak nahi pahunchta. 31 October 2022 ko, Jharkhand ki ek rape appeal decide karte hue, Court ne kaha ki test ka "no scientific basis" hai, ki jo bhi uske directions todkar yeh test karega woh "shall be guilty of misconduct", aur governments ko order diya ki Health Ministry ki 2014 guidelines saare government aur private hospitals tak pahunchaayein aur medical curriculum review karein taaki yeh test ab prescribe na kiya jaaye [[scconline-shailendra-rai-2022]]. Court ne yeh bhi kaha ki kisi aurat ke rape complaint pe sirf isliye shak karna ki woh sexually active hai, patriarchal aur sexist hai. Rights ki bhasha ek disciplinary rule ban gayi, jiska consequence naam lekar likha gaya.

Dignity bail orders tak bhi pahunchti hai. 18 March 2021 ko, Aparna Bhat v. State of Madhya Pradesh mein, Court ne High Court ki woh bail condition radd kar di jisme sexual assault ke accused aadmi se kaha gaya tha ki woh complainant se apne haath pe rakhi bandhwaaye. Court ne kaha ki bail conditions victim se contact ki maang ya ijaazat nahi de sakti, judges compromise ya shaadi ka sujhaav nahi de sakte, aur har judge ko gender-sensitisation training milni chahiye [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]].

## Kaam ki jagah pe equality: Vishaka guidelines law ki tarah

1997 ka Vishaka case Rajasthan ke ek gaon mein ek social worker ke gang rape ke baad shuru hua. Kaam ki jagah pe sexual harassment ka koi law tha hi nahi. Chief Justice J.S. Verma ki bench ne ek likh diya: employers ko complaints committees banani thi jinki head ek aurat ho, aadhe members aurtein hon, aur pressure se bachane ke liye ek bahar ka member ho [[sc-vishaka-rajasthan-1997]].

Parliament ko in guidelines ko statute banane mein 15 saal se zyada lage: workplace harassment law 22 April 2013 ko enact hua aur 9 December 2013 se laagu hua [[sci-posh-enforcement-judgment-2023]]. In saare saalon mein, aurat ka safe workplace ka right ek judgment pe tika tha. Rights pe bane rules legislature se bahut pehle aa sakte hain, lekin kaam tabhi karte hain jab log jaante hain ki woh hain.

## Privacy: "even in a remote manner" bhi pehchaan nahi

Rape victim ka naam lena Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1983 se crime hai, jisne yeh bhi zaroori kiya ki rape trials in camera hon [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Gap tha indirect pehchaan ka: kisi rishtedaar ka naam, school, gaon. 11 December 2018 ko, Nipun Saxena v. Union of India mein, Court ne yeh gap band kiya. Koi bhi victim ka naam publish nahi kar sakta "or even in a remote manner disclose any facts which can lead to the victim being identified" [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Yeh rok ab Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ke Section 72 mein hai.

Privacy courtroom ke andar bhi chalti hai. Rape aur POCSO trials in camera hone chahiye, jahan tak ho sake woman judge ke saamne, aur court ki permission ke bina proceedings ke baare mein kuch bhi publish nahi ho sakta [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Shaadi koi dhaal nahi: 2017 aur 2022 ka abortion ruling

Rape law mein ek exception tha: aadmi ka apni wife ke saath sex rape nahi tha, aur yeh 15 saal jitni kam umar ki wives pe bhi laagu tha. Yeh IPC ke Section 375 ka Exception 2 tha. 11 October 2017 ko, Independent Thought v. Union of India mein, Court ne exception ko read down kiya taaki yeh kisi aise pati ko na bachaaye jiski wife 18 se kam ho [[sc-independent-thought-2017]].

18 aur usse upar ki wives pe exception abhi bhi laagu hai. Ab yeh Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ke Section 63 mein hai, jo kehta hai ki aadmi ka apni wife ke saath sex, agar wife 18 se kam nahi hai, rape nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Lekin 29 September 2022 ko, X v. Principal Secretary mein, Court ne kaha ki abortion rules mein "rape" mein pati dwara kiya gaya rape bhi aata hai, isliye marital rape se pregnant hui aurat bhi kisi bhi doosre rape survivor ki tarah 24 weeks tak termination maang sakti hai [[sc-x-principal-secretary-2022]]. Yeh ruling sirf abortion law pe laagu hai aur criminal exception ka sawaal ek alag pending case pe chhod diya gaya.

> Inme se kai protections Parliament se nahi aaye. Yeh woh rights the jinhe laagu karwane ke liye kisi judge se kaha gaya, ek aise petitioner ne jisne maanne se inkaar kiya ki kuch nahi ho sakta.

Practical seekh: jab koi doctor, editor, police officer ya judge in rules mein se koi todta hai, toh judgment ka naam lo. Jo complaint kehti hai "yeh Supreme Court ke 2022 direction ka violation hai", use taalna us complaint se mushkil hai jo kehti hai "yeh galat laga".

fast-track-courts-2031-plan-arithmetic.en:
On 4 November 2026 the Union Cabinet gave India's Fast Track Special Courts five more years and Rs 3,788.04 crore [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]]. These are the courts meant to try rape and POCSO cases quickly. The announcement counts courts and crores. It does not say how many cases each court must close for the queue to get shorter. That sum can be worked out from figures the government has already given Parliament. Every input below is official; every division is ours.

## What the Cabinet approved on 4 November 2026

The scheme now runs from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031. Of the Rs 3,788.04 crore, the Centre's share is Rs 2,353.15 crore, paid from the Nirbhaya Fund, and states and union territories pay the rest. The plan provides for up to 850 courts [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]]. The approval came seven months into the period it covers.

India has 779 such courts today, in 29 states and union territories, and 399 of them hear only POCSO cases. Since the scheme began on 2 October 2019 they have disposed of 4,02,457 cases [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]]. So "up to 850" means at most 71 more courts than now, an increase of less than a tenth.

The money grows faster than the court count. By July 2026 the Nirbhaya Fund had released Rs 1,234.55 crore for these courts [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]. The new central share is nearly double that. Divide the whole outlay across 850 courts and five years and it comes to about Rs 89 lakh per court per year.

## The queue: 2,02,175 to 2,45,579 in two years

In July 2026 the Law Ministry told the Rajya Sabha how many cases were pending before these courts on 31 December of each year: 2,02,175 in 2023, 2,04,122 in 2024 and 2,45,579 in 2025 [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]]. After a flat year, the queue grew by about a fifth in twelve months.

The same reply shows why. In 2025, 1,43,936 new cases were registered in these courts and 66,500 were disposed of [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]]. More than two cases came in for every one that went out. The courts were also deciding fewer cases than before: disposals were 76,319 in 2023 and 85,595 in 2024, then fell 22% in 2025 [[pib-fast-track-courts-impact-2026]].

One caution. Take the queue at the end of 2024, add the cases registered in 2025 and subtract the disposals, and the result is tens of thousands higher than the pending figure the ministry reports for the end of 2025. The reply does not explain the difference. Treat these as the government's own counts, not an audited ledger.

## The arithmetic of 850 courts

Start with what the courts did. Spread over the 779 courts now working, 66,500 disposals is about 85 cases per court in a year, or seven a month.

Now the target. Assume, generously, that all 850 courts are open and staffed from the first day, and that new cases keep arriving at the 2025 level.

| For the plan to... | Cases each court must close a month |
|---|---|
| repeat 2025 | about 7 |
| stop the queue growing (match 1,43,936 new cases a year) | about 14 |
| also clear the 2,45,579 pending cases by March 2031 | about 19 |

> The plan adds less than a tenth to the number of courts. To stop the queue growing, each court would have to double its 2025 output.

To clear the backlog within the plan's five years, each court would have to work at more than two and a half times the 2025 pace. If nothing changes except the extra courts, the sums run the other way: at the 2025 pace per court and the 2025 level of new cases, the queue would more than double by March 2031.

Imagine a 17-year-old in a district town whose chargesheet is filed this month. Her case joins a list of a few hundred. At seven disposals a month, a case that waits its turn at the back of that list is looking at years, not the months the law promises.

## The wider backlog in all courts

Fast-track courts carry only part of the load. NCRB counts every court. At the end of 2024, 1,85,785 rape cases were pending trial across India, a pendency of 89.8%, along with 2,86,903 POCSO cases, a pendency of 87.7% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The fast-track courts' own queue on that date was 2,04,122 [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]]. The two counts come from different systems and cannot simply be subtracted. Side by side, they show that many cases are waiting in ordinary courts this scheme does not fund.

Speed is also not the same as justice. A disposal is any case that leaves the list, whatever the result. Of the rape trials completed in 2024, 24.4% ended in conviction, which was 5,032 convictions; for POCSO the rate was 32.3% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A plan judged only by disposals can look successful while most trials still end without a conviction.

## What would actually make them fast

The deadlines already exist. A rape trial must finish within two months of the chargesheet [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. A POCSO Special Court must record the child's evidence within 30 days of taking cognisance and complete the trial within one year, "as far as possible" [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. The first carries no consequence when it is missed, and the second leaves itself room. A fast-track court is bound by the same clocks as any other court. What the scheme buys is a dedicated courtroom.

A trial needs more than a courtroom. It needs a chargesheet filed on time, forensic reports, a prosecutor, witnesses who turn up without being pressured, and a judge who stays in the post. None of that shows in a count of courts. Nor is the scheme permanent everywhere: Jharkhand left it in July 2025 [[pib-fast-track-courts-impact-2026]].

So the test of the 2026-2031 plan is not whether 850 courts open. It is three numbers, published for every state every year: cases registered, cases disposed of and cases pending. If the pending count falls, the plan is working. If it keeps rising, India will have paid Rs 3,788.04 crore for a longer queue.

For anyone already in that queue, some rights do not wait for a verdict. Compensation can be claimed from the State or District Legal Services Authority even if the offender is never traced and no trial takes place [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. This is general information, not legal advice.
fast-track-courts-2031-plan-arithmetic.hg:
4 November 2026 ko Union Cabinet ne India ke Fast Track Special Courts ko paanch saal aur Rs 3,788.04 crore diye [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]]. Yeh woh courts hain jinka kaam rape aur POCSO cases ka trial jaldi karna hai. Announcement courts aur crores ginta hai.
