Yeh nahi batata ki queue chhoti karne ke liye har court ko kitne cases close karne honge. Yeh hisaab un figures se nikal sakta hai jo sarkar Parliament ko pehle hi de chuki hai. Neeche har input official hai; har division humara hai.

## 4 November 2026 ko Cabinet ne kya approve kiya

Scheme ab 1 April 2026 se 31 March 2031 tak chalegi. Rs 3,788.04 crore mein se Centre ka hissa Rs 2,353.15 crore hai, jo Nirbhaya Fund se aayega, aur baaki states aur union territories denge. Plan mein zyada se zyada 850 courts ka provision hai [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]]. Approval us period ke saat mahine guzarne ke baad aaya jise yeh cover karta hai.

Aaj India mein aise 779 courts hain, 29 states aur union territories mein, aur inme se 399 sirf POCSO cases sunte hain. 2 October 2019 ko scheme shuru hone ke baad se inhone 4,02,457 cases dispose kiye hain [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]]. Matlab "850 tak" ka seedha sa arth hai abhi se zyada se zyada 71 courts aur, yaani ek-dasve hisse se bhi kam badhotri.

Paisa courts ki ginti se tez badhta hai. July 2026 tak Nirbhaya Fund in courts ke liye Rs 1,234.55 crore release kar chuka tha [[theprint-nirbhaya-fund-rajya-sabha-2026]]. Naya central share uska lagbhag double hai. Poore outlay ko 850 courts aur paanch saal mein baanto toh har court ko saal ke lagbhag Rs 89 lakh milte hain.

## Queue: do saal mein 2,02,175 se 2,45,579

July 2026 mein Law Ministry ne Rajya Sabha ko bataya ki har saal 31 December ko in courts mein kitne cases pending the: 2023 mein 2,02,175, 2024 mein 2,04,122 aur 2025 mein 2,45,579 [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]]. Ek saal flat rehne ke baad, baarah mahine mein queue lagbhag paanchve hisse jitni badh gayi.

Wahi reply wajah bhi dikhata hai. 2025 mein in courts mein 1,43,936 naye cases register hue aur 66,500 dispose hue [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]]. Har ek case jo bahar gaya, uske badle do se zyada andar aaye. Courts pehle se kam cases decide bhi kar rahe the: disposals 2023 mein 76,319 aur 2024 mein 85,595 the, phir 2025 mein 22% gir gaye [[pib-fast-track-courts-impact-2026]].

Ek caution. 2024 ke end ki queue lo, usme 2025 ke registered cases jodo aur disposals ghatao, toh result ministry ke bataye 2025-end pending figure se kayi das hazaar zyada aata hai. Reply is fark ko explain nahi karta. Inhe sarkar ki apni ginti samjho, audited hisaab-kitaab nahi.

## 850 courts ka hisaab

Pehle dekho courts ne kya kiya. 66,500 disposals ko abhi chal rahe 779 courts mein baanto toh har court ne saal mein lagbhag 85 cases close kiye, yaani mahine mein saat.

Ab target. Generous assumption lo ki saare 850 courts pehle din se khule hain aur staff ke saath chal rahe hain, aur naye cases 2025 ki speed se hi aate rahenge.

| Plan ko yeh karna hai... | Har court ko mahine mein kitne cases close karne honge |
|---|---|
| 2025 jaisa hi performance | lagbhag 7 |
| queue ko badhne se rokna (saal ke 1,43,936 naye cases ke barabar) | lagbhag 14 |
| saath mein 2,45,579 pending cases March 2031 tak clear karna | lagbhag 19 |

> Plan courts ki ginti mein ek-dasve hisse se bhi kam jodta hai. Queue ko badhne se rokne ke liye har court ko apna 2025 ka output double karna hoga.

Plan ke paanch saal mein backlog clear karne ke liye har court ko 2025 ki speed se dhai guna se bhi zyada tez kaam karna hoga. Agar extra courts ke alawa kuch nahi badla, toh hisaab ulti disha mein jaata hai: har court ki 2025 wali speed aur 2025 jitne naye cases ke saath, March 2031 tak queue double se bhi zyada ho jaayegi.

Socho ek 17 saal ki ladki kisi district town mein hai, jiske case ki chargesheet is mahine file hui. Uska case kuch sau cases ki list mein jud jaata hai. Mahine ke saat disposals pe, list ke aakhir mein apni baari ka wait karne wala case mahinon nahi, saalon dekh raha hai, jabki law mahinon ka promise karta hai.

## Saare courts ka bada backlog

Fast-track courts load ka sirf ek hissa uthate hain. NCRB har court ko ginta hai. 2024 ke end mein poore India mein 1,85,785 rape cases trial ke liye pending the, 89.8% pendency ke saath, aur 2,86,903 POCSO cases, 87.7% pendency ke saath [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Usi date pe fast-track courts ki apni queue 2,04,122 thi [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]]. Dono ginti alag systems se aati hain aur inhe seedha ghataya nahi ja sakta. Saath rakh ke dekho toh saaf hai ki bahut se cases un normal courts mein wait kar rahe hain jinhe yeh scheme fund nahi karti.

Speed aur insaaf ek cheez bhi nahi hain. Disposal ka matlab hai koi bhi case jo list se nikal gaya, result chahe kuch bhi ho. 2024 mein jo rape trials poore hue, unme se 24.4% conviction pe khatam hue, yaani 5,032 convictions; POCSO ke liye rate 32.3% tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jo plan sirf disposals se judge hota hai, woh successful dikh sakta hai jabki zyada tar trials bina conviction ke khatam ho rahe hon.

## Inhe sach mein fast kya banayega

Deadlines pehle se maujood hain. Rape trial chargesheet ke do mahine ke andar khatam hona chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. POCSO Special Court ko cognisance lene ke 30 din ke andar bachche ki gawahi record karni hai aur ek saal mein trial poora karna hai, "as far as possible" [[indiacode-pocso-act-2012]]. Pehli deadline miss hone pe koi consequence nahi hai, aur doosri ne apne liye jagah chhod rakhi hai. Fast-track court bhi unhi ghadiyon se bandha hai jinse koi bhi aur court. Scheme jo khareedti hai woh hai ek dedicated courtroom.

Trial ko courtroom se zyada chahiye. Use time pe file hui chargesheet chahiye, forensic reports, ek prosecutor, gawah jo bina pressure ke aayein, aur ek judge jo post pe tika rahe. Inme se kuch bhi courts ki ginti mein nahi dikhta. Scheme har jagah permanent bhi nahi hai: Jharkhand ne July 2025 mein ise chhod diya [[pib-fast-track-courts-impact-2026]].

Toh 2026-2031 plan ka test yeh nahi ki 850 courts khulte hain ya nahi. Test hai teen numbers, jo har state ke liye har saal publish hon: kitne cases register hue, kitne dispose hue aur kitne pending hain. Agar pending count girta hai, plan kaam kar raha hai. Agar badhta raha, toh India ne Rs 3,788.04 crore ek lambi queue ke liye diye honge.

Jo log pehle se is queue mein hain, unke kuch rights verdict ka wait nahi karte. Compensation State ya District Legal Services Authority se claim ho sakta hai, chahe offender kabhi trace na ho aur trial hi na ho [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

gang-rape-law-section-70-explained.en:
In most criminal trials, the court's first job is to work out who did what. Gang rape is the exception written into the statute. Under Section 70 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), when a woman is raped by a group, every member of that group is guilty of rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. A member of the group who did not rape her himself faces the same charge, and the same minimum sentence, as the men who did.

This explainer covers what makes an attack gang rape in law, how the sentences work and the bail and investigation rules that follow. It is general information, not legal advice.

## One act in law: why each member is guilty

The section applies where a woman is raped "by one or more persons constituting a group or acting in furtherance of a common intention". The words that matter come next.

> "each of those persons shall be deemed to have committed the offence of rape"

"Deemed" means the law treats each man as if he had committed the rape himself [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The prosecution has to prove that the woman was raped, and that the accused was part of the group or shared its intention. It does not have to prove which of them did what.

Consider a hypothetical. Four men force a woman into a car in Gurugram. One drives. One stops her from getting out. Two rape her. In court, the driver says he never touched her. If the judge finds that the four acted together, with a shared intention, Section 70 treats all four as having raped her.

One effect of this design is that the case does not hang on the survivor saying which man did what. The limit is in the words of the section: the group, or the common intention. A man who was merely present, with no part in the plan, is not a member of the group, and the prosecution still has to prove that each accused acted with the others.

## Twenty years to natural life, and death for under-18s

Each man convicted under Section 70(1) faces rigorous imprisonment of at least 20 years, which can extend to imprisonment for the rest of his natural life [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. That is double the 10-year minimum for rape under Section 64 [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The sentence is not shared out. Four convicts means four sentences of at least 20 years each.

If the girl is under 18, Section 70(2) leaves the court two options: imprisonment for the rest of natural life, or death [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

None of this arrived at once. The 20-year minimum came with the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013, passed after the 2012 Delhi gang rape case and the Justice J.S. Verma Committee's report of 23 January 2013 [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. It wrote that floor into Section 376D of the Indian Penal Code and said any fine "shall be paid to the victim" [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. In 2018 Parliament made gang rape of a girl under 12 punishable with natural-life imprisonment or death [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]]. The BNS stretched that to every girl under 18.

One more rung sits above. A man convicted of rape or gang rape for the second time faces natural life or death under Section 71 [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## No anticipatory bail and a two-month investigation

Anticipatory bail is protection a person asks a court for before he is arrested. Section 482(4) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) shuts that door for anyone accused of gang rape of a girl under 18, and for anyone accused of raping a girl under 16 [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Where the survivor is an adult, the bar does not apply, and the court decides each request.

The BNSS also sets a clock. Police must complete the investigation within two months of recording the information. The trial is to finish within two months of the chargesheet, and an appeal against the sentence within six months [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. The law attaches no consequence to a missed deadline, so the dates work only when someone holds the police to them. The victim is entitled to a progress update within 90 days [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

The clock starts with the FIR. A police officer who fails to record an FIR for rape faces 6 months to 2 years' rigorous imprisonment under Section 199 of the BNS [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. What goes into that FIR matters: if it names or describes one attacker and leaves out the others, the case may begin life as rape by one man.

Support does not wait for a conviction. A survivor can apply to the State or District Legal Services Authority for compensation even if the offenders are never traced [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. NALSA's 2018 scheme sets Rs 5 lakh to Rs 10 lakh for gang rape [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]].

## What the 2024 count includes

The National Crime Records Bureau recorded 1,537 gang-rape cases in 2024, counting Section 70 of the BNS and Section 376D of the IPC together. Of these, 30 involved girls under 18 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

That number is cases, not men and not survivors. It is also a floor. NCRB counts each FIR once, under the offence that carries the heaviest punishment [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Gang rapes of children are often registered under the POCSO Act, and gang rapes that end in death are counted under murder with rape or gang rape, so many of them never show up here [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

One group never appears at all. Section 70 protects women and girls only. The BNS has no counterpart to the old Section 377 of the IPC, so a group sexual assault on an adult man or a transgender person is not rape under the code [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Section 70 settles one question clearly: nobody in the group gets to hide behind the others. Everything before that point still depends on an FIR that records the whole group, an investigation that finishes and a trial that ends.
gang-rape-law-section-70-explained.hg:
Zyada tar criminal trials mein court ka pehla kaam yeh pata karna hota hai ki kisne kya kiya. Gang rape woh exception hai jo law mein hi likha hua hai. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 70 ke tahat, jab ek group kisi aurat ka rape karta hai, toh us group ka har member rape ka doshi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Group ka jo member khud rape nahi karta, us par bhi wahi charge aur wahi minimum saza hai jo rape karne walon par.

Yeh explainer batata hai ki law mein gang rape kya hai, saza kaise kaam karti hai, aur uske baad bail aur investigation ke kaun se rules lagte hain. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Law mein ek hi act: har member doshi kyun hai

Section tab lagta hai jab kisi aurat ka rape "by one or more persons constituting a group or acting in furtherance of a common intention" ho. Asli baat iske baad ke shabdon mein hai.

> "each of those persons shall be deemed to have committed the offence of rape"

"Deemed" ka matlab hai ki law har aadmi ko aise dekhta hai jaise usne khud rape kiya ho [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Prosecution ko yeh saabit karna hota hai ki aurat ka rape hua, aur accused us group ka hissa tha ya uski intention mein shamil tha. Use yeh saabit nahi karna padta ki kisne kya kiya.

Ek hypothetical sochiye. Gurugram mein chaar aadmi ek aurat ko zabardasti car mein bitha lete hain. Ek car chalata hai. Ek use bahar nikalne se rokta hai. Do uska rape karte hain. Court mein driver kehta hai ki usne toh use chhua tak nahi. Agar judge yeh maane ki chaaron ne milkar, ek shared intention se kaam kiya, toh Section 70 chaaron ko rape ka doshi maanta hai.

Is design ka ek asar yeh hai ki case is baat par nahi tikta ki survivor bataye kis aadmi ne kya kiya. Is rule ki had section ke shabdon mein hi hai: group, ya common intention. Jo aadmi sirf wahan maujood tha aur plan ka hissa nahi tha, woh group ka member nahi hai, aur prosecution ko phir bhi saabit karna hota hai ki har accused doosron ke saath milkar kaam kar raha tha.

## Bees saal se natural life tak, aur 18 se kam ke liye death

Section 70(1) mein convict hue har aadmi ko kam se kam 20 saal ki rigorous imprisonment hoti hai, jo uski baaki natural life ki qaid tak ja sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Yeh Section 64 mein rape ke 10 saal ke minimum ka dugna hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Saza aapas mein bant-ti nahi hai. Chaar convicts ka matlab hai chaar sazaayein, har ek kam se kam 20 saal ki.

Agar ladki 18 saal se kam ki hai, toh Section 70(2) court ke paas sirf do options chhodta hai: baaki natural life ki qaid, ya death [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Yeh sab ek saath nahi aaya. 20 saal ka minimum Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 ke saath aaya, jo 2012 ke Delhi gang rape case aur 23 January 2013 ki Justice J.S. Verma Committee report ke baad pass hua [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Usne yeh floor Indian Penal Code ke Section 376D mein likha aur kaha ki koi bhi fine "shall be paid to the victim" [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. 2018 mein Parliament ne 12 saal se kam ki ladki ke gang rape par baaki natural life ki qaid ya death ki saza rakhi [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]]. BNS ne ise 18 saal se kam ki har ladki tak badha diya.

Iske upar ek aur paaydaan hai. Jo aadmi rape ya gang rape mein doosri baar convict ho, use Section 71 mein baaki natural life ki qaid ya death ki saza hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Anticipatory bail nahi, aur do mahine ki investigation

Anticipatory bail woh protection hai jo koi insaan arrest hone se pehle court se maangta hai. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ka Section 482(4) yeh darwaza band kar deta hai un sab ke liye jin par 18 saal se kam ki ladki ke gang rape ka ilzaam hai, aur un ke liye bhi jin par 16 saal se kam ki ladki ke rape ka ilzaam hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Jahan survivor adult hai, wahan yeh rok nahi lagti, aur court har request par khud faisla karta hai.

BNSS ek ghadi bhi chalu karti hai. Police ko information record hone ke do mahine ke andar investigation poori karni hoti hai. Trial chargesheet ke do mahine ke andar poora hona chahiye, aur saza ke khilaaf appeal chhah mahine ke andar [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Deadline miss hone par law mein koi nateeja nahi likha hai, isliye yeh dates tabhi kaam karti hain jab koi police se jawaab maange. Victim ko 90 din ke andar progress update ka haq hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Ghadi FIR se shuru hoti hai. Jo police officer rape ki FIR record nahi karta, use BNS ke Section 199 mein 6 mahine se 2 saal ki rigorous imprisonment ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. FIR mein kya likha jaata hai, yeh maayne rakhta hai: agar usmein ek hi hamlawar ka naam ya huliya ho aur baaki chhoot jaayein, toh case ek aadmi ke rape ke roop mein shuru ho sakta hai.

Madad conviction ka intezaar nahi karti. Survivor State ya District Legal Services Authority mein compensation ke liye apply kar sakti hai, chahe offenders kabhi pakde hi na jaayein [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. NALSA ki 2018 scheme gang rape ke liye Rs 5 lakh se Rs 10 lakh tay karti hai [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]].

## 2024 ke count mein kya shamil hai

National Crime Records Bureau ne 2024 mein gang rape ke 1,537 cases record kiye, jinmein BNS ka Section 70 aur IPC ka Section 376D dono gine gaye. Inmein se 30 mein 18 saal se kam ki ladkiyan thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Yeh number cases ka hai, aadmiyon ka nahi aur survivors ka bhi nahi. Aur asli ginti isse zyada hi hogi. NCRB har FIR ko ek hi baar ginta hai, us offence ke naam par jiski saza sabse bhaari ho [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Bachchon ke gang rape aksar POCSO Act mein register hote hain, aur jo gang rape maut par khatam hote hain, woh murder with rape ya gang rape mein gine jaate hain, isliye unmein se bahut se yahan dikhte hi nahi [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Ek group toh kabhi dikhta hi nahi. Section 70 sirf aurton aur ladkiyon ko protect karta hai. BNS mein IPC ke purane Section 377 jaisa koi section nahi hai, isliye kisi adult aadmi ya transgender insaan par group ka sexual assault is code mein rape nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Section 70 ek sawaal ka saaf jawaab deta hai: group mein koi bhi doosron ke peeche nahi chhup sakta. Us mod tak pahunchne se pehle ka sab kuch ab bhi is par tika hai ki FIR poore group ko record kare, investigation poori ho aur trial khatam ho.

harassment-stalking-cases-court-backlog.en:
Imagine a 21-year-old in Indore. A former classmate waits outside her coaching centre every evening and messages her from a new number each time she blocks him. She has told him to stop, clearly, more than once. This is stalking, a crime under Section 78 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) that carries up to three years in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

If she goes to the police tonight, this is the queue she joins: at the end of 2024, 52,273 stalking cases were pending trial in India's courts, 92.8% of all those before them [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

## The numbers: more than nine in ten cases pending

Stalking is not an exception. Every offence in its family is stuck in the same place [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| Offence, 2024 | Cases pending trial at year-end | Pendency | Conviction rate in completed trials |
|---|---|---|---|
| Assault to outrage modesty | 3,17,491 | 92.3% | 20.1% |
| Sexual harassment | 1,22,888 | 93.3% | 41.9% |
| Insult to modesty | 53,210 | 92.9% | 15.4% |
| Stalking | 52,273 | 92.8% | 25.2% |
| Rape, for comparison | 1,85,785 | 89.8% | 24.4% |

Together the first four heads had more than five lakh cases waiting. Each was more backed up than rape, the offence India treats as its emergency.

The largest pile is "assault on a woman with intent to outrage her modesty", the charge commonly used for molestation. Courts completed 22,796 such trials in 2024. Police registered 48,303 new cases the same year, more than twice as many [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. For every trial that finished, about fourteen cases were left waiting.

These tables undercount. NCRB records each FIR once, under its most serious offence, so harassment that came with a graver crime is not counted here [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## No deadline: how the law ranks the 'lesser' offences

The BNS sets the punishments: one to five years for assault to outrage modesty, up to three for sexual harassment, up to three for stalking and five on a repeat, up to three for words or gestures that insult a woman's modesty [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

The procedure code then sorts cases by those numbers. For rape, the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) tells police to finish the investigation in two months and courts to finish the trial within two months of the charge-sheet [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Those deadlines are widely missed, but they exist, and a survivor can quote them. Sections 74 to 79 are on neither list.

The 779 Fast Track Special Courts running under the central scheme hear rape and POCSO cases [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]]. A stalking case waits in the ordinary criminal courts with everything else.

One more ranking is easy to miss. Section 199 of the BNS makes it a crime for a police officer to fail to record a complaint of rape, assault to outrage modesty, voyeurism or insult to modesty. Stalking and sexual harassment are not on that list [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## The 14-day wait before an FIR

Since 1 July 2024, when the BNSS came into force [[pib-mha-new-criminal-laws-2026]], there is a pause at the very start. Section 173(3) lets police hold a preliminary enquiry of up to 14 days before registering an FIR, if the offence is punishable with three years or more but less than seven and an officer of at least Deputy Superintendent rank has given permission first [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Rape, with a ten-year minimum, is outside this window. On a plain reading, stalking, most sexual harassment and assault to outrage modesty are inside it.

So our student can be told to come back in two weeks, and it may be lawful. Two weeks is long when he knows where she will be tomorrow evening.

The pause leaves no trace in the data. NCRB counts FIRs, not complaints. Registered stalking cases fell from 10,495 in 2023 to 9,865 in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]], and the tables cannot say whether fewer women were stalked, fewer complained, or fewer complaints became FIRs.

## Why delay costs most in stalking cases

Stalking is a pattern, not a single act, and the complaint is usually made while the pattern is still running. A verdict years later does nothing about tomorrow.

The law knows stalkers repeat. A second conviction carries up to five years instead of three [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. But a second conviction needs a first. With 92.8% of cases pending and a conviction in only 25.2% of the trials that finish [[ncrb-cii-2024]], the higher penalty is rarely within reach.

> A stalking complaint can be an early warning. The system files it as a low priority and answers years later.

There is a gap in who is covered, too. Stalking and sexual harassment are written as offences by a man against a woman [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. A man or a transgender person who is stalked cannot use Section 78 and has to rely on more general provisions.

## What a complainant can ask for

- **Any station, or online.** A complaint can be made at any police station, wherever the offence happened, or electronically if signed within three days. The FIR copy is free [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **A woman officer.** A woman's complaint of stalking, sexual harassment or voyeurism must be recorded by a woman officer [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **The paper behind any "enquiry".** Ask which officer approved it, on what date, and when the 14 days end. Without prior permission there is no lawful enquiry.
- **A statement before a magistrate.** In stalking and sexual harassment cases a magistrate must record the woman's statement as soon as police learn of the offence [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Updates.** Police must report progress within 90 days, and the victim must be heard before a prosecution is withdrawn [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **No character trial.** Her character and sexual history are irrelevant to consent in these prosecutions [[indiacode-bsa-2023]].

None of this shortens the queue. It makes a record, and in a system this slow the record is what survives.
harassment-stalking-cases-court-backlog.hg:
Sochiye Indore ki ek 21 saal ki ladki ke baare mein. Uska ek puraana classmate har shaam uske coaching centre ke bahar khada rehta hai, aur jab bhi woh use block karti hai, woh naye number se message karne lagta hai. Woh use ek se zyada baar saaf-saaf keh chuki hai ki ruk jao. Yeh stalking hai, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 78 ke under ek crime, jisme teen saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Agar woh aaj raat police ke paas jaati hai, toh woh is queue mein lagegi: 2024 ke end mein India ki courts mein 52,273 stalking cases trial ke liye pending the, yaani courts ke saamne ke aise sabhi cases ka 92.8% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Numbers: das mein se nau se zyada cases pending

Stalking koi exception nahi hai. Is parivaar ka har offence usi jagah atka hua hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]]:

| Offence, 2024 | Saal ke end mein trial ke liye pending cases | Pendency | Poore hue trials mein conviction rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Assault to outrage modesty | 3,17,491 | 92.3% | 20.1% |
| Sexual harassment | 1,22,888 | 93.3% | 41.9% |
| Insult to modesty | 53,210 | 92.9% | 15.4% |
| Stalking | 52,273 | 92.8% | 25.2% |
| Rape, comparison ke liye | 1,85,785 | 89.8% | 24.4% |

Pehle chaar heads ko milaakar paanch lakh se zyada cases intezaar mein the. Inme se har ek mein pendency rape se zyada thi, jabki rape woh offence hai jise India apni emergency maanta hai.

Sabse bada dher "assault on a woman with intent to outrage her modesty" ka hai, woh charge jo aam taur par molestation ke liye lagaya jaata hai. Courts ne 2024 mein aise 22,796 trials poore kiye. Usi saal police ne 48,303 naye cases register kiye, yaani dugne se bhi zyada [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Har ek poore hue trial ke peeche lagbhag chaudah cases intezaar mein reh gaye.

Yeh tables asli tasveer se kam ginti hain. NCRB har FIR ko ek hi baar ginta hai, uske sabse gambhir offence ke under, isliye jo harassment kisi bade crime ke saath hua, woh yahan gina hi nahi gaya [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Koi deadline nahi: law 'chhote' offences ko kaise rank karta hai

Saza BNS tay karti hai: assault to outrage modesty ke liye ek se paanch saal, sexual harassment ke liye teen saal tak, stalking ke liye teen saal tak aur dobara karne par paanch saal tak, aur aurat ki modesty ka apmaan karne wale shabdon ya ishaaron ke liye teen saal tak [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Phir procedure code inhi numbers ke hisaab se cases ko chhaantta hai. Rape ke liye Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) police se kehti hai ki investigation do mahine mein poori ho, aur courts se kehti hai ki trial charge-sheet ke do mahine ke andar khatam ho [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Yeh deadlines bade paimaane par miss hoti hain, lekin yeh maujood hain, aur survivor inka hawala de sakti hai. Sections 74 se 79 in dono mein se kisi list mein nahi hain.

Central scheme ke under chal rahi 779 Fast Track Special Courts rape aur POCSO ke cases sunti hain [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]]. Stalking ka case baaki sab cases ke saath aam criminal courts mein intezaar karta hai.

Ek aur ranking aasaani se nazar se chhoot jaati hai. BNS ka Section 199 kehta hai ki agar police officer rape, assault to outrage modesty, voyeurism ya insult to modesty ki complaint record nahi karta, toh yeh crime hai. Stalking aur sexual harassment us list mein nahi hain [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## FIR se pehle 14 din ka intezaar

1 July 2024 se, jab BNSS laagu hui [[pib-mha-new-criminal-laws-2026]], bilkul shuruaat mein hi ek pause aa gaya hai. Section 173(3) police ko FIR register karne se pehle 14 din tak ki preliminary enquiry karne deta hai, agar offence ki saza teen saal ya usse zyada lekin saat saal se kam hai aur kam se kam Deputy Superintendent rank ke officer ne pehle se permission di hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Rape, jisme minimum das saal ki saza hai, is window ke bahar hai. Seedhe-seedhe padhein toh stalking, zyada tar sexual harassment aur assault to outrage modesty iske andar aate hain.

Toh hamari student se kaha ja sakta hai ki do hafte baad aana, aur ho sakta hai yeh lawful ho. Do hafte bahut lamba waqt hai jab stalker ko pata hai ki woh kal shaam kahan hogi.

Yeh pause data mein koi nishaan nahi chhodta. NCRB FIRs ginta hai, complaints nahi. Register hue stalking cases 2023 mein 10,495 se ghatkar 2024 mein 9,865 ho gaye [[ncrb-cii-2024]], aur tables yeh nahi bata sakti ki kam auraton ko stalk kiya gaya, kam ne complaint ki, ya kam complaints FIR bani.

## Stalking ke cases mein deri sabse mehngi kyun padti hai

Stalking ek akela act nahi, ek pattern hai, aur complaint aksar tab hoti hai jab pattern abhi chal hi raha hota hai. Saalon baad aaya faisla kal ke baare mein kuch nahi karta.

Law jaanta hai ki stalkers dobara karte hain. Doosre conviction par teen ki jagah paanch saal tak ki saza hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Lekin doosre conviction ke liye pehla conviction chahiye. Jab 92.8% cases pending hain aur poore hue trials mein se sirf 25.2% mein conviction hota hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]], toh yeh badi saza shayad hi kabhi kisi tak pahunch paati hai.

> Stalking ki complaint ek early warning ho sakti hai. System use low priority maan kar file kar deta hai aur jawaab saalon baad deta hai.

Ek gap is baat mein bhi hai ki law kise cover karta hai. Stalking aur sexual harassment aise offences ke roop mein likhe gaye hain jo ek aadmi ek aurat ke khilaaf karta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Jis aadmi ya transgender person ko stalk kiya ja raha hai, woh Section 78 ka istemaal nahi kar sakta aur use zyada general provisions ka sahaara lena padta hai.

## Complainant kya maang sakti hai

- **Koi bhi station, ya online.** Complaint kisi bhi police station mein ki ja sakti hai, chahe offence kahin bhi hua ho, ya electronically, agar teen din ke andar sign kar di jaaye. FIR ki copy free milti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Woman officer.** Stalking, sexual harassment ya voyeurism ki aurat ki complaint woman officer ko record karni hoti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **"Enquiry" ke peeche ka kaagaz.** Poochiye ki kis officer ne ise approve kiya, kis date ko, aur 14 din kab khatam honge. Pehle se permission ke bina koi lawful enquiry nahi hoti.
- **Magistrate ke saamne statement.** Stalking aur sexual harassment ke cases mein, jaise hi police ko offence ka pata chale, magistrate ko aurat ka statement record karna hota hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Updates.** Police ko 90 din ke andar progress batani hoti hai, aur prosecution wapas lene se pehle victim ko suna jaana zaroori hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Character ka trial nahi.** In prosecutions mein uska character aur sexual history consent ke sawaal par irrelevant hai [[indiacode-bsa-2023]].

Inme se koi bhi cheez queue ko chhota nahi karti. Yeh ek record banati hai, aur itne dheeme system mein record hi woh cheez hai jo bachi rehti hai.

high-court-rulings-supreme-court-reverse.en:
A touch over a child's clothes was not sexual assault. A man accused of sexual assault could have bail if he asked the complainant to tie a rakhi on him. Privately viewing or storing child sexual abuse material was no crime. Each was a High Court's reading of the law, and each stood until the Supreme Court set it aside [[barandbench-satish-2021]] [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]] [[sc-handbook-child-rights-2025]]. No correction was automatic: someone had to carry each order to the top court.

## Five rulings, one pattern

| High Court | Its order | Supreme Court |
|---|---|---|
| Bombay, January 2021 | Touching a child over clothes is not sexual assault | Set aside, 18 November 2021 |
| A High Court, Madhya Pradesh case | Bail if the accused asks the complainant to tie a rakhi | Struck down, 18 March 2021 |
| Madras, 11 January 2024 | Case over stored child sexual abuse material quashed | Overturned, 23 September 2024 |
| Allahabad, with the trial court | Alleged honour killing tried as a lesser offence | Set aside, April 2025 |
| A High Court, child's case | Attempt-to-rape charges cut to lesser offences | Taken up on its own; judgment 10 February 2026 |

The fourth is a killing, not a sexual offence; the mistake is the same. The five show three habits: reading a protective law so narrowly that the offence disappears, treating a complainant's safety as negotiable, and cutting a charge down before trial.

Who brought them? The skin-to-skin appeal was brought by the Attorney General for India: the government's top law officer challenged the ruling himself [[barandbench-satish-2021]]. The rakhi order reached the Court as Aparna Bhat v. State of Madhya Pradesh [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. A child-rights alliance appealed over the abuse material [[sc-handbook-child-rights-2025]]. The 2026 case had no appellant: the Court took it up on its own [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]].

## Reading the law too narrowly: skin-to-skin and 'only viewing'

In January 2021 the Bombay High Court held that touching a child over her clothes was not "sexual assault" under Section 7 of the POCSO Act: there was no skin-to-skin contact. On 18 November 2021 the Supreme Court answered: "The important ingredient for constituting the offence of sexual assault under POCSO is sexual intent and not skin to skin contact with the child" [[barandbench-satish-2021]].

Three years later the Madras High Court made the same move. On 11 January 2024 it quashed a case against a person found with child sexual abuse material, reasoning that privately viewing or storing it was no crime. On 23 September 2024 the Supreme Court called that an "egregious error" and restored the case [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]: viewing, possessing and storing such material are crimes under Section 15 of the POCSO Act read with Section 67B of the IT Act [[sc-handbook-child-rights-2025]]. The ruling convicted no one; it sent the case to trial.

## Bail that brings the accused to her door: the rakhi order

The rakhi order did not misread a section. It misread the complainant. The High Court gave bail to a man accused of sexual assault on condition that he visit her house and request her "to tie the Rakhi band to him" [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. It asked a woman who had gone to the police to receive the man she had accused at her own door.

On 18 March 2021 the Supreme Court struck the condition down and wrote rules for every court: "Bail conditions should not mandate, require or permit contact between the accused and the victim." Courts must not suggest compromise or marriage, and must avoid stereotyped, patriarchal ideas about women [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]].

The ruling names the habit it targets: treating a sexual offence as a quarrel that a compromise, or a wedding, can settle.

## Charges cut down: an honour killing and an attempt to rape

The third habit works before a trial starts, because the charge decides what a court will try.

In April 2025 the Supreme Court set aside orders of a trial court and the Allahabad High Court that had let an alleged honour killing in Uttar Pradesh be tried as culpable homicide instead of murder. It called this "a clear case of honour killing" and ordered a murder charge [[barandbench-honour-killing-lesser-charge-2025]].

On 10 February 2026 it ruled in a case it had taken up on its own, over a High Court order that had reduced the charges in a child sexual assault case from attempt to rape to lesser offences. The bench, led by Chief Justice Surya Kant, said the efforts to sensitise judges "have not borne the fruit that was expected" [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]].

## Training judges: the 2023 handbook and the 2026 committee

In March 2021 the Supreme Court ordered gender-sensitisation training for every judge [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. On 16 August 2023 it released a Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes, which states: "Marriage is not a remedy to the violence of rape" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. In February 2026 it asked an expert committee of the National Judicial Academy to draft guidelines on sensitivity in sexual-offence cases [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]].

A handbook can change a judge's vocabulary. Guidelines can list bail conditions a court must never impose. Neither can do what corrected all five orders: put them before a higher court. Nor is the top court always right: in 1978 it acquitted two policemen accused of raping a minor girl in a police station, reversing their conviction by the Bombay High Court [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]]. Protests over that acquittal led Parliament to amend the rape law in 1983 [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

At the end of 2024, 2,86,903 POCSO cases and 1,85,785 rape cases were pending trial [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Consider a hypothetical family: a 14-year-old in a district town whose case has just had its main charge cut. To challenge the order her parents need a lawyer and a hearing in a High Court that may be hours away. An order nobody appeals stays the law for that family, and no statistic records it.

This is general information, not legal advice. But a wrong order is not the last word: it can be challenged in a higher court, and free lawyers are available through the legal services authorities [[nalsa]]. The test of the committee's guidelines will be the courtrooms nobody appeals from.
high-court-rulings-supreme-court-reverse.hg:
Bachche ko kapdon ke upar se chhuna sexual assault nahi tha. Sexual assault ke accused ko bail mil sakti thi, bas woh complainant se rakhi bandhwa le. Child sexual abuse material ko akele mein dekhna ya store karna koi crime nahi tha. Teeno baar yeh kisi High Court ki law ki reading thi, aur har reading tab tak chali jab tak Supreme Court ne use palat nahi diya [[barandbench-satish-2021]] [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]] [[sc-handbook-child-rights-2025]]. Koi bhi sudhaar apne aap nahi hua: har order ko kisi na kisi ko top court tak le jaana pada.

## Paanch faisle, ek pattern

| High Court | Uska order | Supreme Court |
|---|---|---|
| Bombay, January 2021 | Bachche ko kapdon ke upar se chhuna sexual assault nahi | Set aside, 18 November 2021 |
| Ek High Court, Madhya Pradesh ka case | Bail tab, jab accused complainant se rakhi bandhwaye | Struck down, 18 March 2021 |
| Madras, 11 January 2024 | Store kiye gaye child sexual abuse material ka case quash | Palat diya, 23 September 2024 |
| Allahabad, trial court ke saath | Alleged honour killing ka trial halke offence mein | Set aside, April 2025 |
| Ek High Court, bachche ka case | Attempt-to-rape ke charges kaatkar halke offences | Khud case uthaya; judgment 10 February 2026 |

Chautha case ek hatya ka hai, sexual offence ka nahi; lekin galti wahi hai. Paanchon mein teen aadatein dikhti hain: protect karne wale law ko itna tang padhna ki offence hi gayab ho jaaye, complainant ki safety ko mol-bhaav ki cheez samajhna, aur trial shuru hone se pehle hi charge kaat dena.

Inhe Supreme Court tak laaya kaun? Skin-to-skin wali appeal Attorney General for India ne ki thi: sarkar ke sabse bade law officer ne khud is faisle ko challenge kiya [[barandbench-satish-2021]]. Rakhi wala order Aparna Bhat v. State of Madhya Pradesh ke naam se Court tak pahuncha [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. Abuse material wale case mein appeal ek child-rights alliance ne ki [[sc-handbook-child-rights-2025]]. 2026 wale case mein koi appellant tha hi nahi: Court ne use khud uthaya [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]].

## Law ko bahut tang padhna: skin-to-skin aur 'sirf dekhna'

January 2021 mein Bombay High Court ne kaha ki bachchi ko kapdon ke upar se chhuna POCSO Act ke Section 7 ka "sexual assault" nahi hai, kyunki skin-to-skin contact nahi hua. 18 November 2021 ko Supreme Court ne jawab diya: "The important ingredient for constituting the offence of sexual assault under POCSO is sexual intent and not skin to skin contact with the child", yaani POCSO mein sexual assault ke liye zaroori cheez sexual intent hai, bachche ki skin se seedha contact nahi [[barandbench-satish-2021]].

Teen saal baad Madras High Court ne wahi kiya. 11 January 2024 ko usne ek aise shakhs ke khilaaf case quash kar diya jiske paas child sexual abuse material mila tha, is tark par ki ise akele mein dekhna ya store karna crime nahi hai. 23 September 2024 ko Supreme Court ne ise "egregious error", yaani behad gambhir galti, kaha aur case bahaal kar diya [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]: aisa material dekhna, apne paas rakhna aur store karna, POCSO Act ke Section 15 aur IT Act ke Section 67B ko saath padhne par, crime hai [[sc-handbook-child-rights-2025]]. Is faisle ne kisi ko convict nahi kiya; case ko trial ke liye wapas bheja.

## Bail jo accused ko complainant ke darwaaze tak le aayi: rakhi wala order

Rakhi wale order ne koi section galat nahi padha. Usne complainant ko galat padha. High Court ne sexual assault ke ek accused ko is shart par bail di ki woh complainant ke ghar jaaye aur usse request kare "to tie the Rakhi band to him", yaani complainant use rakhi baandhe [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. Jo aurat police ke paas gayi thi, usse kaha gaya ki jis aadmi par usne aarop lagaya hai, use apne hi darwaaze par aane de.

18 March 2021 ko Supreme Court ne yeh shart radd kar di aur har court ke liye rules likhe: "Bail conditions should not mandate, require or permit contact between the accused and the victim", yaani bail ki koi shart accused aur victim ke beech contact na maange, na uski ijaazat de. Courts compromise ya shaadi ka sujhaav nahi dengi, aur auraton ke baare mein stereotyped, patriarchal soch se bachengi [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]].

Yeh faisla us aadat ka naam leta hai jise woh rokna chahta hai: sexual offence ko aisa jhagda maan lena jise compromise ya shaadi se 'settle' kiya ja sake.

## Charge kaat dena: ek honour killing aur ek attempt to rape

Teesri aadat trial shuru hone se pehle kaam karti hai, kyunki charge hi tay karta hai ki court kis cheez ka trial karegi.

April 2025 mein Supreme Court ne ek trial court aur Allahabad High Court ke woh orders set aside kiye jinki wajah se Uttar Pradesh ki ek alleged honour killing ka trial murder ki jagah culpable homicide mein chal raha tha. Court ne ise "a clear case of honour killing" kaha aur murder ka charge lagane ka order diya [[barandbench-honour-killing-lesser-charge-2025]].

10 February 2026 ko usne ek aise case mein faisla diya jo usne khud uthaya tha. Maamla ek High Court order ka tha, jisne ek bachche ke sexual assault case mein charges ko attempt to rape se ghatakar halke offences kar diya tha. Chief Justice Surya Kant ki bench ne kaha ki judges ko sensitise karne ki koshishein "have not borne the fruit that was expected", yaani unka woh nateeja nahi nikla jiski ummeed thi [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]].

## Judges ki training: 2023 ki handbook aur 2026 ki committee

March 2021 mein Supreme Court ne har judge ke liye gender-sensitisation training ka order diya [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. 16 August 2023 ko usne Handbook on Combating Gender Stereotypes jaari ki, jo saaf kehti hai: "Marriage is not a remedy to the violence of rape", yaani shaadi rape ki hinsa ka ilaaj nahi hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. February 2026 mein usne National Judicial Academy ki ek expert committee se kaha ki sexual-offence cases mein sensitivity par guidelines draft kare [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]].

Handbook judge ki bhasha badal sakti hai. Guidelines un bail conditions ki list bana sakti hain jo koi court kabhi na lagaye. Lekin dono mein se koi woh kaam nahi kar sakti jisse yeh paanchon orders theek hue: unhe higher court ke saamne rakhna. Aur top court bhi hamesha sahi nahi hota: 1978 mein usne do policewalon ko bari kar diya tha, jin par police station ke andar ek minor ladki ke rape ka aarop tha, aur Bombay High Court ka diya conviction palat diya [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]]. Us acquittal ke khilaaf hue protests ke baad Parliament ne 1983 mein rape law badla [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

2024 ke end mein 2,86,903 POCSO cases aur 1,85,785 rape cases trial mein pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Ek kaalpanik parivaar ko sochiye: kisi district town ki 14 saal ki ladki, jiske case ka main charge abhi-abhi kaat diya gaya hai. Us order ko challenge karne ke liye uske maa-baap ko ek lawyer chahiye aur ek aise High Court mein hearing, jo ghanton door ho sakta hai. Jis order ke khilaaf koi appeal nahi karta, woh us parivaar ke liye law bana rehta hai, aur kisi statistic mein darj nahi hota.

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi. Lekin galat order aakhri baat nahi hota: use higher court mein challenge kiya ja sakta hai, aur legal services authorities ke zariye free lawyer mil sakta hai [[nalsa]]. Committee ki guidelines ka asli test un courtrooms mein hoga jahan se koi appeal karne nahi jaata.

how-to-read-a-rape-verdict.en:
On the day a sexual-violence verdict comes out, your phone fills with one word. "Convicted." "Acquitted." "Justice." But a criminal judgment is not one word. It is a list: each accused, each charge, a finding on each, and a sentence for each finding. Read only the headline and you can come away believing the opposite of what the court decided. This is general information, not legal advice.

## The parts of a judgment: charges, findings, sentence

A trial court judgment usually arrives in two pieces. First comes the judgment on guilt, which ends in an operative part listing who is convicted or acquitted under which section. The sentence comes afterwards, sometimes the same day and sometimes days later, after the court hears both sides on punishment.

So ask three questions of every verdict. Which sections was each person charged under? Which of those did the court find proved, and which not proved? And what sentence followed each conviction?

The context matters too. In India, most rape trials do not end in a conviction at all. In 2024 courts convicted in 5,032 rape cases and acquitted in 13,980, a conviction rate of 24.4% of the 20,587 trials completed [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A conviction is the exception, which is why its details deserve careful reading.

| Word | What it means |
|---|---|
| Convicted under Section X | Guilt proved for that offence only |
| Acquitted | The prosecution did not prove the charge beyond reasonable doubt |
| Not proved | That charge failed, even if others succeeded |
| In camera | The trial was closed to the public |
| Natural life | Prison for the rest of the convict's life |

## Kathua: one verdict, three kinds of guilt

An eight-year-old girl was raped and murdered in Kathua in 2018. The Supreme Court moved the trial out of Jammu and Kashmir to Pathankot in Punjab and ordered it held in camera, day to day [[theprint-kathua-transfer-2018]].

On 10 June 2019 the Pathankot court convicted six of the seven accused [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]]. "Six convicted" hides three different findings. Three men got life imprisonment for murder, along with 25 years for gang rape. Three policemen got five years each, not for the rape or the murder, but for destroying evidence. One accused was acquitted [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]].

Read correctly, the verdict says two things. Some men committed the crime. And officers whose job was to protect the evidence worked to destroy it. That second finding is a story about policing, and it disappears when the verdict is reported as "six convicted".

## Hathras: convicted, but not of rape

A 19-year-old Dalit woman in Hathras was assaulted on 14 September 2020, died on 29 September, and was cremated by police in the middle of the night without her family's consent. In December 2020 the CBI charged four men with rape, gang rape and murder [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]].

On 2 March 2023 a special SC/ST court acquitted three of the four. It convicted one man of culpable homicide not amounting to murder, under Section 304 of the IPC, and of offences under the SC/ST Act. None of the four was found guilty of gang rape or murder [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]]. He was sentenced to life imprisonment and a Rs 50,000 fine, Rs 40,000 of it for the woman's mother, and the court held that the prosecution had failed to prove rape [[theprint-hathras-verdict-2023]].

"Man convicted in Hathras case, gets life" is true. It also hides the finding that mattered most to the charge sheet. "Not proved" is not the same as "did not happen". It is a statement about what the evidence in that courtroom could establish to the criminal standard, and evidence is shaped from the first hours of a case.

## RG Kar: three sections, one sentence

A trainee doctor was raped and murdered at RG Kar Medical College and Hospital in Kolkata on 9 August 2024. On 20 January 2025 a Sealdah court sentenced the convicted man under three sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita: 64, 66 and 103(1) [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]].

Each number is a separate finding. Section 64 is rape, with at least 10 years and up to life [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Section 66 applies when a rapist causes the woman's death, and allows at least 20 years, imprisonment for the rest of natural life, or death [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Section 103(1) is murder.

The CBI asked for death. The judge refused, holding that the crime did not fall in the "rarest of the rare" category, and imposed life imprisonment for the rest of his natural life, a Rs 50,000 fine and Rs 17 lakh to be paid by the state to the family [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. "Natural life" means he is not released after a fixed term. On 7 February 2025 the Calcutta High Court dismissed the state government's appeal for death, leaving the CBI to pursue its own appeal [[barandbench-rg-kar-hc-2025]]. A trial court sentence is often not the last word.

## Sharing a verdict without naming the survivor

Rape and POCSO trials are held in camera, and nothing about the proceedings may be published without the court's permission [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Publishing the name of a rape survivor, or any detail that could identify her, is a crime under Section 72 of the BNS, punishable with up to two years in prison, unless she authorises it in writing; Section 73 sets the same maximum for publishing court proceedings without permission [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

The Supreme Court has gone further: no one may disclose, "even in a remote manner", facts that could lead to her being identified [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. That covers her photo, her village, her school, her hospital ward and her family's names. It applies even when the name is already trending.

So when you share a verdict, share the part that teaches: the sections, the findings, the sentence, and what failed. Name the case by its place and year. The survivor's identity adds nothing to anyone's understanding of the judgment, and it was never anyone else's to give away.
how-to-read-a-rape-verdict.hg:
Jis din kisi sexual-violence case ka verdict aata hai, tumhara phone ek hi shabd se bhar jaata hai. "Convicted." "Acquitted." "Justice." Lekin criminal judgment ek shabd nahi hota. Woh ek list hota hai: har accused, har charge, har charge pe ek finding, aur har finding ke liye ek saza. Sirf headline padhoge toh ho sakta hai tum court ke faisle ka bilkul ulta samajh lo. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Judgment ke hisse: charges, findings, saza

Trial court ka judgment aksar do hisson mein aata hai. Pehle guilt pe judgment aata hai, jo ek operative part pe khatam hota hai, jisme likha hota hai ki kaun kis section mein convict ya acquit hua. Saza uske baad aati hai, kabhi usi din aur kabhi kuch din baad, jab court punishment pe dono sides ko sun leta hai.

Toh har verdict se teen sawaal poocho. Har insaan pe kin sections mein charge laga tha? Unme se court ne kaunse saabit maane aur kaunse nahi? Aur har conviction ke baad kya saza mili?

Context bhi matter karta hai. India mein zyada tar rape trials conviction pe khatam hi nahi hote. 2024 mein courts ne 5,032 rape cases mein convict kiya aur 13,980 mein acquit, yaani 20,587 poore hue trials mein conviction rate 24.4% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Conviction exception hai, isliye uski details dhyan se padhni chahiye.

| Shabd | Matlab |
|---|---|
| Section X mein convicted | Sirf usi offence ka guilt saabit hua |
| Acquitted | Prosecution charge ko reasonable doubt se pare saabit nahi kar paaya |
| Not proved | Woh charge fail hua, chahe baaki charges saabit hue hon |
| In camera | Trial public ke liye band tha |
| Natural life | Convict ki baaki poori zindagi jail |

## Kathua: ek verdict, teen tarah ka guilt

2018 mein Kathua mein ek aath saal ki bachchi ka rape aur murder hua. Supreme Court ne trial Jammu and Kashmir se bahar Punjab ke Pathankot mein bhej diya aur order diya ki woh in camera, roz ke roz chale [[theprint-kathua-transfer-2018]].

10 June 2019 ko Pathankot court ne saat mein se chhe accused ko convict kiya [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]]. "Chhe convicted" teen alag findings ko chhupa deta hai. Teen aadmiyon ko murder ke liye life imprisonment mili, saath mein gang rape ke liye 25 saal. Teen policemen ko paanch-paanch saal mile, rape ya murder ke liye nahi, balki evidence mitaane ke liye. Ek accused acquit hua [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]].

Sahi se padho toh verdict do baatein kehta hai. Kuch aadmiyon ne crime kiya. Aur jin officers ka kaam evidence bachaana tha, unhone use mitaane ka kaam kiya. Yeh doosri finding policing ki kahani hai, aur jab verdict ko sirf "chhe convicted" bataya jaata hai, toh yeh gayab ho jaati hai.

## Hathras: convicted, lekin rape ke liye nahi

Hathras ki ek 19 saal ki Dalit young woman pe 14 September 2020 ko hamla hua, 29 September ko uski maut hui, aur police ne uski family ki consent ke bina aadhi raat ko uska antim sanskar kar diya. December 2020 mein CBI ne chaar aadmiyon pe rape, gang rape aur murder ke charges lagaye [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]].

2 March 2023 ko ek special SC/ST court ne chaar mein se teen ko acquit kar diya. Ek aadmi ko IPC ke Section 304 mein culpable homicide not amounting to murder aur SC/ST Act ke offences mein convict kiya. Chaaron mein se koi bhi gang rape ya murder ka doshi nahi paaya gaya [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]]. Use life imprisonment aur Rs 50,000 ka fine mila, jisme se Rs 40,000 woman ki maa ke liye the, aur court ne kaha ki prosecution rape saabit nahi kar paaya [[theprint-hathras-verdict-2023]].

"Hathras case mein aadmi convict, life mili" sach hai. Lekin yeh us finding ko chhupa deta hai jo charge sheet ke liye sabse zaroori thi. "Saabit nahi hua" ka matlab "hua hi nahi" nahi hota. Yeh is baare mein ek statement hai ki us courtroom ka evidence criminal standard tak kya establish kar paaya, aur evidence case ke pehle ghanton se hi shape hone lagta hai.

## RG Kar: teen sections, ek saza

9 August 2024 ko Kolkata ke RG Kar Medical College and Hospital mein ek trainee doctor ka rape aur murder hua. 20 January 2025 ko Sealdah court ne convict hue aadmi ko Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ke teen sections mein saza di: 64, 66 aur 103(1) [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]].

Har number ek alag finding hai. Section 64 rape hai, jisme kam se kam 10 saal aur zyada se zyada life ki saza hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Section 66 tab lagta hai jab rapist woman ki maut ka kaaran bane, aur isme kam se kam 20 saal, baaki natural life tak jail, ya death ki saza ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Section 103(1) murder hai.

CBI ne death maangi. Judge ne mana kar diya, yeh kehkar ki crime "rarest of the rare" category mein nahi aata, aur baaki natural life ke liye life imprisonment, Rs 50,000 ka fine, aur state ki taraf se family ko Rs 17 lakh dene ka order diya [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. "Natural life" ka matlab hai ki use kisi fixed term ke baad nahi chhoda jaayega. 7 February 2025 ko Calcutta High Court ne death ke liye state government ki appeal khaarij kar di, aur CBI ko apni appeal ladne ke liye chhod diya [[barandbench-rg-kar-hc-2025]]. Trial court ki saza aksar aakhri shabd nahi hoti.

## Survivor ka naam liye bina verdict share karna

Rape aur POCSO trials in camera hote hain, aur court ki permission ke bina proceedings ke baare mein kuch bhi publish nahi kiya ja sakta [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Rape survivor ka naam, ya koi bhi detail jisse uski pehchaan ho sake, publish karna BNS ke Section 72 mein crime hai, jisme do saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai, jab tak survivor khud likhit mein permission na de; Section 73 bina permission court proceedings publish karne pe bhi utni hi maximum saza rakhta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Supreme Court isse bhi aage gaya hai: koi bhi "even in a remote manner", yaani door se bhi, aise facts nahi bata sakta jinse uski pehchaan ho jaaye [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Isme uski photo, uska gaon, uska school, uska hospital ward aur uski family ke naam sab aate hain. Yeh tab bhi laagu hai jab naam already trend kar raha ho.

Toh jab verdict share karo, woh hissa share karo jo kuch sikhata hai: sections, findings, saza, aur kya fail hua. Case ko uski jagah aur saal se bulao. Survivor ki pehchaan se judgment ko samajhne mein kisi ko koi madad nahi milti, aur woh kabhi kisi aur ki thi hi nahi jo use de diya jaaye.

intent-in-indian-sexual-offence-law.en:
A hand on a woman's shoulder on a crowded bus can be an accident. The same hand, held there, with a look and a remark, can be a crime punishable with up to five years. The act looks almost the same. What separates them in Indian law is a word that appears again and again in sexual-offence sections: intent. To convict, a court often has to decide not only what the accused did, but what he meant by it. This explainer is general information, not legal advice.

## Why the law asks what he meant

Criminal law punishes guilty minds, not only harmful acts. For some sexual offences, the act itself shows the purpose; for many others, the section names a specific intention or knowledge, and the prosecution must prove it beyond reasonable doubt.

Nobody can open a mind, so courts read conduct: what the accused said before, whether he chose a moment when the woman was alone, whether he repeated it, what he did after, what he wrote in messages. Intent is almost always proved this way, from circumstances.

That requirement protects people from being convicted for genuine accidents. It also gives defence lawyers a door to push on: "he did not mean it". How wide courts open that door decides whether the law works.

## Intent to outrage modesty: Section 74

The best-known intent-based sexual offence in India is assault or criminal force on a woman "with intent to outrage her modesty", now Section 74 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), earlier Section 354 IPC. It carries one to five years in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Police registered 48,303 such cases in 2024, a rate of 7.1 per lakh women [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

That 2024 count is a narrower category than in older reports, because sexual harassment, disrobing, voyeurism and stalking are now counted separately [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. So it cannot be compared with older headline figures.

The phrase itself is old-fashioned. It speaks of a woman's "modesty" rather than her body, her consent or her dignity, and it protects only women. A man or a transgender person groped on the same bus is not covered by it. Words and gestures meant to insult a woman's modesty are a separate offence under Section 79, with up to three years [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Knowing her caste: the Atrocities Act's sexual offences

Since the 2015 amendment to the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, Section 3(1)(w) makes it a specific atrocity to intentionally touch a Dalit or Adivasi woman in a sexual manner without her consent, or to use sexual words, acts or gestures towards her, knowing that she belongs to a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe. The punishment is six months to five years and a fine [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

Here the law asks for two mental elements: the touching must be intentional, and the accused must know her caste or tribe. In a village where everyone knows everyone's family, that knowledge is often obvious from the facts. In a city, the defence may argue he did not know. The requirement ties the offence to caste-based sexual violence, but it also means police must record, from the start, how the accused knew who she was.

## No intention to marry: Section 69

Section 69 of the BNS created a new offence: sex obtained by "deceitful means" or by a promise of marriage made "without any intention of fulfilling the same", including a false promise of a job or promotion, or marrying while hiding one's identity. It carries up to 10 years [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Everything turns on intent at the moment of the promise. A relationship that ends, or a promise that later becomes impossible, is not this crime. A promise that was never meant to be kept is. Consider a woman in Indore who was promised marriage for two years and then learned he was engaged to someone else all along. Her messages, and when the engagement was fixed, become the evidence of what he meant on day one.

## Children: sexual intent over skin contact, and stored abuse material

The most damaging misreading came in a child case. In January 2021 the Bombay High Court held that touching a child over her clothes was not "sexual assault" under the POCSO Act because there was no skin-to-skin contact. On 18 November 2021 the Supreme Court set that aside, holding that "the important ingredient for constituting the offence of sexual assault under POCSO is sexual intent and not skin to skin contact with the child" [[barandbench-satish-2021]]. Intent, read properly, widened the protection back to where Parliament had put it.

The same logic applies to child sexual abuse material. On 23 September 2024, in the Just Rights for Children Alliance case, the Supreme Court held that storing or possessing such material is itself an offence under Section 15 of POCSO when the circumstances show the intent the law specifies, even if it is never shared. It set aside a Madras High Court ruling of 11 January 2024, calling it an "egregious error" [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. One of the three offences in Section 15, for instance, covers failing to delete, destroy or report such material with intent to share it.

The lesson across all these sections is the same. Intent is not a loophole if police and prosecutors collect the conduct that proves it, and courts read it as the law means it. For survivors, the details that seem small, the message, the timing, what he said after, are often what the case is built on.
intent-in-indian-sexual-offence-law.hg:
Bheed wali bus mein kisi aurat ke kandhe par haath galti se bhi lag sakta hai. Wahi haath, wahin tika hua, ek nazar aur ek comment ke saath, aisa crime ban sakta hai jiski saza paanch saal tak hai. Kaam lagbhag ek jaisa dikhta hai. Indian law mein dono ko alag karta hai ek shabd jo sexual-offence sections mein baar-baar aata hai: intent, yaani niyat. Convict karne ke liye court ko aksar sirf yeh nahi dekhna padta ki accused ne kya kiya, balki yeh bhi ki uska matlab kya tha. Yeh explainer general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Law yeh kyun poochta hai ki uska matlab kya tha

Criminal law sirf nuksaan wale kaam ko nahi, doshi mann ko saza deta hai. Kuch sexual offences mein kaam khud hi maqsad dikha deta hai; lekin kai doosre sections mein ek khaas iraada ya jaankari likhi hoti hai, aur prosecution ko use reasonable doubt se aage saabit karna padta hai.

Mann koi khol kar nahi dekh sakta, isliye courts bartaav padhti hain: accused ne pehle kya kaha, kya usne woh waqt chuna jab aurat akeli thi, kya usne yeh dohraaya, baad mein kya kiya, messages mein kya likha. Intent lagbhag hamesha isi tarah, haalaat se, saabit hota hai.

Yeh shart logon ko sachchi galti ke liye saza se bachati hai. Lekin isse defence lawyers ko dhakka dene ke liye ek darwaza bhi milta hai: "uska yeh matlab nahi tha". Courts woh darwaza kitna kholti hain, isi se tay hota hai ki law kaam karta hai ya nahi.

## Modesty outrage karne ka iraada: Section 74

India mein sabse jaana-maana intent-based sexual offence hai kisi aurat par "uski modesty outrage karne ke iraade se" assault ya criminal force, jo ab Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ka Section 74 hai, pehle IPC ka Section 354. Iski saza ek se paanch saal ki jail hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Police ne 2024 mein aise 48,303 cases darj kiye, yaani har lakh aurton par 7.1 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

2024 ka yeh count purani reports se patli category hai, kyunki sexual harassment, kapde utaarne ki koshish, voyeurism aur stalking ab alag gine jaate hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Isliye ise purane headline figures se compare nahi kiya ja sakta.

Yeh phrase khud purane zamaane ka hai. Yeh aurat ke shareer, uski consent ya uski izzat ki jagah uski "modesty" ki baat karta hai, aur sirf aurton ko protect karta hai. Usi bus mein jis aadmi ya transgender insaan ko galat tareeke se chhua jaaye, woh is section ke daayre mein nahi aata. Aurat ki modesty ka apmaan karne ke iraade se kahe gaye shabd aur ishaare Section 79 ke tahat alag offence hain, teen saal tak ki saza ke saath [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Uski caste jaanna: Atrocities Act ke sexual offences

SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act mein 2015 ke amendment ke baad, Section 3(1)(w) ke tahat kisi Dalit ya Adivasi aurat ko uski consent ke bina jaan-boojh kar sexual tareeke se chhoona, ya uske saath sexual shabd, harkatein ya ishaare karna, yeh jaante hue ki woh Scheduled Caste ya Scheduled Tribe se hai, ek khaas atrocity hai. Saza chhe mahine se paanch saal aur jurmana hai [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

Yahan law do mental elements maangta hai: chhoona jaan-boojh kar ho, aur accused ko uski caste ya tribe pata ho. Jis gaon mein sab ek doosre ke parivaar ko jaante hain, wahan yeh jaankari facts se aksar saaf hoti hai. Shehar mein defence keh sakta hai ki use pata hi nahi tha. Yeh shart offence ko caste par aadharit sexual violence se jodti hai, lekin iska matlab yeh bhi hai ki police ko shuru se record karna chahiye ki accused ko kaise pata tha ki woh kaun hai.

## Shaadi ka iraada hi nahi tha: Section 69

BNS ke Section 69 ne ek naya offence banaya: "deceitful means" se, yaani dhokhe se, ya shaadi ka aisa vaada karke sex jise "nibhaane ka koi iraada nahi tha", jisme naukri ya promotion ka jhootha vaada, ya apni pehchaan chhupa kar shaadi karna bhi shaamil hai. Iski saza 10 saal tak hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Sab kuch vaade ke waqt ki niyat par tika hai. Ek rishta jo toot jaaye, ya ek vaada jo baad mein poora karna mumkin na rahe, yeh crime nahi hai. Ek vaada jo kabhi nibhaane ke liye kiya hi nahi gaya, woh hai. Sochiye Indore ki ek aurat ko do saal tak shaadi ka vaada kiya gaya, aur phir pata chala ki woh poore waqt kisi aur se engaged tha. Uske messages, aur engagement kab tay hui, yahi saboot bante hain ki pehle din uska matlab kya tha.

## Bachche: skin contact se zyada sexual intent, aur store kiya gaya abuse material

Sabse nuksaandeh galat reading ek bachche ke case mein aayi. January 2021 mein Bombay High Court ne kaha ki kapdon ke upar se bachchi ko chhoona POCSO Act ke tahat "sexual assault" nahi hai, kyunki skin-to-skin contact nahi hua. 18 November 2021 ko Supreme Court ne yeh faisla palat diya aur kaha ki "the important ingredient for constituting the offence of sexual assault under POCSO is sexual intent and not skin to skin contact with the child" [[barandbench-satish-2021]]. Intent ko sahi padha gaya, toh protection wahin wapas pahunchi jahan Parliament ne use rakha tha.

Yahi logic child sexual abuse material par bhi lagta hai. 23 September 2024 ko Just Rights for Children Alliance case mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki aisa material store karna ya rakhna apne aap mein POCSO ke Section 15 ke tahat offence hai, jab haalaat law mein likha iraada dikhate hon, chahe use kabhi share na kiya gaya ho. Court ne Madras High Court ka 11 January 2024 ka faisla radd kar diya aur use "egregious error" kaha [[sc-just-rights-for-children-alliance-2024]]. Misaal ke taur par, Section 15 ke teen offences mein se ek mein aise material ko share karne ke iraade se delete, nasht ya report na karna shaamil hai.

In saare sections ka sabak ek hi hai. Intent koi loophole nahi hai, agar police aur prosecutors woh bartaav ikattha karein jo use saabit karta hai, aur courts use waise padhein jaisa law ka matlab hai. Survivors ke liye, jo details chhoti lagti hain, woh message, woh timing, usne baad mein kya kaha, aksar case unhi par khada hota hai.

ipc-or-bns-which-law-applies-rape.en:
Imagine a 24-year-old in Bhopal who, in November 2026, reports a rape that happened in March 2024. The FIR copy she is handed cites the Indian Penal Code, a law of 1860 that was replaced more than two years ago. Nothing has gone wrong. The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) took over on 1 July 2024 [[air-new-criminal-laws-2024]], but the date of the offence, not the date of the complaint, decides the code. That is why 19,683 of the 29,536 rape cases registered in 2024 were filed under the IPC and only 9,853 under the BNS [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. This Q&A is general information, not legal advice.

## My case happened before 1 July 2024. Which code applies?

The IPC. The three new criminal laws replaced the IPC, the Code of Criminal Procedure and the Evidence Act from 1 July 2024 [[pib-mha-new-criminal-laws-2026]], but they do not reach backwards. Offences committed before that date are registered under the IPC, later ones under the BNS. This follows a basic rule of criminal law: a person can be tried only for what was an offence when the act was done, and cannot be given a heavier penalty than the law then allowed.

So the day you report changes nothing. A rape from 2019 reported in 2026 is an IPC case. If the abuse ran across the changeover, each act falls under the code in force on its own date, so the sections can come from both codes. That is why the date of each incident, or the closest period you can give, matters so much in your statement.

## Is rape defined or punished differently under the BNS?

Hardly. Section 63 of the BNS covers the same acts and keeps the age of consent at 18 [[indiacode-bns-2023]], a definition the IPC has had since 2013 [[indiacode-cla-2013]]. The 10-year minimum under Section 64 [[indiacode-bns-2023]] is the floor the IPC has had since April 2018, when it rose from seven years [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]].

| | IPC (acts before 1 July 2024) | BNS (acts from 1 July 2024) |
|---|---|---|
| Minimum sentence for rape | 10 years, since April 2018 | 10 years (Section 64) |
| Gang rape: natural life or death | Girl under 12 | Girl under 18 (Section 70) |
| Sex by deceit as its own offence | None | Section 69, up to 10 years |
| Non-consensual sex against an adult man or transgender person | Section 377, up to life | No specific offence |

Two rows cut in opposite directions. Under the BNS, every man in a group that rapes a girl under 18 faces natural-life imprisonment or death [[indiacode-bns-2023]]; the IPC's equivalent clause applied only when the girl was under 12 [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]]. The harsher clause cannot reach an act from before July 2024.

The other change takes protection away. Section 377 of the IPC punished non-consensual "carnal intercourse against the order of nature" with up to life imprisonment, and the BNS dropped it without a replacement [[scroll-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]]. An adult man or a transgender person assaulted before 1 July 2024 can still see the accused charged under Section 377. After that date, the new code has no rape provision and no specific offence for them [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Boys under 18 are covered by POCSO either way.

## Can an act before July 2024 be charged as deceit under Section 69?

No. Section 69 of the BNS is a new offence: sex obtained by "deceitful means" or by a promise of marriage made with no intention of keeping it, including a false promise of a job or promotion, or marrying while hiding one's identity. It carries up to 10 years in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Police registered 1,325 cases under it in 2024, every one of them after the BNS took effect [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

An offence that did not exist cannot be charged for an earlier act. For anything before 1 July 2024, the question is whether the facts fit an offence the IPC already had, above all rape. Police do record such complaints as rape: the 2024 rape tables count live-in partners on the pretext of marriage inside a mixed group of 13,879 cases, without separating them out [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Whether a broken promise amounts to rape under the old code depends on the facts of each case. Put that question to a lawyer.

## Why does the 2024 crime data have two columns?

Because 2024 was lived under two codes. The National Crime Records Bureau's tables for the year split cases into an IPC column and a BNS column [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. For rape, that is 19,683 plus 9,853 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The split is not January-to-June against July-to-December. The IPC column holds every case registered in 2024 for an offence committed before 1 July, whether it was reported the next morning or years later. So the IPC column is not a half-year figure, and neither column alone is the year's figure.

## What do I get at the police station either way?

The same rights. The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), which replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure on the same day, governs how a station takes a complaint today. Its Section 173 lets you report a cognizable offence at any police station, wherever it happened (a Zero FIR), or electronically if you sign within three days (an e-FIR), and you must get a copy of the FIR free of cost [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. An officer who fails to record a rape complaint commits an offence under Section 199 of the BNS, punishable with six months to two years of rigorous imprisonment [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Your core protections are older than both codes. Disclosing a rape survivor's identity became a crime in 1983, under Section 228A of the IPC, and rape trials have had to be held in camera since then [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. The BNS carries the identity offence forward as Section 72 [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

> The code on your FIR is decided by a date, not by the officer at the desk. Make sure the date is recorded correctly.

For most survivors the code changes little. The differences sit at the edges: Section 69, gang rape of a minor, Section 377. Give the police the dates as exactly as you can, then read the sections on your free copy.
ipc-or-bns-which-law-applies-rape.hg:
Socho, Bhopal ki ek 24 saal ki ladki November 2026 mein us rape ki report karti hai jo March 2024 mein hua tha. Jo FIR copy uske haath mein aati hai, us par Indian Penal Code likha hai, 1860 ka woh law jiski jagah do saal se zyada pehle naya code aa chuka hai. Yeh koi galti nahi hai. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) 1 July 2024 se lagu hui [[air-new-criminal-laws-2024]], lekin code offence ki date se tay hota hai, complaint ki date se nahi. Isi wajah se 2024 mein register hue 29,536 rape cases mein se 19,683 IPC ke under file hue aur sirf 9,853 BNS ke under [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh sawaal-jawaab general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Mera case 1 July 2024 se pehle ka hai. Kaun sa code lagega?

IPC. Teen naye criminal laws ne 1 July 2024 se IPC, Code of Criminal Procedure aur Evidence Act ki jagah li [[pib-mha-new-criminal-laws-2026]], lekin yeh peeche ki taraf lagu nahi hote. Us date se pehle hue offences IPC ke under register hote hain, baad wale BNS ke under. Yeh criminal law ke ek buniyadi rule se aata hai: kisi insaan par trial sirf us cheez ke liye chal sakta hai jo act ke waqt offence thi, aur use us waqt ke law se zyada bhaari saza nahi di ja sakti.

Isliye tum kis din report karte ho, isse kuch nahi badalta. 2019 ka rape agar 2026 mein report ho, toh woh IPC ka case hai. Agar abuse changeover ke dono taraf chala, toh har act us code ke under aata hai jo us din lagu tha, isliye sections dono codes se aa sakte hain. Isiliye tumhare statement mein har incident ki date, ya jitna kareeb ka period tum bata sako, itni zaroori hai.

## Kya BNS mein rape ki definition ya saza alag hai?

Lagbhag nahi. BNS ka Section 63 wahi acts cover karta hai aur consent ki age 18 hi rakhta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]; yeh definition IPC mein 2013 se thi [[indiacode-cla-2013]]. Section 64 ke under 10 saal ki minimum saza [[indiacode-bns-2023]] wahi floor hai jo IPC mein April 2018 se hai, jab ise saat saal se badhaya gaya tha [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]].

| | IPC (1 July 2024 se pehle ke acts) | BNS (1 July 2024 se baad ke acts) |
|---|---|---|
| Rape ki minimum saza | 10 saal, April 2018 se | 10 saal (Section 64) |
| Gang rape: natural life ya death | Ladki 12 se kam ki ho | Ladki 18 se kam ki ho (Section 70) |
| Dhokhe se sex, alag offence ke roop mein | Koi nahi | Section 69, 10 saal tak |
| Adult aadmi ya transgender person ke saath bina consent sex | Section 377, umrqaid tak | Koi specific offence nahi |

Do rows ulti dishaon mein jaati hain. BNS ke under, 18 se kam umar ki ladki ka rape karne wale group ke har aadmi ko natural-life imprisonment ya death ki saza ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]; IPC ka barabar wala clause tabhi lagta tha jab ladki 12 se kam ki ho [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]]. Yeh zyada sakht clause July 2024 se pehle ke act tak nahi pahunch sakta.

Doosra badlaav protection chheen leta hai. IPC ka Section 377 bina consent ke "carnal intercourse against the order of nature" par umrqaid tak ki saza deta tha, aur BNS ne ise bina kisi replacement ke hata diya [[scroll-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]]. Jis adult aadmi ya transgender person par 1 July 2024 se pehle assault hua, uske case mein accused par ab bhi Section 377 lag sakta hai. Us date ke baad naye code mein unke liye na rape ka provision hai, na koi specific offence [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. 18 se kam umar ke ladke dono soorat mein POCSO se cover hain.

## Kya July 2024 se pehle ka act Section 69 ke under 'deceit' ke roop mein charge ho sakta hai?

Nahi. BNS ka Section 69 ek naya offence hai: "deceitful means" se, ya shaadi ke aise vaade se jise nibhane ka koi iraada na ho, haasil kiya gaya sex. Isme job ya promotion ka jhootha vaada, aur apni pehchaan chhupakar shaadi karna bhi shaamil hai. Saza 10 saal tak ki jail hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Police ne 2024 mein iske under 1,325 cases register kiye, aur saare BNS lagu hone ke baad ke hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Jo offence us waqt tha hi nahi, woh pehle ke act par nahi lagaya ja sakta. 1 July 2024 se pehle ki kisi bhi baat ke liye sawaal yeh hai ki facts IPC ke kisi maujood offence mein fit hote hain ya nahi, sabse pehle rape mein. Police aisi complaints ko rape ke roop mein record karti hai: 2024 ki rape tables mein shaadi ke bahane wale live-in partners 13,879 cases ke ek mile-jule group ke andar gine gaye hain, aur unhe alag karke nahi dikhaya gaya [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Toota hua vaada purane code ke under rape banta hai ya nahi, yeh har case ke facts par depend karta hai. Yeh sawaal kisi lawyer se poocho.

## 2024 ke crime data mein do columns kyun hain?

Kyunki 2024 do codes ke under guzra. National Crime Records Bureau ki us saal ki tables cases ko IPC column aur BNS column mein baantti hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Rape ke liye yeh 19,683 aur 9,853 hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].
