Yeh split January-se-June banaam July-se-December nahi hai. IPC column mein 2024 mein register hua har woh case hai jiska offence 1 July se pehle hua, chahe report agli subah hui ho ya saalon baad. Isliye IPC column aadhe saal ka figure nahi hai, aur akela koi bhi column poore saal ka figure nahi hai.

## Dono soorat mein police station par mujhe kya milega?

Wahi rights. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), jisne usi din Code of Criminal Procedure ki jagah li, aaj yeh tay karti hai ki station complaint kaise lega. Iske Section 173 ke under tum cognizable offence ki report kisi bhi police station mein kar sakte ho, offence chahe kahin bhi hua ho (Zero FIR), ya electronically, agar teen din ke andar sign kar do (e-FIR), aur FIR ki copy tumhe free milni chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Jo officer rape ki complaint record nahi karta, woh BNS ke Section 199 ke under offence karta hai, jiski saza chhe mahine se do saal tak ki rigorous imprisonment hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Tumhare buniyadi protections dono codes se purane hain. Rape survivor ki pehchaan zaahir karna 1983 mein IPC ke Section 228A ke under crime bana, aur tab se rape trials ka in camera hona zaroori hai [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. BNS ne pehchaan wala offence Section 72 ke roop mein aage badhaya hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

> Tumhari FIR par kaun sa code likha jaayega, yeh ek date tay karti hai, desk par baitha officer nahi. Dhyan rakho ki date sahi record ho.

Zyada tar survivors ke liye code se bahut kam badalta hai. Fark kinaaron par hai: Section 69, minor ka gang rape, Section 377. Police ko dates jitni exact ho sake utni exact batao, phir apni free copy par likhe sections padho.

landmark-rape-trials-speed-of-justice.en:
On 9 August 2024 a doctor was raped and murdered at RG Kar Medical College and Hospital in Kolkata. Eleven days later the Supreme Court, acting on its own, set up a national task force on the safety of medical professionals [[livelaw-rg-kar-task-force-2024]]. On 20 January 2025, about five months after the crime, a Sealdah court sentenced the man it had convicted to prison for the rest of his natural life [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]].

Three weeks earlier, 2024 had closed with 1,85,785 rape cases pending trial in India's courts: 89.8% of all the rape cases before them [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A rape trial in India can end in months. Who gets that speed, and what is it made of?

## Fast when watched: four headline timelines

Four closely followed sexual-violence trials ran like this.

| Case | Clock starts | Trial court's decision | Time taken |
|---|---|---|---|
| RG Kar, Kolkata | Crime, 9 August 2024 | Life sentence, 20 January 2025 [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]] | About five months |
| Shakti Mills, Mumbai | Gang rapes, 2013 | Three death sentences under Section 376E of the IPC, 4 April 2014 [[livelaw-shakti-mills-death-sentence-2014]] | Sentenced the year after the crimes |
| Kathua (crime: January 2018) | Trial moved to Pathankot, 7 May 2018 | Six of seven accused convicted, 10 June 2019 [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]] | About 13 months |
| Muzaffarpur shelter home (CBI case: July 2018) | Trial moved to Delhi, 7 February 2019 | 19 of 20 accused convicted, 20 January 2020 [[scconline-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]] | Under a year |

Speed did not mean a rubber stamp: the Kathua and Muzaffarpur courts each acquitted one accused.

## What made them fast: transfers, day-to-day hearings, scrutiny

In Kathua the speed was ordered. On 7 May 2018 a Supreme Court bench headed by Chief Justice Dipak Misra moved the trial from Jammu and Kashmir to Pathankot in Punjab, to be held in camera and day to day [[theprint-kathua-transfer-2018]]. Day to day means the court hears the same case every working day until the evidence is finished.

In Muzaffarpur the CBI had registered the case, and the Supreme Court sent the trial to a POCSO court at Saket in Delhi [[scconline-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]]. In RG Kar the top court stepped in within days, saying "the nation cannot await a rape or murder for real changes on the ground" [[livelaw-rg-kar-task-force-2024]], and the CBI investigated and prosecuted the case [[barandbench-rg-kar-hc-2025]].

The recipe is short: a court that hears one case daily, an investigation under a higher court's eye, a public that keeps asking. The law reserves none of it for famous cases, but each uses up something scarce: a judge's days, a prosecutor's attention.

## The other 1,85,785

Now the cases nobody is watching. In 2024 India's courts had 2,06,777 rape cases before them. They completed 20,587 trials. At the end of the year 1,85,785 were still pending [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The queue is growing. Police sent 24,614 new rape cases to court in 2024, more than the courts finished [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. At the end of 2018 the backlog was 1,38,642 [[ncrb-cii-2018]]. By our arithmetic, at the 2024 pace the courts would need about nine years just to finish the trials already waiting.

The wait does not buy certainty. Of the trials completed in 2024, 5,032 ended in conviction and 13,980 in acquittal, a conviction rate of 24.4% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The data does not say why cases fail. But a long wait gives witnesses time to move away, memories time to fade and pressure to settle time to build.

Imagine a 26-year-old garment worker in Tiruppur who reports a rape by her supervisor. No newspaper has heard of her case. Hearings come weeks apart, and some end in minutes. Each date costs her a day's wages. She is one of the 1,85,785.

## The two-month rule on paper

On paper she is owed more speed than RG Kar got. Under Section 193 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), police must finish a rape investigation within two months of recording the information. Under Section 346, the trial must end within two months of the charge-sheet. An appeal against the sentence must be decided within six months [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Add the first two and the law's own timetable is four months from complaint to verdict. Even RG Kar, with the Supreme Court watching, took about five. The two-month limit on investigations has been law since 2018 [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]]. What the law lacks is any consequence for missing these deadlines. With a backlog more than seven times the number of cases police sent to court in 2024, the two-month trial is the exception.

## Speed without shortcuts: what ordinary cases need

There is a wrong kind of speed. In 2019 four men accused of a rape and murder near Hyderabad were shot dead by police before any trial. A Supreme Court-appointed commission found they were "deliberately fired upon with an intent to cause their death", that three of the four were minors, and recommended that ten police officers be tried for murder [[livelaw-hyderabad-encounter-commission-2022]]. No court ever tested the evidence.

The fast trials went the other way. The RG Kar judge refused the CBI's plea for death and said courts must resist "the temptation to bow to public pressure or emotional appeals" [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. The CBI has appealed for death in the Calcutta High Court [[barandbench-rg-kar-hc-2025]]. And attention fades after a verdict: the Shakti Mills death sentences of April 2014 were commuted to life only on 25 November 2021, when the Bombay High Court held that a constitutional court cannot award punishment based on public opinion [[barandbench-shakti-mills-hc-2021]].

Ordinary cases need what the watched cases got, as routine: daily hearings, an investigation someone senior answers for, a judge who asks why a date was lost. If your own case is stuck, ask the investigating officer for the progress update the BNSS entitles a victim to within 90 days [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. After the charge-sheet, ask the public prosecutor to press for day-to-day hearings. A free lawyer from the District Legal Services Authority [[nalsa]] can advise on what can be done when a trial stalls. This is general information, not legal advice.

Four cases show what Indian courts can do when a case is watched: reach a verdict in roughly a year or less, without skipping a step. The other 1,85,785 are waiting for the same attention.
landmark-rape-trials-speed-of-justice.hg:
9 August 2024 ko Kolkata ke RG Kar Medical College and Hospital mein ek doctor ka rape aur murder hua. Gyarah din baad Supreme Court ne khud is case ko uthaya aur medical professionals ki safety par ek national task force bana di [[livelaw-rg-kar-task-force-2024]]. 20 January 2025 ko, crime ke kareeb paanch mahine baad, Sealdah ki ek court ne jis aadmi ko convict kiya tha use baaki poori zindagi ki jail ki saza sunayi [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]].

Us saza se teen hafte pehle, jab 2024 khatam hua, India ki courts mein 1,85,785 rape cases trial ke intezaar mein the: courts ke saamne maujood sabhi rape cases ka 89.8% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yaani India mein rape trial mahinon mein khatam ho sakta hai. Yeh speed kise milti hai, aur kin cheezon se banti hai?

## Jab nazar ho, tab tezi: chaar headline timelines

Chaar sexual-violence trials, jin par poore desh ki nazar thi, aise chale.

| Case | Ghadi kab shuru hui | Trial court ka faisla | Kitna time laga |
|---|---|---|---|
| RG Kar, Kolkata | Crime, 9 August 2024 | Umrqaid, 20 January 2025 [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]] | Kareeb paanch mahine |
| Shakti Mills, Mumbai | Gang rapes, 2013 | IPC ki Section 376E ke tahat teen logon ko maut ki saza, 4 April 2014 [[livelaw-shakti-mills-death-sentence-2014]] | Crimes ke agle hi saal saza |
| Kathua (crime: January 2018) | Trial Pathankot shift hua, 7 May 2018 | Saat mein se chhe accused convict, 10 June 2019 [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]] | Kareeb 13 mahine |
| Muzaffarpur shelter home (CBI case: July 2018) | Trial Delhi shift hua, 7 February 2019 | 20 mein se 19 accused convict, 20 January 2020 [[scconline-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]] | Ek saal se kam |

Tezi ka matlab rubber stamp nahi tha: Kathua aur Muzaffarpur, dono courts ne ek-ek accused ko bari kiya.

## Tezi kahan se aayi: transfer, roz ki sunwai, upar se nigrani

Kathua mein speed ka baqayda order diya gaya tha. 7 May 2018 ko Chief Justice Dipak Misra ki aguwai wali Supreme Court bench ne trial ko Jammu and Kashmir se Punjab ke Pathankot bhej diya, aur kaha ki sunwai in camera aur day to day ho [[theprint-kathua-transfer-2018]]. Day to day ka matlab hai ki court har working day par wahi case sunti hai, jab tak saara evidence poora na ho jaye.

Muzaffarpur mein case CBI ne register kiya tha, aur Supreme Court ne trial Delhi ke Saket ki ek POCSO court mein bheja [[scconline-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]]. RG Kar mein Supreme Court kuch hi dinon mein beech mein aa gayi. Usne kaha, "the nation cannot await a rape or murder for real changes on the ground", yaani desh zameen par asli badlav ke liye kisi rape ya murder ka intezaar nahi kar sakta [[livelaw-rg-kar-task-force-2024]]. Investigation aur prosecution, dono CBI ne kiye [[barandbench-rg-kar-hc-2025]].

Recipe chhoti si hai: ek court jo roz wahi ek case sune, ek investigation jis par upar ki court ki nazar ho, aur ek public jo sawaal poochti rahe. Law inme se kuch bhi famous cases ke liye reserve nahi karta. Lekin har cheez kuch aisa kharch karti hai jo kam hai: judge ke din, prosecutor ka dhyan.

## Baaki 1,85,785

Ab un cases ki baat jin par kisi ki nazar nahi hai. 2024 mein India ki courts ke saamne 2,06,777 rape cases the. Unhone 20,587 trials poore kiye. Saal ke end par 1,85,785 abhi bhi pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Line lambi hoti ja rahi hai. 2024 mein police ne 24,614 naye rape cases court bheje, jitne courts ne nipataye usse zyada [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 2018 ke end par backlog 1,38,642 tha [[ncrb-cii-2018]]. Hamare hisaab se, 2024 ki raftaar par courts ko sirf pehle se pending trials khatam karne mein kareeb nau saal lagenge.

Aur itne intezaar ke baad bhi nateeja pakka nahi. 2024 mein jo trials poore hue, unme 5,032 mein conviction hua aur 13,980 mein acquittal, yaani conviction rate 24.4% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Data yeh nahi batata ki cases kyun girte hain. Lekin lamba intezaar gawahon ko shehar chhodne ka, yaadon ko dhundhla padne ka aur samjhaute ke dabaav ko badhne ka waqt de deta hai.

Maan lijiye Tiruppur ki ek 26 saal ki garment worker apne supervisor ke khilaaf rape ki report likhwati hai. Kisi akhbaar ne uske case ke baare mein suna tak nahi. Hearings hafton ke gap par aati hain, aur kuch toh minutes mein khatam ho jaati hain. Har tareekh par uski ek din ki dihadi jaati hai. Woh un 1,85,785 mein se ek hai.

## Kaagaz par do mahine ka rule

Kaagaz par use RG Kar se bhi zyada speed milni chahiye. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ki Section 193 ke mutabik police ko rape ki investigation, information record hone ke do mahine ke andar poori karni hai. Section 346 ke mutabik trial charge-sheet ke do mahine ke andar khatam hona chahiye. Saza ke khilaaf appeal ka faisla chhe mahine ke andar hona chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Pehli do limits jodiye toh law ka apna timetable banta hai: complaint se verdict tak chaar mahine. RG Kar ko bhi, Supreme Court ki nigrani ke bawajood, kareeb paanch mahine lage. Investigation ki do mahine wali limit 2018 se law mein hai [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]]. Law mein jo cheez nahi hai, woh hai in deadlines ko todne ka koi nateeja. Jab backlog un cases ke saat guna se bhi zyada ho jo police ne 2024 mein court bheje, toh do mahine ka trial exception hi hai.

## Bina shortcut ki speed: aam cases ko kya chahiye

Ek galat kism ki speed bhi hoti hai. 2019 mein Hyderabad ke paas ek rape aur murder ke chaar accused ko police ne kisi bhi trial se pehle goli maar di. Supreme Court ke banaye commission ne paaya ki woh "deliberately fired upon with an intent to cause their death" the, yaani un par jaan lene ke iraade se jaan-boojh kar goli chalayi gayi thi, aur chaar mein se teen minor the. Commission ne sifarish ki ki das police officers par murder ka trial chale [[livelaw-hyderabad-encounter-commission-2022]]. Evidence ko kisi court ne kabhi parkha hi nahi.

Tez trials ne ulta raasta chuna. RG Kar ke judge ne CBI ki maut ki saza wali maang thukra di aur kaha ki courts ko "the temptation to bow to public pressure or emotional appeals" se bachna hoga, yaani public pressure ya jazbaati appeals ke aage jhukne ke lalach se [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. CBI ne maut ki saza ke liye Calcutta High Court mein appeal ki hai [[barandbench-rg-kar-hc-2025]]. Aur verdict ke baad nazar hat jaati hai: April 2014 mein Shakti Mills case mein di gayi maut ki sazaayein 25 November 2021 ko jaakar umrqaid mein badlin, jab Bombay High Court ne kaha ki constitutional court public opinion ke aadhar par saza nahi de sakti [[barandbench-shakti-mills-hc-2021]].

Aam cases ko wahi chahiye jo in cases ko mila, bas routine ki tarah: roz ki sunwai, aisi investigation jiske liye koi senior jawabdeh ho, aur aisa judge jo pooche ki tareekh kyun bekaar gayi. Agar aapka apna case atka hai, toh investigating officer se woh progress update maangiye jo BNSS ke tahat victim ko 90 din ke andar milna chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Charge-sheet ke baad public prosecutor se kahiye ki woh day-to-day sunwai ki maang kare. District Legal Services Authority ka free lawyer [[nalsa]] bata sakta hai ki trial atakne par kya kiya ja sakta hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

Chaar cases dikhate hain ki jab kisi case par nazar ho, toh India ki courts kya kar sakti hain: bina koi step chhode, kareeb ek saal ya usse kam mein verdict tak pahunchna. Baaki 1,85,785 usi tavajjo ka intezaar kar rahe hain.

life-sentence-remission-rape-convicts.en:
On 15 August 2022, 11 men walked out of Godhra jail in Gujarat. Each was serving a life sentence for the gang rape of a pregnant woman and the murder of 14 of her relatives during the 2002 Gujarat riots [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. No court had cleared them. A state government had signed remission orders. In January 2024 the Supreme Court sent all 11 back. So when a judge says "life", how long is that? This is general information, not legal advice.

## What is remission, and who grants it?

Remission is a government's power to cut short a sentence that a court has passed. The conviction stays on the record. Only the time left to serve is cancelled.

Section 64 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) punishes rape with at least 10 years' rigorous imprisonment, and up to life [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. A life sentence carries no release date. Whether the convict ever leaves prison is not settled in the court where the survivor testified. It is settled years afterwards, on a file, by whichever government the law calls the "appropriate government".

Remission is not an acquittal on appeal, bail, or a court suspending a sentence while an appeal is heard. Judges decide those. Ministers and officials decide remission.

## What happened in the 2002 Gujarat riots gang rape case?

The trial was held in Mumbai, not in Gujarat. On 21 January 2008 a special court there sentenced the 11 men to life imprisonment, and on 4 May 2017 the Bombay High Court upheld their convictions. By orders dated 10 August 2022, the Gujarat government granted all 11 remission under its 1992 remission policy. Five days later they were out [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]].

On 8 January 2024 a Supreme Court bench of Justices B.V. Nagarathna and Ujjal Bhuyan quashed the remission. Gujarat, it held, had no power to grant it: the appropriate government was Maharashtra, where the trial was held. The court also found that its own May 2022 order, which had asked Gujarat to decide, was obtained by suppressing facts and by fraud [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. The 11 men surrendered at Godhra sub-jail late on the night of 21 January 2024 [[scroll-bilkis-surrender-2024]].

The ruling did not say a life convict can never be released early. It said the wrong government had signed. The power to decide moved to another state. It did not disappear.

> A life sentence has no end date written on it. This case turned on who is allowed to write one in later.

## What does "the remainder of natural life" add?

It is Parliament's attempt to close that door for the gravest crimes. The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 set a minimum of 20 years for gang rape under Section 376D of the IPC, extendable to life, "which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person's natural life" [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].

The BNS repeats those words. They cover the 13 aggravated forms of rape in Section 64(2), which include rape by a police officer, a relative, a guardian or a teacher, rape during communal violence and rape of a pregnant woman. They cover gang rape under Section 70. And under Section 71, a second rape conviction leaves a court two choices: natural life or death [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

The label is strong, but it is not a guarantee. It does not end the convict's right to appeal, and it does not stop a higher court from pausing the sentence while that appeal is heard.

## How have courts used it in the Unnao and Muzaffarpur cases?

On 20 December 2019 a Delhi court sentenced former MLA Kuldeep Singh Sengar to imprisonment for the remainder of his life, with a Rs 25 lakh fine, for the 2017 rape of a minor girl in Unnao, Uttar Pradesh [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]]. On 11 February 2020 a court at Saket in Delhi sentenced Brajesh Thakur, who ran the Muzaffarpur shelter home, to life imprisonment for the remainder of his life and a fine of about Rs 32 lakh [[livelaw-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]].

Unnao also shows the limit. In December 2025 the Delhi High Court suspended Sengar's sentence while his appeal was pending, noting among other things that he had served more than seven years. The Supreme Court stayed that order on 29 December 2025 [[scobserver-unnao-stay-2025]]. On 15 May 2026 it set the order aside and sent the question back to the High Court [[livelaw-unnao-sc-2026]]. He was also serving a separate 10-year sentence over the death of the survivor's father [[barandbench-unnao-father-2020]].

A sentence written to last "the remainder of his life" was, for a few days, suspended on paper. It took the Supreme Court to reverse that.

## What can a survivor do if a convict's release is proposed?

Imagine a family in Nagpur, years after a verdict, hearing from a neighbour that the convict has applied for early release. Four things matter.

**Which government decides.** After the 2024 ruling, it is the government of the state where the trial was held [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. In the Gujarat case that was not the state where the crime took place.

**A remission order can be challenged.** The 2024 judgment came on petitions filed in the Supreme Court against the release, one of them the survivor's own [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. A District Legal Services Authority can help with a lawyer.

**Stay informed, and report threats.** For Dalit and Adivasi survivors, Section 15A of the SC/ST Atrocities Act makes it the state's duty to protect victims and witnesses from intimidation, and gives victims a right to timely notice of court proceedings, including bail hearings [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]]. Remission is decided outside a courtroom, so families need to keep asking the prosecutor and the prison authorities. Report any threat to the police in writing, and call 112 in an emergency.

**Compensation is separate.** A victim can apply to the State or District Legal Services Authority under Section 396 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, whatever happens to the convict's sentence [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

A conviction is one decision. The sentence is a second. Release is a third, and the only one taken out of public view. Knowing who takes it, and that it can be questioned, is a survivor's first protection.
life-sentence-remission-rape-convicts.hg:
15 August 2022 ko 11 aadmi Gujarat ki Godhra jail se bahar nikle. Har ek 2002 ke Gujarat riots mein ek pregnant aurat ke gang rape aur uske 14 rishtedaaron ke murder ke liye life sazaa kaat raha tha [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. Kisi court ne unhe bari nahi kiya tha. Ek state government ne remission orders sign kiye the. January 2024 mein Supreme Court ne sabhi 11 ko wapas jail bhej diya. Toh jab judge "life" kehta hai, toh woh kitne time ki hoti hai? Yeh general jaankari hai, legal advice nahi.

## Remission kya hai, aur kaun deta hai?

Remission sarkaar ki woh power hai jisse woh court ki di hui sazaa ko beech mein kam kar sakti hai. Conviction record par rehta hai. Sirf bachi hui sazaa cancel hoti hai.

Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ka Section 64 rape ke liye kam se kam 10 saal ki rigorous qaid deta hai, aur life tak [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Life sazaa par koi release date nahi likhi hoti. Convict kabhi jail se niklega ya nahi, yeh us court mein tay nahi hota jahan survivor ne gawaahi di thi. Yeh saalon baad ek file par tay hota hai, us sarkaar ke dwara jise kaanoon "appropriate government" kehta hai.

Remission appeal mein acquittal nahi hai, bail nahi hai, aur appeal ke dauraan court ka sazaa suspend karna bhi nahi hai. Woh sab judges tay karte hain. Remission ministers aur officials tay karte hain.

## 2002 Gujarat riots gang rape case mein kya hua?

Trial Gujarat mein nahi, Mumbai mein hua tha. 21 January 2008 ko wahan ki special court ne 11 aadmiyon ko life imprisonment di, aur 4 May 2017 ko Bombay High Court ne unke convictions ko sahi thehraaya. 10 August 2022 ke orders se Gujarat government ne apni 1992 ki remission policy ke tahat sabhi 11 ko remission de di. Paanch din baad woh bahar the [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]].

8 January 2024 ko Justices B.V. Nagarathna aur Ujjal Bhuyan ki Supreme Court bench ne remission radd kar di. Court ne kaha ki Gujarat ke paas yeh power thi hi nahi: appropriate government Maharashtra thi, jahan trial hua tha. Court ne yeh bhi paaya ki uska apna May 2022 ka order, jisne Gujarat ko faisla lene ko kaha tha, facts chhupa kar aur fraud se liya gaya tha [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. 11 aadmiyon ne 21 January 2024 ki der raat Godhra sub-jail mein surrender kiya [[scroll-bilkis-surrender-2024]].

Faisle ne yeh nahi kaha ki life convict ko kabhi jaldi nahi chhoda ja sakta. Usne kaha ki galat sarkaar ne sign kiya. Faisla lene ki power doosre state ke paas chali gayi. Khatam nahi hui.

> Life sazaa par koi end date nahi likhi hoti. Yeh case is baat par tika tha ki baad mein woh date likhne ka haq kisko hai.

## "Baaki natural life" sazaa mein kya jodta hai?

Yeh sabse gambhir crimes ke liye woh darwaaza band karne ki Parliament ki koshish hai. Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 ne IPC Section 376D ke tahat gang rape ke liye minimum 20 saal rakhe, jo life tak badh sakte hain, "which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person's natural life", yaani us insaan ki baaki natural life tak qaid [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].

BNS yahi shabd dohraata hai. Yeh Section 64(2) ke 13 aggravated roopon par laagu hote hain, jinmein police officer, rishtedaar, guardian ya teacher dwara rape, communal violence ke dauraan rape aur pregnant aurat ka rape shaamil hain. Yeh Section 70 ke gang rape par bhi laagu hote hain. Aur Section 71 ke tahat, doosre rape conviction par court ke paas sirf do raaste hain: natural life ya maut ki sazaa [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Label mazboot hai, par guarantee nahi. Isse convict ka appeal ka haq khatam nahi hota, aur yeh higher court ko appeal ke dauraan sazaa rokne se bhi nahi rokta.

## Unnao aur Muzaffarpur cases mein courts ne ise kaise use kiya?

20 December 2019 ko Delhi ki ek court ne former MLA Kuldeep Singh Sengar ko Unnao, Uttar Pradesh mein 2017 mein ek naabaalig ladki ke rape ke liye baaki zindagi ki qaid aur Rs 25 lakh fine ki sazaa di [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]]. 11 February 2020 ko Delhi ki Saket court ne Muzaffarpur shelter home chalaane wale Brajesh Thakur ko baaki zindagi ke liye life imprisonment aur lagbhag Rs 32 lakh fine ki sazaa di [[livelaw-muzaffarpur-sentence-2020]].

Unnao is label ki seema bhi dikhaata hai. December 2025 mein Delhi High Court ne appeal pending rehte Sengar ki sazaa suspend kar di, yeh bhi note karte hue ki woh saat saal se zyada kaat chuka tha. Supreme Court ne 29 December 2025 ko us order par rok lagaai [[scobserver-unnao-stay-2025]]. 15 May 2026 ko usne order radd kiya aur sawaal wapas High Court ko bhej diya [[livelaw-unnao-sc-2026]]. Woh survivor ke pita ki maut ke maamle mein alag se 10 saal ki sazaa bhi kaat raha tha [[barandbench-unnao-father-2020]].

Jo sazaa "baaki zindagi" ke liye likhi gayi thi, woh kuch dinon ke liye kaagaz par suspend thi. Use palatne ke liye Supreme Court ko aana pada.

## Agar convict ki rihaai ki baat chale, toh survivor kya kar sakti hai?

Sochiye, Nagpur ka ek parivaar, faisle ke saalon baad, ek padosi se sunta hai ki convict ne jaldi rihaai ki arzi di hai. Chaar cheezein maayne rakhti hain.

**Faisla kaun karta hai.** 2024 ke faisle ke baad, us state ki sarkaar jahan trial hua tha [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. Gujarat wale case mein woh state nahi thi jahan crime hua tha.

**Remission order ko challenge kiya ja sakta hai.** 2024 ka faisla Supreme Court mein rihaai ke khilaaf daali gayi petitions par aaya tha, jinmein se ek khud survivor ki thi [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. District Legal Services Authority vakeel dilaane mein madad kar sakti hai.

**Jaankari rakhiye, aur dhamkiyon ki report kijiye.** Dalit aur Adivasi survivors ke liye SC/ST Atrocities Act ka Section 15A victims aur gawaahon ko dhamkiyon se bachana state ki zimmedaari banata hai, aur victims ko bail hearings samet court proceedings ki samay par jaankari ka haq deta hai [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]]. Remission courtroom ke bahar tay hota hai, isliye parivaaron ko prosecutor aur jail authorities se baar-baar poochhte rehna padta hai. Koi bhi dhamki police ko likhit mein bataiye, aur emergency mein 112 call kijiye.

**Compensation alag hai.** Victim Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita ke Section 396 ke tahat State ya District Legal Services Authority mein apply kar sakti hai, convict ki sazaa ke saath chahe kuch bhi ho [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Conviction ek faisla hai. Sazaa doosra. Rihaai teesra, aur akela aisa jo public ki nazar se door liya jaata hai. Yeh jaanna ki use kaun leta hai, aur ki us par sawaal uthaaya ja sakta hai, survivor ki pehli hifaazat hai.

medical-records-privacy-rape-case.en:
Consider a 22-year-old in Pune the morning after she was raped. She knows she should see a doctor. She also knows what a hospital file contains: an examination, blood tests, perhaps a pregnancy test. She does not know who will read it. Her parents? The police? The man's lawyer? A clerk who knows her cousin?

Silence after violence is already the norm. In the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5), only 14% of women who had faced physical or sexual violence sought help, and 77% never sought help or told anyone [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. The law answers her question differently for each part of the file. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Does the examination happen without my say, and who gets the report?

No examination can lawfully happen without her consent. Under Section 184 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), once police learn of a rape they must send the survivor to a registered doctor, preferably a government doctor, within 24 hours. The section says in terms that nothing in it makes an examination lawful without the woman's consent [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. She can agree to some steps and refuse others.

The doctor's report has one destination: the investigating officer, within 7 days [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. It does not go to her family, her employer or her college. And it may not contain a "two-finger test": in 2022 the Supreme Court held that anyone who conducts it is guilty of misconduct, calling it a practice with "no scientific basis" [[theprint-sc-two-finger-test-2022]].

## The hospital says it must "inform the police". What does that mean?

Section 397 of the BNSS obliges every hospital, public or private, to treat a rape or POCSO survivor immediately and free, and to inform the police [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. A hospital in-charge who refuses free treatment faces up to 1 year under Section 200 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Informing the police is a duty on the hospital. It is not a power to hand her whole file to anyone who asks. For a child, the rule is stricter: under Section 19 of the POCSO Act anyone who knows of child sexual abuse must report it, and failing to do so carries up to 6 months in prison or a fine [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. A doctor cannot promise a minor total secrecy about abuse.

## Will my HIV test result be shared?

This part of the file has its own law. The HIV Act, 2017 forbids HIV testing without informed consent, says no one can be compelled to disclose their HIV status except by a court order, and lets courts hide a person's identity behind a pseudonym in HIV-related cases [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]].

So a survivor offered HIV testing after an assault can say yes or no, and can keep the result to herself. Every state must appoint an HIV Ombudsman, and anyone who ignores its order can be fined up to Rs 10,000, plus up to Rs 5,000 a day while the failure continues [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. The national AIDS helpline, 1097, offers confidential counselling round the clock [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

## If I end a pregnancy, who will know?

Section 5A of the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act, inserted in 2021, bars any registered doctor from revealing the name or other particulars of a woman whose pregnancy was terminated, except to a person authorised by law. Breaking it carries up to 1 year in prison, a fine, or both [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. In 2022 the Supreme Court held that a married woman pregnant from forced sex by her husband counts as a rape survivor under this law, without an FIR [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

Minors face a collision between two laws: POCSO says the doctor must report, the MTP Act says the doctor must protect. In September 2022 the Supreme Court settled it. A doctor terminating a minor's pregnancy need not disclose her identity or personal details in the POCSO report, if she and her guardian ask [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. The request has to be made, so a family that does not know about it will not make it.

> The file is not one document. The examination report must reach the police; the HIV result and the abortion record are locked by their own laws.

## When the case reaches court, who can see the file?

The medical report becomes evidence, so the accused's lawyers will see it. That is part of a fair trial. What the law limits is everyone else. Rape and POCSO trials must be held in camera, as far as practicable before a woman judge, and nothing about the proceedings may be published without the court's permission [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Publishing her name or any detail that could identify her carries up to 2 years under Section 72 of the BNS [[indiacode-bns-2023]], and the Supreme Court has said FIRs in rape and POCSO cases must not be put in the public domain [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

The record is thin. Police registered just 11 cases under Section 72 in July-December 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Since 2013, a survivor's character or previous sexual experience has been irrelevant to consent, first under Section 53A of the Evidence Act [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]] and now under Section 48 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam [[indiacode-bsa-2023]], so her medical history is not a licence to put her past on trial. If anyone leaks her file, she should write down who did it, when and to whom, and take it to the police or, for HIV, to the Ombudsman.
medical-records-privacy-rape-case.hg:
Pune ki ek 22 saal ki ladki ko sochiye, jis subah ke pichhli raat uska rape hua. Use pata hai ki doctor ke paas jaana chahiye. Use yeh bhi pata hai ki hospital file mein kya hota hai: examination, blood tests, shayad pregnancy test. Use yeh nahi pata ki ise padhega kaun. Uske parents? Police? Us aadmi ka lawyer? Koi clerk jo uske cousin ko jaanta hai?

Violence ke baad chuppi pehle se hi aam baat hai. National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5) mein physical ya sexual violence jheli women mein se sirf 14% ne madad maangi, aur 77% ne kabhi madad nahi maangi ya kisi ko nahi bataya [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Law uske sawaal ka jawaab file ke har hisse ke liye alag deta hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Kya examination meri marzi ke bina hoga, aur report kise milegi?

Uski consent ke bina koi examination legally nahi ho sakta. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ke Section 184 ke under, rape ki khabar milte hi police ko survivor ko 24 ghante ke andar registered doctor ke paas bhejna hai, preferably government doctor ke paas. Section saaf kehta hai ki is mein kuch bhi woman ki consent ke bina examination ko legal nahi banata [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Woh kuch steps ke liye haan aur kuch ke liye na keh sakti hai.

Doctor ki report ki ek hi manzil hai: investigating officer, 7 din ke andar [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Woh uski family, employer ya college ke paas nahi jaati. Aur us mein "two-finger test" nahi ho sakta: 2022 mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki jo bhi yeh test karta hai woh misconduct ka doshi hai, aur ise "no scientific basis" wali practice kaha [[theprint-sc-two-finger-test-2022]].

## Hospital kehta hai use "police ko inform karna" padega. Iska matlab kya hai?

BNSS ka Section 397 har hospital, government ya private, pe duty daalta hai ki rape ya POCSO survivor ka turant aur free ilaaj kare, aur police ko inform kare [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Jo hospital in-charge free treatment se mana karta hai, use Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 200 ke under 1 saal tak ki saza ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Police ko inform karna hospital ki duty hai. Yeh uski poori file har maangne wale ko thamaane ki permission nahi hai. Bachche ke case mein rule aur sakht hai: POCSO Act ke Section 19 ke under jo bhi child sexual abuse ke baare mein jaanta hai use report karna hai, aur na karne pe 6 mahine tak ki jail ya fine hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Doctor kisi minor se abuse ke baare mein poori secrecy ka vaada nahi kar sakta.

## Kya mera HIV test result share hoga?

File ke is hisse ka apna law hai. HIV Act, 2017 informed consent ke bina HIV testing mana karta hai, kehta hai ki court order ke bina kisi ko apna HIV status batane pe majboor nahi kiya ja sakta, aur courts ko HIV wale cases mein insaan ki identity pseudonym ke peeche chhupane deta hai [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]].

Toh assault ke baad jis survivor ko HIV test offer hota hai, woh haan ya na keh sakti hai, aur result apne paas rakh sakti hai. Har state ko ek HIV Ombudsman appoint karna hai, aur jo uska order nahi maanta use 10,000 rupaye tak ka fine, plus jab tak failure chale har din 5,000 rupaye tak, ho sakta hai [[naco-hiv-aids-act-2017-gazette]]. National AIDS helpline 1097 chaubees ghante confidential counselling deti hai [[naco-sankalak-2025]].

## Agar main pregnancy khatam karoon, toh kise pata chalega?

Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act ka Section 5A, jo 2021 mein joda gaya, kisi bhi registered doctor ko us woman ka naam ya baaki details batane se rokta hai jiski pregnancy terminate hui, sirf law se authorised insaan ko chhod kar. Ise todne pe 1 saal tak ki jail, fine, ya dono ho sakte hain [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. 2022 mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki jo married woman husband ke zabardasti sex se pregnant hui, woh is law ke under rape survivor maani jaayegi, bina FIR ke [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

Minors ke case mein do laws takraate hain: POCSO kehta hai doctor report kare, MTP Act kehta hai doctor protect kare. September 2022 mein Supreme Court ne yeh suljhaya. Minor ki pregnancy terminate karne wale doctor ko POCSO report mein uski identity ya personal details batane ki zaroorat nahi, agar woh aur uska guardian aisa maangein [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]]. Yeh request karni padti hai, toh jis family ko iske baare mein pata hi nahi, woh yeh request karegi bhi nahi.

> File ek document nahi hai. Examination report police tak jaani hi hai; HIV result aur abortion record apne-apne laws se locked hain.

## Jab case court pahunchta hai, toh file kaun dekh sakta hai?

Medical report evidence ban jaati hai, toh accused ke lawyers use dekhenge. Yeh fair trial ka hissa hai. Law baaki sab ko rokta hai. Rape aur POCSO trials in camera hone chahiye, jahan tak ho sake woman judge ke saamne, aur proceedings ke baare mein court ki permission ke bina kuch publish nahi ho sakta [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Uska naam ya koi bhi detail jisse woh pehchaani jaaye publish karne pe BNS ke Section 72 ke under 2 saal tak ki saza hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]], aur Supreme Court ne kaha hai ki rape aur POCSO cases ki FIRs public domain mein nahi daali ja sakti [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

Record kamzor hai. July-December 2024 mein police ne Section 72 ke under sirf 11 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 2013 se survivor ka character ya pichhla sexual experience consent ke sawaal pe irrelevant hai, pehle Evidence Act ke Section 53A ke under [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]] aur ab Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam ke Section 48 ke under [[indiacode-bsa-2023]], toh uski medical history uske past ko trial pe chadhane ka license nahi hai. Agar koi uski file leak kare, toh use likh lena chahiye kisne kiya, kab aur kisko, aur police ke paas, ya HIV ke case mein Ombudsman ke paas, le jaana chahiye.

officials-punished-for-failing-survivors.en:
Consider this situation. A 20-year-old in Nagpur is raped by a man from her coaching class. At the police station, the officer on duty tells her to come back in the morning with her parents. At a private hospital, the front desk asks for a police memo and a deposit. Under Indian law, both refusals can be crimes.

These duties are not new. The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 already made it an offence for police to refuse to record an FIR for rape or acid attack and required every hospital to treat such survivors free [[indiacode-cla-2013]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

| Who fails | What they owed | Punishment |
|---|---|---|
| Police officer | FIR for rape, sexual assault, acid attack, trafficking | 6 months to 2 years, and a fine |
| Hospital in-charge | Immediate free treatment | Up to 1 year |
| Anyone who knows of child sexual abuse | A report to the police | Up to 6 months, or a fine |
| Head of an institution | A report on a subordinate's abuse | Up to 1 year, and a fine |
| Public servant, Atrocities Act case | Correct sections; charge sheet in 60 days | 6 months to 1 year |
| Employer | An Internal Committee that acts | Fine up to Rs 50,000 |

## The police officer who will not write the FIR

Section 199(c) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) punishes a public servant who fails to record information about rape, gang rape, sexual assault, acid attack or trafficking with rigorous imprisonment of six months to two years, and a fine [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. In 2013 a five-judge Supreme Court bench held in Lalita Kumari v. Government of Uttar Pradesh that registering an FIR is mandatory, adding: "Action must be taken against erring officers who do not register the FIR" [[sc-lalita-kumari-2013]].

Two limits. Sexual harassment (Section 75) and stalking (Section 78) are not on Section 199's list [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. And no section helps unless there is a record showing the officer was told, which is why the paper trail matters.

**Put in writing:** the date, time and station, the officer's name and rank, and the line "Failure to record this is an offence under Section 199 of the BNS." If the station still refuses, Section 173(4) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) lets you post the complaint to the Superintendent of Police and then approach a magistrate [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## The hospital that turns a survivor away

Section 397 of the BNSS obliges every hospital, public or private, to give immediate first aid or treatment, free of cost, to survivors of rape, acid attack and sexual offences against children, and to inform the police [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. The person in charge of a hospital that breaks this rule faces up to one year in prison under Section 200 of the BNS [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

The section's word is "immediately". Nothing in it tells a hospital to wait for an FIR, a police memo or a deposit. The hours matter: medicine to prevent HIV must start within 72 hours of exposure [[who-pep]].

**Put in writing:** a note to the medical superintendent or owner with the time you arrived, who refused, and both section numbers.

## The school, hostel or home that hides abuse of a child

Under the POCSO Act, anyone who knows a child has been sexually abused must report it. Failing to report a case, or to record one, can mean up to six months in prison or a fine; the head of a company or institution who fails to report abuse by a subordinate faces up to one year and a fine [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. A child cannot be punished for staying silent.

A principal who says "we will handle this internally" and quietly transfers the teacher is not protecting the school. She is committing the offence the Act wrote for her chair.

It rarely shows up in the data. Of 69,191 POCSO cases registered in 2024, only 218 fell under Sections 17 to 22, a group that lumps failure to report with abetment, attempt and false complaints [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Police data counts each FIR once, under its most serious offence, so a failure-to-report charge added to an abuse case is hidden; even so, the offence almost never stands alone.

**Put in writing:** a dated complaint to the head, and your own report to the police or Child Helpline 1098, so nobody can later claim they did not know.

## Public servants under the Atrocities Act

For Dalit and Adivasi survivors, the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act aims a duty clause at officials. Under Section 4, as amended in 2015, a public servant who is not from a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe and wilfully neglects duties under the Act faces six months to one year in prison. The duties include registering the FIR under the appropriate sections, filing the charge sheet within 60 days and explaining any delay in writing [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

An FIR that leaves out the Act when it applies also leaves out what it gives a survivor: the state's duty under Section 15A to protect her and her witnesses from intimidation, and her right to notice of court proceedings, bail hearings included [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

**Put in writing:** a request, in the complaint itself, that the Atrocities Act be applied.

## Employers who ignore the POSH Act

The weakest penalty here is the employer's. One who fails to set up an Internal Committee, or to act on its findings, can be fined up to Rs 50,000 [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. There is no jail term, and a court can act only on a complaint by the aggrieved woman or a person authorised by the Internal or Local Committee [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. In 2023 the Supreme Court warned that without strict enforcement the Act would "remain an empty formality" [[sci-posh-enforcement-judgment-2023]].

**Put in writing:** an email to HR asking who sits on the Internal Committee. With fewer than ten workers, or a complaint against the employer, the district's Local Committee takes it [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

None of these clauses enforces itself. Each needs someone to name the section and leave a dated record; the District Legal Services Authority gives free legal aid to do it [[nalsa]]. Officials have gone to jail before: in the Kathua case, a Pathankot trial court in June 2019 gave three policemen five years each for destroying evidence [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]]. The desk that says no is counting on nobody writing it down.
officials-punished-for-failing-survivors.hg:
Ek situation socho. Nagpur ki ek 20 saal ki ladki ka uski coaching class ka ek ladka rape karta hai. Police station par duty officer kehta hai ki subah apne parents ke saath aana. Ek private hospital ka front desk police memo aur deposit maangta hai. Indian law ke hisaab se, ye dono refusals crime ho sakte hain.

Ye duties nayi nahi hain. Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 ne hi rape ya acid attack ki FIR record karne se police ka mana karna offence bana diya, aur har hospital ke liye aise survivors ka free ilaaj zaroori kar diya [[indiacode-cla-2013]]. Ye general information hai, legal advice nahi.

| Kaun fail karta hai | Uski duty kya thi | Saza |
|---|---|---|
| Police officer | Rape, sexual assault, acid attack, trafficking ki FIR | 6 months se 2 years, aur fine |
| Hospital in-charge | Turant free treatment | 1 year tak |
| Child sexual abuse ke baare mein jaanne wala koi bhi | Police ko report | 6 months tak, ya fine |
| Institution ka head | Subordinate ke abuse ki report | 1 year tak, aur fine |
| Public servant, Atrocities Act case | Sahi sections; 60 din mein charge sheet | 6 months se 1 year |
| Employer | Kaam karne wali Internal Committee | Rs 50,000 tak fine |

## Woh police officer jo FIR nahi likhta

Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ka Section 199(c) us public servant ko saza deta hai jo rape, gang rape, sexual assault, acid attack ya trafficking ki information record nahi karta: six months se two years tak rigorous imprisonment, aur fine [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. 2013 mein Supreme Court ki five-judge bench ne Lalita Kumari v. Government of Uttar Pradesh mein kaha ki FIR register karna mandatory hai, aur joda: "Action must be taken against erring officers who do not register the FIR" [[sc-lalita-kumari-2013]].

Do limits samajh lo. Sexual harassment (Section 75) aur stalking (Section 78) Section 199 ki list mein nahi hain [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Aur koi bhi section tabhi kaam aata hai jab record ho ki officer ko bataya gaya tha, isiliye paper trail itna zaroori hai.

**Likhit mein do:** date, time aur station, officer ka naam aur rank, aur ye line: "Failure to record this is an offence under Section 199 of the BNS." Agar station phir bhi mana kare, to Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ka Section 173(4) tumhe complaint Superintendent of Police ko post karne aur phir magistrate ke paas jaane ka raasta deta hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Woh hospital jo survivor ko lauta deta hai

BNSS ka Section 397 har hospital, sarkari ho ya private, par ye duty daalta hai ki rape, acid attack aur bachchon ke khilaaf sexual offences ke survivors ko turant first aid ya treatment free mein de, aur police ko inform kare [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Jo hospital ye rule todta hai, uske in-charge ko BNS ke Section 200 ke under one year tak jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Section ka shabd hai "immediately". Usmein kahin nahi likha ki hospital FIR, police memo ya deposit ka wait kare. Aur ghante maayne rakhte hain: HIV rokne wali dawa exposure ke 72 hours ke andar shuru honi chahiye [[who-pep]].

**Likhit mein do:** medical superintendent ya owner ke naam ek note, jismein tum kab pahunche, kisne mana kiya, aur dono section numbers hon.

## Woh school, hostel ya ghar jo bachche ka abuse chhupata hai

POCSO Act ke under, jo bhi jaanta hai ki kisi bachche ka sexual abuse hua hai, use report karna hi hoga. Case report ya record na karne par six months tak jail ya fine ho sakta hai; jo company ya institution ka head apne subordinate ke abuse ko report nahi karta, use one year tak jail aur fine ho sakta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Chup rehne ke liye bachche ko saza nahi di ja sakti.

Jo principal kehti hai "hum ise andar hi sambhaal lenge" aur teacher ka chupchaap transfer kar deti hai, woh school ko bacha nahi rahi. Woh wahi offence kar rahi hai jo Act ne uski kursi ke liye likha hai.

Data mein ye provision mushkil se dikhta hai. 2024 mein register hue 69,191 POCSO cases mein se sirf 218 Sections 17 se 22 mein the, ek aisa group jismein failure to report ke saath abetment, attempt aur false complaints bhi mila diye jaate hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Police data har FIR ko sirf ek baar, uske sabse serious offence ke under ginta hai, isliye abuse case ke saath joda gaya failure-to-report charge chhup jaata hai; phir bhi ye offence akele lagbhag kabhi register nahi hota.

**Likhit mein do:** head ko dated complaint, aur police ya Child Helpline 1098 ko apni khud ki report, taaki baad mein koi ye na keh sake ki use pata nahi tha.

## Atrocities Act ke under public servants

Dalit aur Adivasi survivors ke liye SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act officials par seedha duty clause lagata hai. 2015 mein amend hue Section 4 ke under, jo public servant Scheduled Caste ya Scheduled Tribe se nahi hai aur Act ki duties jaan-boojh kar neglect karta hai, use six months se one year tak jail ho sakti hai. In duties mein FIR sahi sections mein register karna, 60 din ke andar charge sheet file karna aur kisi bhi delay ki wajah likhit mein dena shaamil hai [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

Jo FIR lagu hone ke bawajood Act ko chhod deti hai, woh survivor se woh sab bhi chheen leti hai jo Act deta hai: Section 15A ke under state ki duty ki woh use aur uske witnesses ko intimidation se bachaye, aur court proceedings, bail hearings samet, ka notice paane ka uska right [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

**Likhit mein do:** complaint mein hi ye request ki Atrocities Act lagaya jaaye.

## POSH Act ignore karne wale employers

Yahan sabse kamzor penalty employer ki hai. Jo employer Internal Committee nahi banata, ya uski findings par action nahi leta, us par Rs 50,000 tak fine lag sakta hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Koi jail term nahi hai, aur court sirf aggrieved woman ya Internal ya Local Committee dwara authorised person ki complaint par hi action le sakta hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. 2023 mein Supreme Court ne warning di ki strict enforcement ke bina ye Act "remain an empty formality" ban kar reh jaayega [[sci-posh-enforcement-judgment-2023]].

**Likhit mein do:** HR ko email jismein poocho ki Internal Committee mein kaun hai. Agar workplace mein ten se kam log hain, ya complaint khud employer ke khilaaf hai, to district ki Local Committee case leti hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

In mein se koi bhi clause apne aap lagu nahi hota. Har ek ke liye kisi ko section ka naam lena padta hai aur dated record chhodna padta hai; District Legal Services Authority iske liye free legal aid deti hai [[nalsa]]. Officials pehle bhi jail gaye hain: Kathua case mein, June 2019 mein Pathankot ki trial court ne teen policemen ko evidence mitaane ke liye five years ki saza di [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]]. Jo desk "nahi" kehta hai, woh is bharose par kehta hai ki koi likh kar nahi rakhega.

police-misconduct-landmark-sexual-violen.en:
In a rape case the police stand between a survivor and the courtroom. They write the FIR, collect the evidence and hold the accused. In five of the most closely followed sexual-violence cases since 2002, that is exactly where the damage was done: an FIR recorded wrongly on purpose, evidence destroyed, a body cremated at night, a father dead in custody, four accused shot before any trial. Put the five side by side and ask one question: what happened to the officers?

## Gujarat, 2002: an FIR written wrong on purpose

During the 2002 Gujarat riots a pregnant woman was gang-raped and 14 of her relatives were murdered. The trial was held in Mumbai, not Gujarat. On 21 January 2008 a special court there sentenced 11 men to life imprisonment. It also convicted a police officer of deliberately recording the FIR incorrectly, and acquitted five other police personnel and two doctors [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]].

An FIR is the document every later step leans on. Written wrongly on purpose, it hands the defence its first argument. On 4 May 2017 the Bombay High Court upheld the 11 convictions and also convicted the seven who had been acquitted [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. That was fifteen years after the crime. In 2019 the Supreme Court ordered the Gujarat government to pay the survivor Rs 50 lakh and give her a job and housing [[livelaw-bilkis-compensation-2019]].

## Kathua, 2018: three policemen convicted of destroying evidence

In January 2018 an eight-year-old girl was raped and murdered in Kathua, Jammu and Kashmir. On 7 May 2018 the Supreme Court moved the trial to Pathankot in Punjab and ordered it held in camera, day to day [[theprint-kathua-transfer-2018]].

On 10 June 2019 the Pathankot court convicted six of the seven accused it tried. Three got life imprisonment for murder. Three policemen got five years each for destroying evidence. One accused was acquitted [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]]. We could not verify the outcome of the appeals.

Read those sentences together: life for the killing, five years for the men in uniform who tried to make sure it could never be proved. The law treats destroying evidence as a smaller crime than the one it hides. For a child's family, it is the same crime carried on.

## Hathras and Unnao: a cremation without consent, a death in custody

In Hathras, Uttar Pradesh, a 19-year-old Dalit woman was assaulted on 14 September 2020 and died on 29 September. Police cremated her in the middle of the night, without her family's consent [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]]. In October 2020 the Allahabad High Court called the cremation "prima facie an infringement upon the human rights of the victim and her family" [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]].

The record stops at that rebuke. We could not verify that any official was punished for that night. In March 2023 a special court acquitted three of the four men the CBI had charged, and found none of the four guilty of gang rape or murder [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]].

In the Unnao case, also in Uttar Pradesh, the man a Delhi court sentenced in December 2019 for the 2017 rape of a minor girl is a former MLA [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]]. In April 2018 the girl's father was assaulted. Police arrested him on an illegal-firearms charge, and he died in custody. On 13 March 2020 a Delhi court sentenced the former MLA and six others to 10 years' imprisonment for culpable homicide over the death [[barandbench-unnao-father-2020]]. By then the Supreme Court had moved all the Unnao trials from Lucknow to Delhi [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]].

## Hyderabad, 2019: an 'encounter' a commission called deliberate

In 2019 police shot dead four men accused of a rape and murder near Hyderabad. On 12 December 2019 the Supreme Court set up an inquiry commission under a former Supreme Court judge, V.S. Sirpurkar [[leaflet-hyderabad-encounter-sc-2022]].

The commission found that the four were "deliberately fired upon with an intent to cause their death", that three of them were minors, and that all ten police officers involved should be tried for murder [[livelaw-hyderabad-encounter-commission-2022]]. On 20 May 2022 the Supreme Court refused Telangana's request to keep the report sealed and sent the matter to the Telangana High Court [[leaflet-hyderabad-encounter-sc-2022]]. We could not confirm that any officer has been prosecuted.

The four were accused, never tried. Their deaths gave the murdered woman's family no trial and no verdict. The only process that could have established who was guilty ended with the shooting.

## What followed, and what to do if you do not trust the local police

| Case | What the record shows | What followed |
|---|---|---|
| Gujarat, 2002 | FIR deliberately recorded incorrectly | One officer convicted in 2008; five more police personnel in 2017 |
| Kathua, 2018 | Evidence destroyed | Three policemen jailed for five years |
| Hathras, 2020 | Night cremation without the family's consent | High Court rebuke; no punishment we could verify |
| Unnao, 2018 | Survivor's father arrested, died in custody | Former MLA and six others jailed for 10 years |
| Hyderabad, 2019 | Four accused shot dead | Commission wanted ten officers tried for murder; no prosecution we could confirm |

Every conviction for what was done to the case itself, the false FIR, the destroyed evidence, the death in custody, came from a court outside the state where the crime took place: Mumbai, Pathankot, Delhi. Where the matter stayed home, the record ends in a rebuke or a recommendation.

A survivor cannot order a transfer. She can build a record that the local station does not control. This is general information, not legal advice.

- **Report anywhere.** A complaint can be given at any police station, or electronically, and the victim must get a free copy of the FIR [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. If a station refuses, Section 173(4) lets you write to the Superintendent of Police and then go to a magistrate [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Refusal is a crime.** An officer who fails to record a rape complaint faces six months to two years in prison under Section 199 of the BNS [[indiacode-bns-2023]], a rule first written in 2013 [[indiacode-cla-2013]].
- **Speak to a magistrate.** Section 183(6) requires a magistrate to record the survivor's statement as soon as police learn of the offence [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. The police also owe her an update on the investigation within 90 days [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Dalit and Adivasi survivors** have more. A non-SC/ST public servant who wilfully neglects duties under the SC/ST Act faces six months to a year in prison, and Section 15A makes the state responsible for protecting victims and witnesses from intimidation [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].
- **Go higher.** Asking a High Court or the Supreme Court to move a trial or change the investigating agency takes a lawyer. Legal aid is free [[nalsa]].

None of this would have stopped a cremation at night. These rights work only when someone outside the station is watching: a magistrate, a lawyer, a higher court. Bring them in early.
police-misconduct-landmark-sexual-violen.hg:
Rape case mein survivor aur courtroom ke beech police khadi hoti hai. Wahi FIR likhti hai, wahi saboot ikattha karti hai, wahi accused ko pakad kar rakhti hai. 2002 ke baad ke paanch sabse zyada follow kiye gaye sexual-violence cases mein nuksaan theek wahin hua: jaan-boojh kar galat likhi gayi FIR, mitaye gaye saboot, raat mein jalaya gaya shareer, custody mein ek pita ki maut, aur trial se pehle hi goli se maare gaye chaar accused. Paanchon ko saath rakhiye aur ek hi sawaal poochiye: officers ke saath kya hua?

## Gujarat, 2002: jaan-boojh kar galat likhi gayi FIR

2002 ke Gujarat riots ke dauraan ek pregnant aurat ka gang rape hua aur uske 14 rishtedaaron ka murder hua. Trial Gujarat mein nahi, Mumbai mein chala. 21 January 2008 ko wahan ki special court ne 11 aadmiyon ko umrqaid di. Usi court ne ek police officer ko FIR jaan-boojh kar galat record karne ke liye convict kiya, aur paanch doosre police personnel aur do doctors ko bari kar diya [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]].

FIR woh document hai jis par aage ka har kadam tika hota hai. Agar use jaan-boojh kar galat likha jaaye, toh defence ko pehla argument wahin se mil jaata hai. 4 May 2017 ko Bombay High Court ne 11 convictions ko barkarar rakha aur jo saat log bari hue the, unhe bhi convict kiya [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. Tab tak crime ko pandrah saal ho chuke the. 2019 mein Supreme Court ne Gujarat sarkar ko survivor ko Rs 50 lakh, ek naukri aur ghar dene ka order diya [[livelaw-bilkis-compensation-2019]].

## Kathua, 2018: teen policewale saboot mitane ke convict

January 2018 mein Jammu and Kashmir ke Kathua mein ek aath saal ki bachchi ka rape aur murder hua. 7 May 2018 ko Supreme Court ne trial ko Punjab ke Pathankot bhej diya aur order diya ki sunwaai band kamre mein (in camera), roz-roz ho [[theprint-kathua-transfer-2018]].

10 June 2019 ko Pathankot court ne jin saat accused ka trial kiya, unme se chhe ko convict kiya. Teen ko murder ke liye umrqaid mili. Teen policewalon ko saboot mitane ke liye paanch-paanch saal ki saza mili. Ek accused bari hua [[theprint-kathua-verdict-2019]]. Appeals ka natija hum verify nahi kar paaye.

In sazaon ko saath padhiye: qatl ke liye umrqaid, aur un vardi walon ke liye paanch saal jinhone koshish ki ki yeh qatl kabhi saabit hi na ho sake. Law saboot mitane ko us crime se chhota maanta hai jise woh chhupata hai. Ek bachchi ki family ke liye yeh wahi crime hai, bas aage badhaya hua.

## Hathras aur Unnao: bina consent ka cremation, custody mein maut

Uttar Pradesh ke Hathras mein 14 September 2020 ko ek 19 saal ki Dalit ladki par hamla hua aur 29 September ko uski maut ho gayi. Police ne aadhi raat ko, family ki consent ke bina, uska cremation kar diya [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]]. October 2020 mein Allahabad High Court ne is cremation ko "prima facie an infringement upon the human rights of the victim and her family" kaha [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]].

Record us daant par ruk jaata hai. Hum verify nahi kar paaye ki us raat ke liye kisi official ko saza mili. March 2023 mein ek special court ne CBI ke charge kiye chaar aadmiyon mein se teen ko bari kar diya, aur chaaron mein se kisi ko gang rape ya murder ka doshi nahi paaya [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]].

Unnao case mein, jo Uttar Pradesh mein hi hai, jis aadmi ko December 2019 mein Delhi ki ek court ne ek nabalig ladki ke 2017 ke rape ke liye saza di, woh ek former MLA hai [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]]. April 2018 mein ladki ke pita par hamla hua. Police ne unhe illegal hathiyaar ke charge mein giraftaar kiya, aur custody mein unki maut ho gayi. 13 March 2020 ko Delhi ki ek court ne us maut ke liye former MLA aur chhe aur logon ko culpable homicide mein 10 saal ki jail di [[barandbench-unnao-father-2020]]. Tab tak Supreme Court Unnao ke saare trials Lucknow se Delhi bhej chuka tha [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]].

## Hyderabad, 2019: ek 'encounter' jise commission ne jaan-boojh kar kiya gaya kaha

2019 mein Hyderabad ke paas police ne ek rape aur murder ke chaar accused ko goli maar di. 12 December 2019 ko Supreme Court ne former Supreme Court judge V.S. Sirpurkar ki adhyakshta mein ek inquiry commission banaya [[leaflet-hyderabad-encounter-sc-2022]].

Commission ne paaya ki chaaron par "deliberately fired upon with an intent to cause their death", yaani maarne ke iraade se jaan-boojh kar goli chalayi gayi, ki unme se teen nabalig the, aur ki is mein shaamil saare das police officers par murder ka trial hona chahiye [[livelaw-hyderabad-encounter-commission-2022]]. 20 May 2022 ko Supreme Court ne Telangana ki report seal rakhne ki maang thukra di aur maamla Telangana High Court ko bhej diya [[leaflet-hyderabad-encounter-sc-2022]]. Hum confirm nahi kar paaye ki kisi officer par mukadma chala.

Woh chaar sirf accused the, unka trial kabhi nahi hua. Unki maut ne murder hui aurat ki family ko na trial diya, na faisla. Jo ek process saabit kar sakta tha ki doshi kaun hai, woh goli chalne ke saath hi khatam ho gaya.

## Aage kya hua, aur agar local police par bharosa na ho toh kya karein

| Case | Record kya dikhata hai | Aage kya hua |
|---|---|---|
| Gujarat, 2002 | FIR jaan-boojh kar galat record ki gayi | 2008 mein ek officer convict; 2017 mein paanch aur police personnel |
| Kathua, 2018 | Saboot mitaye gaye | Teen policewalon ko paanch saal ki jail |
| Hathras, 2020 | Family ki consent ke bina raat mein cremation | High Court ki daant; koi saza jo hum verify kar sakein, nahi |
| Unnao, 2018 | Survivor ke pita giraftaar, custody mein maut | Former MLA aur chhe aur ko 10 saal ki jail |
| Hyderabad, 2019 | Chaar accused goli se maare gaye | Commission chahta tha das officers par murder trial; koi mukadma jo hum confirm kar sakein, nahi |

Case ke saath jo kiya gaya, yaani galat FIR, mitaye gaye saboot, custody mein maut, uske liye har conviction us state ke bahar ki court se aaya jahan crime hua tha: Mumbai, Pathankot, Delhi. Jahan maamla ghar mein hi raha, wahan record ek daant ya ek sifarish par khatam hota hai.

Survivor khud transfer ka order nahi de sakti. Lekin woh ek aisa record bana sakti hai jo local thane ke control mein na ho. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

- **Kahin bhi report kijiye.** Complaint kisi bhi police station mein, ya electronic tareeke se di ja sakti hai, aur victim ko FIR ki free copy milni chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Agar thana mana kare, toh Section 173(4) aapko Superintendent of Police ko likhne aur phir magistrate ke paas jaane ka raasta deta hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Mana karna crime hai.** Jo officer rape ki complaint record nahi karta, use BNS ke Section 199 ke tahat chhe mahine se do saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Yeh rule pehli baar 2013 mein likha gaya tha [[indiacode-cla-2013]].
- **Magistrate se baat kijiye.** Section 183(6) ke mutabik, police ko offence ka pata chalte hi magistrate ko survivor ka statement record karna hota hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Police ko 90 din ke andar investigation ka update bhi dena hota hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Dalit aur Adivasi survivors** ke paas aur bhi hai. Jo non-SC/ST public servant SC/ST Act ke tahat apni duty jaan-boojh kar nazarandaaz kare, use chhe mahine se ek saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai, aur Section 15A victims aur witnesses ko dhamki se bachana state ki zimmedari banata hai [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].
- **Upar jaaiye.** High Court ya Supreme Court se trial transfer karwane ya investigating agency badalwane ke liye lawyer chahiye. Legal aid free hai [[nalsa]].

Inme se koi bhi cheez raat ke us cremation ko nahi rok paati. Yeh rights tabhi kaam karte hain jab thane ke bahar koi dekh raha ho: ek magistrate, ek lawyer, ek higher court. Unhe jaldi shaamil kijiye.

posh-act-political-parties-bar-councils-.en:
Picture a 24-year-old who has spent three years knocking on doors for a political party. She is not paid. A senior office-bearer starts sending her messages at night, then decides who gets a ticket for the municipal election. If she worked in a bank, the law would require her employer to have a committee to hear her complaint. In 2025 India's courts made clear that, because she volunteers for a party, nobody is required to have one for her.

This is general information, not legal advice.

## Political parties: "a Pandora's box"

On 15 September 2025 a three-judge Supreme Court bench led by Chief Justice B.R. Gavai dismissed a challenge to a 2022 Kerala High Court ruling that political parties need not set up Internal Complaints Committees under the POSH Act. "How do you equate political parties as workplace?" the bench asked, adding that bringing parties under the Act "will open a Pandora's box to blackmail the members". Joining a party, it reasoned, is voluntary and unpaid, so it is not employment [[tribune-sc-posh-political-parties-2025]].

The Kerala High Court had held in March 2022 that parties have no employer-employee relationship with their members and so are not bound to form such committees [[kerala-hc-wcc-judgment-2022]]. The petitioner had tried other routes first. In December 2024 the Supreme Court sent her to the Election Commission; she wrote to it in March 2025 and, by August, had received no reply. On 1 August 2025 the court declined a fresh public interest petition, saying "This falls within the Parliament's domain ... It is a policy matter" [[thenewsminute-sc-posh-parties-pil-2025]]. The September order closed the last door in court. The petitioner told the court that only one party, the CPI(M), had an internal complaints committee of any kind [[tribune-sc-posh-political-parties-2025]].

## Lawyers: Bar Councils are "not employers"

On 7 July 2025 the Bombay High Court decided a public interest petition asking for permanent committees for women advocates in the Bar Councils of Maharashtra and Goa. It held that "the provisions of the POSH Act apply where the relationship of employer and employee exists", and that "neither Bar Council of India nor Bar Council of Maharashtra & Goa can be said to be employer of advocates" [[scconline-bombay-hc-posh-advocates-2025]]. Bar Council staff are covered; advocates complaining about other advocates are not. The court pointed instead to Section 35 of the Advocates Act, which lets anyone complain to a State Bar Council about an advocate's misconduct [[scconline-bombay-hc-posh-advocates-2025]].

That is not the end. On 21 November 2025 the Supreme Court issued notice on an appeal by the Supreme Court Women Lawyers Association against the ruling [[barandbench-sc-posh-bar-councils-notice-2025]]. A disciplinary complaint to a body of lawyers about another lawyer is a very different thing from a committee with a mandatory outside member, half of them women, which the POSH Act requires [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

## The same line, drawn three times

Put the 2025 decisions next to one another and a single line appears. The POSH Act's language is wide: it protects any woman "of any age whether employed or not" who is harassed at a workplace [[gazette-posh-act-2013]], and its definition of workplace reaches entertainment businesses, hospitals, sports venues and even private homes where domestic workers are employed [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. But the courts have read the duty to provide a complaints committee as tied to an employer.

The same gap showed up in the film industry. The Kerala High Court has orally remarked that the Act does not cover harassment faced by women who are still seeking work, such as at an audition, and in October 2025 the Kerala government told the court a separate law for the entertainment industry was being drafted [[livelaw-kerala-hc-hema-draft-law-2025]]. Volunteers, independent professionals and job-seekers are exactly the people with the least power and the most to lose by complaining. They are also the ones the employer-based model misses.

## What is left

The courts' worry about misuse is real, but so is the alternative: no forum at all except the police. The criminal law still applies everywhere. The BNS punishes sexual harassment with up to 3 years and stalking with up to 3 years, rising to 5 for a repeat offence [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The district Local Committee hears complaints where the employer itself is accused or the workplace is very small [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. And Parliament, which the Supreme Court said owns this question, can widen the Act whenever it chooses. Until it does, parties can adopt committees voluntarily, and women inside them can ask, in writing, whether theirs has one.
posh-act-political-parties-bar-councils-.hg:
Socho ek 24 saal ki ladki hai jo teen saal se ek political party ke liye ghar ghar ja rahi hai. Use paise nahi milte. Ek senior office-bearer use raat ko messages bhejne lagta hai, aur phir wahi tay karta hai ki municipal election mein ticket kise milega. Agar woh bank mein kaam karti, toh law uske employer ko uski complaint sunne ke liye committee rakhne ko majboor karta. 2025 mein India ke courts ne saaf kar diya ki kyunki woh party ke liye volunteer karti hai, isliye kisi ki zimmedari nahi ki uske liye committee rakhe.

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Political parties: "a Pandora's box"

15 September 2025 ko Chief Justice B.R. Gavai ki teen judges wali Supreme Court bench ne Kerala High Court ke 2022 ke us faisle ke khilaf challenge khaarij kar diya jisme kaha gaya tha ki political parties ko POSH Act ke under Internal Complaints Committees banane ki zaroorat nahi. "How do you equate political parties as workplace?" bench ne poocha, aur kaha ki parties ko Act ke under laana "will open a Pandora's box to blackmail the members". Court ka reasoning tha ki party join karna voluntary aur unpaid hai, isliye yeh employment nahi [[tribune-sc-posh-political-parties-2025]].

Kerala High Court ne March 2022 mein kaha tha ki parties ka apne members ke saath employer-employee relationship nahi hota, isliye woh aisi committees banane ke liye bound nahi [[kerala-hc-wcc-judgment-2022]]. Petitioner ne pehle doosre raaste try kiye the. December 2024 mein Supreme Court ne use Election Commission ke paas bheja; usne March 2025 mein Commission ko likha aur August tak koi jawab nahi aaya. 1 August 2025 ko court ne ek nayi public interest petition sunne se mana kar diya, yeh kehte hue ki "This falls within the Parliament's domain ... It is a policy matter" [[thenewsminute-sc-posh-parties-pil-2025]]. September ke order ne court ka aakhri darwaaza bhi band kar diya. Petitioner ne court ko bataya ki sirf ek party, CPI(M), ke paas kisi tarah ki internal complaints committee thi [[tribune-sc-posh-political-parties-2025]].

## Lawyers: Bar Councils "employer nahi"

7 July 2025 ko Bombay High Court ne ek public interest petition decide ki jisme Maharashtra aur Goa ki Bar Councils mein women advocates ke liye permanent committees maangi gayi thi. Court ne kaha ki "the provisions of the POSH Act apply where the relationship of employer and employee exists", aur "neither Bar Council of India nor Bar Council of Maharashtra & Goa can be said to be employer of advocates" [[scconline-bombay-hc-posh-advocates-2025]]. Bar Council ka staff covered hai; doosre advocates ke khilaf complaint karne wali advocates nahi. Court ne iski jagah Advocates Act ke Section 35 ki taraf ishaara kiya, jo kisi ko bhi kisi advocate ke misconduct ki complaint State Bar Council mein karne deta hai [[scconline-bombay-hc-posh-advocates-2025]].

Kahani yahan khatam nahi hoti. 21 November 2025 ko Supreme Court ne is faisle ke khilaf Supreme Court Women Lawyers Association ki appeal par notice jaari kiya [[barandbench-sc-posh-bar-councils-notice-2025]]. Lawyers ki ek body mein doosre lawyer ke khilaf disciplinary complaint, us committee se bahut alag cheez hai jisme ek bahar ka member zaroori ho aur aadhe members women hon, jaisa POSH Act maangta hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

## Ek hi line, teen baar kheenchi gayi

2025 ke faislon ko saath rakho toh ek line dikhti hai. POSH Act ki bhasha chaudi hai: yeh har woman ko protect karta hai, "of any age whether employed or not", jo workplace par harass hoti hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]], aur iski workplace ki definition entertainment businesses, hospitals, sports venues aur un gharon tak jaati hai jahan domestic workers kaam karti hain [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Lekin courts ne complaints committee dene ki duty ko employer se joda hai.

Film industry mein bhi yahi gap dikha. Kerala High Court ne oral remark kiya hai ki Act un women ki harassment cover nahi karta jo abhi kaam dhoondh rahi hain, jaise audition par, aur October 2025 mein Kerala government ne court ko bataya ki entertainment industry ke liye ek alag law ka draft ban raha hai [[livelaw-kerala-hc-hema-draft-law-2025]]. Volunteers, independent professionals aur kaam dhoondhne wali women hi woh log hain jinke paas sabse kam power hai aur complaint karke sabse zyada khone ko hai. Employer-based model inhi ko miss karta hai.

## Kya bachta hai

Misuse ko lekar courts ki chinta asli hai, lekin doosra raasta bhi asli hai: police ke alawa koi forum nahi. Criminal law har jagah lagu hota hai. BNS sexual harassment ke liye 3 saal tak aur stalking ke liye 3 saal tak ki saza deta hai, jo dobara karne par 5 saal tak ho jaati hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. District ki Local Committee un complaints ko sunti hai jahan khud employer par aarop ho ya workplace bahut chhota ho [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Aur Parliament, jise Supreme Court ne is sawaal ka maalik bataya, jab chahe Act ko chauda kar sakti hai. Tab tak parties apni marzi se committees bana sakti hain, aur unke andar ki women likhit mein pooch sakti hain ki kya unki party mein ek hai.

rape-accused-legal-myths-checked.en:
Every few months a rape case reaches the national news, and the same lines spread within hours: he will never get bail, let him prove he is innocent, hang him, and if police finish him off, good. The anger is real and often justified. The beliefs underneath it mostly are not. Indian courts convicted the accused in only 24.4% of rape trials completed in 2024, and 1,85,785 rape cases were waiting for trial at the end of that year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A system in which three of every four completed trials already end without a conviction cannot afford a public that misunderstands it. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Myth: no rape accused ever gets bail

The truth is narrower. Section 482(4) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 bars anticipatory bail, the protection a person seeks before arrest, only for two offences: raping a girl under 16, and gang rape of a girl under 18 [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. For every other rape charge, an accused can apply for bail before or after arrest, and a judge decides.

Bail is not a verdict. It means the court thinks the accused can wait for trial outside jail without fleeing or threatening anyone. What the law does control is the conditions. In 2021 the Supreme Court struck down a High Court condition that asked a man accused of sexual assault to have the complainant tie a rakhi on him, and ruled that bail conditions must not require or permit contact with the survivor [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. That is the fight worth having: not "no bail ever", but "no bail that puts her at risk".

## Myth: the accused must prove he is innocent

In most criminal trials in India, the prosecution must prove guilt. A major exception is child sexual abuse. Under Section 29 of the POCSO Act, a Special Court must presume that a person prosecuted for penetrative or sexual assault on a child committed the offence unless the contrary is proved [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

For adult women the law shifts something smaller.
