In aggravated rape cases, such as rape by a police officer, public servant, relative, guardian or hospital staff, once intercourse is proved and the woman testifies she did not consent, the court must presume she did not consent [[indiacode-bsa-2023]]. The prosecution still has to prove that the act happened and who did it. That is why the quality of the medical examination, the FIR and the investigation matters so much.

## Myth: every rape carries the death penalty

Rape under Section 64 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) carries at least 10 years' rigorous imprisonment and up to life. Thirteen aggravated forms, including rape by police, relatives, guardians or teachers, carry 10 years up to imprisonment for the rest of the person's natural life [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Death is possible only in a few categories: raping a girl under 12, rape that causes the woman's death or leaves her in a persistent vegetative state, gang rape of a girl under 18, and a second rape conviction [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The Justice Verma Committee, set up after the 2012 Delhi gang rape, advised against the death penalty for rape, noting it "may not have a deterrent effect" [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Even where death is allowed, courts must weigh the facts. In 2014 a Mumbai sessions court used the repeat-offender provision of the old IPC to sentence three men in the 2013 Shakti Mills gang rape cases to death [[livelaw-shakti-mills-death-sentence-2014]]. In 2021 the Bombay High Court commuted all three sentences to life imprisonment, holding that a constitutional court cannot award punishment based on public opinion [[barandbench-shakti-mills-hc-2021]].

> A harsher maximum means little when three of every four completed rape trials end without a conviction. Certainty of punishment does more work than severity.

## Myth: teenage accused always walk free

Since the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, a Juvenile Justice Board must make a "preliminary assessment" of any child aged 16 or above accused of a heinous offence, one with a minimum punishment of seven years or more. The Board can send that case to a Children's Court for trial as an adult [[gazette-juvenile-justice-act-2015]]. Rape is a heinous offence under this test.

The system also gets tested in practice. In 2022 the Supreme Court ruled that an accused in the Kathua case, earlier declared a juvenile, must be tried as an adult [[scroll-kathua-juvenile-2022]]. The Act is built on a choice: hold older teenagers to account for the gravest crimes, through a Board's assessment rather than an automatic rule, and keep the chance of reform for people who were children when they offended.

## Myth: an "encounter" is justice

In 2019, Telangana police shot dead four men accused of the rape and murder of a woman near Hyderabad. A commission appointed by the Supreme Court later found that the four were "deliberately fired upon with an intent to cause their death", that three of the four were minors, and recommended that all ten police officers involved be tried for murder [[livelaw-hyderabad-encounter-commission-2022]].

Consider what that means. No court ever tested whether those four men committed the crime. If they did not, the person who did was never looked for. The woman's family received no verdict, only a police story that a commission called false. An encounter does not deliver justice faster. It replaces the question "who did this?" with "who can police shoot?", and anyone, including a survivor's own brother or son, can end up on the wrong side of that question.

Every shortcut in this list weakens the case that a survivor needs to win. A trial is the only process that can name a man guilty and keep that conviction standing on appeal. What actually helps is a prompt FIR, a careful medical examination, a charge sheet filed on time and a trial that does not drag on for years. Ask for those, loudly, and treat anyone who offers you a quicker kind of justice with suspicion.
rape-accused-legal-myths-checked.hg:
Har kuch mahine mein koi rape case national news tak pahunchta hai, aur ghanton mein wahi lines failne lagti hain: use kabhi bail nahi milegi, use prove karne do ki woh innocent hai, phaansi do, aur agar police ne use khatam kar diya toh achha hua. Gussa asli hai aur aksar sahi bhi. Lekin uske neeche wali zyada tar baatein sahi nahi hain. 2024 mein jo rape trials poore hue, unme Indian courts ne sirf 24.4% mein accused ko convict kiya, aur us saal ke end tak 1,85,785 rape cases trial ka intezaar kar rahe the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jis system mein pehle hi har chaar mein se teen poore hue trials bina conviction ke khatam hote hain, woh aisi public afford nahi kar sakta jo use galat samjhe. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Myth: rape ke kisi accused ko kabhi bail nahi milti

Sach isse kaafi narrow hai. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 ka Section 482(4) anticipatory bail, yaani arrest se pehle maangi jaane wali protection, sirf do offences ke liye rokta hai: 16 saal se kam umar ki ladki ka rape, aur 18 saal se kam umar ki ladki ka gang rape [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Baaki har rape charge mein accused arrest se pehle ya baad bail ke liye apply kar sakta hai, aur faisla judge karta hai.

Bail verdict nahi hai. Iska matlab bas itna hai ki court ko lagta hai accused bina bhaage ya kisi ko dhamkaaye jail ke bahar trial ka intezaar kar sakta hai. Law jo control karta hai, woh hai bail ki conditions. 2021 mein Supreme Court ne High Court ki woh condition hata di jisme sexual assault ke ek accused se kaha gaya tha ki complainant se rakhi bandhwaye, aur kaha ki bail conditions survivor se contact ki maang ya ijaazat nahi de sakti [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. Ladne layak ladaai yahi hai: "kabhi bail nahi" nahi, balki "aisi bail nahi jo use khatre mein daale".

## Myth: accused ko prove karna padta hai ki woh innocent hai

India mein zyada tar criminal trials mein guilt prosecution ko prove karna padta hai. Ek bada exception hai child sexual abuse. POCSO Act ke Section 29 ke tahat Special Court ko maanna padta hai ki jis person par kisi bachche ke saath penetrative ya sexual assault ka case chal raha hai, usne offence kiya hai, jab tak ulta prove na ho [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Adult aurton ke case mein law isse chhoti cheez shift karta hai. Aggravated rape cases mein, jaise police officer, public servant, rishtedaar, guardian ya hospital staff dwara rape, jab intercourse prove ho jaaye aur aurat gawahi de ki usne consent nahi diya, toh court ko maanna padta hai ki consent nahi tha [[indiacode-bsa-2023]]. Phir bhi prosecution ko prove karna padta hai ki act hua aur kisne kiya. Isiliye medical examination, FIR aur investigation ki quality itni zaroori hai.

## Myth: har rape mein death penalty hai

Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 64 ke tahat rape ki saza kam se kam 10 saal ki rigorous imprisonment hai aur life tak ja sakti hai. Terah aggravated forms, jaise police, rishtedaar, guardian ya teacher dwara rape, mein 10 saal se lekar baaki ki poori natural life tak ki jail hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Death sirf kuch categories mein possible hai: 12 saal se kam umar ki ladki ka rape, aisa rape jisse aurat ki maut ho jaaye ya woh persistent vegetative state mein chali jaaye, 18 saal se kam umar ki ladki ka gang rape, aur rape mein doosri baar conviction [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. 2012 ke Delhi gang rape ke baad bani Justice Verma Committee ne rape ke liye death penalty ke khilaf salaah di thi, yeh note karte hue ki yeh "may not have a deterrent effect" [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Jahan death allowed hai, wahan bhi courts ko facts tolne padte hain. 2014 mein Mumbai ke ek sessions court ne purane IPC ke repeat-offender provision ka use karke 2013 ke Shakti Mills gang rape cases mein teen aadmiyon ko death sentence diya [[livelaw-shakti-mills-death-sentence-2014]]. 2021 mein Bombay High Court ne teeno sentences ko life imprisonment mein badal diya, yeh kehte hue ki constitutional court public opinion ke basis par saza nahi de sakta [[barandbench-shakti-mills-hc-2021]].

> Jab har chaar mein se teen poore hue rape trials bina conviction ke khatam hote hain, toh sakht maximum saza ka matlab kam reh jaata hai. Saza milne ki certainty, saza ki sakhti se zyada kaam karti hai.

## Myth: teenage accused hamesha chhoot jaate hain

Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 ke baad se, Juvenile Justice Board ko 16 saal ya usse bade kisi bhi bachche ka "preliminary assessment" karna hota hai jis par heinous offence ka aarop ho, yaani aisa offence jiski minimum saza saat saal ya zyada hai. Board us case ko adult ki tarah trial ke liye Children's Court bhej sakta hai [[gazette-juvenile-justice-act-2015]]. Is test ke hisaab se rape heinous offence hai.

Yeh system practice mein bhi test hota hai. 2022 mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki Kathua case ke ek accused, jise pehle juvenile declare kiya gaya tha, ka trial adult ki tarah hona chahiye [[scroll-kathua-juvenile-2022]]. Act ek choice par bana hai: sabse gambhir crimes ke liye bade teenagers ko jawabdeh banao, automatic rule se nahi balki Board ke assessment se, aur jo log offence ke waqt bachche the, unke liye sudharne ka mauka bachaa ke rakho.

## Myth: "encounter" hi insaaf hai

2019 mein Telangana police ne Hyderabad ke paas ek aurat ke rape aur murder ke chaar accused aadmiyon ko goli maar di. Supreme Court ke appoint kiye gaye ek commission ne baad mein paaya ki chaaron par "deliberately fired upon with an intent to cause their death", ki chaar mein se teen minors the, aur salaah di ki involved saare das police officers par murder ka trial chale [[livelaw-hyderabad-encounter-commission-2022]].

Socho iska matlab kya hai. Kisi court ne kabhi test nahi kiya ki un chaar aadmiyon ne crime kiya tha ya nahi. Agar nahi kiya tha, toh jisne kiya use kabhi dhoondha hi nahi gaya. Aurat ki family ko koi verdict nahi mila, sirf ek police story mili jise commission ne jhooth kaha. Encounter insaaf jaldi nahi deta. Woh sawaal "yeh kisne kiya?" ko badal kar "police kise goli maar sakti hai?" bana deta hai, aur koi bhi, survivor ka apna bhai ya beta bhi, us sawaal ki galat taraf khada ho sakta hai.

Is list ka har shortcut us case ko kamzor karta hai jo survivor ko jeetna hai. Trial hi woh akela process hai jo kisi aadmi ko guilty bata sakta hai aur appeal mein bhi woh conviction tikaa sakta hai. Asli madad karti hai turant FIR, dhyan se kiya gaya medical examination, time par file hui charge sheet aur aisa trial jo saalon tak na ghisate. Inki maang zor se karo, aur jo bhi tumhe insaaf ka koi "shortcut" offer kare, us par shak karo.

rape-by-relative-guardian-teacher-law.en:
The hardest rape to report is the one committed by someone who sits at the same dinner table, pays the school fees or marks the exam papers. In 2024 police registered 2,134 rape cases against family members and 12,584 against family friends, neighbours, employers and other known persons [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Under the POCSO Act, family members were the accused in 3,658 cases of penetrative assault on children that year [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. These are only the cases that reached the police. The answers below explain what the law does when the accused is someone trusted, and how to use it without staying under his roof. This is general information, not legal advice.

## What does the law call "aggravated", and why does it matter?

Rape under Section 64 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) is punishable with at least 10 years' rigorous imprisonment and up to life. Section 64(2) lists 13 aggravated forms. One is rape by a relative, guardian or teacher of the woman, or by anyone in a position of trust or authority towards her. Others cover police, public servants, hospital staff and repeated rape of the same woman [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

For these, the sentence is 10 years to imprisonment for the rest of the offender's natural life [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The legal message is that betraying trust is not a mitigating "family matter". It makes the crime worse.

If the survivor is under 18, the case goes under POCSO. Aggravated penetrative sexual assault on a child carries at least 20 years up to the rest of natural life, or death [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. POCSO protects boys as well as girls. The BNS rape section protects only women, and the new code has no offence covering non-consensual sex against an adult man or a transgender person, a gap survivors and lawyers should know about [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## What changes when the accused is a relative?

In most rape trials, the defence argues about consent. For the aggravated forms in Section 64(2), Section 120 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam changes the starting point. Once sexual intercourse by the accused is proved and the woman tells the court she did not consent, the court must presume she did not consent [[indiacode-bsa-2023]].

"Must presume" means the fact is treated as proved unless the defence disproves it. That matters in homes, where pressure rarely looks like force from the outside. An uncle, a stepfather or a tutor does not need to threaten anyone when he controls the house, the money or the marks.

## Do I have to give my statement in the same house as him?

No. This is where the law's default can work against a survivor, and where she has a choice.

Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), a rape complaint must be recorded by a woman police officer or woman officer. The survivor's statement must be recorded at her residence or at a place of her choice, as far as practicable by a woman officer, and can be video-recorded, including on a mobile phone [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Police also cannot require a woman to come anywhere other than where she lives, though she may choose to go to the station [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

"Residence" is the default, not the rule. When the accused lives in that residence, choose another place: a trusted relative's home, a friend's flat, an NGO office or a One Stop Centre.

A magistrate, as far as practicable a woman magistrate, must also record the survivor's statement as soon as police learn of the offence [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. That statement is taken by a magistrate, not by the police, and not in front of the family.

Consider this situation. A 19-year-old in Bhopal tells her college counsellor that her cousin, who lives with them, has raped her. If police arrive at home to record her statement, he and the relatives who will defend him are in the next room. If she asks for the statement at the district One Stop Centre, she speaks without an audience.

## Where can I go if I need to leave the house?

One Stop Centres, also called Sakhi centres, bring together medical help, police assistance, legal aid, counselling and temporary shelter for women facing violence [[wcd-mission-shakti]]. As of July 2026, 985 of the 1,033 approved centres were operational, and they had assisted over 15.20 lakh women since April 2015 [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]]. The Women Helpline can connect you to the nearest one.

The domestic violence law counts sexual abuse as domestic violence. It is mainly civil: a magistrate can pass protection, residence and maintenance orders, and breaching a protection order is punishable with up to one year in prison or a Rs 20,000 fine [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. These are civil orders, separate from the rape case.

Compensation does not have to wait. A survivor can apply directly to the District Legal Services Authority, even if no trial takes place [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## What if the family pushes me to drop it?

Expect it. The accused may be a breadwinner, an elder or someone the family wants to protect. It may come as talk of the family's name, an apology, or an offer of money or marriage.

Courts are not supposed to treat rape as something for the family to settle. In 2021 the Supreme Court ruled that bail conditions must not require or permit the accused to contact the victim, and that judges must not suggest compromise or marriage [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. If anyone, including an elder, a neighbour or a panchayat, pressures you to withdraw, keep a record and tell the prosecutor or the court.

> Being related to the accused does not weaken the case. In law, it is the reason the charge is aggravated.

If you are the person a survivor tells, believe her first, help her get to a safe place, and let her decide how fast to move. If she is under 18, the law requires anyone who knows of the abuse to report it [[indiacode-pocso-2012]], so tell her honestly that you cannot keep it secret, and call 1098 together.
rape-by-relative-guardian-teacher-law.hg:
Sabse mushkil rape report karna woh hota hai jo kisi aise insaan ne kiya ho jo usi dinner table pe baithta hai, school ki fees bharta hai ya exam papers check karta hai. 2024 mein police ne family members ke khilaaf 2,134 rape cases register kiye, aur family friends, padosiyon, employers aur doosre jaan-pehchaan walon ke khilaaf 12,584 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. POCSO Act ke under, us saal bachchon pe penetrative assault ke 3,658 cases mein accused family member tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh sirf woh cases hain jo police tak pahunche. Neeche ke jawaab batate hain ki jab accused koi bharose wala ho toh law kya karta hai, aur uski chhat ke neeche rahe bina law ko kaise use karna hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Law kise "aggravated" kehta hai, aur iska matlab kya hai?

Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 64 ke under rape ki saza kam se kam 10 saal ki rigorous imprisonment hai, aur life tak ho sakti hai. Section 64(2) mein 13 aggravated forms hain. Inme se ek hai aurat ke rishtedaar, guardian ya teacher dwara rape, ya kisi bhi aise insaan dwara jo uske upar bharose ya authority ki position mein ho. Baaki mein police, public servants, hospital staff aur ek hi aurat ka baar-baar rape shaamil hain [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

In cases mein saza 10 saal se lekar offender ki baaki poori zindagi ki qaid tak hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Law ka message saaf hai: bharosa todna koi narmi wala "ghar ka maamla" nahi hai. Yeh crime ko aur bhaari banata hai.

Agar survivor 18 se kam hai, toh case POCSO ke under jaata hai. Bachche pe aggravated penetrative sexual assault ki saza kam se kam 20 saal se lekar baaki poori zindagi ki qaid, ya maut tak hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. POCSO ladkiyon ke saath ladkon ko bhi protect karta hai. BNS ka rape section sirf aurton ko protect karta hai, aur naye code mein kisi adult aadmi ya transgender insaan ke saath bina consent sex ke liye koi offence nahi hai. Survivors aur lawyers ko yeh gap pata hona chahiye [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Jab accused rishtedaar ho toh kya badalta hai?

Zyada tar rape trials mein defence consent pe behas karta hai. Section 64(2) ke aggravated forms ke liye, Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam ka Section 120 starting point badal deta hai. Ek baar accused ka sexual intercourse prove ho jaaye aur aurat court ko bataaye ki usne consent nahi diya, toh court ko maanna hi hoga ki usne consent nahi diya [[indiacode-bsa-2023]].

"Maanna hi hoga" ka matlab hai ki yeh baat proved maani jaayegi jab tak defence ise galat sabit na kare. Gharon mein yeh bahut maayne rakhta hai, jahan pressure bahar se kabhi zor-zabardasti jaisa nahi dikhta. Ek chacha, sautela baap ya tutor ko kisi ko dhamkaane ki zaroorat nahi padti jab ghar, paisa ya marks uske haath mein hon.

## Kya mujhe usi ghar mein statement dena padega jahan woh hai?

Nahi. Yahi woh jagah hai jahan law ka default survivor ke khilaaf ja sakta hai, aur jahan uske paas choice hai.

Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ke under rape ki complaint woman police officer ya woman officer record karegi. Survivor ka statement uske ghar pe ya uski pasand ki jagah pe record hona chahiye, jahan tak ho sake woman officer dwara, aur iski video recording ho sakti hai, mobile phone pe bhi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Police kisi aurat ko jahan woh rehti hai uske alawa kahin aur aane ke liye majboor bhi nahi kar sakti, haalanki woh khud station jaana chune toh ja sakti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

"Ghar" default hai, rule nahi. Jab accused usi ghar mein rehta hai, toh doosri jagah chuno: kisi bharosemand rishtedaar ka ghar, dost ka flat, kisi NGO ka office ya One Stop Centre.

Ek magistrate, jahan tak ho sake woman magistrate, ko bhi police ko offence ka pata chalte hi survivor ka statement record karna hota hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Yeh statement police nahi, magistrate leta hai, aur family ke saamne nahi.

Yeh situation socho. Bhopal mein ek 19 saal ki ladki apne college counsellor ko batati hai ki uske cousin ne, jo unke saath rehta hai, uska rape kiya. Agar police uska statement lene ghar aati hai, toh woh aur uska bachaav karne wale rishtedaar bagal wale kamre mein hain. Agar woh district ke One Stop Centre pe statement dene ko kehti hai, toh woh bina kisi audience ke bolti hai.

## Agar ghar chhodna pade toh kahan jaaun?

One Stop Centres, jinhe Sakhi centres bhi kehte hain, violence jhel rahi aurton ke liye medical help, police assistance, legal aid, counselling aur temporary shelter ek jagah dete hain [[wcd-mission-shakti]]. July 2026 tak approve hue 1,033 centres mein se 985 chal rahe the, aur April 2015 se inhone 15.20 lakh se zyada aurton ki madad ki thi [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]]. Women Helpline tumhe sabse paas wale centre se jod sakti hai.

Domestic violence law sexual abuse ko domestic violence maanta hai. Yeh zyada tar civil law hai: magistrate protection, residence aur maintenance orders de sakta hai, aur protection order todne pe ek saal tak ki jail ya Rs 20,000 tak ka fine ho sakta hai [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Yeh civil orders hain, rape case se alag.

Compensation ke liye wait zaroori nahi. Survivor seedha District Legal Services Authority mein apply kar sakti hai, chahe trial ho hi na [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Agar family case wapas lene ka pressure daale toh?

Iski ummeed rakho. Accused ghar ka kamaane wala, koi bada ya koi aisa ho sakta hai jise family bachana chahti hai. Pressure family ki izzat ki baat, ek maafi, ya paise ya shaadi ke offer ki shakal mein aa sakta hai.

Courts ko rape ko family ke aapas mein settle karne wali cheez nahi maanna chahiye. 2021 mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki bail conditions accused ko victim se contact karne ki maang ya ijaazat nahi de sakti, aur judges compromise ya shaadi ka sujhaav nahi de sakte [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. Agar koi bhi, chahe ghar ka bada, padosi ya panchayat, tum par case wapas lene ka pressure daale, toh record rakho aur prosecutor ya court ko batao.

> Accused ka rishtedaar hona case ko kamzor nahi karta. Law mein, yahi woh wajah hai jiski wajah se charge aggravated hai.

Agar survivor ne tumhe bataya hai, toh pehle uska yakeen karo, use kisi safe jagah pahunchne mein madad karo, aur use tay karne do ki kitni tezi se aage badhna hai. Agar woh 18 se kam hai, toh law ke hisaab se jise bhi abuse ka pata hai, use report karna zaroori hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]], isliye use imaandaari se batao ki tum yeh secret nahi rakh sakte, aur saath milkar 1098 call karo.

rape-conviction-appeals-explained.en:
A rape conviction feels like the end. In law it is the midpoint. The convicted man can appeal. So can the prosecution, if it thinks the sentence is too light or an acquittal was wrong. While the appeal waits, a High Court can suspend the sentence and release him on bail. Since 2018 the law has said an appeal against a rape sentence should be decided within six months [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]]. In the 2002 Gujarat riots gang rape case, the High Court ruled more than nine years after the trial verdict [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Who can appeal: the convicted, the state, the investigating agency

A rape trial is held in a sessions court. An appeal goes to the High Court, and from there a case can reach the Supreme Court. The cases in this story show who goes back to court:

- **The convicted person**, against the conviction or the sentence. The former MLA convicted in the Unnao case is still pursuing his appeal in the Delhi High Court [[livelaw-unnao-sc-2026]].
- **The prosecution**, against a sentence it finds too light. In the RG Kar case both the West Bengal government and the CBI appealed for death, and only the CBI, which had investigated the case, was allowed to go ahead [[barandbench-rg-kar-hc-2025]].
- **The other side of an acquittal.** In the 2002 Gujarat riots case, seven people acquitted at trial were convicted on appeal [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]].

A survivor may have her own right of appeal too. Which route is open depends on the case, so ask a lawyer early.

## The six-month rule, written in 2018

The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018 raised the minimum punishment for rape from seven years to ten and set deadlines: two months for the police investigation, six months for an appeal [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]]. The BNSS, in force since 1 July 2024 [[air-new-criminal-laws-2024]], repeats the rule in Section 415(4): an appeal against a rape sentence "shall be disposed of within a period of six months" of being filed [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

The deadline has no teeth: the code attaches no consequence to missing it. And we found no official statistic that shows whether it is met. The National Crime Records Bureau's court tables cover trials, where 1,85,785 rape cases were pending at the end of 2024, 89.8% of those before the courts [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. They do not cover appeals.

## Nine years in the 2002 Gujarat riots case, more than four in a #MeToo appeal

The deadline is 6 months. The record in four headline cases:

| Case | Trial court's sentence | Appeal |
|---|---|---|
| 2002 Gujarat riots gang rape case | 21 January 2008 | Decided 4 May 2017 |
| Shakti Mills | 4 April 2014 | Decided 25 November 2021 |
| Unnao | 20 December 2019 | No decision found by 20 November 2026 |
| RG Kar | 20 January 2025 | CBI's appeal: no ruling found by 20 November 2026 |

The first two trial verdicts came before the rule existed; the last two came after it. In the Gujarat riots case, a special court in Mumbai gave 11 men life imprisonment for the gang rape of a pregnant woman and the murder of 14 of her relatives, and acquitted five police personnel and two doctors. The Bombay High Court upheld the 11 convictions and convicted the seven who had been acquitted [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. An appeal does not only help the accused.

Delay hurts outside rape law too. On 17 February 2021 a Delhi court acquitted a woman journalist whom a former Union minister had prosecuted for criminal defamation over her #MeToo allegation of sexual harassment [[delhi-court-metoo-defamation-judgment-2021]]. The Delhi High Court admitted his appeal in January 2022 and listed it for final hearing on 24 September 2026, more than four years later and more than five years after the acquittal [[livelaw-akbar-appeal-2026]]. The six-month rule does not cover defamation, and we could not confirm what happened at that hearing. But for all those years, the woman a court had cleared stayed a respondent in a criminal case.

## RG Kar: two appeals for the death penalty

On 20 January 2025 a Sealdah court sentenced the man convicted of the RG Kar rape and murder to imprisonment for the rest of his natural life, rejecting the CBI's plea for death because the crime was not "rarest of the rare" [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. Both the West Bengal government and the CBI then asked the Calcutta High Court for death. On 7 February 2025 the court dismissed the state's appeal. The CBI had investigated and prosecuted the case, so the appeal that went ahead was the CBI's [[barandbench-rg-kar-hc-2025]].

We could not find a ruling on the CBI's appeal as of 20 November 2026, more than a year and a half after the sentence.

## What happens to the sentence while an appeal is pending

Filing an appeal does not open the prison gate. But the appeal court can suspend the sentence and release the convict on bail until it decides. In December 2025 the Delhi High Court did that for the former MLA convicted in the Unnao case, whom a Delhi court had sentenced on 20 December 2019 to imprisonment for the rest of his life [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]]. Among its reasons: he had already served more than seven years [[scobserver-unnao-stay-2025]]. The wait for his own appeal had become an argument for release. The Supreme Court stayed the order on 29 December 2025 [[scobserver-unnao-stay-2025]] and set it aside on 15 May 2026, asking the High Court to decide the main appeal quickly or pass a fresh order [[livelaw-unnao-sc-2026]].

A death sentence also goes before the High Court. In the Shakti Mills case, three death sentences passed on 4 April 2014 [[livelaw-shakti-mills-death-sentence-2014]] were commuted to life imprisonment by the Bombay High Court on 25 November 2021 [[barandbench-shakti-mills-hc-2021]].

Consider a hypothetical survivor in Kanpur whose attacker has just been sentenced to ten years, the minimum for rape. He appeals. The case is now the State against him, in a High Court she may never visit. She can ask the public prosecutor's office for the appeal number, follow the dates on the High Court's website, and ask a free legal aid lawyer how she can be heard if he asks for his sentence to be suspended [[nalsa]]. The law promises her an answer in six months. She should plan for longer.
rape-conviction-appeals-explained.hg:
Rape ka conviction kahani ka ant lagta hai. Law mein yeh beech ka padaav hai. Jise convict kiya gaya hai, woh appeal kar sakta hai. Prosecution bhi kar sakta hai, agar use lage ki saza kam hai ya acquittal galat tha. Jab tak appeal pending hai, High Court saza suspend karke convict ko bail par chhod sakta hai. 2018 se law kehta hai ki rape ki saza ke khilaaf appeal chhe mahine mein tay honi chahiye [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]]. 2002 ke Gujarat riots gang rape case mein High Court ka faisla trial verdict ke nau saal se bhi zyada baad aaya [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Appeal kaun kar sakta hai: convict, state, investigating agency

Rape ka trial sessions court mein hota hai. Appeal High Court mein jaati hai, aur wahan se case Supreme Court tak pahunch sakta hai. Is story ke cases dikhate hain ki dobara court kaun jaata hai:

- **Convict**, apne conviction ya saza ke khilaaf. Unnao case mein convict hua former MLA abhi bhi Delhi High Court mein apni appeal lad raha hai [[livelaw-unnao-sc-2026]].
- **Prosecution**, us saza ke khilaaf jo use kam lage. RG Kar case mein West Bengal sarkar aur CBI, dono ne death ke liye appeal ki, aur aage sirf CBI ko jaane diya gaya, jisne case ki investigation ki thi [[barandbench-rg-kar-hc-2025]].
- **Acquittal ka doosra paksh.** 2002 ke Gujarat riots case mein trial mein bari hue saat logon ko appeal mein convict kiya gaya [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]].

Survivor ke paas bhi apni appeal ka right ho sakta hai. Kaunsa raasta khula hai, yeh case par nirbhar karta hai, isliye jaldi lawyer se poochiye.

## Six-month rule, jo 2018 mein likha gaya

Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018 ne rape ki minimum saza saat saal se badhakar das saal ki aur deadlines tay ki: police investigation ke liye do mahine, appeal ke liye chhe mahine [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]]. BNSS, jo 1 July 2024 se laagu hai [[air-new-criminal-laws-2024]], yahi rule Section 415(4) mein dohrata hai: rape ki saza ke khilaaf appeal, file hone ke baad, "shall be disposed of within a period of six months", yaani chhe mahine ke andar nipta di jaayegi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Yeh deadline sirf kaagaz par hai: ise miss karne par code mein koi nateeja nahi likha. Aur humein koi official statistic nahi mila jo bataye ki deadline poori hoti hai ya nahi. National Crime Records Bureau ki court tables trials ko ginti hain, jahan 2024 ke end mein rape ke 1,85,785 cases pending the, yaani courts ke saamne aaye cases ka 89.8% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Appeals unme nahi hain.

## 2002 Gujarat riots case mein nau saal, ek #MeToo appeal mein chaar se zyada

Deadline 6 months ki hai. Chaar bade cases ka record:

| Case | Trial court ki saza | Appeal |
|---|---|---|
| 2002 Gujarat riots gang rape case | 21 January 2008 | 4 May 2017 ko tay hui |
| Shakti Mills | 4 April 2014 | 25 November 2021 ko tay hui |
| Unnao | 20 December 2019 | 20 November 2026 tak koi faisla nahi mila |
| RG Kar | 20 January 2025 | CBI ki appeal: 20 November 2026 tak koi faisla nahi mila |

Pehle do trial verdicts rule banne se pehle aaye; aakhri do uske baad. Gujarat riots case mein Mumbai ki ek special court ne ek pregnant aurat ke gang rape aur uske 14 rishtedaaron ke murder ke liye 11 aadmiyon ko umrqaid di, aur paanch police personnel aur do doctors ko bari kar diya. Bombay High Court ne 11 convictions barkaraar rakhe aur jin saat ko bari kiya gaya tha, unhe bhi convict kar diya [[sc-bilkis-remission-2024]]. Appeal sirf accused ke kaam nahi aati.

Deri rape law ke bahar bhi chot karti hai. 17 February 2021 ko Delhi ki ek court ne ek mahila journalist ko bari kiya, jis par ek former Union minister ne uske #MeToo sexual harassment allegation ko lekar criminal defamation ka case kiya tha [[delhi-court-metoo-defamation-judgment-2021]]. Delhi High Court ne January 2022 mein minister ki appeal admit ki aur use 24 September 2026 ko final hearing ke liye list kiya, yaani chaar saal se zyada baad, aur acquittal ke paanch saal se bhi zyada baad [[livelaw-akbar-appeal-2026]]. Six-month rule defamation par laagu nahi hota, aur us hearing mein kya hua, iski pushti hum nahi kar sake. Lekin itne saal tak woh aurat, jise court bari kar chuki thi, ek criminal case mein respondent bani rahi.

## RG Kar: death penalty ke liye do appeals

20 January 2025 ko Sealdah ki ek court ne RG Kar rape aur murder ke convict ko baaki poori natural life ke liye qaid ki saza di, aur CBI ki death ki maang yeh kehkar thukra di ki crime "rarest of the rare" nahi hai [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. Iske baad West Bengal sarkar aur CBI, dono ne Calcutta High Court se death maangi. 7 February 2025 ko court ne state ki appeal dismiss kar di. Investigation aur prosecution CBI ne kiya tha, isliye aage wahi appeal chali jo CBI ki thi [[barandbench-rg-kar-hc-2025]].

20 November 2026 tak, yaani saza ke dedh saal se zyada baad, humein CBI ki appeal par koi faisla nahi mila.

## Jab tak appeal pending hai, saza ka kya hota hai

Appeal file karne se jail ka darwaaza nahi khulta. Lekin appeal sunne wali court faisla aane tak saza suspend karke convict ko bail par chhod sakti hai. December 2025 mein Delhi High Court ne Unnao case mein convict hue former MLA ke liye yahi kiya, jise Delhi ki ek court ne 20 December 2019 ko baaki poori zindagi ke liye qaid ki saza di thi [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]]. Court ke tarkon mein ek yeh tha ki woh saat saal se zyada jail kaat chuka hai [[scobserver-unnao-stay-2025]]. Uski apni appeal ka intezaar hi rihaai ki daleel ban gaya. Supreme Court ne 29 December 2025 ko is order par rok lagayi [[scobserver-unnao-stay-2025]] aur 15 May 2026 ko ise set aside kar diya, aur High Court se kaha ki main appeal jaldi tay kare ya naya order de [[livelaw-unnao-sc-2026]].

Death sentence bhi High Court ke saamne jaati hai. Shakti Mills case mein 4 April 2014 ko di gayi teen death sentences [[livelaw-shakti-mills-death-sentence-2014]] ko Bombay High Court ne 25 November 2021 ko umrqaid mein badal diya [[barandbench-shakti-mills-hc-2021]].

Ek kaalpanik situation sochiye: Kanpur ki ek survivor hai, jiske attacker ko abhi-abhi das saal ki saza hui hai, jo rape ki minimum saza hai. Woh appeal karta hai. Ab case State banaam convict hai, ek aise High Court mein jahan survivor shayad kabhi na jaaye. Woh public prosecutor ke office se appeal ka number maang sakti hai, High Court ki website par dates dekh sakti hai, aur free legal aid lawyer se pooch sakti hai ki agar convict saza suspend karne ki maang kare toh uski apni baat kaise suni jaayegi [[nalsa]]. Law use chhe mahine mein jawab ka vaada karta hai. Use isse zyada ke liye taiyaar rehna chahiye.

rape-law-relationship-status-partner-wif.en:
Picture five women in the same city on the same night. Each is forced into sex by a man she knows. One is his girlfriend, one lives with him, one broke up with him last year, one has moved back to her parents' house while her marriage falls apart, and one is his wife. Indian criminal law treats those five nights in three different ways.

In 2024 police registered 13,879 rape cases in which the accused was a friend, an online friend, a live-in partner or a separated husband [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Those are the relationships this explainer walks through, from the furthest from marriage to the closest. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Girlfriend or live-in partner: the full rape law

For a woman who is not married to the man, the relationship changes nothing. Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) defines rape by what was done and whether she agreed, not by who he is to her [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Consent means an "unequivocal voluntary agreement" communicated by words, gestures or other means, and a woman who does not physically resist is not, for that reason alone, consenting [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

So a boyfriend who forces sex, or a live-in partner who does, faces the same punishment as any other man under Section 64: at least 10 years' rigorous imprisonment, up to life [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Saying yes last week, living together or planning a wedding is not consent tonight.

The BNS also added a separate offence in Section 69: sex obtained through a promise of marriage the man never meant to keep, or through other deceit, carries up to 10 years [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. That is not rape, and it is a different charge from forced sex.

## The ex: stalking and shared images

Breaking up does not end the danger, and the law follows. An ex who keeps following her, contacting her against her clear refusal or tracking her online commits stalking under Section 78: up to 3 years, and up to 5 on a repeat [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Police registered 9,865 stalking cases in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

If he shares intimate images, Section 77 applies. It says plainly that agreeing to a photo being taken is not agreeing to it being shared. Sharing without consent is voyeurism, with 1 to 3 years on a first conviction [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. And if an ex forces sex, that is rape under Section 63 like any other.

## Separated wife: Section 67's 2 to 7 years

Here the law starts to step back. Under Section 67, a husband who has sex with his wife without her consent while they live separately, with or without a court decree, faces 2 to 7 years [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The same act by any other man carries a 10-year minimum.

This is not a rare situation. In the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5), 14% of ever-married women who had faced sexual violence named a former husband [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. A woman who has already left, and may be in the middle of a custody or maintenance fight, gets a weaker criminal law than a stranger would.

> The criminal law asks one question before it asks what he did: was she his wife?

## Wife over 18: the exception

Exception 2 to Section 63 says sex or sexual acts by a man with his own wife, if she is not under 18, is not rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The Supreme Court in 2017 made sex with a wife under 18 rape, but expressly left adult wives undecided [[sc-independent-thought-2017]]. As of 19 November 2026 the Court still had not ruled; it said it would fix the final hearing for 9 or 10 December 2026 [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]].

The women this leaves out are not a few. In NFHS-5, 4.6% of ever-married women aged 18-49 said their husband had physically forced them to have intercourse when they did not want to, and 82% of ever-married women who had faced sexual violence named their current husband [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

One area of law already counts it. In 2022 the Supreme Court held that "rape" in the abortion law includes marital rape, so a wife pregnant from forced sex can seek an abortion up to 24 weeks without an FIR [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

## Beside the criminal law: the Domestic Violence Act

Where the criminal law steps back, a wife is sent to a civil one. The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 counts sexual abuse, any sexual conduct that abuses, humiliates or violates a woman's dignity, as domestic violence. It offers civil remedies such as a protection order. But it is not a rape law: breaching a protection order carries at most 1 year or a Rs 20,000 fine [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

And it is barely used as a criminal route. Only 616 cases were registered across India under the Act in 2024, and 496 of them came from Kerala [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The line is now plain. The further a woman is from marriage, the more the criminal law protects her. The closer she gets, the more she must rely on a protection order, a cruelty case and her own records. Until the Supreme Court decides, knowing exactly where she stands on that line is the first step.
rape-law-relationship-status-partner-wif.hg:
Ek hi shehar mein, ek hi raat, paanch women ko sochiye. Har ek ke saath ek jaan-pehchaan ka aadmi zabardasti sex karta hai. Ek uski girlfriend hai, ek uske saath rehti hai, ek ne pichhle saal usse breakup kiya, ek apni toot-ti shaadi ke beech parents ke ghar wapas aa gayi hai, aur ek uski wife hai. Indian criminal law in paanch raaton ko teen alag tareeke se dekhta hai.

2024 mein police ne 13,879 aise rape cases register kiye jinmein accused dost, online dost, live-in partner ya alag reh raha husband tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh explainer inhi rishton se guzarta hai, shaadi se sabse door wale se lekar sabse kareeb wale tak. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Girlfriend ya live-in partner: poora rape law

Jo woman us aadmi se married nahi hai, uske liye relationship kuch nahi badalta. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ka Section 63 rape ko is se define karta hai ki kya kiya gaya aur kya usne haan kaha, is se nahi ki woh uska kya lagta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Consent ka matlab hai ek "unequivocal voluntary agreement" jo words, gestures ya kisi aur tareeke se bataya gaya ho, aur jo woman physically resist nahi karti, woh sirf is wajah se consent nahi de rahi [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Toh jo boyfriend zabardasti karta hai, ya jo live-in partner karta hai, use Section 64 ke under kisi bhi aur aadmi jitni hi saza milti hai: kam se kam 10 saal ki rigorous imprisonment, life tak [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Pichhle hafte haan kehna, saath rehna ya shaadi plan karna, aaj raat ka consent nahi hai.

BNS ne Section 69 mein ek alag offence bhi joda: shaadi ka aisa vaada karke sex lena jo aadmi kabhi nibhana hi nahi chahta tha, ya kisi aur dhokhe se, pe 10 saal tak ki saza hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Yeh rape nahi hai, aur zabardasti sex se alag charge hai.

## Ex: stalking aur share ki gayi images

Breakup se khatra khatam nahi hota, aur law bhi peecha karta hai. Jo ex uska peecha karta rehta hai, saaf mana karne ke baad bhi contact karta hai ya online track karta hai, woh Section 78 ke under stalking karta hai: 3 saal tak, aur dobara karne pe 5 saal tak [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Police ne 2024 mein stalking ke 9,865 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Agar woh intimate images share karta hai, toh Section 77 lagta hai. Yeh saaf kehta hai ki photo khinchwane ke liye haan kehna, use share karne ke liye haan kehna nahi hai. Bina consent share karna voyeurism hai, pehli conviction pe 1 se 3 saal [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Aur agar ex zabardasti sex karta hai, toh woh bhi baaki sab ki tarah Section 63 ke under rape hai.

## Alag rehti wife: Section 67 ke 2 se 7 saal

Yahan se law peeche hatna shuru karta hai. Section 67 ke under jo husband alag reh rahi wife ke saath uski consent ke bina sex karta hai, court decree ho ya na ho, use 2 se 7 saal milte hain [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Wahi kaam koi aur aadmi kare toh minimum 10 saal hai.

Yeh rare situation nahi hai. National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5) mein sexual violence jhel chuki ever-married women mein se 14% ne former husband ka naam liya [[nfhs5-india-2021]]. Jo woman pehle hi ghar chhod chuki hai, aur shaayad custody ya maintenance ki ladaai ke beech hai, use ek stranger ke case se kamzor criminal law milta hai.

> Criminal law yeh poochhne se pehle ki usne kya kiya, ek sawaal poochhta hai: kya woh uski wife thi?

## 18 se upar ki wife: exception

Section 63 ka Exception 2 kehta hai ki agar wife 18 se kam nahi hai, toh aadmi ka apni wife ke saath sex ya sexual acts rape nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Supreme Court ne 2017 mein 18 se kam umar ki wife ke saath sex ko rape maana, lekin adult wives ka sawaal jaan-boojh kar khula chhoda [[sc-independent-thought-2017]]. 19 November 2026 tak Court ne faisla nahi diya tha. Usne kaha ki final hearing 9 ya 10 December 2026 ko fix karega [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]].

Jo women is se bahar reh jaati hain, woh kam nahi hain. NFHS-5 mein 18-49 saal ki 4.6% ever-married women ne kaha ki husband ne unhe na chahte hue intercourse ke liye physically force kiya, aur sexual violence jhel chuki ever-married women mein se 82% ne apne current husband ka naam liya [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

Law ka ek hissa ise pehle se ginta hai. 2022 mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki abortion law mein "rape" mein marital rape bhi shaamil hai, toh zabardasti sex se pregnant hui wife bina FIR ke 24 weeks tak abortion maang sakti hai [[sc-x-v-principal-secretary-2022]].

## Criminal law ke saath: Domestic Violence Act

Jahan criminal law peeche hatta hai, wahan wife ko ek civil law ki taraf bheja jaata hai. Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 sexual abuse ko, yaani koi bhi sexual conduct jo woman ki dignity ko abuse, humiliate ya violate kare, domestic violence maanta hai. Yeh protection order jaise civil remedies deta hai. Lekin yeh rape law nahi hai: protection order todne pe zyada se zyada 1 saal ya 20,000 rupaye ka fine hai [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]].

Aur criminal raaste ke roop mein yeh mushkil se use hota hai. 2024 mein poore India mein is Act ke under sirf 616 cases register hue, aur un mein se 496 Kerala se the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Line ab saaf hai. Woman shaadi se jitni door hai, criminal law use utna protect karta hai. Jitni kareeb jaati hai, utna use protection order, cruelty case aur apne records pe nirbhar rehna padta hai. Jab tak Supreme Court faisla nahi karta, is line pe woh theek kahan khadi hai, yeh jaanna pehla kadam hai.

rape-punishment-ladder-bns-sections-64-7.en:
Ask what the punishment for rape is in India and you will hear "seven years", "life" or "hanging". The law has no single answer. Sections 64 to 71 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), in force since 1 July 2024 [[air-new-criminal-laws-2024]], work like a ladder. The lowest rung is 10 years in prison and the highest is death [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Where a convicted man lands depends on the survivor's age, the position he held over her and what the attack did to her. What follows is general information, not legal advice.

## The floor: Section 64 and the 10-year minimum

Section 64(1) punishes rape with rigorous imprisonment of at least 10 years, which may extend to imprisonment for life [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

The floor matters more than the ceiling. A court that convicts under Section 64 cannot hand down five years because the man is young or has a family to support.

"Seven years" is an old answer: it was the minimum until the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018, in force from 21 April 2018, raised it to 10 [[indiacode-cla-2018]]. The BNS kept that floor.

## Thirteen aggravated forms, from police officers to relatives

Section 64(2) lists 13 situations that make the offence graver. They include rape by a police officer, a public servant, a member of the armed forces or the staff of a jail or hospital; by a relative, guardian, teacher or anyone in a position of trust or authority; during communal violence; of a pregnant woman or a woman with a disability; and repeated rape of the same woman [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

The minimum is still 10 years. What changes is the top: here "life" is defined as imprisonment for the remainder of the man's natural life [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The extra words spell it out: on this rung, life means the rest of the man's life.

Many of the clauses describe a man who had power over the woman. The law treats that power as a reason to punish more, and it changes a Section 64(2) trial: once intercourse is proved and the woman testifies that she did not consent, the court must presume she did not [[indiacode-bsa-2023]].

The rung is rarely used. In 2024, police registered 27 rape cases under the clause for police personnel, 15 for other public servants, 8 for hospital staff, 3 for staff of jails and other places of custody and 2 for the armed forces [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A case gets here only if police invoke the clause.

## Girls under 16 and under 12: Section 65

On the next rung, age alone moves the case up. Rape of a girl under 16 carries at least 20 years' rigorous imprisonment, up to the rest of natural life. Rape of a girl under 12 carries the same range, or death. Any fine must be paid to the victim [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Both rungs were built in 2018, by the amendment that raised the floor [[indiacode-cla-2018]].

A man accused under Section 65 cannot get anticipatory bail [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. And because sex with any girl under 18 is rape whatever she says [[indiacode-bns-2023]], a case involving a 16- or 17-year-old still starts at the 10-year floor of Section 64. Child cases are usually charged under the POCSO Act too, which protects boys and girls alike [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Consider a hypothetical: a tuition teacher in Kanpur rapes a 15-year-old student. Her age puts the case under Section 65(1), where the court starts at 20 years. Had she been 17, he would face Section 64(2) as a teacher, with a 10-year floor. Had she been 11, death would be an option.

## Death, a vegetative state, a gang, a second conviction: Sections 66, 70 and 71

Section 66 applies when the rape causes the woman's death or leaves her in a persistent vegetative state: at least 20 years, up to natural life, or death [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. "Or death" is a choice for the court, not a rule. On 20 January 2025 a Sealdah court sentenced the man convicted in the RG Kar Medical College case, under Sections 64, 66 and 103(1), to imprisonment for the rest of his natural life, rejecting the CBI's plea for death because the crime was not "rarest of the rare" [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. The CBI has appealed.

Section 70 covers gang rape. Every member of the group is guilty of rape and faces 20 years to natural life; if the girl is under 18, the only options are natural life or death. Section 71 gives the same two options to anyone convicted a second time under Sections 64, 65, 66 or 70 [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

| Section | Situation | Punishment |
|---|---|---|
| 64(1) | Rape | 10 years to life |
| 64(2) | 13 aggravated forms | 10 years to natural life |
| 65(1) | Girl under 16 | 20 years to natural life |
| 65(2), 66 | Girl under 12; death or vegetative state | 20 years to natural life, or death |
| 70(1) | Gang rape | 20 years to natural life |
| 70(2), 71 | Gang rape of a girl under 18; second conviction | Natural life, or death |

## Below the ladder: Sections 67 and 68

Two sections sit beside the ladder and punish less. Under Section 67, a husband who has sex with his wife without her consent while they live separately faces 2 to 7 years. The same act against any other woman starts at 10. If the couple live together and the wife is 18 or older, Exception 2 to Section 63 says it is not rape at all [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Section 68 covers a person in authority, a public servant or the staff of a jail, institution or hospital who abuses that position to get a woman in his custody or care to have sex with him, short of rape: 5 to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Some survivors have no rung at all. The BNS has no counterpart to the old Section 377 of the IPC, so non-consensual penetrative sex against an adult man or a transgender person is not rape under the code [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

And every rung is reached only after a conviction. In 2024, courts convicted in 24.4% of the rape trials they completed [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The sections written on the FIR are where the case starts its climb. A survivor's family should read them, and ask a lawyer whether her age and the accused man's position have been recorded.
rape-punishment-ladder-bns-sections-64-7.hg:
Kisi se poochiye ki India mein rape ki saza kya hai, toh jawaab milega "saat saal", "life" ya "phaansi". Law ke paas koi ek jawaab nahi hai. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Sections 64 se 71, jo 1 July 2024 se laagu hain [[air-new-criminal-laws-2024]], ek seedhi ki tarah kaam karte hain. Sabse neeche ka paaydaan 10 saal ki jail hai aur sabse upar ka death [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Convict hua aadmi kahan pahunchega, yeh teen cheezon par depend karta hai: survivor ki umar, us par uski position, aur hamle ne survivor ke saath kya kiya. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Floor: Section 64 aur 10 saal ka minimum

Section 64(1) rape ke liye kam se kam 10 saal ki rigorous imprisonment deta hai, jo imprisonment for life tak ja sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Yahan ceiling se zyada floor maayne rakhta hai. Section 64 mein convict karne wala court paanch saal ki saza yeh keh kar nahi de sakta ki aadmi jawaan hai ya uske ghar ki zimmedaari us par hai.

"Saat saal" ek purana jawaab hai: 2018 tak yahi minimum tha. Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018 ne, jo 21 April 2018 se laagu maana gaya, ise 10 kar diya [[indiacode-cla-2018]]. BNS ne wahi floor rakha.

## Terah aggravated forms, police officers se rishtedaaron tak

Section 64(2) mein 13 haalaat likhe hain jo offence ko zyada gambhir bana dete hain. Inmein shamil hain: police officer, public servant, armed forces ke member ya jail ya hospital ke staff ka kiya rape; rishtedaar, guardian, teacher ya trust ya authority ki position wale kisi bhi insaan ka kiya rape; communal violence ke dauraan rape; pregnant aurat ya disability wali aurat ka rape; aur ek hi aurat ka baar-baar rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Minimum yahan bhi 10 saal hai. Badalta hai upar ka sira: yahan "life" ka matlab us aadmi ki baaki natural life ki qaid likha gaya hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Yeh extra shabd saaf kar dete hain: is paaydaan par life ka matlab aadmi ki baaki poori zindagi hai.

Kai clauses aise aadmi ki baat karte hain jiske paas us aurat par power thi. Law us power ko zyada saza ki wajah maanta hai, aur Section 64(2) ke trial ko bhi badal deta hai: ek baar intercourse saabit ho jaaye aur aurat gawaahi de ki usne consent nahi diya tha, toh court ko yahi maan kar chalna hoga ki consent nahi tha [[indiacode-bsa-2023]].

Par yeh paaydaan kam hi istemaal hota hai. 2024 mein police ne police personnel wale clause mein 27 rape cases register kiye, doosre public servants ke liye 15, hospital staff ke liye 8, jail aur custody ki doosri jagahon ke staff ke liye 3 aur armed forces ke liye 2 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Case is paaydaan tak tabhi pahunchta hai jab police yeh clause lagaye.

## 16 aur 12 saal se kam ki ladkiyan: Section 65

Agle paaydaan par sirf umar hi case ko upar le jaati hai. 16 saal se kam ki ladki ke rape par kam se kam 20 saal ki rigorous imprisonment hai, jo baaki natural life tak ja sakti hai. 12 saal se kam ki ladki ke rape par wahi range hai, ya death. Jo bhi fine lage, woh victim ko diya jaana chahiye [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Dono paaydaan 2018 mein bane, usi amendment se jisne floor badhaya tha [[indiacode-cla-2018]].

Section 65 ke accused ko anticipatory bail nahi mil sakti [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Aur kyunki 18 saal se kam ki kisi bhi ladki ke saath sex rape hai, chahe woh kuch bhi kahe [[indiacode-bns-2023]], 16 ya 17 saal ki ladki ka case bhi Section 64 ke 10 saal ke floor se shuru hota hai. Bachchon ke cases aam taur par POCSO Act mein bhi charge hote hain, jo ladkon aur ladkiyon dono ko protect karta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Ek hypothetical sochiye: Kanpur ka ek tuition teacher apni 15 saal ki student ka rape karta hai. Uski umar case ko Section 65(1) mein daalti hai, jahan court 20 saal se shuru karta hai. Agar woh 17 ki hoti, toh wahi aadmi teacher hone ki wajah se Section 64(2) mein aata, 10 saal ke floor ke saath. Agar woh 11 ki hoti, toh death bhi ek option hota.

## Maut, vegetative state, gang, doosri conviction: Sections 66, 70 aur 71

Section 66 tab lagta hai jab rape se aurat ki maut ho jaaye ya woh persistent vegetative state mein chali jaaye: kam se kam 20 saal, baaki natural life tak, ya death [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. "Ya death" court ka choice hai, rule nahi. 20 January 2025 ko Sealdah ke ek court ne RG Kar Medical College case ke convict ko Sections 64, 66 aur 103(1) mein baaki natural life ki qaid di, aur CBI ki death ki maang yeh keh kar thukra di ki crime "rarest of the rare" nahi tha [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. CBI ne appeal ki hai.

Section 70 gang rape ke liye hai. Group ka har member rape ka doshi hai aur use 20 saal se baaki natural life tak ki qaid ho sakti hai; agar ladki 18 se kam ki hai, toh sirf do options hain: baaki natural life ki qaid ya death. Section 71 yahi do options us insaan ke liye rakhta hai jo Sections 64, 65, 66 ya 70 mein doosri baar convict ho [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

| Section | Haalaat | Saza |
|---|---|---|
| 64(1) | Rape | 10 saal se life |
| 64(2) | 13 aggravated forms | 10 saal se natural life |
| 65(1) | 16 saal se kam ki ladki | 20 saal se natural life |
| 65(2), 66 | 12 saal se kam ki ladki; maut ya vegetative state | 20 saal se natural life, ya death |
| 70(1) | Gang rape | 20 saal se natural life |
| 70(2), 71 | 18 saal se kam ki ladki ka gang rape; doosri conviction | Natural life, ya death |

## Seedhi ke neeche: Sections 67 aur 68

Do sections seedhi ke bagal mein baithe hain aur kam saza dete hain. Section 67 mein, jo pati alag reh rahi patni ke saath uski consent ke bina sex kare, use 2 se 7 saal ki saza hai. Wahi kaam kisi aur aurat ke saath ho, toh saza 10 saal se shuru hoti hai. Aur agar pati-patni saath rehte hain aur patni 18 ya usse zyada ki hai, toh Section 63 ka Exception 2 kehta hai ki yeh rape hai hi nahi [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Section 68 us person in authority, public servant ya jail, institution ya hospital ke staff ke liye hai jo apni position ka galat istemaal karke apni custody ya care mein rakhi aurat se sex kare, jo rape ki definition tak na pahunche: 5 se 10 saal ki rigorous imprisonment [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Kuch survivors ke liye toh koi paaydaan hi nahi hai. BNS mein IPC ke purane Section 377 jaisa koi section nahi hai, isliye kisi adult aadmi ya transgender insaan ke saath non-consensual penetrative sex is code mein rape nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Aur har paaydaan conviction ke baad hi aata hai. 2024 mein courts ne jitne rape trials poore kiye, unmein se 24.4% mein convict kiya [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. FIR par likhe sections se hi tay hota hai ki case seedhi par kahan se chadhna shuru karega. Survivor ke parivaar ko unhe padhna chahiye, aur lawyer se poochna chahiye ki uski umar aur accused ki position record hui hai ya nahi.

rape-survivor-character-evidence-law-tim.en:
A rape trial is supposed to ask one question about consent: did she agree to this act, with this person, at this time? For most of independent India's history, courts asked other questions instead. Did she have injuries? Did she fight? What kind of woman was she? The answers decided cases. This timeline follows the four changes in the law that moved those questions out of the courtroom, and the gap that remains between the statute and the witness box. It is general information, not legal advice.

## Before 1983: when her past was evidence

- **15 September 1978:** a three-judge Supreme Court bench acquits two policemen accused of raping a minor girl inside a police station in Maharashtra in 1972, reversing the Bombay High Court, which had convicted them [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]].
- In that judgment the court notes that no marks of injury were found on the girl, describes the alleged intercourse as "a peaceful affair" and concludes that it was "not proved to amount to rape" [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]].

The reasoning reflected a common assumption of the time. A survivor's body was expected to show a struggle, and her silence or lack of injuries was read as agreement. A girl held in a police station, alone with policemen, was judged as if she had been free to resist.

## 1983: the custodial-rape presumption

- **25 December 1983:** after protests over the 1978 acquittal, the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1983 comes into force. It makes custodial rape a separate aggravated offence, tells courts to presume absence of consent in custodial rape trials (Section 114A of the Indian Evidence Act), provides for rape trials in camera and makes it a crime to disclose a rape victim's identity [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

The presumption flipped the burden in one narrow set of cases. If a woman in custody said she had not consented, the court would start from believing her. Today the rule lives in Section 120 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA): in a prosecution for the aggravated forms of rape in Section 64(2) of the BNS, such as rape by a police officer, a relative or hospital staff, once intercourse is proved and the woman testifies that she did not consent, the court must presume she did not [[indiacode-bsa-2023]]. It still does not apply to every rape trial.

## 2013: not resisting is not consent

After the 2012 Delhi gang rape, the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 rewrote the rules of evidence for sexual offences [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]:

- **Consent defined:** "an unequivocal voluntary agreement", and a woman who does not physically resist penetration is not, for that reason alone, to be regarded as consenting. The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita carries the same words into Section 63 [[indiacode-bns-2023]].
- **Section 53A, Indian Evidence Act:** where consent is in issue, evidence of the victim's character or previous sexual experience with any person is not relevant to consent or its quality.

The same year, in April, the Supreme Court held that the "two-finger test" violates a rape survivor's right to privacy, physical and mental integrity and dignity [[barandbench-lillu-2013]]. A survivor's body was no longer to be examined for clues about her sexual past.

In 2015 Parliament wrote the same consent rule into the SC/ST Atrocities Act for Dalit and Adivasi women: not resisting is not consent, and her sexual history does not imply consent [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

## 2023: the new evidence code and cross-examination

The BSA replaced the Indian Evidence Act from 1 July 2024. It keeps the rule and spells out what a defence lawyer cannot do [[indiacode-bsa-2023]]:

- **Section 48:** in prosecutions for rape, gang rape, sexual harassment, voyeurism, stalking and related offences, a survivor's character or previous sexual experience is not relevant to consent.
- **Section 149:** in rape cases, no evidence may be offered and no question put in cross-examination about the victim's "general immoral character" or previous sexual experience to prove consent.

> Her past relationships cannot be used to prove she said yes this time. That is now written into India's evidence code, not left to a judge's goodwill.

## The handbook, and what still happens in court

In 2023 the Supreme Court published a handbook naming the stereotypes judges must stop repeating. It lists as false the ideas that a woman's clothing, drinking or smoking invites sexual contact, that rapists are usually strangers, and that a genuine survivor cries incessantly or never speaks to the accused again. "There is no 'correct' or 'appropriate' way in which a survivor or victim behaves," it says [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

The handbook also shows how recent the old thinking is. It quotes a 2022 sessions court bail order in Kozhikode, Kerala, which said photographs showed the complainant "exposing to dresses which are having some sexual provocative one" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. That order came nine years after Section 53A. And in October 2022 the Supreme Court had to rule again that the two-finger test "has no scientific basis" and that anyone who conducts it in breach of the court's directions is guilty of misconduct [[scconline-shailendra-rai-2022]].

Consider a hypothetical: a 22-year-old in Pune testifying against a former boyfriend. The law says her earlier relationship with him cannot prove she consented, and the defence may not ask about her other relationships to suggest it. Whether that protection holds depends on a prosecutor who objects and a judge who stops the question. A survivor is entitled to insist on both.
rape-survivor-character-evidence-law-tim.hg:
Rape trial ko consent ke baare mein ek hi sawaal poochhna chahiye: kya usne is act ke liye, is insaan ke saath, is waqt haan kahi thi? Aazaad India ke itihaas ke zyada tar hisse mein courts ne iske badle doosre sawaal poochhe. Kya use chot lagi thi? Kya usne ladaai ki? Woh kis tarah ki aurat thi? Inhi jawaabon se case tay hote the. Yeh timeline kaanoon ke un chaar badlaavon ko follow karti hai jinhone yeh sawaal courtroom se bahar kiye, aur us faasle ko bhi jo aaj bhi kaanoon ki kitaab aur witness box ke beech bacha hai. Yeh general jaankari hai, legal advice nahi.

## 1983 se pehle: jab uska ateet saboot tha

- **15 September 1978:** Supreme Court ki teen judges ki bench Maharashtra ke ek police station ke andar 1972 mein ek naabaalig ladki ke rape ke aaropi do policewalon ko bari kar deti hai, aur Bombay High Court ka faisla palat deti hai, jisne unhe convict kiya tha [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]].
- Us judgment mein court note karti hai ki ladki par chot ke koi nishaan nahi mile, kathit intercourse ko "a peaceful affair" kehti hai, aur nateeja nikaalti hai ki woh "not proved to amount to rape" [[sc-tukaram-maharashtra-1978]].

Yeh soch us zamaane ki ek aam dhaarna dikhaati thi. Survivor ke shareer par ladaai ke nishaan hone ki ummeed ki jaati thi, aur uski khaamoshi ya chot na hona haan samjha jaata tha. Police station mein band ek ladki, jo policewalon ke saath akeli thi, ko aise jaancha gaya jaise woh virodh karne ke liye aazaad thi.

## 1983: custodial rape mein presumption

- **25 December 1983:** 1978 ke acquittal par protests ke baad Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1983 laagu hota hai. Yeh custodial rape ko alag aggravated offence banata hai, courts se kehta hai ki custodial rape trials mein maana jaaye ki consent nahi tha (Indian Evidence Act ka Section 114A), rape trials in camera karne ka provision deta hai, aur rape victim ki pehchaan zaahir karna crime banata hai [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

Is presumption ne ek chhote se daayre ke cases mein bojh palat diya. Agar custody mein rahi aurat kehti ki usne consent nahi diya, toh court uska yakeen karke shuru karti. Aaj yeh niyam Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) ke Section 120 mein hai: BNS Section 64(2) ke aggravated rape ke cases mein, jaise police officer, rishtedaar ya hospital staff dwara rape, jab intercourse saabit ho jaaye aur aurat gawaahi de ki usne consent nahi diya, toh court ko maanna hi hoga ki consent nahi tha [[indiacode-bsa-2023]]. Yeh ab bhi har rape trial par laagu nahi hota.

## 2013: virodh na karna consent nahi hai

2012 ke Delhi gang rape ke baad Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 ne sexual offences ke liye evidence ke niyam dobara likhe [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]:

- **Consent ki definition:** "an unequivocal voluntary agreement", yaani saaf aur apni marzi se di gayi haan; aur jo aurat penetration ka shaareerik virodh nahi karti, use sirf is wajah se consent dene wali nahi maana jaayega. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita yahi shabd Section 63 mein le aati hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].
- **Indian Evidence Act ka Section 53A:** jahan consent ka sawaal ho, wahan victim ke character ya kisi ke bhi saath uske pichhle sexual experience ka saboot consent ya uski quality ke liye relevant nahi hai.

Usi saal April mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki "two-finger test" rape survivor ke privacy, shaareerik aur maansik integrity aur dignity ke haq ka ullanghan hai [[barandbench-lillu-2013]]. Survivor ke shareer ko ab uske sexual ateet ke suraag dhoondhne ke liye jaancha nahi jaana tha.

2015 mein Parliament ne yahi consent ka niyam Dalit aur Adivasi auraton ke liye SC/ST Atrocities Act mein likha: virodh na karna consent nahi hai, aur uski sexual history se consent saabit nahi hota [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

## 2023: naya evidence code aur cross-examination

BSA ne 1 July 2024 se Indian Evidence Act ki jagah li. Yeh niyam ko banaaye rakhta hai aur saaf likhta hai ki defence ka vakeel kya nahi kar sakta [[indiacode-bsa-2023]]:

- **Section 48:** rape, gang rape, sexual harassment, voyeurism, stalking aur aise doosre offences ke prosecution mein survivor ka character ya pichhla sexual experience consent ke liye relevant nahi hai.
- **Section 149:** rape cases mein consent saabit karne ke liye victim ke "general immoral character" ya pichhle sexual experience par na koi saboot diya ja sakta hai, na cross-examination mein koi sawaal poochha ja sakta hai.

> Uske purane rishte yeh saabit karne ke liye use nahi kiye ja sakte ki is baar usne haan kahi. Yeh ab India ke evidence code mein likha hai, kisi judge ki meharbaani par nahi chhoda gaya.

## Handbook, aur court mein aaj bhi kya hota hai

2023 mein Supreme Court ne ek handbook nikaali jismein woh stereotypes gine gaye jinhe judges ko dohraana band karna hai. Ismein yeh baatein galat bataayi gayin ki aurat ke kapde, sharaab ya cigarette peena sexual contact ko nyota deta hai, ki rapists aksar anjaan hote hain, aur ki sachchi survivor lagaataar roti hai ya accused se kabhi baat nahi karti. Handbook kehti hai, "There is no 'correct' or 'appropriate' way in which a survivor or victim behaves", yaani survivor ke bartaav ka koi ek "sahi" tareeka nahi hota [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Handbook yeh bhi dikhaati hai ki purani soch kitni haal ki hai. Ismein Kozhikode, Kerala ki ek sessions court ka 2022 ka bail order quote hai, jisne kaha tha ki photos mein complainant "exposing to dresses which are having some sexual provocative one" [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]. Yeh order Section 53A ke nau saal baad aaya. Aur October 2022 mein Supreme Court ko phir se kehna pada ki two-finger test ka "no scientific basis" hai aur jo bhi court ke nirdeshon ka ullanghan karke ise karega woh misconduct ka doshi hoga [[scconline-shailendra-rai-2022]].

Ek hypothetical sochiye: Pune ki ek 22 saal ki ladki, jo apne ex-boyfriend ke khilaaf gawaahi de rahi hai. Uske liye iska kya matlab hai? Kaanoon kehta hai ki uska us aadmi ke saath pehle ka rishta yeh saabit nahi kar sakta ki usne consent diya, aur defence yeh dikhane ke liye uske doosre rishton ke baare mein nahi poochh sakta. Yeh suraksha tikti hai ya nahi, yeh is par nirbhar hai ki prosecutor objection kare aur judge sawaal roke. Survivor ko dono maangne ka poora haq hai.

repeat-sexual-offenders-second-convictio.en:
Imagine a man in Bhopal who follows women from the bus stop near a college. Over five years three women complain. One withdraws after his family visits hers. One case is still in court. The third ends in acquittal because a witness turns hostile. If a fourth woman reports him today, the law treats him as a first offender.

Indian law does punish repeat sexual offenders more harshly, in more places than most people realise. But every such provision starts from the same condition: a previous conviction. This explainer maps the second-conviction rules law by law, and shows why they bite so rarely. It is general information, not legal advice.

## The second-conviction rule across sexual offences

A first conviction is treated as a warning. A second one for the same kind of offence means the warning failed, so the law raises the ceiling, sometimes the floor, and sometimes removes the judge's choice altogether.

| Offence | First conviction | Second or later conviction |
|---|---|---|
| Rape (BNS Sections 64, 65, 66, 70) | At least 10 years, up to life (Section 64) | Natural life or death (Section 71) |
| Voyeurism (BNS Section 77) | 1 to 3 years | 3 to 7 years |
| Stalking (BNS Section 78) | Up to 3 years | Up to 5 years |
| Sexually explicit material online (IT Act Section 67A) | Up to 5 years and Rs 10 lakh | Up to 7 years |
| Doctor or clinic doing sex determination (PC-PNDT Act) | Up to 3 years and Rs 10,000 | Up to 5 years and Rs 50,000 |
| Employer ignoring the POSH Act | Fine up to Rs 50,000 | Twice the punishment, possible licence cancellation |

## Section 71: natural life or death for a repeat rapist

Section 71 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) says that anyone previously convicted of rape under Sections 64, 65, 66 or 70, who is convicted again under any of them, shall be punished with imprisonment for the rest of his natural life, or with death [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. A first rape conviction already carries at least 10 years and up to life [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The difference is that Section 71 leaves the judge only two options: prison for the rest of the offender's natural life, or death.

The rule was added to the IPC as Section 376E by the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013, after the 2012 Delhi gang rape case [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]]. It was first used on 4 April 2014, when a Mumbai sessions court sentenced three repeat offenders in the 2013 Shakti Mills gang rape cases to death [[livelaw-shakti-mills-death-sentence-2014]]. On 25 November 2021 the Bombay High Court commuted those sentences to life imprisonment, holding that a constitutional court cannot award punishment based on public opinion [[barandbench-shakti-mills-hc-2021]]. The first test of the repeat-offender rule ended with its harshest option set aside.

## Stalking, voyeurism and online material: the escalating terms

For lesser sexual offences, the steps are smaller but real. Voyeurism, watching or capturing images of a woman in a private act, carries 1 to 3 years on a first conviction and 3 to 7 years on a repeat. Stalking carries up to 3 years, rising to 5 [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Online abuse follows the same logic under the Information Technology Act. Publishing obscene material carries up to 3 years on a first conviction and up to 5 on a repeat. Sexually explicit material, and child sexual abuse material, including creating, browsing or downloading it, carry up to 5 years and a Rs 10 lakh fine the first time and up to 7 years after that [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].

## Sex selection and the POSH Act: repeat penalties outside the BNS

Two laws aimed at institutions use the same ladder. Under the PC-PNDT Act, a doctor or clinic that conducts sex determination faces up to 3 years and a Rs 10,000 fine, rising to 5 years and Rs 50,000. The doctor's registration is cancelled for 5 years after a first conviction and permanently after a second [[indiacode-pcpndt-1994]]. A person who seeks sex selection faces up to 3 years and Rs 50,000, rising to 5 years and Rs 1 lakh. The law presumes a pregnant woman was compelled by her husband or relatives, and does not punish a woman who was forced [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]].

Under the POSH Act, an employer who fails to set up an Internal Committee or act on its findings can be fined up to Rs 50,000. A repeat offence brings twice the punishment and can cost the business its licence or registration [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

## Second offences, first convictions: the catch

All of this depends on a first conviction, and in sexual-offence cases that is the exception. In 2024, courts convicted in 5,032 rape cases and acquitted in 13,980, a conviction rate of 24.4% of the 20,587 trials completed [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. At the end of that year, 1,85,785 rape cases were still pending trial, 89.8% of all those before the courts [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

For stalking online the numbers are starker. Of 4,348 cyber stalking and bullying cases against women and children before courts in 2024, only 33 ended in conviction, and 95.3% were still pending [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A man cannot be a repeat offender in law until a court has finished with him once.

> A tough sentence for a second conviction is only as strong as the system's ability to deliver the first.

The practical lesson is that each complaint carried to a verdict is what makes the next one count. That is not a burden any survivor owes anyone, and nobody should be pushed to keep a case going against her own safety or wishes. But if you choose to report, ask the police and prosecutor whether the accused has a record, refuse pressure to "settle", and get a free lawyer from the District Legal Services Authority to help you see the case through.
repeat-sexual-offenders-second-convictio.hg:
Socho Bhopal mein ek aadmi hai jo ek college ke paas wale bus stop se ladkiyon ka peecha karta hai. Five saal mein teen women complaint karti hain. Ek complaint tab wapas ho jaati hai jab uski family ladki ke ghar "milne" aati hai. Ek case abhi bhi court mein hai. Teesra acquittal par khatam hota hai kyunki ek witness hostile ho jaata hai. Agar aaj ek chauthi woman uski report kare, toh law use first offender hi maanega.

Indian law repeat sexual offenders ko sach mein zyada sakht saza deta hai, aur zyada tar log jitna sochte hain usse zyada jagahon par. Lekin har aisa provision ek hi shart se shuru hota hai: pehle ka conviction. Yeh explainer law-by-law second-conviction rules ka map banata hai, aur dikhata hai ki yeh itna kam kyun lagte hain. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Sexual offences mein second-conviction ka rule

Pehle conviction ko ek warning maana jaata hai. Usi tarah ke offence mein doosra conviction matlab warning kaam nahi aayi, isliye law saza ki upar ki limit badhata hai, kabhi neeche ki limit bhi, aur kabhi judge ka choice hi khatam kar deta hai.

| Offence | Pehla conviction | Doosra ya usse aage ka conviction |
|---|---|---|
| Rape (BNS Sections 64, 65, 66, 70) | Kam se kam 10 years, life tak (Section 64) | Natural life ya death (Section 71) |
| Voyeurism (BNS Section 77) | 1 se 3 years | 3 se 7 years |
| Stalking (BNS Section 78) | 3 years tak | 5 years tak |
| Online sexually explicit material (IT Act Section 67A) | 5 years tak aur Rs 10 lakh | 7 years tak |
| Sex determination karne wala doctor ya clinic (PC-PNDT Act) | 3 years tak aur Rs 10,000 | 5 years tak aur Rs 50,000 |
| POSH Act ko ignore karne wala employer | Rs 50,000 tak fine | Doguni saza, licence cancel ho sakta hai |

## Section 71: repeat rapist ke liye natural life ya death

Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ka Section 71 kehta hai ki jo pehle Sections 64, 65, 66 ya 70 ke under rape mein convict ho chuka hai, aur inmein se kisi ke under dobara convict hota hai, use apni baaki natural life ki jail ya death ki saza milegi [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Pehle rape conviction mein hi kam se kam 10 years aur life tak ki saza hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Farak yeh hai ki Section 71 judge ke paas sirf do options chhodta hai: offender ki baaki natural life ki jail, ya death.

Yeh rule 2012 ke Delhi gang rape case ke baad Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 se IPC mein Section 376E ke roop mein joda gaya tha [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].
