Iska pehla istemaal 4 April 2014 ko hua, jab Mumbai ki ek sessions court ne 2013 ke Shakti Mills gang rape cases ke teen repeat offenders ko death sentence diya [[livelaw-shakti-mills-death-sentence-2014]]. 25 November 2021 ko Bombay High Court ne yeh sentences life imprisonment mein badal diye, aur kaha ki ek constitutional court public opinion ke base par saza nahi de sakta [[barandbench-shakti-mills-hc-2021]]. Repeat-offender rule ka pehla test uske sabse sakht option ke hatne par khatam hua.

## Stalking, voyeurism aur online material: badhti hui saza

Chhote sexual offences mein steps chhote hain, lekin asli hain. Voyeurism, yaani kisi woman ko private act mein dekhna ya uski images capture karna, pehle conviction par 1 se 3 years aur repeat par 3 se 7 years ki saza laata hai. Stalking mein 3 years tak ki saza hai, jo badhkar 5 tak ho jaati hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Online abuse mein Information Technology Act bhi yahi logic follow karta hai. Obscene material publish karne par pehle conviction mein 3 years tak aur repeat par 5 tak ki saza hai. Sexually explicit material aur child sexual abuse material, jismein use banana, browse karna ya download karna bhi shaamil hai, pehli baar 5 years tak aur Rs 10 lakh fine, aur uske baad 7 years tak ki saza laate hain [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].

## Sex selection aur POSH Act: BNS ke bahar repeat penalties

Institutions par focus karne wale do laws bhi yahi seedhi use karte hain. PC-PNDT Act ke under sex determination karne wale doctor ya clinic ko 3 years tak aur Rs 10,000 fine ho sakta hai, jo badhkar 5 years aur Rs 50,000 ho jaata hai. Doctor ka registration pehle conviction ke baad 5 years ke liye aur doosre ke baad hamesha ke liye cancel hota hai [[indiacode-pcpndt-1994]]. Sex selection maangne wale ko 3 years tak aur Rs 50,000, jo badhkar 5 years aur Rs 1 lakh ho jaata hai. Law maan kar chalta hai ki pregnant woman ko uske husband ya rishtedaaron ne majboor kiya, aur jis woman par zabardasti hui use saza nahi deta [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]].

POSH Act ke under jo employer Internal Committee nahi banata ya uske findings par action nahi leta, use Rs 50,000 tak fine ho sakta hai. Repeat offence par doguni saza hoti hai aur business ka licence ya registration ja sakta hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

## Doosra offence, pehla conviction: asli pench

Yeh sab pehle conviction par tika hai, aur sexual-offence cases mein conviction exception hai. 2024 mein courts ne 5,032 rape cases mein conviction diya aur 13,980 mein acquit kiya, yaani poore hue 20,587 trials mein conviction rate 24.4% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Us saal ke aakhir mein 1,85,785 rape cases trial ke intezaar mein the, courts ke saamne ke saare cases ka 89.8% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Online stalking mein numbers aur bhi kade hain. 2024 mein women aur children ke khilaaf cyber stalking aur bullying ke jo 4,348 cases courts ke saamne the, unmein se sirf 33 conviction par khatam hue, aur 95.3% pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jab tak court ek baar kisi aadmi ka case khatam nahi karta, tab tak woh law mein repeat offender ban hi nahi sakta.

> Doosre conviction ki sakht saza utni hi mazboot hai jitna system pehla conviction dila paata hai.

Practical sabak yeh hai ki har complaint jo verdict tak pahunchti hai, wahi agli complaint ko wazan deti hai. Yeh kisi survivor par kisi ka karz nahi hai, aur kisi ko bhi apni safety ya marzi ke khilaaf case chalane ke liye dhakela nahi jaana chahiye. Lekin agar aap report karna chunti hain, toh police aur prosecutor se poochiye ki accused ka koi record hai ya nahi, "settle" karne ke dabaav ko mana kijiye, aur case ko aakhir tak le jaane ke liye District Legal Services Authority se free lawyer lijiye.

reverse-burden-of-proof-sexual-offence-l.en:
In an Indian criminal court, the prosecution carries the load. It must prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt, and the accused does not have to prove innocence. But in a few sexual and gender crimes Parliament has written a different opening line: the court shall presume. Presume that a person accused of sexually assaulting a child did it. Presume that a woman raped by someone in authority did not consent. Presume that a pregnancy from rape injures her mental health, and that a pregnant woman who sought sex selection was pushed into it. This explainer takes four such rules in turn. It is general information, not legal advice.

## Why presumptions exist in criminal law

A presumption does not create evidence. It decides who has to move first. Under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), which replaced the Evidence Act, when a court "shall presume" a fact, the fact is treated as proved unless it is disproved [[indiacode-bsa-2023]].

Parliament uses this tool where a crime happens behind a closed door and the accused holds power over the victim: an officer over a woman in custody, an adult over a child, a household over a pregnant woman.

| Law | What is presumed |
|---|---|
| POCSO, Section 29 | The accused committed the offence against the child |
| BSA, Section 120 | The woman did not consent, in aggravated rape |
| MTP Act | A pregnancy from rape gravely injures her mental health |
| PC-PNDT Act, Section 24 | The pregnant woman was compelled by her husband or relatives |

These are not the only ones. In a dowry death, the husband or in-laws are deemed to have caused the death [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The first presumption in a rape trial came in 1983, after protests over a 1978 acquittal in a custodial rape case. That year Parliament made custodial rape a separate aggravated offence and introduced a presumption of absence of consent, as Section 114A of the Indian Evidence Act [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

## POCSO Section 29: the accused must disprove

The strongest of the four reverses the usual burden outright. When a person is prosecuted for penetrative or sexual assault on a child, Section 29 says the Special Court must presume that he committed the offence unless the contrary is proved [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Imagine a nine-year-old in Bhopal who tells the court what her tuition teacher did. In an ordinary trial the defence needs only to raise a doubt. Under Section 29 it is the accused who must bring something: proof that he was elsewhere, or a reason the charge was invented. "Unless the contrary is proved" means he can. The presumption is rebuttable, as it should be.

It has limits. POCSO protects only those under 18 [[indiacode-pocso-2012]], so the child's age still has to be shown. And if a frightened child stops speaking, there is nothing left for the presumption to rest on.

## BSA Section 120: when her 'no' is presumed true

The 1983 rule was rewritten in 2013 and now sits in Section 120 of the BSA. It applies to prosecutions for aggravated rape under Section 64(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, the forms where the accused holds authority or trust: a police officer, a public servant, a relative, a guardian, hospital staff [[indiacode-bsa-2023]].

Two things must come first. Sexual intercourse by the accused has to be proved, and the woman has to state in her evidence that she did not consent. Then the court shall presume that she did not [[indiacode-bsa-2023]].

The rule is narrow. It is about consent, not about whether the act took place. And it does not reach every rape trial: outside the aggravated forms, the prosecution must still prove that she did not agree.

## Beyond rape: the abortion and sex-selection presumptions

Two presumptions sit outside the rape trial. They shield a woman instead of pointing at an accused.

Under the MTP Act, when a pregnant woman alleges that her pregnancy was caused by rape, the anguish it causes is presumed to be a grave injury to her mental health, which is a legal ground for termination. The same presumption was in the 1971 text, which makes it the oldest of the four [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. The word that matters is "alleges". The Supreme Court held in 2022 that she does not have to prove rape through formal legal proceedings: no FIR, no court finding, no conviction [[sc-x-principal-secretary-2022]]. For a girl under 18 one thing differs: POCSO's mandatory reporting rule still binds the doctor [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

The sex-selection law makes a presumption about families. Anyone who seeks sex selection faces up to three years in prison and a fine of up to Rs 50,000. But the court must presume, unless the contrary is proved, that the pregnant woman was compelled by her husband or another relative. A woman who was forced is not punished, and the relative is liable for abetment [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]]. The law starts from an assumption about Indian homes: that the woman in the clinic is not the one who decided.

## Why presumptions have not delivered convictions

If presumptions convicted people, POCSO courts would convict nearly everyone. In 2024 they convicted in 32.3% of the cases whose trials ended: 12,672 convictions against 25,476 acquittals [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. In rape trials the rate was 24.4% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. And police registered just 31 cases under the PC-PNDT Act that year, though such cases are often filed as court complaints by health authorities, so NCRB may undercount them [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

A presumption settles who loses when the evidence is in balance. It cannot supply an age certificate nobody collected, or keep a family from pressing a child to say she does not remember. It cannot shorten the wait: 2,86,903 POCSO cases were pending trial at the end of 2024, 87.7% of those before the courts [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

> A presumption tilts the scale. It does not put anything on it.

That is why the fixes lie outside the statute: fast recording of the child's evidence, protection for witnesses, investigations done as if no presumption existed. A reverse burden is a serious thing to do to an accused person, which is why Parliament has kept it to a few crimes. It works only when the evidence reaches the court.
reverse-burden-of-proof-sexual-offence-l.hg:
Indian criminal court mein bojh prosecution uthata hai. Use guilt reasonable doubt se pare saabit karna hota hai, aur accused ko apni begunahi saabit nahi karni hoti. Lekin kuch sexual aur gender crimes mein Parliament ne ek alag pehli line likhi hai: the court shall presume. Maan kar chalo ki jis insaan pe bachche ke sexual assault ka ilzaam hai, usne kiya hai. Maan kar chalo ki jis aurat ka rape kisi authority wale insaan ne kiya, usne consent nahi di thi. Maan kar chalo ki rape se hui pregnancy uski mental health ko chot pahunchati hai, aur jis pregnant aurat ne sex selection karwana chaha, use isme dhakela gaya tha. Yeh explainer aise chaar rules ko ek-ek karke dekhta hai. Yeh general jaankari hai, legal advice nahi.

## Criminal law mein presumptions hote hi kyun hain

Presumption evidence paida nahi karta. Woh yeh tay karta hai ki pehla kadam kise uthana hai. Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), jisne Evidence Act ki jagah li, ke tehat jab court kisi fact ko "shall presume" karta hai, to woh fact saabit maana jaata hai, jab tak use galat saabit na kar diya jaaye [[indiacode-bsa-2023]].

Parliament yeh tool wahan use karti hai jahan crime band darwaze ke peeche hota hai aur accused ke paas victim pe taaqat hoti hai: custody mein aurat pe ek officer ki, bachche pe ek adult ki, pregnant aurat pe ek poore ghar ki.

| Kanoon | Kya maan kar chala jaata hai |
|---|---|
| POCSO, Section 29 | Accused ne bachche ke khilaaf offence kiya hai |
| BSA, Section 120 | Aurat ne consent nahi di thi, aggravated rape mein |
| MTP Act | Rape se hui pregnancy uski mental health ko gehri chot pahunchati hai |
| PC-PNDT Act, Section 24 | Pregnant aurat ko uske pati ya rishtedaaron ne majboor kiya tha |

Yeh akele aise rules nahi hain. Dowry death mein pati ya sasural walon ke baare mein yeh maana jaata hai ki maut unhi ki wajah se hui [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Rape trial mein pehla presumption 1983 mein aaya, jab custodial rape ke ek case mein 1978 ke acquittal pe protests hue. Us saal Parliament ne custodial rape ko ek alag aggravated offence banaya aur consent na hone ka presumption laayi, Indian Evidence Act ke Section 114A ke roop mein [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

## POCSO Section 29: ulta saabit karna accused ka kaam

Chaaron mein sabse mazboot rule aam bojh ko seedha palat deta hai. Jab kisi insaan pe bachche ke penetrative ya sexual assault ka case chalta hai, to Section 29 kehta hai ki Special Court ko maan kar chalna hoga ki offence usi ne kiya hai, jab tak ulta saabit na ho [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Sochiye, Bhopal ki ek nau saal ki bachchi court ko batati hai ki uske tuition teacher ne kya kiya. Ek aam trial mein defence ko bas ek shak khada karna hota hai. Section 29 mein kuch laana accused ko padta hai: yeh saboot ki woh us waqt kahin aur tha, ya yeh wajah ki ilzaam gadha kyun gaya. "Unless the contrary is proved" ka matlab hai ki woh aisa kar sakta hai. Presumption rebut ho sakta hai, aur hona bhi chahiye.

Iski seemaayein hain. POCSO sirf 18 se kam umar walon ko protect karta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]], isliye bachche ki umar phir bhi dikhani padti hai. Aur agar dari hui bachchi bolna band kar de, to presumption ke paas tikne ko kuch nahi bachta.

## BSA Section 120: jab uski 'na' sach maani jaati hai

1983 ka rule 2013 mein dobara likha gaya aur ab BSA ke Section 120 mein hai. Yeh Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita ke Section 64(2) ke tehat aggravated rape ke prosecutions pe lagta hai, yaani un roopon pe jahan accused ke paas authority ya bharosa hota hai: police officer, public servant, rishtedaar, guardian, hospital staff [[indiacode-bsa-2023]].

Do cheezein pehle honi chahiye. Accused ka sexual intercourse saabit hona chahiye, aur aurat ko apni gawahi mein kehna hoga ki usne consent nahi di thi. Tab court maan kar chalega ki usne consent nahi di [[indiacode-bsa-2023]].

Yeh rule tang hai. Yeh consent ke baare mein hai, is baare mein nahi ki act hua ya nahi. Aur yeh har rape trial tak nahi pahunchta: aggravated roopon ke bahar prosecution ko ab bhi saabit karna hota hai ki woh raazi nahi thi.

## Rape ke aage: abortion aur sex selection ke presumptions

Do presumptions rape trial ke bahar hain. Yeh kisi accused ki taraf ungli uthane ke bajaye ek aurat ko bachate hain.

MTP Act ke tehat, jab pregnant aurat allege karti hai ki uski pregnancy rape se hui, to us pregnancy se hone wali takleef ko uski mental health pe grave injury maana jaata hai, aur yeh termination ka ek legal ground hai. Yahi presumption 1971 ke text mein bhi tha, isliye yeh chaaron mein sabse puraana hai [[gazette-mtp-amendment-act-2021]]. Yahan asli shabd hai "alleges". Supreme Court ne 2022 mein kaha ki use formal legal proceedings se rape saabit nahi karna hota: na FIR, na court ki finding, na conviction [[sc-x-principal-secretary-2022]]. 18 se kam umar ki ladki ke liye ek cheez alag hai: POCSO ka mandatory reporting rule doctor pe phir bhi laagu rehta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Sex selection wala kanoon families ke baare mein ek presumption banata hai. Jo bhi sex selection karwana chahta hai, use teen saal tak ki jail aur Rs 50,000 tak ka fine ho sakta hai. Lekin court ko maan kar chalna hota hai, jab tak ulta saabit na ho, ki pregnant aurat ko uske pati ya kisi aur rishtedaar ne majboor kiya tha. Jis aurat ko majboor kiya gaya use saza nahi hoti, aur rishtedaar abetment ke liye zimmedaar hota hai [[goi-pcpndt-act-1994]]. Kanoon Indian gharon ke baare mein ek assumption se shuru hota hai: ki clinic mein baithi aurat woh nahi hai jisne yeh faisla kiya.

## Presumptions convictions kyun nahi dila paaye

Agar presumptions se hi saza ho jaati, to POCSO courts lagbhag har accused ko convict kar dete. 2024 mein unhone un cases mein se 32.3% mein convict kiya jinke trials khatam hue: 12,672 convictions ke saamne 25,476 acquittals [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Rape trials mein yeh rate 24.4% tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Aur us saal police ne PC-PNDT Act ke tehat sirf 31 cases register kiye, haalanki aise cases aksar health authorities ki court complaints ke roop mein file hote hain, isliye NCRB inhe kam gin sakta hai [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Presumption yeh tay karta hai ki jab evidence barabar tula ho to kaun haarega. Woh ek aisa age certificate nahi la sakta jo kisi ne jama hi nahi kiya, aur family ko bachche pe yeh dabaav daalne se nahi rok sakta ki woh keh de "mujhe yaad nahi". Woh intezaar chhota nahi kar sakta: 2024 ke end mein 2,86,903 POCSO cases trial ka intezaar kar rahe the, yaani courts ke saamne aaye cases ka 87.7% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

> Presumption tarazu ko jhukata hai. Us pe kuch rakhta nahi.

Isiliye ilaaj kanoon ke bahar hai: bachche ka evidence jaldi record ho, gawahon ko suraksha mile, aur investigation aise ho jaise koi presumption hai hi nahi. Ulta bojh daalna accused ke saath ek serious cheez hai, isiliye Parliament ne ise kuch hi crimes tak rakha hai. Yeh tabhi kaam karta hai jab evidence court tak pahunche.

same-act-different-law-victim-identity.en:
Consider one act. An adult man forces penetrative sex on another person. Now change only one thing: who that person is. Indian law gives the same act a different name, a different court and a different sentence each time, and in one case no name at all. The differences do not measure harm. They exist because the laws were written separately, in different decades, for different groups of people. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Women: rape under Section 63

If the survivor is a woman, the act is rape. Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) defines it as penetration, or the insertion of any object or body part, done against a woman's will or without her consent [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

The punishment under Section 64 is at least 10 years' rigorous imprisonment and can extend to life [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. A woman officer must record the complaint, and the trial is held in camera [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

But the section fixes two words: only "a man" can commit rape, and only "a woman" can be its victim. Even for women the door has a lock. Exception 2 says sex by a man with his own wife, if she is not under 18, is not rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Every other door exists because of how narrowly this one was cut.

## Children of any gender: POCSO

If the survivor is under 18, a second law opens. The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, in force since 14 November 2012, defines a child as any person below 18 [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Its offences are written as acts against "a child", so boys are covered as victims just as girls are [[pocso-act-2012]].

Penetrative sexual assault carries at least 10 years, and at least 20 if the child is under 16. Aggravated cases can bring imprisonment for the rest of natural life, or death [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

A girl has both laws, because Section 63 also treats sex with a girl under 18 as rape whatever she says [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. A boy has only POCSO, and it is used: police recorded 892 boys among the 44,567 child victims of penetrative sexual assault in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. His protection ends on his eighteenth birthday.

## Dalit and Adivasi women: what the Atrocities Act adds

Caste does not change the rape charge, which stays under the BNS. It adds a second law on top. Since a 2015 amendment, Section 3(1)(w) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act makes it a separate atrocity to touch a Dalit or Adivasi woman in a sexual manner without her consent, or to use sexual words, acts or gestures towards her, knowing her caste or tribe. The punishment is six months to five years and a fine [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

States must also set up Exclusive Special Courts that, as far as possible, finish atrocity trials within two months of the charge sheet. A non-SC/ST public servant who wilfully fails to register the FIR under the correct sections faces six months to one year in prison [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

That duty matters because this door opens only when police write the Act into the FIR. NCRB counts a crime as an atrocity only when the Act is invoked [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]]. In 2024 it recorded 4,262 rape cases with Scheduled Caste victims and 1,268 with Scheduled Tribe victims [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A case where the sections were left out is in neither number.

## Transgender survivors: Section 18 and its two-year cap

If the survivor is a transgender person, the specific law is the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019. The word Section 18 uses is not rape but "sexual abuse". It lists this in the same clause as physical, verbal, emotional and economic abuse, and gives them all one sentence: six months to two years and a fine [[indiacode-transgender-persons-2019]].

The minimum for raping a woman is 10 years. The maximum for sexually abusing a transgender person is two.

Parliament has reopened this section since. The 2026 amendment, which received assent on 30 March 2026 and is under challenge in the Supreme Court, added offences carrying 10 years to life for kidnapping a person and causing grievous hurt to force them to present as transgender. It left the penalty for sexual abuse where it was [[gazette-transgender-amendment-2026]].

## Adult men: the offence that disappeared in 2024

Until 1 July 2024, a man assaulted this way had Section 377 of the Indian Penal Code, which punished non-consensual "carnal intercourse against the order of nature" with up to life imprisonment [[scroll-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]]. The BNS has no counterpart. Non-consensual penetrative sex against an adult man or a transgender person is not rape under the new code, and no specific offence replaced it [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

NCRB counted 888 cases under Section 377 in 2023. In its 2024 tables the category is gone, marked "deleted in BNS" [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. What remains are general offences such as hurt, which carries at most one year in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

| If the survivor is | The law calls it | Prison term |
|---|---|---|
| A woman | Rape (BNS) | 10 years to life |
| A child under 16, any gender | Penetrative sexual assault (POCSO) | At least 20 years |
| A transgender person | "Sexual abuse" (Transgender Persons Act) | 6 months to 2 years |
| An adult man | No specific offence; general charges such as hurt (BNS) | Hurt: up to 1 year |

Parliament was warned. On 10 November 2023, its Standing Committee on Home Affairs said dropping Section 377 would leave non-consensual sexual offences against men and transgender persons unpunished, and recommended keeping it. The government did not [[prs-standing-committee-bns-2023]]. In October 2024 the Supreme Court declined a plea to fill the gap, saying it cannot direct Parliament to create an offence [[livelaw-sc-bns-sexual-offences-men-pil-2024]]. In March 2026 the Delhi High Court revived a petition on the question because, in its words, "the decision is nowhere in sight" [[theprint-pti-delhi-hc-restores-pil-2026]].

The body does not sort itself into these categories. Whoever the survivor is, HIV post-exposure prophylaxis must start as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours after exposure [[who-pep]]. A police complaint can still be filed. Closing the gaps is Parliament's job, and its own committee has told it so in writing.
same-act-different-law-victim-identity.hg:
Ek act sochiye. Ek adult aadmi kisi doosre insaan ke saath zabardasti penetrative sex karta hai. Ab sirf ek cheez badaliye: woh insaan kaun hai. Indian law har baar usi act ko alag naam deta hai, alag court deta hai aur alag saza deta hai, aur ek case mein to koi naam hi nahi deta. Yeh farq nuksaan ka naap nahi hain. Yeh isliye hain kyunki kanoon alag-alag likhe gaye, alag-alag dashakon mein, alag-alag logon ke liye. Yeh general jaankari hai, legal advice nahi.

## Auratein: Section 63 ke tehat rape

Survivor aurat ho to yeh act rape hai. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ka Section 63 ise aise define karta hai: penetration, ya koi bhi object ya body part daalna, jo aurat ki marzi ke khilaaf ya uski consent ke bina kiya gaya ho [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Section 64 ke tehat saza kam se kam 10 saal ki rigorous imprisonment hai, jo life tak ja sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Complaint ek woman officer ko record karni hoti hai, aur trial in camera hota hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Lekin yeh section do shabd pakke kar deta hai: rape sirf "a man" kar sakta hai, aur uski victim sirf "a woman" ho sakti hai. Auraton ke liye bhi is darwaze pe ek taala hai. Exception 2 kehta hai ki aadmi ka apni patni ke saath sex, agar patni 18 se kam ki nahi hai, rape nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Baaki saare darwaze isi wajah se hain ki yeh wala itna tang kaata gaya.

## Kisi bhi gender ke bachche: POCSO

Survivor 18 se kam ka ho to ek doosra kanoon khulta hai. Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, jo 14 November 2012 se laagu hai, child ko aise define karta hai: 18 se kam umar ka koi bhi insaan [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Iske offences "a child" ke khilaaf kiye gaye acts ke roop mein likhe hain, isliye ladke bhi victim ke taur pe waise hi cover hote hain jaise ladkiyan [[pocso-act-2012]].

Penetrative sexual assault pe kam se kam 10 saal ki saza hai, aur bachcha 16 se kam ka ho to kam se kam 20 saal. Aggravated cases mein baaki poori natural life ki qaid, ya death, ho sakti hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Ladki ke paas dono kanoon hain, kyunki Section 63 bhi 18 se kam umar ki ladki ke saath sex ko rape maanta hai, chahe woh kuch bhi kahe [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Ladke ke paas sirf POCSO hai, aur woh use hota bhi hai: 2024 mein police ne penetrative sexual assault ke 44,567 child victims mein 892 ladke record kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Uski yeh suraksha uske atharahvein birthday pe khatam ho jaati hai.

## Dalit aur Adivasi auratein: Atrocities Act kya jodta hai

Caste se rape ka charge nahi badalta, woh BNS ke tehat hi rehta hai. Caste uske upar ek doosra kanoon jod deti hai. 2015 ke amendment ke baad se, SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act ka Section 3(1)(w) ise ek alag atrocity banata hai: kisi Dalit ya Adivasi aurat ko uski consent ke bina sexual tareeke se chhoona, ya uski taraf sexual shabd, harkatein ya ishaare karna, yeh jaante hue ki uski caste ya tribe kya hai. Saza chhah mahine se paanch saal aur fine hai [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

States ko Exclusive Special Courts bhi banane hote hain, jo jahan tak ho sake atrocity ke trials charge sheet ke do mahine ke andar poore karein. Jo non-SC/ST public servant jaan-boojhkar FIR sahi sections ke tehat register nahi karta, use chhah mahine se ek saal ki jail ho sakti hai [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

Yeh duty isliye maayne rakhti hai kyunki yeh darwaza tabhi khulta hai jab police FIR mein yeh Act likhe. NCRB kisi crime ko atrocity tabhi ginta hai jab yeh Act lagaya gaya ho [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]]. 2024 mein usne Scheduled Caste victims wale 4,262 rape cases aur Scheduled Tribe victims wale 1,268 rape cases record kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jis case mein yeh sections chhoot gaye, woh in dono numbers mein kahin nahi hai.

## Transgender survivors: Section 18 aur uski do saal ki seema

Survivor transgender person ho to specific kanoon hai Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019. Section 18 jo shabd use karta hai woh rape nahi, "sexual abuse" hai. Yeh use usi clause mein rakhta hai jismein physical, verbal, emotional aur economic abuse hain, aur in sab ke liye ek hi saza deta hai: chhah mahine se do saal aur fine [[indiacode-transgender-persons-2019]].

Aurat ke rape ki kam se kam saza 10 saal hai. Transgender person ke sexual abuse ki zyada se zyada saza do saal hai.

Parliament is section ko uske baad dobara khol chuki hai. 2026 ka amendment, jise 30 March 2026 ko assent mila aur jise Supreme Court mein challenge kiya gaya hai, naye offences laaya jin pe 10 saal se life tak ki saza hai: kisi ko kidnap karna aur grievous hurt pahunchana taaki woh majboori mein khud ko transgender ke roop mein pesh kare. Sexual abuse ki saza usne wahin chhod di jahan thi [[gazette-transgender-amendment-2026]].

## Adult aadmi: woh offence jo 2024 mein gaayab ho gaya

1 July 2024 tak, jis aadmi pe aisa assault hota, uske paas Indian Penal Code ka Section 377 tha, jo non-consensual "carnal intercourse against the order of nature" pe life imprisonment tak ki saza deta tha [[scroll-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]]. BNS mein iska koi counterpart nahi hai. Naye code mein adult aadmi ya transgender person ke saath non-consensual penetrative sex rape nahi hai, aur uski jagah koi specific offence nahi aaya [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

NCRB ne 2023 mein Section 377 ke tehat 888 cases gine the. 2024 ki tables mein yeh category hi nahi hai, uske aage likha hai "deleted in BNS" [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jo bacha hai woh hurt jaise general offences hain, jismein zyada se zyada ek saal ki jail hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

| Survivor kaun hai | Kanoon ise kya kehta hai | Jail ki saza |
|---|---|---|
| Aurat | Rape (BNS) | 10 saal se life tak |
| 16 se kam ka bachcha, kisi bhi gender ka | Penetrative sexual assault (POCSO) | Kam se kam 20 saal |
| Transgender person | "Sexual abuse" (Transgender Persons Act) | 6 mahine se 2 saal |
| Adult aadmi | Koi specific offence nahi; hurt jaise general charges (BNS) | Hurt: 1 saal tak |

Parliament ko pehle hi bataya gaya tha. 10 November 2023 ko uski apni Standing Committee on Home Affairs ne kaha tha ki Section 377 hatane se aadmiyon aur transgender persons ke khilaaf non-consensual sexual offences bina saza ke reh jayenge, aur ise rakhne ki sifarish ki thi. Government ne nahi maana [[prs-standing-committee-bns-2023]]. October 2024 mein Supreme Court ne yeh gap bharne ki plea sunne se mana kar diya, yeh kehte hue ki woh Parliament ko offence banane ka direction nahi de sakta [[livelaw-sc-bns-sexual-offences-men-pil-2024]]. March 2026 mein Delhi High Court ne isi sawaal pe ek petition dobara zinda ki kyunki, uske shabdon mein, "the decision is nowhere in sight" [[theprint-pti-delhi-hc-restores-pil-2026]].

Shareer khud ko in categories mein nahi baantta. Survivor koi bhi ho, HIV post-exposure prophylaxis jitni jaldi ho sake shuru hona chahiye, aur exposure ke 72 ghante ke baad nahi [[who-pep]]. Police complaint ab bhi ki ja sakti hai. In gaps ko band karna Parliament ka kaam hai, aur uski apni committee use yeh likh kar bata chuki hai.

section-69-job-promotion-identity-deceit.en:
Consider a hypothetical. A 22-year-old in Pune has cleared two interview rounds for her first job. The man running the hiring tells her the offer letter is ready, and that one thing stands between her and it. She gives in. There was never a vacancy. Under the old Indian Penal Code, what he did had no offence of its own. The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) gave it one, in a section most people think is only about marriage. This is general information, not legal advice.

## What does Section 69 say beyond marriage?

Section 69 punishes a man who has sex with a woman "by deceitful means", or by a promise of marriage made with no intention of keeping it. The sentence can go up to 10 years in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Public argument has been almost entirely about the marriage half.

The other half sits in the section's Explanation. "Deceitful means", it says, includes an inducement for, or a false promise of, employment or promotion, and "marrying by suppressing identity" [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. A recruiter, a manager or a man who marries under a hidden identity stands under the same section as a boyfriend who lied about a wedding.

Police registered 1,325 cases under Section 69 between July and December 2024, its first six months [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB prints the whole section as one row, so the figure cannot tell us how many cases involved a job, a promotion or an identity. Its cyber crime tables separately count 99 cases under the section [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. These are FIRs, not a measure of how often this happens.

## A false job or promotion: what has to be proved?

Going by the section's words, three things. That sexual intercourse took place. That it was obtained by deceit: the job or promotion was held out to get sex, and the promise was false. And that the act does not amount to rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

The third point decides which law applies. Section 63 treats sex as rape when it is against a woman's will, without her consent, or when her consent comes from fear of death or hurt [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Rape carries at least 10 years [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Section 69 is for the cases where she agreed, and the agreement was bought with a lie. If she refused, or was frightened into it, calling it "deceit" shrinks the crime.

The offence is new, and courts will settle case by case how "false promise" is read. What can be shown matters: was there a vacancy, could he hire or promote, what did he write, what happened afterwards.

One protection travels with the charge. In a Section 69 prosecution, the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam says a woman's character and her past sexual experience with anyone are not relevant to the question of consent [[indiacode-bsa-2023]].

The section has limits. It speaks only of a woman, so a man or a transgender person deceived in the same way is not covered. And if a girl is under 18, no promise matters: sex with her is rape whatever she says [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## What does 'marrying by suppressing identity' mean?

The law gives only those four words [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. It does not say which facts make up an identity, and that will be argued in courtrooms.

Two things can be read from the text. The example is about marrying, not about a false profile on a dating app. But the Explanation says deceitful means "shall include" its examples, so the list is not closed.

One kind of impersonation is treated more seriously: if a man gets consent by posing as the woman's husband, that is rape under Section 63 [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

The clause names no religion, caste or community. It is aimed at concealment. Two adults who marry knowing who the other is have hidden nothing, whatever their families think of the match.

## Section 68, Section 69 or the POSH Act: which applies when?

| Law | What it covers | What follows |
|---|---|---|
| Section 68, BNS | A person in authority who abuses that position to get sex from a woman in his custody or care | 5 to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment |
| Section 69, BNS | Sex obtained by a false promise of marriage, a job or a promotion, or by marrying with a hidden identity | Up to 10 years in prison |
| Section 75, BNS | Sexual harassment | Up to 3 years |
| POSH Act, 2013 | Sexual harassment of women at a workplace | A committee inquiry, to finish within 90 days |

Section 68 covers a person in authority, a public servant, or jail, institution or hospital staff, and sets a floor of 5 years [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Section 69 needs no custody and no post: only the lie.

The POSH Act is not a criminal trial. Every employer must set up an Internal Complaints Committee, districts run Local Committees for workplaces with fewer than 10 workers, a complaint must be filed within 3 months (extendable by up to 3 more), and an employer who does not comply can be fined up to Rs 50,000 [[indiacode-posh-2013]]. Its "workplace" is wide, covering places visited for work and employer-provided transport [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

Recruitment is where it gets shaky. The Act protects a woman "of any age whether employed or not" [[gazette-posh-act-2013]], yet the Kerala High Court has remarked orally that it does not reach women who are still seeking work [[livelaw-kerala-hc-hema-draft-law-2025]]. Section 69 does not ask whether she was ever on the payroll.

Section 69 has a gap of its own. The BNSS tells police to finish rape investigations within two months, and that list includes Section 68 but not Section 69 [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## How do I report it, and what should I keep?

A complaint about a cognizable offence can be given at any police station, wherever the offence happened, or sent electronically and signed within 3 days. You must get a copy of the FIR free of cost [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Tell the police everything, including any threat or force, so the right sections are applied.

If it happened in a working relationship, a written complaint to the Internal Committee or the Local Committee is a separate route. One does not close the other, but the committee's 3-month clock is short [[indiacode-posh-2013]].

Keep the trail a false promise leaves: the job advertisement, the offer letter or its absence, emails, chats, call logs, and the names of people who knew about the offer. Do not delete conversations that embarrass you. Write a dated note of what was promised, when and where. Women Helpline 181 can guide you to support.

A man who trades a job for sex counts on the woman believing that she "agreed" and so has no case. The law now says otherwise.
section-69-job-promotion-identity-deceit.hg:
Ek hypothetical socho. Pune ki ek 22 saal ki ladki ne apni pehli job ke do interview rounds clear kar liye hain. Hiring sambhaalne wala aadmi kehta hai ki offer letter ready hai, bas ek cheez beech mein hai. Woh maan jaati hai. Vacancy kabhi thi hi nahi. Purane Indian Penal Code mein is harkat ka apna koi offence nahi tha. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ne ise ek offence diya, aur woh bhi us section mein jise zyada tar log sirf shaadi ke baare mein samajhte hain. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Section 69 shaadi ke alawa kya kehta hai?

Section 69 us aadmi ko saza deta hai jo "deceitful means" yaani dhoke se, ya shaadi ka aisa promise karke jise nibhane ka koi intention na ho, kisi woman ke saath sex karta hai. Saza 10 saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Public behes lagbhag poori tarah shaadi wale hisse pe hi rahi hai.

Doosra hissa section ki Explanation mein hai. Woh kehti hai ki "deceitful means" mein naukri ya promotion ka laalach ya jhootha promise, aur "identity chhupakar shaadi karna" shaamil hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Yaani recruiter, manager, ya chhupi identity ke saath shaadi karne wala aadmi usi section ke neeche khada hai jiske neeche shaadi ka jhooth bolne wala boyfriend.

Police ne July se December 2024 ke beech, yaani iske pehle chhe mahino mein, Section 69 mein 1,325 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB poore section ko ek hi row mein chhaapta hai, isliye yeh number nahi bata sakta ki kitne cases mein job, promotion ya identity ka maamla tha. Uski cyber crime tables alag se is section ke 99 cases ginti hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh FIRs hain, yeh is baat ka naap nahi ki aisa kitni baar hota hai.

## Jhoothi job ya promotion: kya saabit karna padta hai?

Section ke shabdon ke hisaab se, teen cheezein. Ki sex hua. Ki woh dhoke se haasil kiya gaya: job ya promotion sex paane ke liye saamne rakha gaya, aur promise jhootha tha. Aur ki yeh kaam rape tak nahi pahunchta [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Teesri baat hi tay karti hai ki kaunsa law lagega. Section 63 sex ko rape maanta hai jab woh woman ki marzi ke khilaaf ho, bina uski consent ke ho, ya jab uski consent maut ya chot ke darr se li gayi ho [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Rape mein kam se kam 10 saal ki saza hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Section 69 un cases ke liye hai jahan woman ne haan kahi, lekin woh haan ek jhooth se khareedi gayi. Agar usne mana kiya tha, ya use daraakar manaaya gaya, toh use "dhoka" kehna crime ko chhota kar deta hai.

Offence naya hai, aur courts case-by-case tay karenge ki "jhootha promise" kaise padha jaaye. Jo dikhaya ja sake, wahi kaam aata hai: kya vacancy thi, kya woh aadmi hire ya promote kar sakta tha, usne kya likha, aur baad mein kya hua.

Ek protection is charge ke saath chalti hai. Section 69 ke prosecution mein, Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam ke hisaab se, woman ka character aur kisi ke bhi saath uska pichhla sexual experience consent ke sawaal pe relevant nahi hai [[indiacode-bsa-2023]].

Section ki apni limits hain. Yeh sirf woman ki baat karta hai, toh agar kisi man ya transgender person ke saath aisa hi dhoka ho, toh woh cover nahi hote. Aur agar ladki 18 se kam hai, toh koi promise matter nahi karta: uske saath sex rape hai, chahe woh kuch bhi kahe [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## 'Identity chhupakar shaadi' ka matlab kya hai?

Law sirf itne hi shabd deta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Woh yeh nahi batata ki kaunsi baatein milkar identity banti hain, aur is pe courtrooms mein behes hogi.

Text se do baatein padhi ja sakti hain. Example shaadi ka hai, dating app pe fake profile ka nahi. Lekin Explanation kehti hai ki deceitful means mein yeh examples "shaamil honge", yaani list band nahi hai.

Ek tarah ka impersonation zyada serious maana jaata hai: agar aadmi khud ko woman ka pati batakar consent leta hai, toh woh Section 63 ke under rape hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Is clause mein kisi dharm, jaati ya community ka naam nahi hai. Iska nishaana chhupana hai. Do adults jo ek doosre ko jaante hue shaadi karte hain, unhone kuch nahi chhupaya, chahe unki families is rishte ke baare mein kuch bhi sochein.

## Section 68, Section 69 ya POSH Act: kab kya lagta hai?

| Law | Kya cover karta hai | Aage kya hota hai |
|---|---|---|
| Section 68, BNS | Authority wala insaan jo apni position ka galat use karke custody ya care mein rahi woman se sex haasil kare | 5 se 10 saal rigorous imprisonment |
| Section 69, BNS | Shaadi, naukri ya promotion ke jhoothe promise se, ya chhupi identity ke saath shaadi karke haasil kiya sex | 10 saal tak jail |
| Section 75, BNS | Sexual harassment | 3 saal tak |
| POSH Act, 2013 | Workplace pe women ka sexual harassment | Committee inquiry, 90 din mein poori honi chahiye |

Section 68 authority wale insaan, public servant, ya jail, institution ya hospital staff ko cover karta hai, aur kam se kam 5 saal ki saza rakhta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Section 69 ke liye na custody chahiye, na koi post: sirf jhooth.

POSH Act criminal trial nahi hai. Har employer ko Internal Complaints Committee banani hoti hai, 10 se kam workers wali jagahon ke liye district Local Committees chalaata hai, complaint 3 mahine ke andar deni hoti hai (jo 3 mahine aur badh sakti hai), aur jo employer law nahi maanta use Rs 50,000 tak ka fine ho sakta hai [[indiacode-posh-2013]]. Iski "workplace" ki definition badi hai: kaam ke liye jaayi gayi jagahein aur employer ka diya transport bhi isme aata hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]].

Recruitment pe aakar baat dagmagaati hai. Act "kisi bhi umar ki woman, chahe employed ho ya nahi" ko protect karta hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]], phir bhi Kerala High Court ne oral remark kiya hai ki yeh un women tak nahi pahunchta jo abhi kaam dhoondh rahi hain [[livelaw-kerala-hc-hema-draft-law-2025]]. Section 69 yeh nahi poochta ki woh kabhi payroll pe thi ya nahi.

Section 69 ka apna ek gap hai. BNSS police ko rape investigations do mahine mein poori karne ko kehta hai, aur us list mein Section 68 hai, Section 69 nahi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Report kaise karein, aur kya sambhaal ke rakhein?

Cognizable offence ki complaint kisi bhi police station mein di ja sakti hai, chahe offence kahin bhi hua ho, ya electronically bheji ja sakti hai jise 3 din ke andar sign karna hota hai. FIR ki copy tumhe free milni chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Police ko sab kuch batao, koi dhamki ya zabardasti bhi, taaki sahi sections lagein.

Agar yeh kisi working relationship mein hua, toh Internal Committee ya Local Committee ko likhit complaint ek alag raasta hai. Ek raasta doosre ko band nahi karta, lekin committee ki 3 mahine ki ghadi chhoti hai [[indiacode-posh-2013]].

Jhootha promise jo nishaan chhodta hai, woh rakho: job advertisement, offer letter ya uska na hona, emails, chats, call logs, aur un logon ke naam jinhe offer ke baare mein pata tha. Jo baatcheet sharmindagi wali lage, use bhi delete mat karo. Ek dated note likho ki kya promise hua, kab aur kahan. Women Helpline 181 tumhe support tak pahuncha sakti hai.

Jo aadmi sex ke badle naukri ka sauda karta hai, woh is bharose pe chalta hai ki woman maanegi ki usne "haan kahi thi", isliye uska koi case nahi banta. Law ab kuch aur kehta hai.

sexual-harassment-which-law-applies-wher.en:
Consider one act in four places. A man makes a sexual remark to a woman and will not stop. If he is her manager, one law applies. If he is a relative she lives with, another. If he is a stranger on a bus, a third. If he does it through her phone, a fourth.

Police records blur this map. Of the 15,609 sexual harassment cases registered in India in 2024, 12,592, or 81%, were recorded at "other places" [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The law is more precise. This guide matches each setting to its law, its forum and its deadline. It is general information, not legal advice.

| Where it happens | Main law | First door |
|---|---|---|
| Workplace | POSH Act, 2013 | Internal Committee or Local Committee |
| Home | Domestic Violence Act, 2005 | Magistrate's court |
| Street, transport | BNS Sections 74 to 79 | Any police station |
| Online | IT Act, BNS Section 77 | Platform, cybercrime.gov.in, police |

## At work: the POSH Act and its committees

"Workplace" is wider than an office. The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013 (the POSH Act) covers private entertainment businesses, hospitals, any sports institute, stadium or competition venue, places visited in the course of work, including transport the employer provides, and homes where domestic workers are employed [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. It protects a woman "of any age whether employed or not", so a client, a patient or a visiting student can complain too.

Every employer must set up an Internal Complaints Committee [[indiacode-posh-2013]]. Where a workplace has fewer than 10 workers, or the complaint is against the employer himself, it goes to the district's Local Committee. A domestic worker also complains there, and the Local Committee must send a prima facie case to the police within seven days [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Complaints can be lodged online on the government's SHe-Box portal as well [[shebox]]. The Act protects only women.

This route has the tightest clock. The complaint must be in writing and filed within 3 months of the incident, or of the last incident in a series. The committee can extend that by up to 3 more months if circumstances stopped the woman from complaining in time. The inquiry must then finish within 90 days [[indiacode-posh-2013]].

## At home: the Domestic Violence Act's 'sexual abuse'

The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 counts "sexual abuse" as domestic violence: any conduct of a sexual nature that abuses, humiliates, degrades or otherwise violates a woman's dignity [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. A woman facing this from someone she lives with as family can ask a magistrate's court for protection and residence orders.

This is mainly a civil law. The abuse is not itself punished under the Act; breaching a protection order is, with up to 1 year in prison or a Rs 20,000 fine [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. That is why police registered only 616 cases under it in 2024, 496 of them in Kerala [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The number shows how rarely the Act's criminal clause is used, not how much abuse happens in homes.

The criminal sections described next apply inside a house as much as on a road. And when the person harassed at home is under 18, of any gender, the law is POCSO [[pocso-act-2012]].

## On the street and in transport: BNS Sections 74 to 79

In public, the law is the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the forum is the police [[indiacode-bns-2023]]:

- **Section 74**, assault to outrage a woman's modesty: 1 to 5 years.
- **Section 75**, sexual harassment: up to 3 years, or up to 1 year for sexually coloured remarks.
- **Section 76**, assault to disrobe: 3 to 7 years.
- **Section 77**, voyeurism: 1 to 3 years on a first conviction, 3 to 7 on a repeat.
- **Section 78**, stalking: up to 3 years, rising to 5 on a repeat.
- **Section 79**, words or gestures insulting a woman's modesty: up to 3 years.

You can report at any police station, wherever it happened, or by electronic communication that you sign within 3 days, and you must get a free copy of the FIR. A woman's complaint of sexual harassment, stalking or voyeurism must be recorded by a woman officer [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. One catch: for offences punishable with three to under seven years, police may, with a Deputy Superintendent's permission, hold a preliminary enquiry of up to 14 days before registering the case [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

These sections are written around women as victims, and sexual harassment and stalking can, by their wording, be committed only by a man. Others get thinner cover: sexual abuse of a transgender person carries only six months to two years under the Transgender Persons Act [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

## Online: the IT Act, Section 77 and the cybercrime portal

Two laws overlap here. Section 66E of the Information Technology Act punishes capturing, publishing or transmitting an image of any person's private area without consent with up to 3 years in prison, a fine of up to Rs 2 lakh, or both [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. Section 77 of the BNS treats sharing a private image of a woman without her consent as voyeurism even if she agreed to the image being taken: 1 to 3 years on a first conviction [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Three doors are open, and you can use all of them. Platforms must remove nude, sexual or morphed images of a person within two hours of that person's complaint, a rule in force since 20 February 2026 [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. The National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, cybercrime.gov.in, was launched with a specific focus on crimes against women and children [[pib-mha-i4c-launch-2020]], and its helpline is 1930 [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]]. The police route is the same as for the street.

## Using two routes at once

These routes are not either-or. Imagine a nurse whose supervisor corners her on the ward and messages her at night. The hospital is a workplace, so she can go to the Internal Committee, within 3 months. The same conduct can be reported to the police as sexual harassment. If he shares a private image of her, Section 77, the platform and the cybercrime portal come in.

Or imagine a wife whose husband sends her intimate pictures to others. She can seek a protection order under the Domestic Violence Act and report the images under Section 77 and the IT Act.

Three rules help in choosing.

- **Shortest clock first.** The POSH window is 3 months. File there before it closes, even if you also go to the police.
- **Evidence before action.** Save messages, dates and names before you block, report or confront.
- **Safety before both.** If you are in danger, call 112.

No door is perfect. Knowing which one fits the place where it happened saves time you cannot get back.
sexual-harassment-which-law-applies-wher.hg:
Ek hi harkat ko chaar jagah rakh kar dekho. Ek aadmi kisi woman par sexual remark karta hai aur rukta nahin. Agar woh uska manager hai, toh ek law lagta hai. Agar woh ghar mein saath rehne wala rishtedaar hai, toh doosra. Agar woh bus mein mila koi ajnabi hai, toh teesra. Aur agar woh yeh sab uske phone ke zariye karta hai, toh chautha.

Police ke records is map ko dhundhla kar dete hain. 2024 mein India mein sexual harassment ke jo 15,609 cases darj hue, unmein se 12,592, yaani 81%, "other places" ke khaane mein likhe gaye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Law isse kahin zyada saaf hai. Yeh guide har jagah ko uske law, uske forum aur uski deadline se jodti hai. Yeh general jaankari hai, legal advice nahin.

| Kahan hua | Main law | Pehla darwaza |
|---|---|---|
| Workplace | POSH Act, 2013 | Internal Committee ya Local Committee |
| Ghar | Domestic Violence Act, 2005 | Magistrate ki court |
| Sadak, transport | BNS Sections 74 se 79 | Koi bhi police station |
| Online | IT Act, BNS Section 77 | Platform, cybercrime.gov.in, police |

## Kaam ki jagah par: POSH Act aur uski committees

"Workplace" ka matlab sirf office nahin hai. Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013 (POSH Act) private entertainment businesses, hospitals, har sports institute, stadium ya competition venue, kaam ke silsile mein jahan jaana pade woh jagah, employer ka diya hua transport, aur woh ghar bhi cover karta hai jahan domestic workers kaam karti hain [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Yeh us woman ko protect karta hai jo "of any age whether employed or not" ho, yaani kisi bhi umar ki, naukri par ho ya nahin. Isliye client, patient ya visit par aayi student bhi complaint kar sakti hai.

Har employer ko Internal Complaints Committee banani hoti hai [[indiacode-posh-2013]]. Jahan 10 se kam workers hain, ya complaint khud employer ke khilaaf hai, wahan complaint district ki Local Committee ke paas jaati hai. Domestic worker bhi wahin complaint karti hai, aur Local Committee ko prima facie case saat din ke andar police ko bhejna hota hai [[gazette-posh-act-2013]]. Complaint government ke SHe-Box portal par online bhi di ja sakti hai [[shebox]]. Yeh Act sirf women ko protect karta hai.

Is raaste ki ghadi sabse tez chalti hai. Complaint likhit mein honi chahiye aur incident ke, ya ek ke baad ek hue incidents mein aakhri incident ke, 3 months ke andar deni hoti hai. Agar haalaat ne woman ko time par complaint karne se roka tha, toh committee yeh time 3 months tak aur badha sakti hai. Uske baad inquiry 90 din ke andar poori honi chahiye [[indiacode-posh-2013]].

## Ghar par: Domestic Violence Act ka 'sexual abuse'

Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 "sexual abuse" ko domestic violence maanta hai: sexual nature ka koi bhi conduct jo woman ko abuse kare, humiliate kare, degrade kare ya kisi aur tarah uski dignity ko thes pahunchaye [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Jis woman ke saath yeh uske saath family ki tarah rehne wala koi insaan kar raha ho, woh magistrate ki court se protection aur residence orders maang sakti hai.

Yeh mainly ek civil law hai. Is Act mein abuse ki apne aap mein koi saza nahin hai; saza protection order todne par hai, 1 saal tak ki jail ya Rs 20,000 ka fine [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Isi wajah se 2024 mein police ne iske under sirf 616 cases darj kiye, jinmein se 496 Kerala ke the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh number batata hai ki Act ka criminal clause kitna kam use hota hai, yeh nahin ki gharon mein kitna abuse hota hai.

Aage jo criminal sections bataye gaye hain, woh ghar ke andar bhi utne hi laagu hain jitne sadak par. Aur agar ghar mein harass hone wala insaan 18 se kam umar ka hai, gender koi bhi ho, toh law POCSO hai [[pocso-act-2012]].

## Sadak par aur transport mein: BNS Sections 74 se 79

Public jagah par law Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) hai aur forum police hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]:

- **Section 74**, woman ki modesty outrage karne ke liye assault: 1 se 5 saal.
- **Section 75**, sexual harassment: 3 saal tak, aur sexually coloured remarks ke liye 1 saal tak.
- **Section 76**, disrobe karne ke liye assault: 3 se 7 saal.
- **Section 77**, voyeurism: pehli conviction par 1 se 3 saal, dobara par 3 se 7 saal.
- **Section 78**, stalking: 3 saal tak, dobara karne par 5 saal tak.
- **Section 79**, woman ki modesty ka insult karne wale shabd ya ishaare: 3 saal tak.

Report kisi bhi police station mein ho sakti hai, baat chahe kahin bhi hui ho, ya electronic communication se, jis par 3 din ke andar sign karna hota hai. FIR ki copy free milni chahiye. Jab koi woman sexual harassment, stalking ya voyeurism ki complaint kare, toh use woman officer hi record karegi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Ek catch hai: jin offences ki saza teen saal se lekar saat saal se kam tak hai, unmein police, Deputy Superintendent ki permission se, case darj karne se pehle 14 din tak ki preliminary enquiry kar sakti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Yeh sections women ko victim maan kar likhe gaye hain, aur apne shabdon ke hisaab se sexual harassment aur stalking sirf ek aadmi hi kar sakta hai. Baaki logon ke paas kam suraksha hai: transgender person ke sexual abuse par Transgender Persons Act ke under sirf chhe mahine se do saal ki saza hai [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

## Online: IT Act, Section 77 aur cybercrime portal

Yahan do laws ek saath lagte hain. Information Technology Act ka Section 66E kisi bhi insaan ke private area ki image uski consent ke bina capture, publish ya transmit karne par 3 saal tak ki jail, Rs 2 lakh tak ka fine, ya dono ki saza deta hai [[indiacode-it-act-2000]]. BNS ka Section 77 kisi woman ki private image uski consent ke bina share karne ko voyeurism maanta hai, chahe image lene ke liye woh raazi rahi ho: pehli conviction par 1 se 3 saal [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Teen darwaze khule hain, aur teeno ek saath use kiye ja sakte hain. Platforms ko kisi insaan ki nude, sexual ya morphed images uski complaint ke do ghante ke andar hataani hoti hain; yeh rule 20 February 2026 se laagu hai [[meity-it-amendment-rules-2026]]. National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, cybercrime.gov.in, women aur bachchon ke khilaaf crimes par khaas focus ke saath launch hua tha [[pib-mha-i4c-launch-2020]], aur iski helpline 1930 hai [[pib-mha-cyber-awareness-2026]]. Police wala raasta wahi hai jo sadak ke liye hai.

## Do raaste ek saath

Yeh raaste "ya yeh, ya woh" nahin hain. Socho ek nurse hai jiska supervisor use ward mein gher leta hai aur raat ko messages bhejta hai. Hospital ek workplace hai, isliye woh 3 months ke andar Internal Committee ke paas ja sakti hai. Wahi harkat police mein sexual harassment ke taur par report ho sakti hai. Agar woh uski koi private image share karta hai, toh Section 77, platform aur cybercrime portal bhi saath aa jaate hain.

Ya socho ek wife hai jiska husband uski intimate pictures doosron ko bhej deta hai. Woh Domestic Violence Act ke under protection order maang sakti hai aur images ki report Section 77 aur IT Act ke under kar sakti hai.

Chunte waqt teen rules kaam aate hain.

- **Sabse chhoti deadline pehle.** POSH ki window 3 months ki hai. Uske band hone se pehle wahan complaint do, chahe saath mein police ke paas bhi jao.
- **Action se pehle evidence.** Block, report ya saamna karne se pehle messages, dates aur naam save karo.
- **Dono se pehle safety.** Khatra ho toh 112 call karo.

Koi bhi darwaza perfect nahin hai. Par yeh pata ho ki jahan baat hui wahan kaun sa darwaza khulta hai, toh woh time bachta hai jo wapas nahin milta.

sexual-offences-ranked-by-punishment-ind.en:
Put every punishment in India's sexual-offence laws on one table and sort it from lightest to heaviest. At the bottom sits a fine of up to Rs 20,000 [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. At the top sits death [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The order in between records which harms Parliament treated as grave, which it treated as minor, and whose bodies it had in mind when it wrote each law.

The table ranks six offences by the most a court can give. It is general information, not legal advice.

| Offence | Law | Punishment |
|---|---|---|
| Breaching a domestic-violence protection order | Domestic Violence Act, 2005 | up to 1 year or Rs 20,000 |
| Sexual abuse of a transgender person | Transgender Persons Act, Section 18 | 6 months to 2 years |
| Sexual harassment | BNS Section 75 | up to 3 years |
| Husband forcing sex on a separated wife | BNS Section 67 | 2 to 7 years |
| Acid attack | BNS Section 124(1) | 10 years to life |
| Second rape conviction | BNS Section 71 | natural life or death |

## Fines and short terms: the bottom of the table

The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 counts sexual abuse as a form of domestic violence. But it is mainly a civil law of protection, residence and maintenance orders. The crime it creates for an abuser is breaching a protection order: at most 1 year in prison, a fine of up to Rs 20,000, or both [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Police registered only 616 criminal cases under the Act in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

If a husband forces sex on a wife who is 18 or older and lives with him, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) says it is not rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The Domestic Violence Act can order the abuse to stop, but the only jail term it carries punishes disobeying the court, not the sexual violence itself.

One step up is Section 18 of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019: sexual abuse of a transgender person carries 6 months to 2 years and a fine [[indiacode-transgender-persons-2019]]. An amendment that received assent on 30 March 2026 rewrote the section and kept that range [[gazette-transgender-amendment-2026]].

An adult man has less still. The BNS has no counterpart to the old Section 377 of the IPC, so non-consensual penetrative sex against him is not rape under the code, and no specific offence replaced it. Only general offences may apply, such as voluntarily causing hurt: at most 1 year, a fine of up to Rs 10,000, or both [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Up to three years: harassment, voyeurism, image abuse

The next band holds what many women know from a bus, a classroom or a phone. Sexual harassment (Section 75) and words or gestures meant to insult a woman's modesty (Section 79) each carry up to 3 years. Stalking carries up to 3 years, and 5 on a repeat (Section 78). Voyeurism, which includes sharing a private image a woman agreed to have taken but not passed on, carries 1 to 3 years on first conviction and 3 to 7 on a repeat (Section 77) [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Under Section 66E of the IT Act, capturing or publishing an image of any person's private area without consent carries up to 3 years, a fine of up to Rs 2 lakh, or both [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].

A low maximum also changes what happens at the police station. For offences punishable with three to under seven years, police may, with a Deputy Superintendent's permission, hold a preliminary enquiry of up to 14 days before registering the case. Rape, with its 10-year minimum, falls outside that window [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Offences with a floor: disrobing, acid attacks, rape

In the next band every offence comes with a minimum, a floor below which a court cannot go. Assault meant to outrage a woman's modesty carries 1 to 5 years (Section 74), and assault to disrobe her 3 to 7 (Section 76). A husband who has sex with his wife without her consent while they live separately faces 2 to 7 years (Section 67). A person in authority who abuses his position to get a woman in his custody to have sex with him, short of rape, faces 5 to 10 years (Section 68) [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Then the scale jumps. An acid attack that causes damage, burns or disability carries at least 10 years and up to life, with a fine paid to the victim for treatment (Section 124). Rape carries at least 10 years' rigorous imprisonment and up to life (Section 64) [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## The top: natural life and death

Above the 10-year floor, the BNS adds rungs for the cases it treats as worst. Thirteen aggravated forms of rape, including rape by a police officer, a relative or a teacher, carry 10 years to imprisonment for the rest of natural life. Rape of a girl under 16 carries 20 years to natural life; under 12, the same or death. Gang rape carries 20 years to natural life for every member of the group, and natural life or death if the girl is under 18. A second rape conviction carries natural life or death, with no term of years at all [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

For children, the POCSO Act punishes aggravated penetrative sexual assault on a child with 20 years to natural life, or death, and it protects boys and girls alike [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

## What the ranking says about whose harm counts

Read the table by victim instead of by offence. Take one act: forced penetrative sex. Against a woman who is not the man's wife, the floor is 10 years. Against a wife living apart from him, the range is 2 to 7 years. Against a wife aged 18 or older who lives with him, it is not rape. Against a transgender person, the charge is "sexual abuse", with a ceiling of 2 years. Against an adult man, the BNS has no specific offence to charge.

Parliament was told about that last gap. On 10 November 2023 its Standing Committee on Home Affairs warned that dropping Section 377 would leave non-consensual sexual offences against men and transgender persons unpunished, and recommended keeping it. The government did not accept the recommendation [[prs-standing-committee-bns-2023]].

A maximum also says nothing about what courts do. It is the most a judge may give, and only after a conviction. In 2024, courts convicted in 24.4% of the rape trials they completed. Of 804 acid-attack cases on women before the courts that year, trials finished in 24 and 13 ended in conviction [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

A low rung is still a crime, and still worth reporting. Where the table has a gap, the fault lies in the statute, not in the person who was harmed.
sexual-offences-ranked-by-punishment-ind.hg:
India ke sexual-offence laws ki har saza ko ek table par rakhiye aur sabse halki se sabse bhaari tak laga dijiye. Sabse neeche Rs 20,000 tak ka fine hai [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. Sabse upar death hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Beech ka order batata hai ki Parliament ne kis nuksaan ko gambhir maana, kise chhota, aur har law likhte waqt uske dimaag mein kiska shareer tha.

Yeh table chhah offences ko us saza ke hisaab se rank karti hai jo court zyada se zyada de sakta hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

| Offence | Law | Saza |
|---|---|---|
| Domestic-violence protection order todna | Domestic Violence Act, 2005 | 1 saal tak ya Rs 20,000 |
| Transgender insaan ka sexual abuse | Transgender Persons Act, Section 18 | 6 mahine se 2 saal |
| Sexual harassment | BNS Section 75 | 3 saal tak |
| Alag reh rahi patni par pati ka zabardasti sex | BNS Section 67 | 2 se 7 saal |
| Acid attack | BNS Section 124(1) | 10 saal se life |
| Rape ki doosri conviction | BNS Section 71 | natural life ya death |

## Fine aur chhoti sazaayein: table ka sabse nichla hissa

Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 sexual abuse ko domestic violence ka ek roop maanta hai. Par yeh zyada tar ek civil law hai, jo protection, residence aur maintenance ke orders deta hai. Abuser ke liye isme jo crime banta hai, woh hai protection order todna: zyada se zyada 1 saal ki jail, Rs 20,000 tak ka fine, ya dono [[indiacode-pwdva-2005]]. 2024 mein police ne is Act ke tahat sirf 616 criminal cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Agar pati apni 18 saal ya usse zyada umar ki patni ke saath, jo uske saath rehti hai, zabardasti sex kare, toh Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) kehti hai ki yeh rape nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Domestic Violence Act abuse rokne ka order de sakta hai, par isme jo ikloti jail ki saza hai woh court ka order na maanne ki hai, khud sexual violence ki nahi.

Ek kadam upar Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019 ka Section 18 hai: transgender insaan ke sexual abuse par 6 mahine se 2 saal ki qaid aur fine [[indiacode-transgender-persons-2019]]. Jis amendment ko 30 March 2026 ko assent mila, usne yeh section dobara likha aur yahi range rakhi [[gazette-transgender-amendment-2026]].

Adult aadmi ke paas isse bhi kam hai. BNS mein IPC ke purane Section 377 jaisa koi section nahi hai, isliye uske saath non-consensual penetrative sex is code mein rape nahi hai, aur uski jagah koi specific offence bhi nahi aaya. Sirf general offences lag sakte hain, jaise voluntarily causing hurt: zyada se zyada 1 saal, Rs 10,000 tak ka fine, ya dono [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Teen saal tak: harassment, voyeurism, image abuse

Agle band mein woh sab hai jo bahut si aurtein bus, classroom ya phone se jaanti hain. Sexual harassment (Section 75) aur aurat ki modesty ka apmaan karne wale shabd ya ishaare (Section 79), dono mein 3 saal tak ki saza hai. Stalking par 3 saal tak, aur dobara karne par 5 saal tak (Section 78). Voyeurism, jismein woh private image share karna bhi shamil hai jo aurat ne khinchwane ke liye toh haan kaha tha par aage bhejne ke liye nahi, pehli conviction par 1 se 3 saal aur dobara par 3 se 7 saal (Section 77) [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. IT Act ke Section 66E mein kisi bhi insaan ke private area ki image uski consent ke bina capture ya publish karne par 3 saal tak ki jail, Rs 2 lakh tak ka fine, ya dono [[indiacode-it-act-2000]].

Kam maximum saza police station par bhi asar daalti hai. Jin offences mein teen saal se lekar saat saal se kam ki saza hai, unmein police Deputy Superintendent ki permission se, case register karne se pehle, 14 din tak ki preliminary enquiry kar sakti hai. Rape, jiska minimum hi 10 saal hai, is window se bahar hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Jin offences ka floor hai: disrobing, acid attacks, rape

Agle band mein har offence ke saath ek minimum aata hai, ek floor jiske neeche court nahi ja sakta. Aurat ki modesty outrage karne ke iraade se assault par 1 se 5 saal (Section 74), aur use disrobe karne ke liye assault par 3 se 7 saal (Section 76). Jo pati alag reh rahi patni ke saath uski consent ke bina sex kare, use 2 se 7 saal (Section 67). Jo person in authority apni position ka galat istemaal karke apni custody mein rakhi aurat se sex kare, jo rape tak na pahunche, use 5 se 10 saal (Section 68) [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Phir scale ek dum upar jaata hai. Jis acid attack se damage, burns ya disability ho, usmein kam se kam 10 saal aur life tak ki saza hai, aur fine victim ko ilaaj ke liye diya jaata hai (Section 124). Rape par kam se kam 10 saal ki rigorous imprisonment aur life tak (Section 64) [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

## Sabse upar: natural life aur death

10 saal ke floor ke upar BNS un cases ke liye paaydaan jodti hai jinhe woh sabse bura maanti hai. Rape ke terah aggravated forms, jaise police officer, rishtedaar ya teacher ka kiya rape, 10 saal se baaki natural life tak ki qaid. 16 saal se kam ki ladki ka rape, 20 saal se natural life tak; 12 se kam ki ho toh wahi ya death. Gang rape mein group ke har member ko 20 saal se natural life tak, aur ladki 18 se kam ki ho toh natural life ya death. Rape ki doosri conviction par natural life ya death, saalon ki koi ginti hi nahi [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Bachchon ke liye POCSO Act hai, jo bachche par aggravated penetrative sexual assault ke liye 20 saal se natural life tak, ya death ki saza deta hai, aur ladkon aur ladkiyon dono ko protect karta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

## Yeh ranking kya batati hai ki kiska nuksaan gina jaata hai

Table ko offence ke bajaye victim ke hisaab se padhiye. Ek hi harkat lijiye: zabardasti penetrative sex. Agar woh aisi aurat ke saath ho jo us aadmi ki patni nahi hai, toh floor 10 saal hai. Usse alag reh rahi patni ke saath ho, toh range 2 se 7 saal hai. Saath reh rahi 18 saal ya usse badi patni ke saath ho, toh yeh rape nahi hai. Transgender insaan ke saath ho, toh charge "sexual abuse" ka hai, jiski ceiling 2 saal hai. Aur adult aadmi ke saath ho, toh BNS mein lagane ke liye koi specific offence hi nahi hai.

Is aakhri gap ke baare mein Parliament ko bataya gaya tha. 10 November 2023 ko uski Standing Committee on Home Affairs ne warn kiya ki Section 377 hatane se aadmiyon aur transgender logon ke khilaaf non-consensual sexual offences bina saza ke reh jaayenge, aur ise rakhne ki recommendation ki. Sarkaar ne yeh recommendation nahi maani [[prs-standing-committee-bns-2023]].

Maximum saza yeh bhi nahi batati ki courts asal mein kya karte hain. Yeh sirf woh had hai jahan tak judge ja sakta hai, aur woh bhi conviction ke baad. 2024 mein courts ne jitne rape trials poore kiye, unmein se 24.4% mein convict kiya. Us saal courts ke saamne aurton par acid attack ke 804 cases the; trial 24 mein poora hua aur 13 mein conviction hui [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Nichla paaydaan bhi crime hai, aur report karne laayak hai. Aur jahan table mein gap hai, wahan galti law ki hai, us insaan ki nahi jise nuksaan pahunchaya gaya.

sexual-violence-cases-courts-yet-to-deci.en:
Consider three people waiting on India's courts in November 2026. A 24-year-old wife whose husband forces sex on her: in law, that is not rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. A seven-year-old whose family has fixed a date for her khatna, the genital cutting of girls: no specific Indian law bans it [[scobserver-sabarimala-day13-2026]]. A 30-year-old man who was sexually assaulted: the penal code has no rape offence that covers him [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Each gap is before a court, with two more questions: who the law counts as transgender, and whether acid should be sold over a counter. This is general information, not legal advice.

| Case | Court | Status on 20 November 2026 |
|---|---|---|
| Marital rape exception | Supreme Court | Hearing to be fixed for 9 or 10 December |
| Khatna (Sabarimala reference) | Supreme Court, nine judges | Judgment reserved, 14 May |
| Missing offence for men and transgender people | Delhi High Court | Revived, March 2026; no final order confirmed |
| 2026 transgender amendment | Supreme Court | Heard, 17 August |
| Acid sales | Supreme Court | Centre told to revisit policy, 27 October |

## Marital rape: the December 2026 hearing

Exception 2 to Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) says sex by a man with his own wife is not rape if she is 18 or older [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The Supreme Court will decide whether that exception is valid, and whether a husband can be prosecuted for rape while it stands [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]].

On 9 September 2026 a bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant posted the petitions for final hearing; the Union government had opposed criminalising marital rape in an October 2024 affidavit [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]]. One petition, filed on 24 April 2025, targets the exception in its BNS form [[clpr-aweksha-v-union-2025]]. In November the bench said it would fix the hearing on 9 or 10 December 2026 [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]].

If the exception goes, forced sex by a husband falls under the same rape law as forced sex by any other man. If it stays, the second question decides whether a husband can be tried for rape anyway. In NFHS-5, 4.6% of ever-married women aged 18 to 49 said their husband had physically forced them to have intercourse [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Khatna and the nine-judge bench

A 2017 petition, Sunita Tiwari v. Union of India, asks the Supreme Court to ban khatna as practised in the Dawoodi Bohra community, arguing that it violates girls' rights to equality and bodily autonomy. Community members answer that it is protected religious practice [[scobserver-sunita-tiwari-fgm-case]].

The petition is tagged to the Sabarimala reference, which a nine-judge bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant began hearing on 7 April 2026 [[scobserver-sabarimala-reference-2026]]. The bench reserved judgment on 14 May 2026, after 16 days of hearings [[scobserver-sabarimala-day16-2026]]. At the time of writing it was still awaited.

The nine judges are not deciding the khatna petition itself, but the test for when a court may examine a practice a community calls essential to its faith. Our reading: a test that lets courts weigh a child's bodily autonomy clears the way for the petition; one that defers to the community makes a court-ordered ban much harder.

## The missing offence for men and transgender survivors

When the BNS replaced the Indian Penal Code on 1 July 2024, it dropped Section 377, which had punished non-consensual "carnal intercourse against the order of nature", and added no replacement [[scroll-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]]. A public interest petition in the Delhi High Court asks for that protection back.

On 28 August 2024 the court asked the Centre to decide within six months: "there can't be a vacuum to an offence" [[barandbench-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]]. In March 2026, after about a year and a half without a decision, it revived the case, said "the decision is nowhere in sight" and gave the Centre four weeks to file an affidavit [[theprint-pti-delhi-hc-restores-pil-2026]]. We could not confirm a final order as of 20 November 2026.

Expect less from this case. On 14 October 2024 the Supreme Court refused a similar plea, saying it cannot direct Parliament to create an offence [[livelaw-sc-bns-sexual-offences-men-pil-2024]]. A court can make the government answer. Only Parliament can write the crime.

## The 2026 transgender amendment

The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act, 2026, in force since 25 May 2026, deletes the right to self-perceived gender identity and lets a District Magistrate issue a transgender certificate only after a medical board's recommendation [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

It belongs here because the same Act holds the offence of sexual abuse of a transgender person, punishable with six months to two years, a range the amendment left unchanged [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. Who the Act recognises as transgender decides who that section covers.

On 17 August 2026 a Supreme Court bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant heard challenges to it, and the Union said identity cards already issued under the 2019 Act would continue to operate while the case is pending [[scobserver-transgender-amendment-hearing-2026]]. If the amendment is struck down, the right to self-identify returns. If it stands, a medical board stays between a person and their legal identity.

## Acid sales and the Centre's 'failed' guidelines

On 18 July 2013, in a public interest case on acid attacks, the Supreme Court barred over-the-counter acid sales unless the seller keeps a register and the buyer shows a government photo ID, and banned sales to anyone under 18 [[sc-laxmi-2013]]. On 27 October 2026, hearing a fresh petition on acid attacks, the Court told the Centre that its acid-sale guidelines had "miserably failed", and asked it to revisit the policy, including whether acid needs to be sold at retail [[livelaw-acid-policy-failure-2026]].

The bench spoke of rising attacks. Police data show a flat line: 202 acid attacks in 2022, 207 in 2023 and 207 in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. More than a decade after the 2013 rules, attacks have not fallen. Trials are stuck too: of 804 acid-attack cases on women before the courts in 2024, 778 were still pending at year-end [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. A ruling can tighten the rules or end retail sale; enforcement stays with governments.

Five cases, five different powers: striking out an exception, setting a test, demanding an answer, striking down a statute, supervising a policy. Knowing which is which tells you what a ruling can deliver, and when to press Parliament instead. Nobody has to wait for a verdict to ask for help.
sexual-violence-cases-courts-yet-to-deci.hg:
Sochiye, teen log hain jo November 2026 mein India ki courts ke faisle ka intezaar kar rahe hain. 24 saal ki ek patni, jiske saath uska pati zabardasti sex karta hai: law ki nazar mein yeh rape nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Saat saal ki ek bachchi, jiske parivaar ne uske khatna, yaani ladkiyon ki genital cutting, ki taareekh tay kar di hai: India ka koi specific law ise ban nahi karta [[scobserver-sabarimala-day13-2026]]. 30 saal ka ek aadmi, jis par sexual assault hua: penal code mein aisa koi rape offence nahi jo us par laagu ho [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Har gap kisi court ke saamne hai, aur saath mein do sawaal aur hain: law kise transgender maanega, aur kya acid dukaan ke counter par bikna chahiye. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

| Case | Court | 20 November 2026 ko status |
|---|---|---|
| Marital rape exception | Supreme Court | Hearing 9 ya 10 December ke liye tay hogi |
| Khatna (Sabarimala reference) | Supreme Court, nau judges | Judgment reserved, 14 May |
| Mardon aur transgender logon ke liye missing offence | Delhi High Court | March 2026 mein phir khula; final order confirm nahi |
| 2026 ka transgender amendment | Supreme Court | Sunwai hui, 17 August |
