| Acid ki bikri | Supreme Court | Centre se policy dobara dekhne ko kaha gaya, 27 October |

## Marital rape: December 2026 ki hearing

Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 63 ka Exception 2 kehta hai ki agar patni 18 saal ya usse badi hai, toh pati ka uske saath sex rape nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Supreme Court tay karega ki yeh exception valid hai ya nahi, aur jab tak yeh law mein hai, kya tab tak kisi pati par rape ka case chal sakta hai [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]].

9 September 2026 ko Chief Justice Surya Kant ki bench ne petitions ko final hearing ke liye list kiya; Union government October 2024 ke ek affidavit mein marital rape ko crime banane ka virodh kar chuki thi [[livelaw-marital-rape-final-hearing-2026]]. Ek petition, jo 24 April 2025 ko file hui, exception ko uske BNS wale roop mein challenge karti hai [[clpr-aweksha-v-union-2025]]. November mein bench ne kaha ki woh hearing 9 ya 10 December 2026 ke liye tay karegi [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]].

Agar exception hat jaata hai, toh pati ki zabardasti par bhi wahi rape law laagu hoga jo kisi bhi doosre aadmi ki zabardasti par hota hai. Agar exception bach jaata hai, toh doosra sawaal tay karega ki pati par phir bhi rape ka trial chal sakta hai ya nahi. NFHS-5 mein 18 se 49 saal ki 4.6% ever-married aurton ne bataya ki unke pati ne unhe physically force karke intercourse kiya [[nfhs5-india-2021]].

## Khatna aur nau judges ki bench

2017 ki ek petition, Sunita Tiwari v. Union of India, Supreme Court se maang karti hai ki Dawoodi Bohra community mein hone wale khatna par ban lage, kyunki yeh ladkiyon ke equality aur bodily autonomy, yaani apne shareer par apne haq, ke rights todta hai. Community ke members ka jawab hai ki yeh protected religious practice hai [[scobserver-sunita-tiwari-fgm-case]].

Yeh petition Sabarimala reference ke saath tag hai, jise Chief Justice Surya Kant ki nau judges ki bench ne 7 April 2026 se sunna shuru kiya [[scobserver-sabarimala-reference-2026]]. Bench ne 16 din ki hearings ke baad 14 May 2026 ko judgment reserve kar liya [[scobserver-sabarimala-day16-2026]]. Yeh story likhe jaane tak judgment ka intezaar tha.

Nau judges khud khatna petition ka faisla nahi kar rahe. Woh yeh test tay kar rahe hain ki court kab kisi aisi practice ko jaanch sakti hai jise community apne dharm ka zaroori hissa kehti hai. Hamari reading: agar test courts ko bachche ki bodily autonomy tolne deta hai, toh petition ka raasta khulta hai; agar test faisla community par chhod deta hai, toh court ke zariye ban bahut mushkil ho jaayega.

## Mardon aur transgender survivors ke liye missing offence

1 July 2024 ko jab BNS ne Indian Penal Code ki jagah li, toh usne Section 377 hata diya, jo non-consensual "carnal intercourse against the order of nature" ki saza deta tha, aur uski jagah kuch nahi rakha [[scroll-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]]. Delhi High Court mein ek public interest petition yeh suraksha wapas maangti hai.

28 August 2024 ko court ne Centre se chhe mahine mein decide karne ko kaha: "there can't be a vacuum to an offence", yaani kisi offence ki jagah khaali nahi chhodi ja sakti [[barandbench-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]]. March 2026 mein, lagbhag dedh saal tak koi decision na aane par, court ne case phir khola, kaha ki "the decision is nowhere in sight", yaani faisla door-door tak nazar nahi aata, aur Centre ko chaar hafte mein affidavit file karne ko kaha [[theprint-pti-delhi-hc-restores-pil-2026]]. 20 November 2026 tak hum kisi final order ki pushti nahi kar sake.

Is case se kam ummeed rakhiye. 14 October 2024 ko Supreme Court ne aisi hi ek plea sunne se mana kar diya tha, yeh kehkar ki woh Parliament ko naya offence banane ka nirdesh nahi de sakta [[livelaw-sc-bns-sexual-offences-men-pil-2024]]. Court sarkar ko jawab dene par majboor kar sakti hai. Crime sirf Parliament likh sakti hai.

## 2026 ka transgender amendment

Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act, 2026, jo 25 May 2026 se laagu hai, self-perceived gender identity ka right hata deta hai, aur District Magistrate ko transgender certificate sirf medical board ki recommendation ke baad jaari karne deta hai [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]].

Yeh is list mein isliye hai kyunki isi Act mein transgender person ke sexual abuse ka offence hai, jiski saza chhe mahine se do saal hai, aur amendment ne is range ko nahi badla [[gazette-transgender-amendment-act-2026]]. Act kise transgender maanta hai, isi se tay hota hai ki woh section kis par laagu hoga.

17 August 2026 ko Chief Justice Surya Kant ki Supreme Court bench ne is amendment ke khilaaf challenges sune, aur Union ne kaha ki 2019 Act ke under pehle se jaari identity cards case pending rehne tak chalte rahenge [[scobserver-transgender-amendment-hearing-2026]]. Agar amendment strike down hota hai, toh self-identify karne ka right laut aayega. Agar yeh bana rehta hai, toh ek insaan aur uski legal identity ke beech medical board khada rahega.

## Acid ki bikri aur Centre ki 'failed' guidelines

18 July 2013 ko, acid attacks par ek public interest case mein, Supreme Court ne over-the-counter acid ki bikri par rok lagayi, jab tak seller register na rakhe aur buyer sarkari photo ID na dikhaye, aur 18 se kam umar walon ko bikri ban kar di [[sc-laxmi-2013]]. 27 October 2026 ko, acid attacks par ek nayi petition sunte hue, Court ne Centre se kaha ki uski acid-sale guidelines "miserably failed" hain, yaani buri tarah fail hui hain, aur policy dobara dekhne ko kaha, jisme yeh sawaal bhi hai ki acid ki retail bikri zaroori hai ya nahi [[livelaw-acid-policy-failure-2026]].

Bench ne badhte attacks ki baat ki. Police data mein line flat hai: 2022 mein 202 acid attacks, 2023 mein 207 aur 2024 mein 207 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. 2013 ke rules ke das saal se zyada baad bhi attacks kam nahi hue. Trials bhi atke hain: 2024 mein courts ke saamne aurton par acid attack ke 804 cases the, jinmein se 778 saal ke end tak pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Faisla rules sakht kar sakta hai ya retail bikri band kar sakta hai; unhe laagu karna phir bhi sarkaron ka kaam rahega.

Paanch cases, paanch alag powers: exception ko hatana, test tay karna, jawab maangna, poore law ko strike down karna, policy par nazar rakhna. Kaun si power kahan lagti hai, yeh jaan lenge toh samajh aayega ki faisla kya de sakta hai, aur kab Parliament par dabaav banana hai. Madad maangne ke liye kisi ko faisle ka intezaar nahi karna hai.

survivor-is-a-witness-state-prosecutes.en:
Look at the title of any rape trial in India. It is never the survivor against the man she accused. It is *State of Maharashtra v.* someone, or *State v.* someone. The crime is treated as an offence against society, so the State prosecutes it. The survivor, in the eyes of the court, is the most important witness. That one fact explains much of what feels unfair to survivors: decisions about their own case are made by people who never ask them.

## Who owns a criminal case in India

Once an FIR is registered, the case belongs to the police. They decide whom to question, what to seize and which sections to charge. After the charge sheet, a public prosecutor, a lawyer paid by the government, takes over in court. The prosecutor represents the State, not the survivor.

The same rule runs all the way up. In the RG Kar Medical College case in Kolkata, a Sealdah court sentenced the convict on 20 January 2025 to life imprisonment for the rest of his natural life [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. The West Bengal government appealed for the death penalty. The CBI, which had investigated and prosecuted the case, opposed the state's appeal, and on 7 February 2025 the Calcutta High Court dismissed it, leaving the CBI to pursue its own appeal [[barandbench-rg-kar-hc-2025]]. Two arms of government argued over who could seek a harsher sentence. The family whose daughter was killed was not the one deciding.

This is general information, not legal advice. But the pattern matters: if the system is the owner of the case, the survivor's power lies in the rights the law has carved out for her. They are narrower than most people think, and more useful than most survivors are told.

## What a survivor is entitled to know: the FIR, 90 days, 14 days

The first right is a piece of paper. The victim must get a copy of the FIR free of cost, and a complaint can be given at any police station, whatever the area, or electronically [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Read it before leaving. The sections written on it shape everything that follows.

The second is time-bound news. Under Section 193(3) of the BNSS, police must tell the survivor how the investigation is progressing within 90 days [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

The third depends on having a lawyer. Under Section 230, if the survivor is represented by an advocate, she must get free copies of the police report, the FIR and the recorded statements within 14 days of the accused first appearing in court [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Without a lawyer, she may not see the case the State is building on her word.

There is also a record the police do not control. Section 183(6) requires a magistrate, a woman magistrate as far as practicable, to record a rape survivor's statement as soon as police learn of the offence [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Withdrawal, compensation and the right to be heard

The State can, with the court's permission, withdraw a prosecution. Imagine a 22-year-old in Patna who learns, months after her FIR, that the case against a powerful local man is being dropped. Under Section 360 of the BNSS, no court may allow that withdrawal without first giving the victim a chance to be heard [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. It is a right to speak, not a veto, but it means nothing can be closed quietly.

Money is the one area where she can act alone. Every state must run a victim compensation scheme, and a victim can apply directly to the State or District Legal Services Authority even if the offender is never traced and no trial takes place. The authority must finish its inquiry within two months [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Under NALSA's 2018 scheme, a rape survivor is entitled to Rs 4 lakh to Rs 7 lakh, and a gang-rape survivor to Rs 5 lakh to Rs 10 lakh [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]]. The limits are 50% higher for a minor [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]].

Some protections date from 2013, the year after the Delhi gang rape case. That year the law made it a crime for police to refuse a rape FIR, required every hospital to treat survivors free, and made a survivor's character or past sexual experience irrelevant to the question of consent [[indiacode-cla-2013]].

## Dalit and Adivasi survivors: notice of every hearing

The SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act goes further than general law. Section 15A, added in 2015, makes it the State's duty to protect victims, their dependants and witnesses from intimidation, coercion, inducement or violence. It also gives victims the right to timely notice of every court proceeding, including bail hearings [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

That last right matters. Bail decides whether the accused can walk back into the same village or lane as the survivor. Under this Act she is entitled to know, in time, when that hearing is.

## A lawyer of her own: legal aid and the public prosecutor

The single biggest change a survivor can make is to stop relying only on the public prosecutor. Her own advocate can collect the 14-day documents, press for the 90-day update, file the compensation application and speak up before any withdrawal. Free legal aid is available through the legal services authorities [[nalsa]].

Her own lawyer does not take the case away from the State, which still runs it. But a survivor with a lawyer of her own is no longer only a name on a witness list. She is someone the court has to inform, hear and answer.
survivor-is-a-witness-state-prosecutes.hg:
India mein kisi bhi rape trial ka title dekhiye. Woh kabhi survivor versus woh aadmi nahi hota jis par usne aarop lagaya. Woh hota hai *State of Maharashtra v.* koi, ya *State v.* koi. Crime ko samaj ke khilaaf offence maana jaata hai, isliye prosecution State karta hai. Court ki nazar mein survivor sabse important witness hai, bas. Yahi ek baat samjhati hai ki survivors ko itna kuch unfair kyun lagta hai: unke apne case ke faisle aise log lete hain jo unse kabhi poochte hi nahi.

## India mein criminal case ka maalik kaun hai

FIR darj hote hi case police ka ho jaata hai. Wahi tay karti hai ki kisse poochtaachh ho, kya seize ho, aur kaun se sections lagein. Charge sheet ke baad court mein public prosecutor aata hai, yaani sarkar ka salary wala lawyer. Prosecutor State ko represent karta hai, survivor ko nahi.

Yahi rule upar tak chalta hai. Kolkata ke RG Kar Medical College case mein 20 January 2025 ko Sealdah ki ek court ne convict ko zindagi ki aakhri saans tak umrqaid di [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. West Bengal sarkar ne death penalty ke liye appeal ki. CBI ne, jisne investigation aur prosecution kiya tha, state ki appeal ka virodh kiya, aur 7 February 2025 ko Calcutta High Court ne woh appeal kharij kar di. Death penalty ki appeal ab sirf CBI ke paas rahi [[barandbench-rg-kar-hc-2025]]. Sarkar ke do hisse is baat par lade ki saza badhwane ki maang kaun kar sakta hai. Jis family ki beti maari gayi, faisla unke haath mein nahi tha.

Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi. Lekin pattern samajhna zaroori hai: agar case ka maalik system hai, toh survivor ki taakat un rights mein hai jo law ne khaas uske liye nikaale hain. Yeh rights log jitna sochte hain usse kam hain, aur survivors ko jitna bataya jaata hai usse zyada kaam ke hain.

## Survivor ko kya jaanne ka haq hai: FIR, 90 din, 14 din

Pehla right ek kaagaz hai. Victim ko FIR ki copy free milni chahiye, aur complaint kisi bhi police station mein di ja sakti hai, area chahe jo ho, ya electronic tareeke se [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Thane se nikalne se pehle use padhiye. Us par likhe sections aage sab kuch tay karte hain.

Doosra hai time ke saath khabar. BNSS ke Section 193(3) ke tahat police ko 90 din ke andar survivor ko batana hai ki investigation kahan tak pahunchi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Teesra right lawyer hone par tika hai. Section 230 ke tahat, agar survivor ki taraf se advocate hai, toh accused ke court mein pehli baar pesh hone ke 14 din ke andar use police report, FIR aur record kiye gaye statements ki free copies milni chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Lawyer ke bina ho sakta hai woh woh case dekh hi na paaye jo State uski baat par khada kar raha hai.

Ek record aisa bhi hai jo police ke control mein nahi. Section 183(6) ke mutabik, police ko offence ka pata chalte hi ek magistrate ko, jahan tak ho sake mahila magistrate ko, rape survivor ka statement record karna hota hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Case wapas lena, compensation aur sune jaane ka haq

State court ki permission se prosecution wapas le sakta hai. Sochiye Patna ki ek 22 saal ki ladki ko FIR ke mahino baad pata chalta hai ki ek taaqatwar local aadmi ke khilaaf case drop kiya ja raha hai. BNSS ke Section 360 ke tahat koi court victim ko sune bina yeh withdrawal allow nahi kar sakti [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Yeh bolne ka haq hai, veto nahi, lekin iska matlab hai ki kuch bhi chupchaap band nahi ho sakta.

Paisa woh ek jagah hai jahan woh akele kadam utha sakti hai. Har state ko victim compensation scheme chalani hai, aur victim seedhe State ya District Legal Services Authority mein apply kar sakti hai, chahe offender kabhi pakda na jaaye aur trial hi na ho. Authority ko do mahine mein inquiry poori karni hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. NALSA ki 2018 scheme ke tahat rape survivor Rs 4 lakh se Rs 7 lakh ki haqdaar hai, aur gang-rape survivor Rs 5 lakh se Rs 10 lakh ki [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]]. Nabalig ke liye yeh limits 50% zyada hain [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]].

Kuch protections 2013 se hain, Delhi gang rape case ke agle saal se. Us saal law ne police ka rape FIR likhne se mana karna crime bana diya, har hospital ko survivors ka free ilaaj karna zaroori kiya, aur consent ke sawaal par survivor ke character ya past sexual experience ko irrelevant bana diya [[indiacode-cla-2013]].

## Dalit aur Adivasi survivors: har hearing ki notice

SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act general law se aage jaata hai. 2015 mein joda gaya Section 15A victims, unke dependants aur witnesses ko dhamki, dabaav, laalach ya violence se bachana State ki duty banata hai. Yeh victims ko har court proceeding ki samay par notice ka haq bhi deta hai, bail hearings ki bhi [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

Yeh aakhri right bahut maayne rakhta hai. Bail se tay hota hai ki accused usi gaon ya usi gali mein survivor ke saamne wapas aa sakta hai ya nahi. Is Act ke tahat use samay rehte pata hona chahiye ki woh hearing kab hai.

## Apna lawyer: legal aid aur public prosecutor

Survivor sabse bada badlaav yeh kar sakti hai ki sirf public prosecutor ke bharose na rahe. Uska apna advocate 14 din wale documents le sakta hai, 90 din wale update ke liye dabaav daal sakta hai, compensation ki application file kar sakta hai aur kisi bhi withdrawal se pehle bol sakta hai. Legal services authorities ke through free legal aid milti hai [[nalsa]].

Apna lawyer hone se case State ke haath se nahi nikalta, use ab bhi State hi chalata hai. Lekin jis survivor ka apna lawyer hai, woh witness list mein sirf ek naam nahi rehti. Woh aisi insaan ban jaati hai jise court ko batana padta hai, sunna padta hai aur jawab dena padta hai.

survivor-rights-report-card-2026.en:
Indian law makes a woman who reports rape five promises that can be checked against a number: a crisis centre in her district, a police investigation finished in two months, a trial finished two months after the charge-sheet, compensation even if her attacker is never caught, and her name kept out of print and off every screen.

Here is the report card, on official figures from 2024 to July 2026. The grades are ours, not the government's.

| Promise | Latest official figure | Our grade |
|---|---|---|
| A One Stop Centre in every district | 985 of 1,033 approved centres operational (July 2026) | Late |
| Investigation in two months | 8,905 rape cases still under investigation (end of 2024) | Not measured |
| Trial in two months | 89.8% of rape cases in court pending (end of 2024) | Fail |
| Compensation without a conviction | Rs 4 lakh to Rs 7 lakh promised; payouts not counted here | Not measured |
| Anonymity | 11 cases registered (July-December 2024) | Barely enforced |

One caveat first. The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) defines rape as an act by a man against a woman, so an adult man or a transgender person who is sexually assaulted is outside most of these promises [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. POCSO protects boys and girls under 18 alike [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

## Promise one: a One Stop Centre in every district

**The promise.** On 11 December 2018, in Nipun Saxena v. Union of India, the Supreme Court asked every state and union territory to set up at least one One Stop Centre in every district within a year [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. These are government crisis centres for women affected by violence.

**The number.** By July 2026, 985 of 1,033 approved centres were operational. They had assisted over 15.20 lakh women since April 2015 [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]].

**What it hides.** The deadline was December 2019. More than six years later, 48 approved centres were still not running. A count of centres does not show how far a survivor must travel to reach one. **Grade: late.**

## Promise two: an investigation in two months

**The promise.** Section 193 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) says police must complete a rape investigation within two months of recording the information. The same limit covers sexual assault on children under POCSO [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

**The number.** In 2024 police filed charge-sheets in 24,614 rape cases, a charge-sheeting rate of 81.3%. At the end of the year 8,905 rape cases were still under investigation [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

**What it hides.** The rate shows how investigations ended, not how long they took. A case registered in December is not late on 31 December, so 8,905 is not a count of broken deadlines. The law sets no consequence for missing the limit. **Grade: not measured.** What a survivor can enforce is information: the BNSS entitles her to a progress update within 90 days [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Promise three: a trial in two months

**The promise.** Under Section 346 of the BNSS, a rape trial must be completed within two months of the charge-sheet [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

**The number.** At the end of 2024, 1,85,785 rape cases were pending trial, 89.8% of the 2,06,777 before the courts that year [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

**What it hides.** Very little. Police sent 24,614 new rape cases to court in 2024, and the pending pile is more than seven times that. A two-month trial cannot be the norm in a system carrying years of cases forward. **Grade: fail.**

## Promise four: compensation without a conviction

**The promise.** Section 396 of the BNSS makes every state run a victim compensation scheme. A survivor can apply to the State or District Legal Services Authority even if the offender is never traced and no trial takes place, and the authority must finish its inquiry within two months [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

**The number.** The model scheme framed by the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) in 2018 sets Rs 4 lakh to Rs 7 lakh for a rape survivor and Rs 5 lakh to Rs 10 lakh for a gang-rape survivor, with limits 50% higher for a minor [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]]. The Centre has released Rs 200 crore from the Nirbhaya Fund as a one-time grant to states for victim compensation [[pib-nirbhaya-fund-2025]].

**What it hides.** These figures show what is promised and what was set aside. This report card has no verified national figure for how many survivors were paid. **Grade: not measured.** It is still the promise she can enforce most directly: the claim is hers to file, without waiting for an arrest or a verdict.

## Promise five: anonymity, and the 11 cases filed

**The promise.** Section 72 of the BNS makes it a crime, punishable with up to two years in prison and a fine, to print or publish the name of a rape survivor or anything that could identify her, unless she authorises it in writing [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. In 2018 the Supreme Court spelt it out: no one may name her in print, electronic or social media, or "even in a remote manner" disclose facts that could identify her [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

**The number.** Between July and December 2024, the first six months of the BNS, police across India registered 11 cases under Section 72 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB counts only the most serious offence in each FIR, so a disclosure filed alongside a graver charge would not show up here.

**What it hides.** Eleven could mean almost nobody breaks this law. The record suggests otherwise. In April 2018 the Delhi High Court directed 12 media houses to pay Rs 10 lakh each for revealing the identity of the child killed in the Kathua case; their lawyers said they had wrongly believed a dead victim could be named [[thehindu-delhi-hc-kathua-media-2018]]. **Grade: barely enforced.**

Read the card as a whole. The promises a survivor can act on herself, a centre to walk into or a claim to file, at least put something in her hands. The promises that run on someone else's deadline, the police's or the court's, are the ones nobody answers for missing.

Imagine a 23-year-old in Guwahati who reports a rape tonight. On the numbers, the crisis centre probably exists and the compensation claim is hers to file this week. The charge-sheet, the verdict and her anonymity are things she will have to chase. This is general information, not legal advice.
survivor-rights-report-card-2026.hg:
Indian law rape ki report karne wali aurat se paanch aise vaade karta hai jinhe numbers se jaancha ja sakta hai: uske district mein ek crisis centre, do mahine mein poori hui police investigation, charge-sheet ke do mahine baad poora hua trial, attacker kabhi na pakda jaye tab bhi compensation, aur uska naam na kisi akhbaar mein, na kisi screen par.

Yeh raha report card, 2024 se July 2026 tak ke official figures par. Grades hamare hain, sarkar ke nahi.

| Vaada | Latest official figure | Hamara grade |
|---|---|---|
| Har district mein One Stop Centre | 1,033 approved centres mein se 985 chalu (July 2026) | Late |
| Do mahine mein investigation | 8,905 rape cases abhi bhi investigation mein (2024 ka end) | Naapa nahi gaya |
| Do mahine mein trial | Court mein 89.8% rape cases pending (2024 ka end) | Fail |
| Conviction ke bina compensation | Rs 4 lakh se Rs 7 lakh ka vaada; kitni survivors ko paisa mila, iski ginti yahan nahi | Naapa nahi gaya |
| Pehchaan ki hifazat | 11 cases register hue (July-December 2024) | Mushkil se enforce |

Pehle ek baat saaf kar dein. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) rape ko aise define karti hai ki woh ek aadmi ka ek aurat ke khilaaf kiya gaya act hai. Isliye jis adult aadmi ya transgender person par sexual assault hota hai, woh in zyada tar vaadon ke bahar reh jaata hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. POCSO 18 saal se kam ke ladkon aur ladkiyon, dono ko barabar protect karta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

## Pehla vaada: har district mein One Stop Centre

**Vaada.** 11 December 2018 ko, Nipun Saxena v. Union of India mein, Supreme Court ne har state aur union territory se kaha ki ek saal ke andar har district mein kam se kam ek One Stop Centre banaya jaye [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Yeh violence jhelne wali auraton ke liye sarkari crisis centres hain.

**Number.** July 2026 tak 1,033 approved centres mein se 985 chal rahe the. April 2015 se inhone 15.20 lakh se zyada auraton ki madad ki thi [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]].

**Number kya chhupata hai.** Deadline December 2019 thi. Chhe saal se zyada baad bhi 48 approved centres shuru nahi hue the. Centres ki ginti yeh nahi batati ki survivor ko wahan tak pahunchne ke liye kitni door jaana padta hai. **Grade: late.**

## Doosra vaada: do mahine mein investigation

**Vaada.** Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ki Section 193 kehti hai ki police ko rape ki investigation, information record hone ke do mahine ke andar poori karni hogi. Yahi limit POCSO ke tahat bachchon par sexual assault ke cases par bhi lagti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

**Number.** 2024 mein police ne 24,614 rape cases mein charge-sheet file ki, yaani charge-sheeting rate 81.3% raha. Saal ke end par 8,905 rape cases abhi bhi investigation mein the [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

**Number kya chhupata hai.** Rate yeh batata hai ki investigations ka ant kaise hua, yeh nahi ki unme kitna time laga. December mein register hua case 31 December ko late nahi hota, isliye 8,905 tooti hui deadlines ki ginti nahi hai. Law mein limit todne ka koi nateeja bhi nahi likha hai. **Grade: naapa nahi gaya.** Survivor jo cheez enforce kar sakti hai, woh hai information: BNSS ke tahat use 90 din ke andar progress update paane ka haq hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Teesra vaada: do mahine mein trial

**Vaada.** BNSS ki Section 346 ke tahat rape trial charge-sheet ke do mahine ke andar poora hona chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

**Number.** 2024 ke end par 1,85,785 rape cases trial ke liye pending the, yaani us saal courts ke saamne aaye 2,06,777 cases ka 89.8% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

**Number kya chhupata hai.** Bahut kam. Police ne 2024 mein 24,614 naye rape cases court bheje, aur pending dher uske saat guna se bhi zyada hai. Jis system mein saalon ke cases aage sarkaaye jaate hon, wahan do mahine ka trial aam baat ho hi nahi sakta. **Grade: fail.**

## Chautha vaada: conviction ke bina compensation

**Vaada.** BNSS ki Section 396 ke tahat har state ko victim compensation scheme chalani hoti hai. Survivor State ya District Legal Services Authority mein tab bhi apply kar sakti hai jab offender kabhi trace na ho aur koi trial na chale, aur authority ko apni inquiry do mahine ke andar poori karni hoti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

**Number.** National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) ki 2018 ki model scheme rape survivor ke liye Rs 4 lakh se Rs 7 lakh aur gang-rape survivor ke liye Rs 5 lakh se Rs 10 lakh tay karti hai, aur survivor minor ho toh limits 50% zyada hain [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]]. Centre ne Nirbhaya Fund se Rs 200 crore, ek baar ki grant ke roop mein, states ko victim compensation ke liye diye hain [[pib-nirbhaya-fund-2025]].

**Number kya chhupata hai.** Yeh figures batate hain ki vaada kitne ka hai aur kitna paisa alag rakha gaya. Is report card ke paas koi verified national figure nahi hai ki kitni survivors ko paisa mila. **Grade: naapa nahi gaya.** Phir bhi yahi woh vaada hai jise survivor sabse seedhe enforce kar sakti hai: claim file karna uske apne haath mein hai, bina arrest ya verdict ka intezaar kiye.

## Paanchva vaada: pehchaan ki hifazat, aur sirf 11 cases

**Vaada.** BNS ki Section 72 ke tahat rape survivor ka naam, ya aisi koi bhi cheez jisse uski pehchaan ho sake, print ya publish karna crime hai, jab tak woh khud likhit mein ijazat na de. Saza do saal tak ki jail aur fine hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. 2018 mein Supreme Court ne ise aur saaf kiya: koi bhi print, electronic ya social media mein uska naam nahi le sakta, aur na hi "even in a remote manner", yaani door-door tak bhi, aise facts bata sakta hai jinse uski pehchaan ho jaye [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

**Number.** July se December 2024 ke beech, yaani BNS ke pehle chhe mahinon mein, poore India ki police ne Section 72 ke tahat 11 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. NCRB har FIR mein sirf sabse gambhir offence ginta hai, isliye agar pehchaan zaahir karne ka case kisi zyada gambhir charge ke saath darj hua, toh woh yahan nahi dikhega.

**Number kya chhupata hai.** Gyarah ka matlab yeh ho sakta hai ki yeh law lagbhag koi todta hi nahi. Record kuch aur kehta hai. April 2018 mein Delhi High Court ne 12 media houses mein se har ek ko Rs 10 lakh jama karne ka order diya, kyunki unhone Kathua case mein maari gayi bachchi ki pehchaan zaahir ki thi. Unke lawyers ne kaha ki unhe galatfehmi thi ki mar chuki victim ka naam liya ja sakta hai [[thehindu-delhi-hc-kathua-media-2018]]. **Grade: mushkil se enforce.**

Poore card ko ek saath padhiye. Jin vaadon par survivor khud kadam utha sakti hai, jaise ek centre jahan woh ja sake ya ek claim jo woh file kar sake, woh kam se kam uske haath mein kuch dete hain. Jo vaade kisi aur ki deadline par chalte hain, police ki ya court ki, unhe todne par koi jawabdeh nahi hota.

Maan lijiye Guwahati ki ek 23 saal ki aurat aaj raat rape ki report karti hai. Numbers ke hisaab se crisis centre shayad maujood hai, aur compensation ka claim woh isi hafte file kar sakti hai. Charge-sheet, verdict aur apni pehchaan ki hifazat ke liye use khud peeche padna hoga. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

survivor-rights-timeline-1983-2024.en:
Imagine a 20-year-old in Patna walking into a police station today to report a rape. She can give her complaint at any station she chooses. A woman officer should write it down. She must be handed a copy free of cost. A hospital cannot charge her. Her name cannot be printed. None of this existed when India's rape law was first written. Each right was added, one amendment at a time, usually after a case made the gap impossible to ignore. This is general information, not legal advice.

## 1983: closed courtrooms and a protected name

The first big change came out of protests over the 1978 custodial rape acquittal. The protests pushed Parliament to pass the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1983, in force from 25 December 1983 [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

That Act made custodial rape a separate, aggravated offence and placed a presumption of absence of consent in custodial rape trials. For every survivor, it did two more things. It made disclosing a rape victim's identity a crime, under Section 228A of the IPC, and it required rape trials to be held in camera, under Section 327(2) of the CrPC [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

Both rights survive under the new codes. Rape and POCSO trials must still be held in camera, as far as practicable before a woman judge, and nothing about them may be published without the court's permission [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## 2013: an FIR that must be written, treatment that must be free

After the 2012 Delhi gang rape case, a committee headed by Justice J.S. Verma reported on 23 January 2013 [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 followed, and with it the rights a survivor uses in the first hours. A police officer who fails to record her information became punishable with six months to two years of rigorous imprisonment [[indiacode-cla-2013]].

Every hospital, public or private, was required to give rape and acid-attack victims first aid or medical treatment immediately and free of cost, and to inform the police. A person in charge of a hospital who refuses became punishable too, under Section 166B of the IPC [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].

Both duties carried over into the new codes. Refusing to record a rape complaint is now punished under Section 199 of the BNS, with the same six months to two years, and a hospital in charge who refuses free treatment faces up to a year under Section 200 [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The duty to treat now sits in Section 397 of the BNSS [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

The same Act shut a door in the courtroom: evidence of a survivor's character or past sexual experience was made irrelevant on the question of consent [[indiacode-cla-2013]].

## 2018: two months to investigate, a centre in every district

The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018, was deemed in force from 21 April 2018. Besides raising the minimum sentence for rape from seven to ten years [[indiacode-cla-2018]], it gave survivors deadlines: police must finish a rape investigation within two months, and appeals must be decided within six months [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]].

In December 2018 the Supreme Court added two more protections. It directed that FIRs in rape and POCSO cases must not be put in the public domain, and asked every state and union territory to set up at least one One Stop Centre for survivors in every district within a year [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

## 2023: Zero FIR, video statements, 90-day updates

The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), passed in 2023, came into force on 1 July 2024 along with the BNS [[air-new-criminal-laws-2024]]. It wrote several practices into statute.

| Right | Where it is |
|---|---|
| Report at any police station (Zero FIR), or electronically (e-FIR), with a free copy of the FIR | Section 173, BNSS |
| Complaint recorded by a woman officer; statement taken at home or a place of her choice, which may be video-recorded | Sections 173 and 176, BNSS |
| An update on the investigation within 90 days | Section 193(3), BNSS |
| Free copies of the police report and statements within 14 days of the accused's first appearance, if she has a lawyer | Section 230, BNSS |
| A hearing before any prosecution is withdrawn | Section 360, BNSS |

The e-FIR must be signed within 3 days [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. A rape survivor's statement is to be taken at her residence or a place she chooses, as far as practicable by a woman officer, and may be recorded on a mobile phone [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. The 90-day update, the documents and the right to be heard before withdrawal treat her as a party to her own case rather than a witness the state summons [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Compensation sits beside these: she can apply to the State or District Legal Services Authority even if the offender is never traced [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## The rights survivors still struggle to claim

Rights on paper depend on systems that do not always show up. As of July 2026, 985 of the 1,033 approved One Stop Centres were operational, years after the Supreme Court's one-year deadline ran out [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]].

NCRB does not publish how many investigations meet the two-month deadline. What it does show is that 8,905 rape cases were still under investigation at the end of 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. And the trial waits longest: 1,85,785 rape cases were pending in court at the end of 2024, 89.8% of all rape cases before the courts that year [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Anonymity is easier to promise than to enforce. In the second half of 2024, police registered just 11 cases under Section 72 of the BNS for disclosing a victim's identity [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

The refused FIR and the hospital that asks for money are the hardest to fight, because they happen at the worst moment, often with no witness. That is why knowing the section numbers matters. A survivor, or the friend beside her, who can say "Section 173" at the police desk or "free treatment is the law" at the hospital counter is using rights that took four decades to win.
survivor-rights-timeline-1983-2024.hg:
Socho, Patna ki ek 20 saal ki ladki aaj rape report karne police station jaati hai. Woh apni marzi ke kisi bhi station mein complaint de sakti hai. Ek woman officer ko use likhna chahiye. Use FIR ki copy free mein milni chahiye. Koi hospital usse paise nahi le sakta. Uska naam chhapa nahi ja sakta. Jab India ka rape law pehli baar likha gaya tha, tab inme se kuch bhi nahi tha. Har haq ek-ek amendment karke joda gaya, aksar tab jab kisi case ne gap ko nazarandaaz karna namumkin kar diya. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## 1983: band courtroom aur surakshit naam

Pehla bada badlaav 1978 ke custodial rape acquittal ke khilaaf hue protests se aaya. Protests ne Parliament ko Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1983 paas karne pe majboor kiya, jo 25 December 1983 se laagu hua [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

Is Act ne custodial rape ko ek alag, aggravated offence banaya aur custodial rape trials mein yeh presumption rakha ki consent nahi thi. Har survivor ke liye isne do aur kaam kiye. Isne rape victim ki pehchaan bataana IPC ke Section 228A mein crime banaya, aur CrPC ke Section 327(2) mein rape trials ko in camera, yaani band courtroom mein chalaana zaroori kiya [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

Dono haq naye codes mein bhi bache hain. Rape aur POCSO trials aaj bhi in camera hone chahiye, jahan tak ho sake ek woman judge ke saamne, aur court ki permission ke bina unke baare mein kuch bhi publish nahi ho sakta [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## 2013: FIR jo likhni hi padegi, ilaaj jo free hi hoga

2012 ke Delhi gang rape case ke baad Justice J.S. Verma ki adhyakshta wali committee ne 23 January 2013 ko apni report di [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. Uske baad Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 aaya, aur uske saath woh haq jo survivor pehle kuch ghanton mein use karti hai. Jo police officer uski information record na kare, use chhe mahine se do saal tak ki rigorous imprisonment ho sakti hai [[indiacode-cla-2013]].

Har hospital, sarkari ho ya private, ko rape aur acid-attack victims ko turant aur free first aid ya medical treatment dena aur police ko inform karna zaroori kiya gaya. Mana karne wale hospital in-charge ko bhi IPC ke Section 166B mein saza ho sakti hai [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2013]].

Yeh dono zimmedariyan naye codes mein bhi aayi hain. Rape complaint record karne se mana karna ab BNS ke Section 199 mein usi chhe mahine se do saal ki saza wala crime hai, aur free ilaaj se mana karne wale hospital in-charge ko Section 200 mein ek saal tak ki saza ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Ilaaj ki zimmedari ab BNSS ke Section 397 mein hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Isi Act ne courtroom mein ek darwaza band kiya: survivor ke character ya pichhle sexual experience ka evidence consent ke sawaal pe irrelevant bana diya gaya [[indiacode-cla-2013]].

## 2018: investigation ke liye do mahine, har district mein ek centre

Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2018 ko 21 April 2018 se laagu maana gaya. Rape ki minimum saza saat se das saal karne ke alawa [[indiacode-cla-2018]], isne survivors ko deadlines di: police ko rape investigation do mahine mein poori karni hogi, aur appeals ka faisla chhe mahine mein hona chahiye [[gazette-criminal-law-amendment-act-2018]].

December 2018 mein Supreme Court ne do aur protections jodi. Usne kaha ki rape aur POCSO cases ki FIRs public domain mein nahi daali jaayengi, aur har state aur union territory se kaha ki ek saal ke andar har district mein survivors ke liye kam se kam ek One Stop Centre banaye [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]].

## 2023: Zero FIR, video statement, 90 din ka update

Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), jo 2023 mein paas hui, BNS ke saath 1 July 2024 se laagu hui [[air-new-criminal-laws-2024]]. Isne kai practices ko statute mein likh diya.

| Haq | Kahan likha hai |
|---|---|
| Kisi bhi police station mein report (Zero FIR), ya electronically (e-FIR), FIR ki free copy ke saath | Section 173, BNSS |
| Woman officer complaint record kare; statement ghar pe ya uski chuni jagah pe, jo video pe record ho sakta hai | Sections 173 aur 176, BNSS |
| 90 din ke andar investigation ka update | Section 193(3), BNSS |
| Accused ki pehli appearance ke 14 din ke andar police report aur statements ki free copies, agar uska lawyer hai | Section 230, BNSS |
| Koi bhi prosecution wapas lene se pehle sunwaai | Section 360, BNSS |

e-FIR ko 3 din ke andar sign karna hota hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Rape survivor ka statement uske ghar pe ya uski chuni hui jagah pe liya jaana hai, jahan tak ho sake woman officer dwara, aur use mobile phone pe bhi record kiya ja sakta hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. 90 din ka update, documents, aur withdrawal se pehle sune jaane ka haq use apne hi case ka ek party maanta hai, sirf ek gawah nahi jise state bulaata hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Inke saath compensation bhi hai: woh State ya District Legal Services Authority mein apply kar sakti hai, chahe offender kabhi trace na ho [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Woh haq jinke liye survivors aaj bhi ladti hain

Kaagaz pe likhe haq un systems pe tikte hain jo hamesha saamne nahi aate. July 2026 tak, approve hue 1,033 One Stop Centres mein se 985 chal rahe the, Supreme Court ki ek saal ki deadline khatam hone ke saalon baad [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]].

NCRB yeh publish nahi karta ki kitni investigations do mahine ki deadline ke andar poori hoti hain. Woh itna zaroor dikhata hai ki 2024 ke ant mein 8,905 rape cases abhi bhi investigation mein the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Aur sabse lamba intezaar trial ka hai: 2024 ke ant mein 1,85,785 rape cases court mein pending the, yaani us saal courts ke saamne aaye saare rape cases ka 89.8% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Pehchaan chhupaane ka vaada karna aasaan hai, use laagu karwana mushkil. 2024 ke doosre half mein police ne victim ki pehchaan bataane ke liye BNS ke Section 72 mein sirf 11 cases register kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Mana ki gayi FIR aur paise maangne wala hospital sabse mushkil ladaai hain, kyunki yeh sabse bure waqt pe hote hain, aksar bina kisi gawah ke. Isiliye section numbers jaanna zaroori hai. Jo survivor, ya uske saath khadi dost, police desk pe "Section 173" ya hospital counter pe "free treatment law hai" bol sakti hai, woh un haqon ka use kar rahi hai jinhe jeetne mein chaar dashak lage.

union-government-positions-sexual-violen.en:
When a sexual-violence law is challenged in court, the Union of India is usually a respondent. The government that drafts the criminal code then explains, in a sworn written statement called an affidavit, why the law should stay as it is. These documents get a day of headlines and are forgotten. Read side by side, they record what the state is willing to say about consent, and what it did after saying it. This is general information, not legal advice.

## The government as litigant

The Union government speaks in two rooms. In Parliament it is the lawmaker: it brings Bills and answers MPs' questions. In court it is a litigant: its law officers argue and its ministries file affidavits. A statement in court can steer a hearing, but it changes no statute. A statement in Parliament tells you whether a Bill is coming. To know where a law is headed, read both.

| When | Where | What the Union government said or did |
|---|---|---|
| 2018 | Supreme Court | Opposed khatna as a violation of fundamental rights |
| 2023 | Parliament | Did not accept a committee's advice to keep an offence covering non-consensual sex against men and transgender persons |
| July 2024 | Home Ministry note | Called offences in the new code "gender-neutral" |
| October 2024 | Supreme Court | Called marital rape "more of a social issue rather than a legal issue" |
| December 2024 | Rajya Sabha | Said it had no proposal to criminalise marital rape |

## 2018: khatna, opposed in court

A public interest petition filed in the Supreme Court in 2017 seeks a ban on khatna, the genital cutting of girls practised in the Dawoodi Bohra community [[scobserver-sunita-tiwari-fgm-case]]. In December 2017, responding to that petition, the Ministry of Women and Child Development said there was "no official data or study which supports the existence of FGM in India" [[guardian-fgm-india-study-2018]].

In 2018 the government's top law officer took a firmer line. Attorney General K.K. Venugopal told the court that the Union government opposed the practice as a violation of fundamental rights, and that it was banned in countries including the US, the UK, Australia and around 27 African nations [[toi-fgm-five-judge-bench-2018]]. On 24 September 2018 he asked for the case to go to a larger bench, and the court agreed [[sc-sunita-tiwari-order-2018]].

Set that against the statute book. A report of the Supreme Court hearing of 7 May 2026 noted that no specific Indian law bans the practice [[scobserver-sabarimala-day13-2026]]. A nine-judge bench reserved judgment on 14 May 2026 in the religious-freedom reference that will shape the khatna case [[scobserver-sabarimala-day16-2026]]. A government that tells a court a practice violates girls' rights does not need the court's permission to bring a Bill. Its opposition was stated in a courtroom and went no further.

## 2023-2024: the missing offence and the gender-neutral claim

Until the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) replaced the Indian Penal Code on 1 July 2024, Section 377 punished non-consensual "carnal intercourse against the order of nature" with any man, woman or animal [[scroll-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]]. On 10 November 2023, Parliament's Standing Committee on Home Affairs warned that dropping it would leave non-consensual sexual offences against men and transgender persons unpunished, and recommended keeping it. The government did not accept the recommendation [[prs-standing-committee-bns-2023]]. The new code has no equivalent, so forced penetrative sex against an adult man or a transgender person is not rape under it [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Then came the claim. In a July 2024 note the Home Ministry said "various offences against women and children have been made gender-neutral in BNS, covering all victims and perpetrators regardless of gender" [[pib-new-criminal-laws-2024]]. The text is narrower. The BNS lets the pronoun "he" cover any person, "whether male, female or transgender", but it defines "man" as male and "woman" as female, which keeps rape in Section 63 limited to a man assaulting a woman [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Police registered 888 cases of "unnatural offences" under Section 377 in 2023. In the 2024 data the category is gone, marked "deleted in BNS" [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The figure does not separate victims by gender, but it shows a working offence that was removed.

On 28 August 2024 the Delhi High Court asked the Centre to decide within six months whether to restore it [[barandbench-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]]. In March 2026 the court revived the petition, said "the decision is nowhere in sight" and ordered an affidavit within four weeks [[theprint-pti-delhi-hc-restores-pil-2026]]. For about a year and a half, the government's position on this gap was to take none.

## 2024: marital rape, a social issue and no plan to change the law

Exception 2 to Section 63 of the BNS says sexual acts by a man with his own wife, if she is 18 or older, are not rape [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Petitions against that exception are before the Supreme Court.

In an affidavit verified on 3 October 2024, the Union government told the court that marital rape is "more of a social issue rather than a legal issue", and that treating it as rape could be "excessively harsh and therefore, disproportionate" [[union-counter-affidavit-marital-rape-2024]]. It argued that other laws, including the domestic violence law, already give married women remedies [[scobserver-marital-rape-exception-2025]].

If the issue is social and not legal, the place to deal with it is Parliament. Yet in December 2024 the government told the Rajya Sabha that it had no proposal to criminalise marital rape, pointing to the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 and BNS sections 74, 75, 76 and 85 [[scroll-no-proposal-marital-rape-2024]].

> In court, the government says this is a question for society. In Parliament, it says there is no proposal. A wife is told to wait in both rooms.

The Justice Verma Committee recommended deleting the exception in January 2013 [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. As of 19 November 2026 the Supreme Court had still not ruled; the bench said it would fix the final hearing for 9 or 10 December 2026 [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]].

## Answering an affidavit: what citizens can do

An affidavit is a public argument, and citizens are allowed to argue back.

Start with the document. The October 2024 affidavit and the parliamentary answers are public records. Read them and test each claim against the text of the law, as the sections above do.

Use your MP. The December 2024 statement came as a reply to a member's question in the Rajya Sabha [[scroll-no-proposal-marital-rape-2024]]. A question in Parliament puts a ministry's position on record, and you can ask your MP to raise one.

Use the doors courts leave open. Individual Bohra women filed intervention applications in the khatna case [[ht-fgm-seven-judge-bench-2019]]. On 14 October 2024 the Supreme Court refused to entertain a plea on offences against men and transgender persons, saying it cannot direct Parliament to create an offence [[livelaw-sc-bns-sexual-offences-men-pil-2024]]. That refusal sends the question back to Parliament and to the ministry that drafts the Bill, which is where letters and questions from citizens count.

Watch the next deadline. On 5 February 2026 the UN CEDAW Committee asked India what steps it has taken to review the BNS to criminalise marital rape, and what plans it has for a law prohibiting female genital cutting. India's report is due on 3 February 2027 [[cedaw-india-loipr-2026]]. That reply will be the government's next written position. Read it against everything above.
union-government-positions-sexual-violen.hg:
Jab kisi sexual-violence law ko court mein challenge kiya jaata hai, toh Union of India aam taur par ek respondent hota hai. Jo government criminal code draft karti hai, wahi phir ek sworn written statement mein, jise affidavit kehte hain, samjhaati hai ki law jaisa hai waisa kyun rehna chahiye. In documents ko ek din headlines milti hain, phir sab bhool jaate hain. Lekin inhe saath rakh kar padho, toh pata chalta hai ki state consent ke baare mein kya kehne ko taiyaar hai, aur kehne ke baad usne kiya kya. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## The government as litigant: government ek party bhi hai

Union government do kamron mein bolti hai. Parliament mein woh lawmaker hai: Bills laati hai aur MPs ke sawaalon ka jawab deti hai. Court mein woh ek litigant hai: uske law officers argue karte hain aur ministries affidavits file karti hain. Court mein diya gaya statement hearing ki disha badal sakta hai, lekin koi statute nahi badalta. Parliament ka statement batata hai ki koi Bill aa raha hai ya nahi. Law kis taraf ja raha hai, yeh jaanna hai toh dono padhne padenge.

| Kab | Kahan | Union government ne kya kaha ya kiya |
|---|---|---|
| 2018 | Supreme Court | Khatna ko fundamental rights ka violation bata kar oppose kiya |
| 2023 | Parliament | Committee ki yeh salaah nahi maani ki men aur transgender persons ke against non-consensual sex ka offence rakha jaaye |
| July 2024 | Home Ministry note | Naye code ke offences ko "gender-neutral" bataya |
| October 2024 | Supreme Court | Marital rape ko "more of a social issue rather than a legal issue" kaha |
| December 2024 | Rajya Sabha | Kaha ki marital rape ko crime banane ka koi proposal nahi hai |

## 2018: khatna, court mein oppose kiya

2017 mein Supreme Court mein ek public interest petition file hui jo khatna par ban maangti hai. Khatna ladkiyon ki genital cutting hai jo Dawoodi Bohra community mein hoti hai [[scobserver-sunita-tiwari-fgm-case]]. December 2017 mein is petition ke jawab mein Ministry of Women and Child Development ne kaha ki "no official data or study which supports the existence of FGM in India" [[guardian-fgm-india-study-2018]].

2018 mein government ke sabse bade law officer ne zyada sakht line li. Attorney General K.K. Venugopal ne court ko bataya ki Union government is practice ko fundamental rights ka violation maan kar oppose karti hai, aur yeh US, UK, Australia aur lagbhag 27 African countries mein banned hai [[toi-fgm-five-judge-bench-2018]]. 24 September 2018 ko unhone case ko bade bench ke paas bhejne ki maang ki, aur court maan gaya [[sc-sunita-tiwari-order-2018]].

Ab ise statute book ke saamne rakho. 7 May 2026 ki Supreme Court hearing ki ek report ne note kiya ki India mein koi specific law is practice ko ban nahi karta [[scobserver-sabarimala-day13-2026]]. Nau judges ki bench ne 14 May 2026 ko us religious-freedom reference mein judgment reserve kiya jo khatna case ki disha tay karega [[scobserver-sabarimala-day16-2026]]. Jo government court ko kehti hai ki koi practice ladkiyon ke rights todti hai, use Bill laane ke liye court ki permission nahi chahiye. Uska virodh courtroom mein bola gaya, aur wahin ruk gaya.

## 2023-2024: missing offence aur gender-neutral wala claim

1 July 2024 ko Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ne Indian Penal Code ki jagah li. Usse pehle tak Section 377 kisi bhi man, woman ya animal ke saath non-consensual "carnal intercourse against the order of nature" ko punish karta tha [[scroll-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]]. 10 November 2023 ko Parliament ki Standing Committee on Home Affairs ne warning di ki ise hataane se men aur transgender persons ke against non-consensual sexual offences bina saza ke reh jaayenge, aur ise rakhne ki salaah di. Government ne yeh recommendation nahi maani [[prs-standing-committee-bns-2023]]. Naye code mein iska koi equivalent nahi hai, isliye kisi adult aadmi ya transgender person ke saath forced penetrative sex is code ke tahat rape nahi hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Phir aaya claim. July 2024 ke ek note mein Home Ministry ne kaha ki "various offences against women and children have been made gender-neutral in BNS, covering all victims and perpetrators regardless of gender" [[pib-new-criminal-laws-2024]]. Text isse kaafi narrow hai. BNS pronoun "he" ko har person par laagu karta hai, "whether male, female or transgender", lekin "man" ko male aur "woman" ko female define karta hai. Iska matlab Section 63 mein rape abhi bhi sirf ek aadmi ka ek aurat par assault hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Police ne 2023 mein Section 377 ke tahat "unnatural offences" ke 888 cases register kiye. 2024 ke data mein yeh category gayab hai, aur uske aage likha hai "deleted in BNS" [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh figure victims ko gender ke hisaab se alag nahi karta, lekin dikhata hai ki ek chalta hua offence hata diya gaya.

28 August 2024 ko Delhi High Court ne Centre se kaha ki chhe mahine mein tay kare ki ise wapas laana hai ya nahi [[barandbench-delhi-hc-unnatural-offences-bns-2024]]. March 2026 mein court ne petition dobara khol di, kaha ki "the decision is nowhere in sight" aur chaar hafton mein affidavit maanga [[theprint-pti-delhi-hc-restores-pil-2026]]. Lagbhag dedh saal tak is gap par government ki position yahi thi ki koi position na lo.

## 2024: marital rape, "social issue" aur law badalne ka koi plan nahi

BNS Section 63 ka Exception 2 kehta hai ki agar biwi 18 ya usse zyada umar ki hai, toh pati ke uske saath sexual acts rape nahi hain [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Is exception ke khilaf petitions Supreme Court mein pending hain.

3 October 2024 ko verify kiye gaye ek affidavit mein Union government ne court ko kaha ki marital rape "more of a social issue rather than a legal issue" hai, aur ise rape maanna "excessively harsh and therefore, disproportionate" ho sakta hai [[union-counter-affidavit-marital-rape-2024]]. Usne argue kiya ki domestic violence law samet doosre laws pehle se shaadi-shuda aurton ko remedies dete hain [[scobserver-marital-rape-exception-2025]].

Agar issue social hai, legal nahi, toh use deal karne ki jagah Parliament hai. Phir bhi December 2024 mein government ne Rajya Sabha ko bataya ki marital rape ko crime banane ka uske paas koi proposal nahi hai, aur Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 aur BNS sections 74, 75, 76 aur 85 ki taraf ishaara kiya [[scroll-no-proposal-marital-rape-2024]].

> Court mein government kehti hai ki yeh society ka sawaal hai. Parliament mein kehti hai ki koi proposal nahi hai. Biwi ko dono kamron mein intezaar karne ko kaha jaata hai.

Justice Verma Committee ne January 2013 mein is exception ko hataane ki salaah di thi [[thehindu-verma-2013]]. 19 November 2026 tak Supreme Court ne faisla nahi diya tha; bench ne kaha ki final hearing 9 ya 10 December 2026 ko fix karegi [[lawbeat-marital-rape-hearing-2026]].

## Answering an affidavit: citizens kya kar sakte hain

Affidavit ek public argument hai, aur citizens ko uska jawab dene ka haq hai.

Shuruaat document se karo. October 2024 ka affidavit aur parliamentary answers public records hain. Unhe padho aur har claim ko law ke text se test karo, jaise upar ke sections mein kiya gaya hai.

Apne MP ko use karo. December 2024 wala statement Rajya Sabha mein ek member ke sawaal ke jawab mein aaya tha [[scroll-no-proposal-marital-rape-2024]]. Parliament mein poocha gaya sawaal ministry ki position ko record par laata hai, aur tum apne MP se aisa sawaal uthane ko keh sakte ho.

Courts jo darwaaze khule chhodte hain, unka istemaal karo. Khatna case mein Bohra community ki kuch aurton ne intervention applications file ki [[ht-fgm-seven-judge-bench-2019]]. 14 October 2024 ko Supreme Court ne men aur transgender persons ke against offences par ek plea sunne se mana kar diya, yeh kehte hue ki woh Parliament ko naya offence banane ka direction nahi de sakta [[livelaw-sc-bns-sexual-offences-men-pil-2024]]. Is inkaar se sawaal wapas Parliament aur us ministry ke paas pahunchta hai jo Bill draft karti hai, aur wahin citizens ke letters aur sawaal kaam aate hain.

Agli deadline par nazar rakho. 5 February 2026 ko UN CEDAW Committee ne India se poocha ki marital rape ko crime banane ke liye BNS ko review karne ke liye usne kya kadam uthaye hain, aur female genital cutting ko prohibit karne wale law ka kya plan hai. India ki report 3 February 2027 tak due hai [[cedaw-india-loipr-2026]]. Wahi jawab government ki agli written position hogi. Use upar likhi har baat ke saath padho.

when-a-rape-survivor-dies-family-rights.en:
In 2024, police in India registered 266 cases of murder with rape or gang rape, with 274 victims [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Each leaves a family facing a police station, a court and reporters at the door in the week it starts to grieve.

The law does not stop protecting a woman when she dies, and some of its protections pass to her family. Here are five questions such a family runs into, answered from court records and the criminal codes in force since 1 July 2024 [[air-new-criminal-laws-2024]]. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Can anyone publish her name now that she has died?

No. In December 2018, in Nipun Saxena v. Union of India, the Supreme Court ruled that a rape victim's identity must not be disclosed even if she is dead, and even if her next of kin authorise it, unless a Sessions Judge decides that disclosure is justified [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. The judges noted that the victim of the 2012 Delhi gang rape, known only by a pseudonym, "became the most effective symbol of protest the country has ever known".

The belief that death lifts the ban has cost newsrooms money. On 18 April 2018 the Delhi High Court directed 12 media houses that had identified the eight-year-old victim in the Kathua case to pay Rs 10 lakh each to Jammu and Kashmir's victim compensation fund. Their lawyers said they had wrongly believed a dead victim could be named [[thehindu-delhi-hc-kathua-media-2018]].

Today the offence is Section 72 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS): publishing her name, or any detail that could identify her, carries up to 2 years in prison and a fine [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Police registered just 11 cases under it between July and December 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

A family can demand answers and lead a protest without her name or photograph. If you want her named, the route is an application to the Sessions Judge, not a press conference.

## Who decides about her body and her last rites?

Her family should. The Hathras case shows what happens when the state decides instead. A 19-year-old Dalit woman was assaulted on 14 September 2020 and died on 29 September 2020. Police cremated her in the middle of the night, without her family's consent [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]].

In October 2020 the Allahabad High Court found that the local administration had taken the decision jointly and carried it out on the District Magistrate's orders. This action, it observed, "though in the name of law and order situation, is prima facie an infringement upon the human rights of the victim and her family" [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]].

> A law-and-order worry does not cancel a family's right to its daughter's last rites.

If officials press you to hurry, ask for the order in writing, note names and times, and tell a lawyer the same day. The Hathras trial ended on 2 March 2023, nearly two and a half years after her death: three of the four accused were acquitted, one was convicted of culpable homicide not amounting to murder, and no one was found guilty of gang rape or murder [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]].

## What must the police and the court tell us?

More than most families are told. Under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), police must inform "the informant or the victim" of the progress of the investigation within 90 days. If the victim's side has an advocate, it must get free copies of the police report, the FIR and the recorded statements within 14 days of the accused first appearing in court. And no court may let a prosecution be withdrawn without hearing the victim [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

The update goes to the informant, so the relative who lodged the FIR should keep a current phone number with the investigating officer. The case papers depend on having a lawyer; if you cannot afford one, the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) gives free legal aid [[nalsa]].

Dalit and Adivasi families have more. Section 15A of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act makes it the state's duty to protect victims, their dependants and witnesses from intimidation, and gives a victim or dependant the right to timely notice of every court proceeding, including bail hearings [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

## What compensation can the family claim?

Section 396 of the BNSS makes every state run a victim compensation scheme for victims and their dependants. The application goes to the State or District Legal Services Authority, which must finish its inquiry within two months. It can be made even if the offender is never traced and no trial takes place, and compensation is available even after an acquittal [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

NALSA's 2018 scheme for women sets Rs 5 lakh to Rs 10 lakh for the family of a woman who is killed, with limits 50% higher when the victim is a minor [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]]. It is a model scheme: the amount actually paid is decided by state and district authorities.

Courts can go further. When a Sealdah court in Kolkata sentenced the man convicted in the RG Kar Medical College case on 20 January 2025, it also ordered the state to pay the family Rs 17 lakh [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]].

Applying is not a compromise with anyone: the money comes from the state's scheme, not from the accused.

## What punishment does the law set when a rape ends in death?

Section 66 of the BNS applies when a man commits rape and, in the course of it, inflicts an injury that causes the woman's death or leaves her in a persistent vegetative state. The punishment is at least 20 years' rigorous imprisonment, which can extend to imprisonment for the rest of his natural life, or death [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Death is the maximum, not the rule. In the RG Kar case the court convicted under Sections 64, 66 and 103(1) of the BNS and imposed imprisonment for the rest of the convict's natural life. It rejected the CBI's plea for death because the crime was not "rarest of the rare" [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. On 7 February 2025 the Calcutta High Court dismissed the West Bengal government's appeal for the death penalty, leaving the CBI to pursue its own [[barandbench-rg-kar-hc-2025]]. We could not find a ruling on that appeal as of November 2026.

None of this makes the loss smaller. It does mean the family is not a bystander in its own daughter's case. If grief becomes too heavy for anyone at home, Tele-MANAS counsellors are available free, round the clock, on 14416 [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].
when-a-rape-survivor-dies-family-rights.hg:
2024 mein India ki police ne murder with rape ya gang rape ke 266 cases darj kiye, jinmein 274 victims the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Har case ke peeche ek family hoti hai jise usi hafte police station, court aur darwaze par khade reporters ka saamna karna padta hai jis hafte uska dukh shuru hota hai.

Kisi woman ki maut ke baad law uski hifazat karna band nahin karta, aur uski kuch protections uski family ke paas aa jaati hain. Yahan paanch sawaal hain jo aisi family ke saamne aate hain. Jawab court records se aur un criminal codes se liye gaye hain jo 1 July 2024 se laagu hain [[air-new-criminal-laws-2024]]. Yeh general jaankari hai, legal advice nahin.

## Kya uski maut ke baad koi bhi uska naam chhaap sakta hai?

Nahin. December 2018 mein Nipun Saxena v. Union of India mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki rape victim ki identity disclose nahin ki ja sakti, chahe uski maut ho chuki ho, aur chahe uske next of kin iski ijazat de dein. Yeh sirf tab ho sakta hai jab Sessions Judge tay kare ki disclosure justified hai [[sc-nipun-saxena-2018]]. Judges ne yaad dilaya ki 2012 ke Delhi gang rape ki victim, jise desh sirf ek pseudonym se jaanta tha, "became the most effective symbol of protest the country has ever known", yaani desh ka sabse asardaar protest symbol bani.

Yeh soch ki maut ke baad paabandi hat jaati hai, newsrooms ko mehngi padi hai. 18 April 2018 ko Delhi High Court ne un 12 media houses ko, jinhone Kathua case ki aath saal ki victim ki identity bata di thi, Rs 10 lakh each Jammu and Kashmir ke victim compensation fund mein jama karne ko kaha. Unke lawyers ne maana ki unhe galatfehmi thi ki jis victim ki maut ho chuki hai uska naam liya ja sakta hai [[thehindu-delhi-hc-kathua-media-2018]].

Aaj yeh offence Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ka Section 72 hai: uska naam, ya koi bhi detail jisse uski pehchaan ho sake, publish karne par 2 saal tak ki jail aur fine ho sakta hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. July se December 2024 ke beech police ne iske under sirf 11 cases darj kiye [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Family uske naam ya photo ke bina bhi jawab maang sakti hai aur protest lead kar sakti hai. Agar aap chahte hain ki uska naam liya jaaye, toh raasta Sessions Judge ke paas application hai, press conference nahin.

## Uski body aur antim sanskar ka faisla kaun karega?

Uski family ko karna chahiye. Hathras case dikhata hai ki jab yeh faisla state kar le toh kya hota hai. 19 saal ki ek Dalit woman par 14 September 2020 ko assault hua aur 29 September 2020 ko uski maut ho gayi. Police ne aadhi raat ko uska cremation kar diya, family ki consent ke bina [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]].

October 2020 mein Allahabad High Court ne paaya ki yeh faisla local administration ne mil kar liya tha aur ise District Magistrate ke orders par amal mein laaya gaya. Court ne kaha ki yeh action, "though in the name of law and order situation, is prima facie an infringement upon the human rights of the victim and her family", yaani law and order ke naam par hone ke bawajood yeh pehli nazar mein victim aur uski family ke human rights ka violation hai [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]].

> Law and order ki chinta kisi family se uski beti ke antim sanskar ka haq nahin chheen sakti.

Agar officials jaldi karne ka pressure daalein, toh order likhit mein maango, naam aur time note karo, aur usi din kisi lawyer ko batao. Hathras ka trial 2 March 2023 ko khatam hua, uski maut ke lagbhag dhai saal baad: chaar mein se teen accused bari ho gaye, ek ko culpable homicide not amounting to murder ka doshi maana gaya, aur gang rape ya murder ka doshi kisi ko nahin paaya gaya [[livelaw-hathras-verdict-2023]].

## Police aur court ko hamein kya-kya batana hoga?

Jitna zyadatar families ko bataya jaata hai, usse kaafi zyada. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ke under police ko 90 din ke andar "the informant or the victim", yaani informant ya victim ko, batana hota hai ki investigation kahan tak pahunchi. Agar victim ki taraf se advocate hai, toh accused ke pehli baar court mein pesh hone ke 14 din ke andar police report, FIR aur record kiye gaye statements ki free copies milni chahiye. Aur koi bhi court victim ko sune bina prosecution wapas lene ki ijazat nahin de sakti [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Update informant ko jaata hai, isliye jis rishtedaar ne FIR likhwayi thi, woh investigating officer ke paas apna chaalu phone number zaroor rakhe. Case ke papers lawyer hone par hi milte hain. Agar lawyer ka kharcha nahin utha sakte, toh District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) free legal aid deti hai [[nalsa]].

Dalit aur Adivasi families ke paas isse zyada rights hain. SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act ka Section 15A state ki duty banata hai ki woh victims, unke dependants aur witnesses ko dhamki aur dabaav se bachaye. Yahi section victim ya dependant ko har court proceeding ka, bail hearings samet, time par notice paane ka right deta hai [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

## Family kaun sa compensation claim kar sakti hai?

BNSS ka Section 396 har state se victim compensation scheme chalwata hai, victims aur unke dependants ke liye. Application State ya District Legal Services Authority ke paas jaati hai, jise apni inquiry do mahine ke andar poori karni hoti hai. Application tab bhi di ja sakti hai jab offender kabhi pakda hi na jaaye aur koi trial na ho, aur compensation acquittal ke baad bhi mil sakta hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

NALSA ki 2018 ki women wali scheme us woman ki family ke liye Rs 5 lakh se Rs 10 lakh tay karti hai jiski jaan chali gayi, aur victim minor ho toh limits 50% zyada hain [[nalsa-compensation-scheme-women-2018]]. Yeh ek model scheme hai: asal mein kitna paisa milega, yeh state aur district authorities tay karti hain.

Courts isse aage bhi ja sakti hain. Kolkata ki Sealdah court ne 20 January 2025 ko jab RG Kar Medical College case ke convict ko saza sunayi, toh state ko family ko Rs 17 lakh dene ka order bhi diya [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]].

Apply karna kisi se samjhauta karna nahin hai: paisa state ki scheme se aata hai, accused se nahin.

## Jab rape ki wajah se maut ho jaaye, toh law kya saza rakhta hai?

BNS ka Section 66 tab lagta hai jab koi aadmi rape kare aur usi dauraan aisi chot pahunchaye jisse woman ki maut ho jaaye ya woh persistent vegetative state mein chali jaaye. Saza kam se kam 20 saal ki rigorous imprisonment hai, jo uski baaki natural life tak ki jail tak badh sakti hai, ya phir death [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Death maximum saza hai, rule nahin. RG Kar case mein court ne BNS ke Sections 64, 66 aur 103(1) ke under convict kiya aur convict ko uski baaki natural life tak ki jail di. CBI ne death maangi thi, par court ne mana kar diya kyunki yeh crime "rarest of the rare" nahin tha [[tribune-rg-kar-sentence-2025]]. 7 February 2025 ko Calcutta High Court ne death penalty ke liye West Bengal government ki appeal dismiss kar di, aur CBI ke liye apni appeal aage badhane ka raasta khula raha [[barandbench-rg-kar-hc-2025]]. November 2026 tak hamein us appeal par koi faisla nahin mila.

In sab se dukh chhota nahin hota. Par iska matlab yeh zaroor hai ki apni hi beti ke case mein family sirf tamashbeen nahin hai. Agar ghar mein kisi ke liye bhi dukh bahut bhaari ho jaaye, toh Tele-MANAS ke counsellors 14416 par free aur 24 ghante available hain [[pib-garima-greh-lok-sabha-2025]].

which-court-hears-sexual-offence-cases.en:
Imagine four FIRs registered in one district in the same week. A 26-year-old woman reports a rape. A mother reports the sexual assault of her 12-year-old son. A Dalit farm worker reports being sexually assaulted by a landowner who knows her caste. In a fourth rape case, the accused turns out to be 17. All four are "sexual-offence cases". They can end up in four different courtrooms, each with its own procedure and its own deadline. India built this patchwork one law at a time, and the court a case lands in shapes how long a survivor waits, how she is questioned and sometimes what sentence is possible. This is general information, not legal advice.

## Sessions courts and the in-camera rule

An adult rape case is usually tried in a sessions court, the senior criminal court of a district. Under Section 366 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), it must be held in camera, as far as practicable before a woman judge, and nothing about the proceedings may be published without the court's permission [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. The same law says a rape trial must be completed within two months of the chargesheet [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

At the end of 2024, 1,85,785 rape cases were pending trial, 89.8% of all the rape cases before the courts that year [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Fast Track Special Courts: 779 and counting

Fast Track Special Courts are the Centre's answer to that backlog: courts funded under a scheme launched on 2 October 2019 to hear rape and POCSO cases. In November 2026 there were 779 of them in 29 states and union territories, 399 reserved for POCSO, and they had disposed of 4,02,457 cases since the scheme began. The Cabinet has extended it to March 2031, with room for up to 850 courts [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]].

A fast-track court is a dedicated courtroom, not a different law. The two-month rule and the in-camera rule are the same ones that bind any sessions court. The queue has followed the cases in: about 2,45,579 rape and POCSO cases were pending before these courts on 31 December 2025 [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]].

## POCSO Special Courts: the child's 30 days

If the survivor is under 18, boy or girl, the case goes to a Special Court under the POCSO Act, and every district must have one [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. This court runs on different rules. The child's evidence must be recorded within 30 days of the court taking cognizance, and the trial completed, as far as possible, within one year. Lawyers put their questions to the child through the judge. Aggressive questioning and repeated calls to testify are barred, the child is kept from seeing the accused, by video link, one-way mirror or curtain if needed, and a parent or trusted person stays in the room [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

It also runs on a different presumption. Under Section 29, the Special Court must presume that a person prosecuted for penetrative or sexual assault on a child committed the offence unless the contrary is proved [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. The wait is still long: 2,86,903 POCSO cases were pending trial at the end of 2024, 87.7% of those before the courts [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Atrocities Act courts and the two-month target

When a sexual offence against a Dalit or Adivasi woman is charged under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, a third kind of court comes in. Since the 2015 amendment, touching her sexually without consent, or using sexual words or gestures towards her, knowing her caste or tribe, is a specific atrocity punishable with six months to five years in prison [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

The same amendment requires states to set up Exclusive Special Courts, to hear trials day to day and, as far as possible, to finish them within two months of the charge sheet. It also gives victims the right to timely notice of court proceedings, including bail hearings [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]]. The record is far from the target. In 2023, 20,622 rape cases involving Scheduled Caste victims, 92.3%, were still pending trial at the end of the year, and the conviction rate was 30.5% [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]].

## When the accused is 16 or 17: the Juvenile Justice Board

The accused's age can pull a case out of all these courts. A child accused of an offence goes before a Juvenile Justice Board, not a criminal court. Since the Juvenile Justice Act of 2015, the Board must make a "preliminary assessment" of any child aged 16 or above who is accused of a heinous offence, meaning one with a minimum punishment of seven years or more. The assessment can send the case to a Children's Court for trial as an adult [[gazette-juvenile-justice-act-2015]]. Rape, with its 10-year minimum, qualifies [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

The Act received assent on 31 December 2015 [[gazette-juvenile-justice-act-2015]], the year the juvenile accused in the 2012 Delhi gang rape case was released after three years in a correctional home [[tribune-nirbhaya-execution-2020]]. Even whether an accused is a juvenile can be fought to the top: in the Kathua case, the Supreme Court ruled in November 2022 that an accused earlier declared a juvenile must be tried as an adult [[scroll-kathua-juvenile-2022]].

| The case | The court | The clock on paper |
|---|---|---|
| Rape of an adult woman | Sessions court or Fast Track Special Court | Trial within 2 months of the chargesheet |
| Sexual offence against anyone under 18 | POCSO Special Court | Evidence in 30 days; trial in 1 year |
| Offence charged under the Atrocities Act | Exclusive Special Court | Trial within 2 months of the charge sheet |
| Accused aged 16 or 17, heinous offence | Juvenile Justice Board, then possibly a Children's Court | Preliminary assessment first |

One survivor is missing from this table. The new penal code has no rape provision for an adult man or a transgender person, so there is no rape trial for any of these courts to hear [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

> Four doors, four deadlines, and a queue behind every one. Knowing which door is yours tells you which promise to hold the court to.
which-court-hears-sexual-offence-cases.hg:
Socho, ek hi district mein ek hi hafte mein chaar FIRs register hoti hain. 26 saal ki ek aurat rape ki report karti hai. Ek maa apne 12 saal ke bete par hue sexual assault ki report karti hai.
