Ek Dalit khet mazdoor batati hai ki ek zameendar ne, jo uski caste jaanta hai, us par sexual assault kiya. Chauthe rape case mein pata chalta hai ki accused 17 saal ka hai. Chaaron "sexual-offence cases" hain. Lekin yeh chaar alag courtrooms mein pahunch sakte hain, har ek ka apna procedure aur apni deadline. India ne yeh patchwork ek-ek law karke banaya, aur case jis court mein pahunchta hai, usi se tay hota hai ki survivor kitna intezaar karegi, usse sawaal kaise pooche jaayenge aur kabhi-kabhi kaun si saza mumkin hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Sessions courts aur in-camera rule

Adult ke rape case ka trial aam taur par sessions court mein hota hai, jo district ka senior criminal court hai. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ke Section 366 ke under trial in camera hona chahiye, jahan tak ho sake mahila judge ke saamne, aur court ki permission ke bina proceedings ke baare mein kuch bhi publish nahi ho sakta [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Yahi law kehta hai ki rape trial chargesheet ke do mahine ke andar poora hona chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

2024 ke end par 1,85,785 rape cases trial ke liye pending the, yaani us saal courts ke saamne aaye saare rape cases ka 89.8% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Fast Track Special Courts: 779 aur ginti jaari

Fast Track Special Courts is backlog ka Centre wala jawab hain: 2 October 2019 ko launch hui scheme ke under fund kiye gaye courts, jo rape aur POCSO cases sunte hain. November 2026 mein 29 states aur union territories mein aise 779 courts the, jinme se 399 POCSO ke liye reserved the, aur scheme shuru hone se ab tak inhone 4,02,457 cases dispose kiye the. Cabinet ne scheme ko March 2031 tak badha diya hai, aur 850 courts tak ki gunjaish rakhi hai [[pib-ftsc-scheme-continuation-2026]].

Fast-track court ek dedicated courtroom hai, koi alag law nahi. Do mahine wala rule aur in-camera rule wahi hain jo kisi bhi sessions court par lagu hote hain. Cases ke saath line bhi andar aa gayi: 31 December 2025 ko in courts ke saamne lagbhag 2,45,579 rape aur POCSO cases pending the [[pib-ftsc-rajya-sabha-2026-07]].

## POCSO Special Courts: bachche ke 30 din

Agar survivor 18 se kam umar ka hai, ladka ho ya ladki, toh case POCSO Act ke under Special Court mein jaata hai, aur har district mein aisa ek court hona zaroori hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Yeh court alag rules par chalta hai. Bachche ka evidence court ke cognizance lene ke 30 din ke andar record hona chahiye, aur trial, jahan tak mumkin ho, ek saal ke andar poora hona chahiye. Lawyers apne sawaal judge ke zariye bachche se poochte hain. Aggressive questioning aur baar-baar gawahi ke liye bulana mana hai, bachche ko accused ke saamne aane se bachaya jaata hai, zaroorat ho toh video link, one-way mirror ya curtain se, aur ek parent ya bharose ka insaan kamre mein rehta hai [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

Yeh ek alag presumption par bhi chalta hai. Section 29 ke under Special Court ko yeh maanna hota hai ki jis insaan par bachche par penetrative ya sexual assault ka prosecution chal raha hai, usne offence kiya hai, jab tak ulta saabit na ho [[indiacode-pocso-2012]]. Intezaar ab bhi lamba hai: 2024 ke end par 2,86,903 POCSO cases trial ke liye pending the, yaani courts ke saamne aaye cases ka 87.7% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

## Atrocities Act courts aur do mahine ka target

Jab kisi Dalit ya Adivasi aurat ke khilaaf sexual offence SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act ke under charge hota hai, toh ek teesri tarah ka court aata hai. 2015 ke amendment ke baad se, uski caste ya tribe jaante hue use bina consent sexual tareeke se chhoona, ya uski taraf sexual shabd ya ishaare istemaal karna, ek specific atrocity hai jiski saza chhe mahine se paanch saal tak ki jail hai [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]].

Yahi amendment states se kehta hai ki Exclusive Special Courts banayein, trials day-to-day sunein aur, jahan tak mumkin ho, charge sheet ke do mahine ke andar unhe poora karein. Yeh victims ko court proceedings ka time par notice paane ka haq bhi deta hai, bail hearings samet [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]]. Record target se bahut door hai. 2023 mein Scheduled Caste victims wale 20,622 rape cases, yaani 92.3%, saal ke end par bhi trial ke liye pending the, aur conviction rate 30.5% tha [[ncrb-cii-2023-vol2]].

## Jab accused 16 ya 17 ka ho: Juvenile Justice Board

Accused ki umar case ko in saare courts se bahar kheench sakti hai. Jis bachche par offence ka ilzaam ho, woh criminal court ke saamne nahi, Juvenile Justice Board ke saamne jaata hai. 2015 ke Juvenile Justice Act ke baad se Board ko 16 ya usse zyada umar ke us bachche ka "preliminary assessment" karna hota hai jis par heinous offence ka ilzaam ho, yaani aisa offence jiski minimum saza saat saal ya usse zyada hai. Is assessment ke baad case Children's Court mein adult ki tarah trial ke liye bheja ja sakta hai [[gazette-juvenile-justice-act-2015]]. Rape, jiski minimum saza 10 saal hai, isme aata hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Is Act ko 31 December 2015 ko assent mila [[gazette-juvenile-justice-act-2015]], usi saal jab 2012 ke Delhi gang rape case ka juvenile accused correctional home mein teen saal rehne ke baad release hua [[tribune-nirbhaya-execution-2020]]. Accused juvenile hai ya nahi, yeh sawaal bhi sabse upar ke court tak ja sakta hai: Kathua case mein Supreme Court ne November 2022 mein kaha ki jis accused ko pehle juvenile maana gaya tha, us par adult ki tarah trial chalega [[scroll-kathua-juvenile-2022]].

| Case | Court | Kaagaz par ghadi |
|---|---|---|
| Adult aurat ka rape | Sessions court ya Fast Track Special Court | Chargesheet ke 2 mahine ke andar trial |
| 18 se kam umar ke kisi bhi bachche ke khilaaf sexual offence | POCSO Special Court | 30 din mein evidence; 1 saal mein trial |
| Atrocities Act ke under charge hua offence | Exclusive Special Court | Charge sheet ke 2 mahine ke andar trial |
| Accused 16 ya 17 ka, heinous offence | Juvenile Justice Board, phir shayad Children's Court | Pehle preliminary assessment |

Is table mein ek survivor gayab hai. Naye penal code mein adult aadmi ya transgender person ke liye rape ka koi provision nahi hai, isliye in courts mein se kisi ke paas sunne ke liye unka rape trial hota hi nahi [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

> Chaar darwaze, chaar deadlines, aur har darwaze ke peeche ek line. Tumhara darwaza kaun sa hai, yeh jaan lo, toh pata chalega ki court ko kis vaade par pakadna hai.

who-is-who-in-a-rape-case.en:
A rape case in India is not handled by "the system". It is handled by particular people, one after another, and since 1 July 2024 the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) gives each of them a named duty and often a deadline. Imagine a 22-year-old in Nagpur who walks into a police station on a Monday night. Before any verdict she will meet a woman officer, an investigating officer, a doctor, a magistrate, a prosecutor and a judge. Two more offices exist to help her, and it is possible that no one will tell her about them. At the end of 2024, 1,85,785 rape cases were pending trial [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. When a case stalls, the useful question is whose job the next step was. This is general information, not legal advice.

## The police station: a woman officer and the FIR

The first person is a woman. When a woman reports rape, Section 173 of the BNSS says her information must be recorded by a woman police officer or any woman officer [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. The station cannot send her elsewhere: police must record a cognizable offence wherever it was committed (the Zero FIR) and give her a copy free of cost [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. An officer who fails to record a rape complaint commits an offence under Section 199 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), punishable with six months to two years of rigorous imprisonment [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

The second person is the investigating officer, who holds the case until the chargesheet. The survivor's statement must be taken at her home or a place of her choice, as far as practicable by a woman officer [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. The investigation must be completed within two months, and she is owed a progress update within 90 days [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Ask for that update in writing, and keep the reply.

## The hospital: the doctor's 24 hours and 7 days

Under Section 184, police must send the survivor to a registered medical practitioner, preferably a government doctor, within 24 hours of receiving the information. The doctor may examine her only with her consent, and must send the report to the investigating officer within seven days [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Treatment is a separate duty. Every hospital, public or private, must give a rape survivor immediate first aid or treatment free of cost and inform the police [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. A hospital in-charge who refuses faces up to one year in prison [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. The doctor is also the person to ask about two medicines that run on their own clocks: emergency contraception, usable up to five days after the assault and better taken sooner [[who-ec]], and HIV post-exposure prophylaxis, which must start as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours after exposure [[who-pep]].

## The magistrate's chamber: the survivor's own statement

The next person is a judicial officer, not a police officer. Under Section 183(6), a magistrate must record the survivor's statement as soon as the offence is brought to the notice of the police. As far as practicable this should be a woman magistrate; in her absence, a male magistrate records it in the presence of a woman [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

This puts her account on record before a court officer, not only in a police file. If she has a physical or mental disability, the magistrate must use an interpreter or special educator and record the statement on audio-video. That recording then counts as her examination-in-chief, so she does not have to repeat it at the trial, though she can still be cross-examined [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## The courtroom: an in-camera trial and a special court

In court the case belongs to the State. A public prosecutor conducts it, and the survivor is its main witness. If she has her own advocate, she is entitled to free copies of the police report, the FIR and the statements, and no court may let the prosecution be withdrawn without hearing her [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

The judge's duties sit in Section 366. The trial must be held in camera, as far as practicable before a woman judge, and nothing about the proceedings may be published without the court's permission [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. A rape trial is meant to finish within two months of the chargesheet [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. If the survivor is under 18, the case goes to a POCSO Special Court, which every district must have, and the child's evidence must be recorded within 30 days of the court taking cognizance [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

| Who | BNSS section | Duty | Clock |
|---|---|---|---|
| Woman police officer | 173 | Records the complaint; free FIR copy | At once |
| Investigating officer | 193 | Completes the investigation; updates the survivor | 2 months; 90 days |
| Doctor | 184 | Examines only with consent; sends the report | 24 hours; 7 days |
| Magistrate | 183 | Records the survivor's statement | As soon as police are told |
| Trial judge | 366, 346 | Holds the trial in camera | 2 months from chargesheet |
| Legal Services Authority | 396 | Decides compensation | 2 months |

## Outside court: One Stop Centres and Legal Services Authorities

Two offices sit outside this chain, and neither depends on the verdict. Under Section 396, every state must run a victim compensation scheme. A survivor can apply to the State or District Legal Services Authority even if the offender is never traced and no trial takes place, and the authority must finish its inquiry within two months [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. The same authorities provide free legal aid [[nalsa]].

The One Stop Centre is the government's support centre for women affected by violence, and the place to ask about any of these steps. In July 2026, 985 of the 1,033 approved centres were operational, and they had assisted over 15.20 lakh women between April 2015 and June 2026 [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]]. The centres and the Women Helpline both come under Mission Shakti [[wcd-mission-shakti]].

One limit runs through this whole chain. Most of these duties are written for a woman, because the BNS defines rape as an act by a man against a woman. A child of any gender is covered by POCSO and its Special Court. An adult man or a transgender survivor has no rape provision in the new code at all [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

> Every stage has a person, a section and usually a deadline. Delay is easier to challenge once you can name all three.
who-is-who-in-a-rape-case.hg:
India mein rape case ko "system" nahi sambhalta. Use kuch khaas log sambhalte hain, ek ke baad ek, aur 1 July 2024 se Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) har ek ko ek tay duty aur aksar ek deadline deti hai. Socho, Nagpur ki ek 22 saal ki ladki Monday ki raat police station pahunchti hai. Kisi bhi verdict se pehle woh ek mahila officer, ek investigating officer, ek doctor, ek magistrate, ek prosecutor aur ek judge se milegi. Do aur offices uski madad ke liye bane hain, aur ho sakta hai koi use unke baare mein bataye hi na. 2024 ke end par 1,85,785 rape cases trial ke liye pending the [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Jab case atak jaaye, toh kaam ka sawaal yeh hai ki agla step kiski zimmedari thi. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Police station: mahila officer aur FIR

Pehli insaan ek mahila hai. Jab koi aurat rape ki report karti hai, toh BNSS ka Section 173 kehta hai ki uski information mahila police officer ya koi bhi mahila officer hi record karegi [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Station use kahin aur nahi bhej sakta: police ko cognizable offence record karna hi hai, chahe woh kahin bhi hua ho (Zero FIR), aur use FIR ki copy free deni hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Jo officer rape ki complaint record nahi karta, woh Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) ke Section 199 ke under offence karta hai, jiski saza chhe mahine se do saal tak ki rigorous imprisonment hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Doosra insaan investigating officer hai, jiske paas chargesheet tak case rehta hai. Survivor ka statement uske ghar par ya uski pasand ki jagah par liya jaana chahiye, aur jahan tak ho sake mahila officer le [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Investigation do mahine ke andar poori honi chahiye, aur 90 din ke andar use progress update milna uska haq hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Yeh update likhit mein maango, aur jawaab sambhaal kar rakho.

## Hospital: doctor ke 24 ghante aur 7 din

Section 184 ke under police ko information milne ke 24 ghante ke andar survivor ko registered medical practitioner ke paas bhejna hota hai, behtar ho ki sarkari doctor ke paas. Doctor sirf uske consent se examination kar sakta hai, aur use report saat din ke andar investigating officer ko bhejni hoti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Ilaaj ek alag duty hai. Har hospital ko, sarkari ho ya private, rape survivor ko turant first aid ya treatment free dena hai aur police ko inform karna hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Jo hospital in-charge mana kare, use ek saal tak ki jail ho sakti hai [[indiacode-bns-2023]]. Doctor hi woh insaan hai jisse do dawaiyon ke baare mein poochna hai, jinki apni ghadi chalti hai: emergency contraception, jo assault ke paanch din baad tak li ja sakti hai aur jitni jaldi lo utna behtar [[who-ec]], aur HIV post-exposure prophylaxis, jo jitni jaldi ho sake shuru honi chahiye aur exposure ke 72 ghante se zyada late nahi [[who-pep]].

## Magistrate ka chamber: survivor ka apna statement

Agla insaan ek judicial officer hai, police officer nahi. Section 183(6) ke under, jaise hi offence police ke notice mein aaye, magistrate ko survivor ka statement record karna hota hai. Jahan tak ho sake yeh mahila magistrate honi chahiye; woh na ho, toh male magistrate ek mahila ki maujoodgi mein statement record karta hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Isse uski baat court ke officer ke saamne record par aa jaati hai, sirf police file mein nahi rehti. Agar use koi physical ya mental disability hai, toh magistrate ko interpreter ya special educator rakhna hoga aur statement audio-video par record karna hoga. Wahi recording phir uska examination-in-chief maana jaata hai, toh use trial mein sab dobara nahi batana padta, haalaanki uska cross-examination ho sakta hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Courtroom: in-camera trial aur special court

Court mein case State ka hota hai. Use public prosecutor chalata hai, aur survivor uski main witness hoti hai. Agar uske paas apna advocate hai, toh use police report, FIR aur statements ki free copies milne ka haq hai, aur koi court use sune bina prosecution wapas lene ki ijaazat nahi de sakta [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Judge ki duties Section 366 mein hain. Trial in camera hona chahiye, jahan tak ho sake mahila judge ke saamne, aur court ki permission ke bina proceedings ke baare mein kuch bhi publish nahi ho sakta [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Rape trial chargesheet ke do mahine ke andar poora hona chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Agar survivor 18 se kam umar ki hai, toh case POCSO Special Court mein jaata hai, jo har district mein hona zaroori hai, aur bachche ka evidence court ke cognizance lene ke 30 din ke andar record hona chahiye [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].

| Kaun | BNSS section | Duty | Ghadi |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mahila police officer | 173 | Complaint record karti hai; FIR ki free copy | Turant |
| Investigating officer | 193 | Investigation poori karta hai; survivor ko update deta hai | 2 mahine; 90 din |
| Doctor | 184 | Sirf consent se examination; report bhejta hai | 24 ghante; 7 din |
| Magistrate | 183 | Survivor ka statement record karta hai | Police ko pata chalte hi |
| Trial judge | 366, 346 | Trial in camera chalata hai | Chargesheet se 2 mahine |
| Legal Services Authority | 396 | Compensation tay karti hai | 2 mahine |

## Court ke bahar: One Stop Centres aur Legal Services Authorities

Do offices is chain ke bahar hain, aur dono mein se koi bhi verdict par depend nahi karta. Section 396 ke under har state ko victim compensation scheme chalani hai. Survivor State ya District Legal Services Authority mein tab bhi apply kar sakti hai jab offender kabhi pakda na jaaye aur koi trial na ho, aur authority ko apni inquiry do mahine ke andar poori karni hoti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Yahi authorities free legal aid bhi deti hain [[nalsa]].

One Stop Centre violence jhelne wali auraton ke liye sarkar ka support centre hai, aur in mein se kisi bhi step ke baare mein poochne ki jagah. July 2026 mein 1,033 approved centres mein se 985 chal rahe the, aur April 2015 se June 2026 ke beech inhone 15.20 lakh se zyada auraton ki madad ki thi [[pib-osc-lok-sabha-2026-07]]. Yeh centres aur Women Helpline dono Mission Shakti ke under aate hain [[wcd-mission-shakti]].

Is poori chain mein ek limit hai. Zyada tar duties ek aurat ke liye likhi gayi hain, kyunki BNS rape ko ek aadmi ka ek aurat ke khilaaf kiya gaya act maanti hai. Kisi bhi gender ka bachcha POCSO aur uske Special Court se cover hai. Adult aadmi ya transgender survivor ke liye naye code mein rape ka koi provision hai hi nahi [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

> Har stage par ek insaan hai, ek section hai aur aksar ek deadline hai. Jab tum teeno ka naam le sako, toh deri ko challenge karna aasaan ho jaata hai.

why-rape-trials-end-in-acquittal.en:
In 2024, Indian courts finished 20,587 rape trials. They convicted in 5,032 and acquitted in 13,980, a conviction rate of 24.4% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. For every trial that ended in a conviction, almost three ended in an acquittal.

The common reading is that most complaints must have been false. The record does not say that. It shows a chain with weak points so well known that Parliament and the Supreme Court have written a rule for each. This investigation takes one case past four of them. It is general information, not legal advice.

## What an acquittal means, and what it does not

A criminal court does not rule on who is lying. It asks whether the prosecution has proved guilt beyond reasonable doubt. If a doubt remains, the accused walks free. That standard should stay.

So an acquittal is a finding about proof, and NCRB's tables do not record why the proof failed. A medical report that came late, a witness worn out by years of hearings, a family that "settled" and a complaint that was untrue all land in the same column [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Police filed charge-sheets in 81.3% of the rape cases they disposed of in 2024 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The acquittals came in cases that investigators had judged fit for court.

One limit: the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita defines rape as an act by a man against a woman, so adult men and transgender survivors do not appear in these tables at all [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Now consider a 19-year-old in a district town who reports that a neighbour raped her.

## Weak point one: the first 24 hours

Section 184 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) says she must be sent to a doctor within 24 hours of police receiving the information, and only with her consent. The doctor must send the report to the investigating officer within seven days [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Physical evidence does not wait.

Many women cannot report the same day, and the data points to why: in 96.8% of rape cases registered in 2024, the accused was someone she knew [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. The Supreme Court's 2023 handbook on gender stereotypes rejects the belief that a woman who delays reporting is lying; fear of repercussions or a lack of family support can cause the delay [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

But a late examination finds less, and a bad one does harm. In October 2022 the Supreme Court had to rule that the "two-finger test" has "no scientific basis" and that anyone who conducts it is guilty of misconduct [[theprint-sc-two-finger-test-2022]]. A trial that starts with thin medical evidence rests almost entirely on her testimony.

## Weak point two: the years before the witness box

On paper the timetable is short. A magistrate must record her statement as soon as police learn of the offence. Police must finish the investigation within two months. The trial must end within two months of the charge-sheet [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

In court it is not. At the end of 2024, 1,85,785 rape cases were pending trial, 89.8% of those before the courts [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. That pile is about nine times the number of trials completed in the year.

So our 19-year-old may be well into her twenties when she is cross-examined on what she said at 19. Every gap between an old statement and a tired memory becomes a "contradiction". That is why the early statement before a magistrate matters: it is a judicial record made close to the event. For a survivor with a disability, the video-recorded statement counts as her examination-in-chief, so she need not repeat it at trial [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Weak point three: when the accused lives next door

Of the 28,597 rape cases in 2024 where the offender was known, 2,134 named a family member and 12,584 a family friend, neighbour, employer or other known person. The other 13,879 named a friend, online friend, live-in partner or separated husband [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

An accused like that, out on bail, does not disappear. He is in her lane, her workplace or her home. The pressure seldom looks like a threat. It looks like an elder saying the family has suffered enough, an offer of money, a proposal of marriage. If she then goes back on her statement in court, the case is likely to become one more acquittal.

The Supreme Court dealt with this in 2021, in Aparna Bhat v. State of Madhya Pradesh. It struck down a High Court bail order that told the accused to ask the complainant to tie a rakhi on him. It ruled that bail conditions must not require or permit contact with the victim, and that courts must not suggest compromise or marriage [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. The handbook is blunter [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]:

> "Marriage is not a remedy to the violence of rape."

## Weak point four: the courtroom itself

The law has tried to change the room where she testifies. Rape trials must be held in camera, as far as practicable before a woman judge [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), her character and previous sexual experience are irrelevant to consent (Section 48), and she may not be cross-examined on them to prove consent (Section 149) [[indiacode-bsa-2023]].

Rules still depend on the person on the bench. On 10 February 2026, in a case it took up on its own after a High Court reduced the charges in a child sexual assault case from attempt to rape to lesser offences, the Supreme Court said efforts to sensitise judges "have not borne the fruit that was expected". It asked a National Judicial Academy expert committee to draft guidelines on sensitivity in sexual-offence cases [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]].

None of this is an argument for convicting on weaker proof. It is an argument for building proof early and protecting it. A survivor can ask by name for the examination within 24 hours and the magistrate's statement, and police owe her a progress update within 90 days [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

The 13,980 is not a count of women who lied. It is a count of cases the State did not prove, in a system whose weak points are already written into its own rule book.
why-rape-trials-end-in-acquittal.hg:
2024 mein India ki courts ne 20,587 rape trials poore kiye. 5,032 mein conviction hua aur 13,980 mein acquittal, yaani conviction rate 24.4% raha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Har ek conviction ke saamne lagbhag teen acquittals.

Aam taur par iska matlab yeh nikaala jaata hai ki zyada tar complaints jhoothi rahi hongi. Record aisa nahi kehta. Record ek chain dikhata hai jiski kamzor kadiyaan itni jaani-pehchaani hain ki Parliament aur Supreme Court ne har ek ke liye alag rule likha hai. Yeh investigation ek case ko unme se chaar kadiyon se guzaarti hai. Yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

## Acquittal ka matlab kya hai, aur kya nahi

Criminal court yeh tay nahi karti ki jhooth kaun bol raha hai. Woh yeh poochti hai ki kya prosecution ne guilt ko "beyond reasonable doubt" saabit kiya. Agar shaq bacha rehta hai, toh accused chhoot jaata hai. Yeh standard aisa hi rehna chahiye.

Yaani acquittal saboot ke baare mein ek faisla hai, aur NCRB ki tables yeh record nahi karti ki saboot kyun kam pada. Der se aayi medical report, saalon ki tareekhon se thaka hua gawah, "samjhauta" kar chuka parivaar aur jhoothi complaint, sab ek hi column mein girte hain [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

2024 mein police ne jitne rape cases dispose kiye, unme se 81.3% mein charge-sheet file ki [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yaani acquittals un cases mein aaye jinhe investigators ne khud court ke layak maana tha.

Ek seema bhi hai: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita rape ko aise define karti hai ki woh ek aadmi dwara ek aurat ke khilaaf kiya gaya act hai. Isliye adult men aur transgender survivors in tables mein kahin dikhte hi nahi [[indiacode-bns-2023]].

Ab ek district town ki 19 saal ki ladki ke baare mein sochiye, jo report karti hai ki ek padosi ne uska rape kiya.

## Pehli kamzor kadi: pehle 24 ghante

Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) ka Section 184 kehta hai ki police ko information milne ke 24 ghante ke andar use doctor ke paas bheja jaana chahiye, aur sirf uski consent se. Doctor ko report saat din ke andar investigating officer ko bhejni hoti hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Physical evidence intezaar nahi karta.

Bahut si auratein usi din report nahi kar paati, aur data iski wajah ki taraf ishaara karta hai: 2024 mein register hue 96.8% rape cases mein accused koi aisa tha jise woh jaanti thi [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Supreme Court ki 2023 ki gender stereotypes handbook is soch ko khaarij karti hai ki der se report karne wali aurat jhooth bol rahi hai; anjaam ka darr ya parivaar ka saath na milna deri ki wajah ho sakta hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]].

Lekin der se hua examination kam cheezein pakad paata hai, aur galat tareeke se hua examination nuksaan karta hai. October 2022 mein Supreme Court ko yeh kehna pada ki "two-finger test" ka "no scientific basis" hai aur jo bhi ise karega woh misconduct ka doshi hoga [[theprint-sc-two-finger-test-2022]]. Jis trial ki shuruaat kamzor medical evidence se hoti hai, woh lagbhag poori tarah uski gawahi par tika hota hai.

## Doosri kamzor kadi: witness box tak pahunchne mein lage saal

Kaagaz par timetable chhota hai. Jaise hi police ko offence ka pata chale, magistrate ko uska statement record karna hota hai. Police ko do mahine ke andar investigation poori karni hoti hai. Trial charge-sheet ke do mahine ke andar khatam hona chahiye [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

Court mein aisa nahi hota. 2024 ke end mein 1,85,785 rape cases trial ke liye pending the, yaani courts ke saamne jitne cases the unka 89.8% [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Yeh dher us saal poore hue trials ka lagbhag nau guna hai.

Toh hamari 19 saal ki ladki shayad apne twenties mein kaafi aage pahunch chuki hogi jab cross-examination mein usse poocha jaayega ki 19 ki umar mein usne kya kaha tha. Puraane statement aur thaki hui yaaddasht ke beech ka har fark "contradiction" ban jaata hai. Isiliye magistrate ke saamne shuru mein diya gaya statement itna zaroori hai: yeh ghatna ke kareeb bana ek judicial record hai. Disability wali survivor ke liye video-recorded statement uska examination-in-chief maana jaata hai, toh use trial mein woh sab dobara nahi kehna padta [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

## Teesri kamzor kadi: jab accused pados mein hi rehta hai

2024 ke jin 28,597 rape cases mein offender jaana-pehchaana tha, unme se 2,134 mein parivaar ka koi member tha aur 12,584 mein family friend, padosi, employer ya koi aur jaan-pehchaan wala. Baaki 13,879 mein dost, online friend, live-in partner ya alag reh raha pati tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Aisa accused bail par bahar aakar gaayab nahi hota. Woh uski gali mein, uske workplace par ya uske ghar mein hi hota hai. Dabaav aksar dhamki jaisa nahi dikhta. Woh aisa dikhta hai: koi bada-buzurg keh raha hai ki parivaar bahut seh chuka, paison ka offer, ya shaadi ka proposal. Agar iske baad woh court mein apne statement se palat jaati hai, toh case ke ek aur acquittal banne ki poori sambhavna hai.

Supreme Court ne 2021 mein Aparna Bhat v. State of Madhya Pradesh mein isi par baat ki. Usne ek High Court ka woh bail order radd kiya jisme accused se kaha gaya tha ki woh complainant se rakhi bandhwaane ki request kare. Court ne kaha ki bail conditions mein victim se contact na zaroori kiya ja sakta hai, na uski ijaazat di ja sakti hai, aur courts compromise ya shaadi ka sujhaav nahi de sakti [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]]. Handbook isse bhi seedhi baat kehti hai [[sc-handbook-gender-stereotypes-2023]]:

> "Marriage is not a remedy to the violence of rape."

## Chauthi kamzor kadi: khud courtroom

Law ne us kamre ko badalne ki koshish ki hai jahan woh gawahi deti hai. Rape trials in camera hone chahiye, aur jahan tak ho sake woman judge ke saamne [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) ke under uska character aur pichhla sexual experience consent ke sawaal par irrelevant hai (Section 48), aur consent saabit karne ke liye cross-examination mein in par sawaal nahi pooche ja sakte (Section 149) [[indiacode-bsa-2023]].

Phir bhi rules us insaan par depend karte hain jo bench par baitha hai. 10 February 2026 ko Supreme Court ne ek aise case mein faisla diya jo usne khud uthaya tha, jab ek High Court ne child sexual assault ke ek case mein charges ko attempt to rape se ghata kar halke offences kar diya tha. Court ne kaha ki judges ko sensitise karne ki koshishein "have not borne the fruit that was expected". Usne National Judicial Academy ki ek expert committee se sexual-offence cases mein sensitivity par guidelines banane ko kaha [[sc-judgments-and-gender-2026]].

Iska matlab yeh nahi ki kamzor saboot par saza de di jaaye. Matlab yeh hai ki saboot jaldi banaya jaaye aur use bachaya jaaye. Survivor naam lekar maang sakti hai: 24 ghante ke andar examination aur magistrate ke saamne statement. Aur police ko 90 din ke andar use investigation ka progress update dena hota hai [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].

13,980 un auraton ki ginti nahi hai jinhone jhooth bola. Yeh un cases ki ginti hai jinhe State saabit nahi kar paaya, ek aise system mein jiski kamzor kadiyaan uski apni rule book mein pehle se likhi hain.

witness-protection-gaps-rape-trials.en:
In most rape trials the main witness is the survivor herself, and the accused is usually someone she knows. In 96.8% of the rape cases registered in India in 2024, 28,597 of 29,536, the offender was someone the victim knew [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Between the FIR and the verdict she has to stay housed, employed and willing to speak, sometimes within walking distance of him. This is an account of who is supposed to protect her in that time, and where the protection runs out.

## Testifying against someone you know

NCRB sorts the known offenders into three groups: family members in 2,134 cases; family friends, neighbours, employers or other known persons in 12,584; and friends, online friends, live-in partners on the pretext of marriage or separated husbands in 13,879 [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Each is a man with a route to her door, her phone or her wages.

Then comes the wait. The law says a rape trial should finish within two months of the chargesheet, but sets no consequence when it does not [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. At the end of 2024, 1,85,785 rape cases were pending trial, 89.8% of the 2,06,777 before the courts that year [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Consider this situation: a 23-year-old domestic worker in a small town reports her employer's son. He gets bail. She loses the job the same week, her landlord is his uncle, and every court date costs a day's pay. Nobody has threatened her. Everything around her has.

## What the law offers: in camera, no-contact bail, state protection

- **A closed courtroom.** Rape and POCSO trials must be held in camera, as far as practicable before a woman judge, and nothing may be published about them without the court's permission [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Shields for children.** In a POCSO trial, for boys as well as girls, the court must keep the child from being exposed to the accused, using video links, one-way mirrors or curtains if needed [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].
- **No-contact bail.** On 18 March 2021, in Aparna Bhat v. State of Madhya Pradesh, the Supreme Court ruled that bail conditions "should not mandate, require or permit contact between the accused and the victim" [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]].

Only one law on this list puts the burden on the state in so many words. Section 15A of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, added in 2015, says:

> "It shall be the duty and responsibility of the State to make arrangements for the protection of victims, their dependents, and witnesses against any kind of intimidation or coercion or inducement or violence or threats of violence."

It also gives victims the right to notice of court proceedings, including bail hearings [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]]. But it covers only Dalit and Adivasi victims in cases under that Act. For every other survivor, protection outside the courtroom mostly has to be asked for, and it helps only the witness who knows to ask. The other protections work inside a courtroom or a bail order. The pressure works everywhere else.

## Unnao: what happened when protection failed

In 2017 a minor girl in Unnao, Uttar Pradesh, was raped by a man who was then an MLA. In April 2018 her father was assaulted, then arrested on an illegal-firearms charge, and died in custody [[barandbench-unnao-father-2020]].

What finally worked was distance. The Supreme Court moved all the Unnao trials from Lucknow to Delhi, and on 20 December 2019 a Delhi court sentenced the former MLA, Kuldeep Singh Sengar, to imprisonment for the remainder of his life [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]]. On 13 March 2020 a Delhi court gave him and six others 10 years for culpable homicide over the father's death [[barandbench-unnao-father-2020]].

In December 2025 the Delhi High Court suspended the life sentence pending his appeal; the Supreme Court stayed that order on 29 December 2025 [[scobserver-unnao-stay-2025]] and set it aside on 15 May 2026, sending the matter back to the High Court, where the appeal is pending [[livelaw-unnao-sc-2026]].

The courts punished men for the father's death. Nothing prevented it. Relief came only when the country's highest court stepped in, and few families can reach that court.

## Fear as evidence: what the Hema Committee heard

Fear of testifying is rarely written down. In 2017 the Kerala government set up the Justice K. Hema Committee to study sexual harassment and gender inequality in the Malayalam film industry [[hindu-hema-coverage-2024]]. Many women it approached were at first reluctant to speak because "they were afraid they would lose their jobs". The committee wrote: "In the beginning, we found their fear strange but as our study progressed we realised it was well-founded. We are concerned about their and their close relatives' safety" [[bbc-hema-report-2024]].

When the report came out in August 2024, 63 pages of the 295-page draft were held back to protect the identities of witnesses and those accused [[nie-hema-report-release-2024]].

The committee treated fear as a finding. A court records only the result: of 20,587 rape trials completed in 2024, 13,980 ended in acquittal and 5,032 in conviction [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Those figures do not say how many acquittals followed a witness who stopped speaking.

## Asking for protection: who to approach and what to document

This is general information, not legal advice. In practice, protection has to be asked for, in writing.

1. **Keep a threat log:** dates, screenshots, call records, and the names of anyone who arrives with an "offer".
2. **Report every contact in writing** to the investigating officer and the public prosecutor, and ask the court to cancel bail.
3. **Ask for courtroom protections by name:** an in-camera hearing and, for a child, a video link or screen.
4. **Under the Atrocities Act,** cite Section 15A to the Special Court and insist on notice of every hearing.
5. **Get your own lawyer.** The District Legal Services Authority gives free legal aid [[nalsa]]. In danger, call 112.

If local power is the danger, a higher court can move the trial: in May 2018 the Supreme Court sent the Kathua trial out of Jammu and Kashmir to Pathankot [[theprint-kathua-transfer-2018]].

Until protection is something the state must offer rather than something a survivor must request, many trials will turn on how long one frightened witness can hold out.
witness-protection-gaps-rape-trials.hg:
Zyada tar rape trials mein main witness khud survivor hoti hai, aur accused aksar koi aisa hota hai jise woh jaanti hai. 2024 mein India mein register hue 96.8% rape cases mein, yaani 29,536 mein se 28,597 mein, offender victim ka jaan-pehchaan wala tha [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. FIR aur verdict ke beech use apna ghar, apni naukri aur bolne ki himmat bachaye rakhni hoti hai, kabhi-kabhi usse bas kuch galiyon ki doori par. Ye report is baare mein hai ki us dauraan use bachana kiski zimmedari hai, aur protection kahan khatam ho jaati hai.

## Jise jaante ho, uske khilaaf gawahi

NCRB jaan-pehchaan wale offenders ko teen groups mein baantta hai: 2,134 cases mein family members; 12,584 mein family friends, neighbours, employers ya doosre jaan-pehchaan wale; aur 13,879 mein friends, online friends, shaadi ke bahaane live-in partners ya alag rehne wale husbands [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Har ek aisa aadmi hai jiske paas uske darwaaze, uske phone ya uski kamai tak ka raasta hai.

Phir aata hai intezaar. Law kehta hai ki rape trial chargesheet ke two months ke andar khatam ho jaana chahiye, lekin aisa na hone par koi consequence tay nahi karta [[indiacode-bnss-2023]]. 2024 ke end mein 1,85,785 rape cases trial ke liye pending the, us saal court ke saamne aaye 2,06,777 cases ka 89.8% [[ncrb-cii-2024]].

Ek situation socho: ek chhote shehar ki 23 saal ki domestic worker apne employer ke bete ke khilaaf report karti hai. Ladke ko bail mil jaati hai. Usi hafte uski naukri chali jaati hai, uska landlord us ladke ka chacha hai, aur har court date par ek din ki kamai kat jaati hai. Kisi ne use dhamki nahi di. Uske aas-paas sab kuch dhamki ban gaya hai.

## Law kya deta hai: in camera, no-contact bail, state protection

- **Band courtroom.** Rape aur POCSO trials in camera hone chahiye, jahan tak ho sake woman judge ke saamne, aur court ki permission ke bina unke baare mein kuch publish nahi kiya ja sakta [[indiacode-bnss-2023]].
- **Bachchon ke liye shield.** POCSO trial mein, ladke ho ya ladkiyan, court ko bachche ko accused ke saamne aane se bachana hota hai, zaroorat ho to video link, one-way mirror ya curtain se [[indiacode-pocso-2012]].
- **No-contact bail.** 18 March 2021 ko Aparna Bhat v. State of Madhya Pradesh mein Supreme Court ne kaha ki bail conditions "should not mandate, require or permit contact between the accused and the victim" [[livelaw-aparna-bhat-2021]].

Is list mein sirf ek law hai jo saaf shabdon mein bojh state par daalta hai. SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act ka Section 15A, jo 2015 mein joda gaya, kehta hai:

> "It shall be the duty and responsibility of the State to make arrangements for the protection of victims, their dependents, and witnesses against any kind of intimidation or coercion or inducement or violence or threats of violence."

Ye victims ko court proceedings, bail hearings samet, ka notice paane ka right bhi deta hai [[gazette-sc-st-poa-amendment-act-2015]]. Lekin ye sirf us Act ke cases mein Dalit aur Adivasi victims ko cover karta hai. Baaki har survivor ke liye, courtroom ke bahar protection zyada tar maangni padti hai, aur woh sirf us witness ki madad karti hai jise maangna pata ho. Baaki protections courtroom ya bail order ke andar kaam karti hain. Pressure baaki har jagah kaam karta hai.

## Unnao: jab protection fail hui

2017 mein Unnao, Uttar Pradesh ki ek minor ladki ka rape ek aise aadmi ne kiya jo tab MLA tha. April 2018 mein uske father par hamla hua, phir unhe illegal-firearms charge mein arrest kiya gaya, aur custody mein unki maut ho gayi [[barandbench-unnao-father-2020]].

Aakhir mein jo kaam aaya, woh tha doori. Supreme Court ne Unnao ke saare trials Lucknow se Delhi shift kar diye, aur 20 December 2019 ko Delhi court ne former MLA Kuldeep Singh Sengar ko remainder of his life ki imprisonment ki saza di [[barandbench-unnao-sentence-2019]]. 13 March 2020 ko Delhi court ne use aur chhe aur logon ko father ki maut ke liye culpable homicide mein 10 years ki saza di [[barandbench-unnao-father-2020]].

December 2025 mein Delhi High Court ne appeal pending rehne tak life sentence suspend kar diya; Supreme Court ne 29 December 2025 ko us order par stay lagaya [[scobserver-unnao-stay-2025]] aur 15 May 2026 ko use set aside karke matter wapas High Court bhej diya, jahan appeal pending hai [[livelaw-unnao-sc-2026]].

Sequence ko seedha padho. Courts ne father ki maut ke liye logon ko saza di. Us maut ko kisi ne roka nahi. Rahat tab mili jab desh ki sabse oonchi court ne dakhal diya, aur bahut kam families us court tak pahunch paati hain.

## Darr bhi evidence hai: Hema Committee ne kya suna

Gawahi dene ka darr shayad hi kabhi likha jaata hai. 2017 mein Kerala government ne Malayalam film industry mein sexual harassment aur gender inequality ki study ke liye Justice K. Hema Committee banayi [[hindu-hema-coverage-2024]]. Committee jin auraton tak pahunchi, unmein se kai shuru mein bolne se hichkichaayi kyunki "they were afraid they would lose their jobs". Committee ne likha: "In the beginning, we found their fear strange but as our study progressed we realised it was well-founded. We are concerned about their and their close relatives' safety" [[bbc-hema-report-2024]].

Jab August 2024 mein report bahar aayi, to 295-page draft ke 63 pages witnesses aur accused ki identity bachane ke liye roke gaye [[nie-hema-report-release-2024]].

Committee ne darr ko ek finding maana. Court sirf nateeja record karta hai: 2024 mein poore hue 20,587 rape trials mein se 13,980 acquittal aur 5,032 conviction par khatam hue [[ncrb-cii-2024]]. Ye figures nahi batate ki kitne acquittals tab hue jab ek witness ne bolna band kar diya.

## Protection maangna: kiske paas jaana hai aur kya document karna hai

Ye general information hai, legal advice nahi. Practically, protection likhit mein maangni padti hai.

1. **Threat log rakho:** dates, screenshots, call records, aur har us insaan ka naam jo koi "offer" lekar aaye.
2. **Har contact ki report likhit mein do** investigating officer aur public prosecutor ko, aur court se bail cancel karne ko kaho.
3. **Courtroom protections naam lekar maango:** in-camera hearing aur, bachche ke liye, video link ya screen.
4. **Atrocities Act ke under,** Special Court mein Section 15A cite karo aur har hearing ke notice par zor do.
5. **Apna lawyer lo.** District Legal Services Authority free legal aid deti hai [[nalsa]]. Khatre mein ho to 112 call karo.

Agar local power hi khatra hai, to higher court trial shift kar sakti hai: May 2018 mein Supreme Court ne Kathua trial ko Jammu and Kashmir se bahar Pathankot bhej diya [[theprint-kathua-transfer-2018]].

Jab tak protection aisi cheez nahi banti jo state ko deni hi padti hai, na ki aisi jo survivor ko maangni padti hai, tab tak kai trials is baat par tike rahenge ki ek dari hui witness kitni der tak tik paati hai.
